artifact.sources_used: <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 7.800 s.v. Soteria add. no. 2 (J.-C. Balty), 409 s.v. Phylonoe 4 no. 1 (L. Kahil), 604 s.v. Pylios 1 no. 1, pl. 488 (M. artifact.context: Athens (from the pyre of a grave near the Acharnian Gate).<lb>Lid restored from
artifact.graffiti: Shapiro (37) suggests that Pylios' name has a "princely" connection with the Neleid dynasty of Pylos); his relation to Basileia may then be explained by the sanctuary that Basile shared in Athens with Neleus and Kodros.
artifact.decoration_description:
Lid: Birth of Erichthonios, attended by Soteria.

Body: Athena punishing the daughters of Kekrops. The three girls run to the left, rushing as the snake rears up from the chest they had opened, in disobedience of the goddess; Athena also rushes 3/4-view to the left behind Aglauros, right leg advanced, wearing an aegis over a chiton (?), with a himation flying behind her, and an Attic helmet, holds an olive branch in her outstretched right hand, and a spear in her bent left arm; Basileia runs 3/4-view to the right, head turned profile to the left, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, and a himation draped around her left shoulder, and flying behind her, and a kekryphylon, reaches both hands (fingers spread) to the right; nude, youthful Pylios, standing 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his right leg, wearing a chlamys over his left shoulder, and calf-length, strap boots, holds two spears diagonally, in his lowered left hand, and rests his right hand on his hip; Chryseis, running 3/4-view to the left, with her head turned profile to the right, and weight on her forward, bent, right leg, wearing a belted peplos, kekryphylon (?), and stephane (?), holds an unidentified object in her upraised right hand, and reaches her left arm seemingly to the right; Eunoe, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted chiton with shoulder straps, and a high pony tail, raises both arms to the sides; Philonoe (?), seated profile to the left, wearing a himation over a chiton (?), and a sphendone.

artifact.name: Louvre S 1677
artifact.summary: Gigantomachy
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Zeus descends in his quadriga, driven by Nike, on a giant and an Amazon. To his right are Dionysos, driving a panther biga to the right, Poseidon on horseback, and Hekate, aiming an arrow to the left. Beneath them are Demeter and Hermes. Beneath Zeus are Athena, attacking a giant to her left, and Herakles, struggling with the opponents of Zeus. To Zeus' left are Apollo (facing left) and Artemis (facing right), brandishing torches.

Side B: Ares, climbing up to a chariot (to the right), conducted by Aphrodite, battles against three giants. A small Eros is perched on one of the horses, and aims his bow. Beneath are Kore (Persephone) and a giant; to the right are the Dioskouroi, both on horseback, one of whom battles an adversary of Ares.
artifact.shape_description: Neck amphora with twisted handles

artifact.name: Louvre N 3157
artifact.summary: Side A (above): Busts of Hermes, a woman, Pan, and a young satyr<lb>Side A (below): Kadmos and the dragon<lb>Side B: A woman between a youth and a Pan-satyr
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Kadmos, nude except his pilos (helmet) and chlamys (cape), lunges 3/4-view to the right at a coiled snake (dragon), who rises from a spring (amid rocks). Kadmos holds an amphora (which he hopes to fill with water) in his lowered left hand, and a rock in his raised right arm, with which he threatens the snake. Behind him stands a woman, probably Harmonia, wearing a himation draped around her hips, over a sleevless chiton, holding a phiale in her right hand, at waist level. Opposite her, behind the snake, stands a similarly dressed woman, probably Ismene (the personification of the spring), who holds her drapery over her right shoulder with her right hand, and holds a sprig in her lowered left hand. Above them are busts of Hermes, holding a caduceus, and wearing a wreath, petasos (floppy hat), and chlamys; a woman looking at a mirror, Pan, and a young satyr holding a thyrsos and a wreath.

Side B: A youth, wearing a himation around his waist and lower body, and a wreath, stands 3/4-view to the right, and rests his weight on his left leg, and a staff under his left hand. A woman, wrapped in a himation, draped across her torso diagonally, and a kekryphylon, stands in a similar posture. She holds her right hand across her chest and holds an egg, in her left hand, at waist level, which she offers to a nude, beardless satyr (?) opposite her. This satyr stands profile to the left, with his weight on his right leg. He wears a wreath and some garlands around his body. He holds a fillet in his lowered left hand, and raises his right hand toward the woman.

artifact.name: Louvre MNE 961
artifact.summary: Tondo: A satyr dances in front of a table that supports a kantharos<lb>Side A: Youths draped in himatia, holding staffs; a seated youth holds a lyre<lb>Side B: Youths, draped, sitting and standing
artifact.other_bibliography: <bibl>Kunisch 1997, 70, fig. 33, pl. 164</bibl>; <bibl><hi rend="ital">Bulletin des Musees et Monuments Lyonnais</hi>4 (1996) 42-43, figs. 4a-b</bibl>; <hi rend="ital">Revue du Louvre</hi> 41 (1991) 5-6, 13-16
artifact.decoration_description:
Tondo: A nude satyr, wearing a red fillet tied around his head, is shown in a frontal pose, with his head turned profile to the left; he dances, with his weight temporarily on his right leg, holds both hands on his waist, and looks down at a table to the left, on which a kantharos rests.

Side A: A youth, wearing a himation, leans 3/4-view to the right, on his staff, and holds his hand on his hip. A second youth, wearing a himation and a narrow red taenia, sits profile to the right on a box, and plays a lyre; behind him is a cross ornament. A third youth, wearing a himation, leans profile to the left, on his staff, and holds a sprig forward, in his right hand, as a gesture to the musician.

Side B: A youth, wearing a himation, sits near profile to the right on a box; he holds a sprig in his right hand, and a staff upright in his left hand. A second youth, swathed in a himation, sits profile to the right on a box; behind him is a cross ornament. A third youth, wearing a himation, leans profile to the left, on his staff, and holds his right hand in front of his face, in a speaking gesture.

artifact.name: Louvre K 570
artifact.summary: Apollo, Marsyas, and Muses
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>Paquette 1984, 126-27, fig. C47</bibl>; <bibl>Trendall 1952, no. 63</bibl>; <bibl>Trendall 1936, no. 51, pl. 11c, fig. 23</bibl>
artifact.decoration_description: A white temple, shown in 3/4-view, sets the scene. To the right of the temple sits Marsyas, a balding, bearded satyr, 3/4-view to the right. He wears high leather boots and a chlamys, and plays double pipes. In front of him sits Apollo, wearing high boots, a belted, short Oriental tunic, a chlamys, and a wreath. He sits profile to the right, playing a kithara. A muse, also seated profile to the right, wearing a belted, short-sleeved chiton and a himation (draped around her hips), with a kithara on her lap, turns her head profile to the left, to face Apollo. She rests her upraised right arm on a shield (?) behind her. Another muse (?), seated profile to the right, dressed similarly to the first muse, but with drapery veiled over the back of her head, holds a wreath in her left hand, and opens a box with her left hand. Opposite her is another muse, seated profile to the left, with her upper torso in 3/4-view. She wears the himation wrapped around her hips and legs, over a belted, sleeveless, chiton. She holds a barbiton in her lowered left hand, and raises her right hand in front of her face (a speaking or singing gesture?).

artifact.name: Louvre K 240
artifact.summary: Side A: Papposilen, Dionysos, a maenad, and a satyr boy, moving to the right<lb>Side B: A woman, a goose, and Eros
artifact.other_bibliography: <bibl>LIMC, 3.891 (Eros) no. 485b, pl. 635.2</bibl>; Schauenburg, in <bibl>Moon 1983, 276, figs. 17, 38</bibl>; <bibl>Webster 1978, 104</bibl>; <bibl>Trendall 1967, 92 no. xii, pl. 14c</bibl>; <bibl>Trendall 1952, no. 91</bibl>; <bibl>Trendall 1936, no. 54, fig. 14</bibl>
artifact.decoration_description: On side A, four figures advance to the right: a nude Papposilen, with a white beard, holds a cista in his left hand, a thyrsos--from which dangles a female mask--over his left shoulder, and raises his hand above his head. Dionysos, half-draped, rides on the back of a panther. He wears a himation draped over his hips and legs, holds a wreath in his right hand, and in his left hand a thyrsos, also with a female mask. A maenad, shown in near profile, wearing a belted, sleeveless tunic and a wreath, plays a flute which she holds with both hands. A nude satyr boy who holds a flute in his upraised left hand, reaches his right hand to the maenad behind him. On side B two figures stand on either side of a goose: a standing woman, shown 3/4-view to the right, wears a belted peplos. She holds a phiale in her left hand, at waist level, and raises her right arm above her shoulder. Behind her is a short stele. Opposite her stands Eros, profile to the left, nude except a wreath, who holds a wreath in his lowered right hand, and a phiale in his upraised left hand.

artifact.summary: Komasts

Side B: A bearded man wearing a chlamys draped over his right arm, and a thick taenia, advances to the left; he holds a kylix in his right hand and a staff horizontally in his left hand.

A plastically rendered lion's head serves as the bottom of the rhyton; the lion is shown with white teeth and a red tongue lolling out of his opened mouth.

artifact.name: Louvre G 477
artifact.summary: Tondo: A woman with a basket, between a door and an altar<lb>Sides A and B: more women
artifact.collection_history: Said to have been found in Italy in 1863.
artifact.decoration_description:
Tondo: A woman, wearing a himation over a medium-sleved chiton, an earring, and a sakkos, stands in a frontal view, and holds a large box in both hands; she looks profile to the left, at a door, behind her; to her right is a low altar crowned with a volute, from which flames billow.

Side A: A woman standing in 3/4-view to the left, wearing a himation over a short-sleeved chiton, holds a hoop (wreath?) in her right hand, and turns her head profile to the right, to face another woman, who stands in a frontal pose, in front of a klismos (chair), is dressed like the first, but also wears a sakkos. She turns her head profile to the left to smell a rose; an Ionic column divides this woman from a third woman, who is entirely enveloped in a himation, draped over a chiton. She stands profile to the right and faces a cloth sack that hangs on the wall.

Side B: A woman standing in 3/4-view to the right, in front of a klismos (chair), wearing a himation over a chiton, holds a unidentifiable object in her left hand. She faces another woman, who stands 3/4-view to the left, and reaches her right hand our in front of her. An Ionic column divides this woman from a third woman, who, dressed similarly to the first two, but also wears a sakkos on her head, stands in a frontal view, with her head turned profile to the left, and raises her arms, as if in fright.

The area beneath each handle is decorated with a palmette, above volutes.
artifact.shape_description: Kylix

artifact.name: Louvre G 457
artifact.summary: Tondo: Linos and Mousaios<lb>Sides A: Two athletes between a man and a woman<lb>Side B: Athletes
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.10 m; Diam. (lip) 0.25 m; W. (max.) 0.33 m
artifact.collection_history: Said to have been found at Cerveteri in 1863.
artifact.decoration_description:
Tondo: Mousaios, a nude youth wearing a white taenia, stands profile to the right, with his right hand on his hip, and holds a tablet in his upraised left hand; behind him is a footed box; in front of him, on a klismos, sits his teacher, Linos, a bearded man wearing a himation around his lower body and a wreath; he unrolls a book scroll on which letters are barely distinguishable.

Side A: A bearded man (a trainer?), standing in a frontal pose, with his head turned profile to the left, wears a himation draped over his left shoulder and a white wreath; he holds a forked stick upright in his left hand. A nude athlete, wearing a white wreath, stands profile to the right, and holds halteres (jumping weights) ahead of his body, in both hands, while he leans back; another nude athlete, standing in a relaxed pose, profile to the right, seemingly talks with the woman opposite him, who stands 3/4-view to the left, and wears a himation over an undergarment, as well as a narrow taenia.

Side B: An athlete, standing in a frontal pose, with his head profile to the right, holds a strigil in his lowered right hand and a pick (shown upside down) in his left hand. Next to him stands another nude athlete, in a frontal pose, with his left hand on his hip and his right hand held up to his head. A third athlete, standing in a frontal pose, with his head profile to the right, holds his right arm directly to the left, and rests his left hand on his hip. Next to him stands another nude athlete, shown in a 3/4 back view, scraping his arm with a strigil; between them hangs an animal skin that seems to act as a shower, emitting water.

The area around each handle is decorated with palmettes: enclosed palmettes are placed on either side of the handle, and two symetrically arranged palmettes, divided by volutes, decorate the space beneath the handle.
artifact.inscriptions: White dipinti label the figures, generally above their heads: On the tondo: <Foreign lang=Greek>*M*O*S*A*I*O*S, *L*I*N*O*S</Foreign>; on side A; on side B
artifact.shape_description: Kylix

artifact.name: Louvre G 448
artifact.summary: Tondo: A satyr with a maenad<lb>Side A: Youths with a horse<lb>Side B: A man with youths
artifact.decoration_description:
Tondo: A nude, ithyphallic, balding, bearded satyr, leans profile to the right, toward a woman who runs to the right, but turns her head profile to the left, to look at the satyr. She wears a short himation over a medium-sleeved chiton, while a sakkos covers her hair, and carries a kantharos in her right hand, and a thyrsos in her left hand.

Side A: A youth, standing in a frontal pose, leaning on a staff under his left arm, and wearing a himation, turns his head profile to the right, and thrusts the palm of his hand, shown in a rare frontal pose, out towards the viewer; to his right stands another youth, dressed in Thracian boots (embades), a chitoniskos belted over a long overfold, a chlamys, and a (Thracian) fox-skin hat, reaches to the right, to stroke the nose of his horse. The horse stands profile to the left, in front of a schematic Ionic capital, supporting a narrow entablature. The horse is somewhat agitated, as indicated by his advancing left foot and the open lips. A youth, standing in a 3/4-view to the left, but leaning on a staff below his left arm, turns his head profile to the right, to look at another youth, who stands in near profile to the left, holds a staff in his left hand, and gestures with his opened right palm; both wear himatia.

View of side B: two youths, both wearing himatia, stand together and talk. The first is shown frontally, with his head turned profile to the right; he rests his right hand on his hip and holds a staff in his lowered left hand. The second youth stands profile to the left, facing him, and points his finger aggressively at the first youth. A bearded man, wearing a himation around his legs and lower torso, sits profile to the right on a stool (diphros), rests his left hand on a staff, and holds his right hand over his head. To the right of him stand two more youths, both wrapped in himation. The first, show profile to the left, tilts his head down slightly, and holds a staff beneath his right arm. The second, standing in a frontal pose, with his head turned profile to the right, reaches to touch the first youth on the shoulder.
artifact.shape_description: Kylix

artifact.name: Louvre G 44
artifact.summary: Side A: A warrior, mounting a chariot<lb>Side B: A mature woman, a man, and a youth
artifact.collection_history: Acquired by the Louvre in 1848.
artifact.graffiti: There is an incised graffito on the underside of the base (resting surface).
artifact.inscriptions:
On side A: *D*A[*M]*A*S* X*A*I[*R*E] *S*O*S*I*S and *X*A*R*X*H.

On Side B: [...]*A*S (retrograde), *X*A*I*R*E and *T*I[...]

artifact.name: Louvre G 25
artifact.summary: Tondo: A man vomiting, accompanied by a dog<lb>Sides A and B (exterior): Warriors
artifact.collection_history: Ex Coll. Branteghem; acquired by the Louvre in 1892.
artifact.inscriptions: On the tondo: <Foreign lang=Greek>*L*E*A*G*R*O*S</Foreign>; on side A: <Foreign lang=Greek>*L*E*A*G*R*O*S *K*A*L*O*S</Foreign>; on side B: <Foreign lang=Greek>*L*E*A[*G]*R*O*S *K*A*L*O*S</Foreign>

artifact.name: Louvre G 13
artifact.summary: Tondo: An amorous youth, holding a cup and a staff, hugging a female lyre player<lb>Sides A and B: Individuals making love
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.195 m; W. 0.32 m; Diam. (lip) ca. 0.25 m; Diam. (foot) 0.095 m
artifact.inscriptions: There are several (repeated) kalos inscriptions. On the tondo: <Foreign lang=Greek>*E*P*I*L*U*K*O*S *K*A*L*O*S</Foreign>, "Epilykos is beautiful." <Foreign lang=Greek>*E*P*I*L*U[*K*O*S*K*A*L*O*S]</Foreign>. On side B: <Foreign lang=Greek>[*E*P*I]*L*U*K*O*S*K*A*L*O*S</Foreign>.
artifact.shape_description: Type B

artifact.name: Louvre G 10
artifact.summary: Tondo: Hermes holding a flower<lb>Side A: Herakles and Acheloos<lb>Side B: lost
artifact.inscriptions: The misleading "signature" on the tondo, <Foreign lang=Greek>*E*P*I*L*U*K*O[*S*E*G*R*A*F]*S*E*N*K*A*L*O*S</Foreign>, which reads "Beautiful Epilykos painted it," is explained by Beazley as a mistake, a conflation of an artist's signature with a kalos inscription, for Skythes (in whose style the vase is painted) frequently inscribed his vases with kalos inscriptions for Epilykos.

artifact.name: Louvre F 75
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos and Ariadne among satyrs and maenads<lb>Side B: hoplites and cavalrymen
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.145 m; Diam. (lip) 0.25 m; W. (incl. handles) 0.325 m
artifact.collection_history: Acquired by the Louvre in the Paravey sale, 1879.
artifact.shape_description: Band cup

artifact.name: Louvre F 55
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and Geryon, with Eurytion, the herdsman, between them<lb>Side B: Dionysos and satyrs
artifact.graffiti: Under the foot is an incised graffito.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora

artifact.name: Louvre F 53
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and Geryon, with Eurytion between them<lb>Side B: Anchippos (a warrior) leaving home in a quadriga (four-horse chariot)
artifact.collection_history: Acquired by the Louvre in 1883.
artifact.inscriptions:
Black dipinti name all characters, among other inscriptions. On side A, behind Herakles, is Exekias' signature, *E*X*S*E*K*I*A*S*E*P*O*I*E*S*E, "Exekias made it."

Also on side A: to the right of Herakles's head, *H*E*R*A*K*L*E*S ("Herakles"); above Eurytion's body, retrograde, *E*U*R*U*T*I*O*N, "Eurytion"; between the legs of Geryon, *G*E*R*U*O*N*E[*S], "Geryon"; on the right side, a kalos inscription, *S*T*E*S*I*W*S*K*A*L*O*S, "Stesios is beautiful."

On side B, to the right of Anchippos' head, *A*N*X*I*P*O*S, "Anchippos"; to the right of the siren, the name of one horse, [...]*S*E*M*O*S; in the top right, the name of another horse, *P*U*R*O*K*O*M[...]; in the bottom right, the name of a third horse: *K*A*L*I*&koppa;*O*M*E[...]; and beneath the belly of the foremost horse, *K*A*L*I*F*O*R*A.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora

artifact.name: Louvre F 36
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and Kyknos, between Athena and Ares<lb>Side B: Dionysos with revellers

artifact.name: Louvre F 30
artifact.summary: Herakles entering Olympos, with Poseidon, Hermes, and Athena
artifact.collection_history: Acquired by the Louvre in 1880; from an unknown provenance.
artifact.comparanda: Beazley (in <bibl>ABV</bibl>) compares the subject to that on <rs type="vase">Tarquinia RC 1871</rs>.
artifact.inscriptions: Signed in black dipinti, between the figures of Athena and Hermes: <Foreign lang=Greek>*M*E*P*O*I*E[*S*E]*N *A*M*A*S*I*S</Foreign>, "Amasis made me."
artifact.shape_description: Olpe with trefoil mouth.

artifact.name: Louvre F 26
artifact.summary: Side A: A warrior with youths, one winged (Zethos?)<lb>Side B: A youth with a hare (gift), approaching a man, between two other men
artifact.graffiti: A graffito under the foot seems to indicate the characters<Foreign lang=Greek>*H*D</Foreign>
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora

artifact.name: Louvre F 203
artifact.summary: Side A: Preparation of Amazons<lb>Side B: Women (Amazons?) bathing
artifact.other_bibliography: <bibl>Boardman 1975, fig. 4</bibl>
artifact.collection_history: Said to have been acquired in Etruria in 1863.
artifact.decoration_description: Beazley notes that this vase is decorated with a special technique, similar to red figure, but on a white ground.
artifact.inscriptions: Inscribed on the foot is Andokides' signature: <Foreign lang=Greek>*A*N*D*O*K*I*D*E*S*E*P*O*E*S*E*N</Foreign>
artifact.shape_description: Type A amphora

artifact.name: Louvre F 201
artifact.summary: Side A (neck): Ajax with the body of Achilles, flanked by an archer and a woman<lb>Side B (neck): Dionysos between a satyr and a maenad

artifact.name: Louvre F 19
artifact.summary: Side A: Departure of warriors, with Hermes, Poseidon, and others<lb>Side B: Horsemen; departure of a warrior<lb>Friezes on handles: Bellerophon and Pegasos, among others<lb>Neck: Departure of a warrior (side A); Komasts and Poseidon (side B)
artifact.shape_description: Neck amphora with ribbed handles

artifact.name: Louvre F 125
artifact.summary: Side A (Red Figure): Horse between eyes<lb>Side B (Red Figure): nude youth, running to the right, between eyes<lb>Tondo (Black Figure): Bearded man, wearing boots, chlamys, and ivy wreath, running to the right
artifact.collection_history: Found on the land of the Ania family at Cavalupo, December 1828. Formerly in the Canino Collection.
artifact.inscriptions: Black dipinto on the bottom of the tondo: <Foreign lang=Greek>[*N*I*]K*O*S*Q*E*N*E*S *E*P*O*I*E*S[*E*N]</Foreign>, "(Niko?)sthenes made it."
artifact.shape_description: Eye cup

artifact.name: Louvre F 123
artifact.summary: Ships with dolphins under each handle
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.11 m; Diam. (lip) 0.28 m; Diam. (max.) 0.35 m
artifact.collection_history: Ex Colls. Canino, Durand, Beugnot, Hope, and Ronel. Given to the Louvre in 1866.
artifact.decoration_description: The scenes on both sides are almost exact: Two ships, almost parallel to each other, each manned by one oarsman and one navigator (?), clad in a himation, standing at the prow. To the right of each scene is a Siren, sitting on a branch near the handle.
artifact.inscriptions: Dipinto (in black) above sails on side A, right: <Foreign lang=Greek>*N*I*K*O*S*Q*E*N*E*S*E[*P]*O*I*E[*S*E*N]</Foreign>, "Nikosthenes made it."

artifact.name: Louvre F 122
artifact.summary: Tondo: Gorgon<lb>Side A: Aeneas and Anchises, with Ascanius, between eyes<lb>Side B: A fight, between eyes<lb>A vine is shown at each handle
artifact.collection_history: From Doganella, excavated by the Prince of Canino, October 1828.
artifact.inscriptions: Dipinto under the eyebrow on side A, left: <Foreign lang=Greek>*N*I*K*O*S*Q*E*N*E*S*E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N</Foreign>, "Nikias made it."
artifact.shape_description: Eye cup

artifact.summary: Neck (both): Naked woman with a dog (?)<lb>Handles (both): tripods

artifact.shape_description: Nikosthenic type neck amphora

artifact.name: Louvre E 876
artifact.summary: Top frieze: Troilos and Polyxena at the fountain; Centauromachy; komos; return of Hephaistos; symposium<lb>Main frieze: a hoplite and infantry battle<lb>Bottom frieze: a horse race
artifact.inscriptions: <Foreign lang=Greek>*H*E*R*A*K*L*E*S *D*R*O*M*A*S *F*K*G*O*S *L*U*F*O*S *A*L*A*K*E *F*O*R*A*X8S *K*A*L*L*I*E *K*E*G*E*S *O*N...*M*O*S *M*N*E*S*A*R*X*O*S</Foreign> ("chos" is retrograde) <Foreign lang=Greek>*K*L*E*P*T*O*L*E*M*E *D*E*I*P*T*E*S *T*E*L*A*M*O*N *E*L*E*S*O*S</Foreign> (retrograde) <Foreign lang=Greek>*D*E*I*L*O*N*E*F*E*S *T*O*S*X*O*F*N*E ...*A*I*E*A *M*E*D*A*S*A*S</Foreign> (retrograde) <Foreign lang=Greek>*A*N*TE*R*E*A*S *E*U*F*O*R*B*O*S .*P*A*T*L*I. *I*E*N... *P*I*S*T*O...*L*E*O*N *K*E*G*E*S *O*N.*M*O*S</Foreign> (most of the sigmas are retrograde).

artifact.name: Louvre E 817
artifact.summary: Side A: Lion divided by a floral decoration<lb>Side B: Sphinxes divided by a floral decoration supporting a swan<lb>Lower frieze: Sirens, panthers, and a goat between lions
artifact.decoration_description:
Two distinct scenes fill the main zone. On side A, two antithetical standing sphinxes face each other; between them sits a crane on top of an abstracted floral element. On side B are two antithetical standing lions.

A continuous frieze fills the lower zone. From side A, left are shown a lion advancing profile to the right; a goat advancing profile to the right, and grazing; a panther advancing profile to the right; and a siren standing profile to the right, facing another siren.
artifact.shape_description: Belly amphora

artifact.name: Louvre E 803
artifact.summary: Main scene: Herakles and the centaur Nessos, with Deianeira<lb>Shoulder: fawns
artifact.decoration_description:
On the body is depicted the rape of Deianeira by Nessos. On the left stands a woman with a Daedalic hairstyle, wearing a red himation over a black chiton, and a red polos (?), profile to the right. Herakles, wearing his belted lion skin over a short tunic, and his quiver on his back, advances to the right, toward the centaur Nessos, wielding his sword in his right hand. Herakles' wife, Deianeira, wearing a red peplos, rides side-saddle, profile to the right, on the back of the centaur Nessos, but turns her head profile to the left, with her arms upraised, beseeching Herakles to help her. Nessos holds his left hand at waist level and his right hand to his head, seemingly in surprise. On the far right stands a woman, wearing a red himation over a black peplos, profile to the right, holding her himation out in her upraised right hand.

Two antithetical fawns, grazing, with a rosette above their ears.

The base is decorated with rays.

artifact.name: Louvre E 668
artifact.summary: Tondo: Zeus and his eagle
artifact.decoration_description: In the tondo sits a bearded man (Zeus?), profile to the right, facing an eagle; rosettes fill the fields between them, above and below.

artifact.name: Athens, Agora P 12641
artifact.summary: A: Herakles and the Cretan bull.<lb>B: Theseus' centauromachy (Wedding of Peirithoos).
artifact.sources_used: M.B. Moore, <hi rend="ital">Agora</hi> 29 (1998) no. 584, pls. 59-60; <bibl>Matheson 1995</bibl>, 444 no. PEM 15, pl. 166; <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 6.133-34 s.v. Krete no. 7 (M. Andreadakis-Vlasakis); <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 5.s.v. Herakles no. 2309 (ill.) (J. Boardman et al.); <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 4.88 s.v. Europe 1 no. 217 (ill.) (M. Robertson); <bibl>Vollkommer 1988</bibl>, 8-10; R. Vollkommer, "Heraclès et le taureau. L'identification de la scène sur les vases attiques de la deuxième moitié du Ve siècle," <hi rend="ital">BCH</hi> 111 (1987) 153 figs. 2a-b; <bibl>Para</bibl>, 444; C. Callipolitis-Feytmans, <hi rend="ital">Les 'louteria' attiques</hi> (Athens 1965) 35-36; B.B. Shefton, "Herakles and Theseus on a Red-Figured Louterion," <hi rend="ital">Hesperia</hi> 31 (1962) 330-68, pls. 105-106; Brommer, VL 1.132 B 3, 152 B 40, 2.153, 169; J.D. Beazley, "Excavations at Al Mina, Sueidia III. The Red-figured Vases," <hi rend="ital">JHS</hi> 59 (1939) 20; T.L. Shear, "The Campaign of 1938," <hi rend="ital">Hesperia</hi> 8 (1939) 215.
artifact.collection_history: Excavated in the Agora, Section <Foreign lang=Greek>*W</Foreign> #558, in a well.
artifact.decoration_description: A: A female figure, a youth (Iolaos?), standing 3/4-view to the right, carrying two spears, Athena, Herakles, a bull, behind him a female figure, Krete (labelled in retrograde red dipinti) fleeing to the right (only the foot and the bottom of drapery are preserved) near a male figure (Minos?), standing profile to the left; under each handle sits a quietly seated female figure, with her back to the scene (local deities [Shefton], nymphs, or Europe and Pasiphae [Vollkommer]).

artifact.name: Leuven (KUL-A)-1000
artifact.summary: Epidauros and Asklepios with Eukleia
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>Shapiro 1993</bibl>, 65, 234 no. 20, fig. 18; <bibl>Boardman 1989a</bibl>, fig. 305; Burn 1989, 65, 79, fig. 2; <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 4.47 s.v. Eudaimonia 1 no. 3 (H.A. Shapiro), 50 s.v. Eukleia no. 12 (A. Kossatz-Deissmann); <bibl>Shapiro 1988</bibl>, 206; <bibl>Burn 1987</bibl>, 100 M 33, pl. 46; <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 3.803 s.v. Epidauros no. 1 (N. Yalouris); <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 2.868 s.v. Asklepios no. 1, pl. 631 (B. Holtzmann); <bibl>Schefold 1981</bibl>, fig. 70; D. Cramers and E. Simon, "Ein neues Werk des Meidiasmalers," <hi rend="ital">AA</hi> 1978, 67-73.
artifact.collection: Leuven, Katholieke Universiteit, Didaktisch Museum, Archeologie
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Cramers Collection G 36
artifact.decoration_description:
A female figure, perhaps Eukleia or Eutychia (labelled), leaning 3/4-view to the right, with weight on her right leg, wearing a chiton (preserved from the knees down), probably rests her right elbow on the shoulder of Epidauros (missing); Epidauros (labelled), standing near frontal, with her head profile to the right, wearing a peplos, and a two-band stephane, holds a nude baby (top part preserved), Asklepios (labelled), seated frontal in her arms, with long curly hair and a wreath, hangs his left arm at his side (missing below the upper arm), and rests his right arm on the shoulder of Epidauros; a tripod on an Ionic column with a two-stepped base, is slightly obscured by Eudaimonia (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left on her himation, with her legs crossed, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton, a sphendone, dotted disk earrings, a black band necklace, and two white bands on each wrist. She holds a garland between her raised right hand and her lowered left hand.

Simon and Cramers have suggested that the tripod alludes to a victory in a Dithyrambic contest, the winning poem of which probably told a story of Asklepios' birth, and that Eudaimonia's wreath may be another victory symbol.

artifact.name: Boston 50.1743
artifact.summary: Narrow band at base of neck. Close-set grooves around body
artifact.collection_history: Bequest of Charles B. Hoyt
artifact.shape_description: Wide-mouthed amphora

artifact.name: Louvre C 10918
artifact.summary: Cooking scenes decorate the entire surface
artifact.other_bibliography: <bibl>Images 1984, 52, fig. 78</bibl>
artifact.decoration_description:
The tondo depicts a bearded man standing profile to the right, wearing drapery around his waist and hips, holding something (meat?) in his left hand, and reaching his right hand into a large cauldron on a tripod.

The exterior scenes seem to show butchers. Side A depicts a youth (?), advancing profile to the right, behind a long table, who holds a meat clever in his lowered right hand, and an animal leg in his outstretched left hand. Another man, standing profile to the left, reaches for the animal leg, with his right hand, and holds a skewer in his lowered left hand. On side B is depicted another youth (?), advancing profile to the right, who holds skewers in both hands.
artifact.shape_description: Kylix

artifact.name: Louvre C 10793
artifact.summary: Side A: Three herms<lb>Side B: A girl with a sacrificial basket on her head, and a youth reaching for a hydria
artifact.decoration_description: The extant fragments depict, on side A, three herms, the center one shown frontally, with the others turned profile towards it; on side B, a girl, wearing a short-sleeved chiton with a long overfold, advancing profile to the right, holding a sacrificial basket on her head, while a nude youth, behind her (shown in 3/4-view to the left) reaches down to a hydria.

artifact.name: Louvre CA 823
artifact.summary: Above: Herakles and Nereus<lb>Below: A helmet between lions<lb>Back, below: A bird
artifact.material_description: H. Payne and others thought that this piece might be Boeotian.
artifact.decoration_description:
On the shoulder is depicted bearded Herakles, grasping Nereus, a snaky monster, shown profile to the right; Herakles turns profile to the left, to face a lion's head, an epiphany of Nereus as he changes magically into another form.

The main frieze depicts two confronting lions, both shown in profile, with an Attic helmet, shown profile to the right, between them, on the ground; rosettes fill the field behind each lion while, at the back, stands a bird, profile to the left, with his head turned profile to the right.

artifact.name: Louvre CA 598
artifact.summary: Herakles and the Hydra accompanied by Athena and Iolaos
artifact.other_bibliography: <bibl>LIMC 5, s.v. Herakles 2004, pl. 54</bibl>; <bibl>Boardman 1974, fig. 270</bibl>
artifact.decoration_description: Athena, wearing her Aegis and helmet, holding a spear in her lowered right hand, advances profile to the right, and reaches her left arm towards Herakles, seemingly to help him. Herakles and Iolaos both reach to the Hydra, from the left and right respectively. Herakles, wearing his belted lion skin, advances profile to the right, holding a scythe in his upraised left hand, with which to damage the Hydra; Hera's crab is beneath Herakles. Iolaos, wearing greaves, a chlamys over a short tunic, a sword, and a Corinthian helmet, advances profile to the left, grasping the Hydra with his upraised right hand; he grasps a torch in his upraised left hand, which he has lit on a fire, behind him.

artifact.name: Louvre CA 587
artifact.summary: Women engaged in weaving and other household activities
artifact.decoration_description: A continuous figural frieze decorates the outside of the pyxis. A woman seated profile to the right on a klismos, wearing a himation over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a taenia, holds a spindle in her left hand, reaches to her neck with her left hand, and turns her head to a frontal view, as if in surprise. A similarly dressed woman stands 3/4-view to the left, holding a hand loom in her lowered right hand. Another woman, wearing a chiton with a long overfold, and a broad taenia, stands profile to the right and holds an alabastron in her outstretched right hand. On the other side of a footed box stands a woman draped in a himation and wearing a sakkos on her head, profile to the left. A bird stands profile to the right. A woman, seated profile to the right, wears a himation over a sleeveless chiton, and a sphendone in her hair. A lekythos hangs (on the wall) above her. A woman standing in a frontal pose, with her head profile to the left, wears a sleevless chiton and a kekryphylon, and folds a sheet (?). Another woman, standing profile to the left, wearing a peplos and a taenia, holds a footed box. An attenuated Doric column precedes the door to the house; the opened right half of the door reveals, within, a bed piled high with pillows.
artifact.shape_description: Beazley's type B, with a large ring serving as a handle.

artifact.name: Louvre CA 3482
artifact.summary: Side A: The death of Aktaion<lb>Side B: Women and youths
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A hunter, wearing leather boots, a chlamys, and a wreath, and holding an arrow, leans to the right, and faces an olive tree, on either side of which two gilded birds are heraldically arranged. Artemis, wearing a belted peplos, a himation veiled over her head, and a crown, rides a biga (two-horse chariot) of deer, 3/4-view to the right, while Aktaion, a youthful hunter, is attacked by his hunting dogs, and falls backward to the ground (as punishment for having witnessed Artemis' bath). Another youthful hunter, shown in 3/4-back view, wearing leather boots, a chlamys, and a pilos (which falls from his head), drops his club and flees to the right, pursued by a hunting dog, while a bearded man, wearing a taenia and chlamys, and holding a scepter (?), stands in a frontal view, with his head turned profile to the left. A woman wearing a sakkos and a himation over her undergarments sits in a hunched posture, profile to the left.

Side B: A youth wearing a himation and a taenia stands in a frontal view, with his head profile to the left, and rests his left hand on a staff, while, to his right, a woman wearing a himation over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a taenia, stands in a frontal view, with her head profile to the left. She holds a globular vase in her left hand. Another woman, wearing a himation over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a taenia, stands in 3/4-view to the left, and holds a garland (or string of beads?) in her outstretched left hand, and a third woman, wearing a himation and a sakkos, stands profile the the left. A youth, wearing a himation, stands in a frontal view, with his head profile to the left, and supports his right hand on a staff.

Nearly symmetrical palmettes decorate the space between the handles.
artifact.shape_description: Volute krater

artifact.name: Louvre CA 2192
artifact.summary: An owl, wearing a crest, and carrying a spear and shield, advances to the right, toward an olive frond that springs from the ground

artifact.name: Louvre CA 2183
artifact.summary: Shoulder: Erotes<lb>Body: A "clinic" scene
artifact.date_description: The "Clinic Painter" is a follower of Makron.
artifact.decoration_description:
On the shoulder two nude Erotes, with mature bodies and taeniae in their light-colored hair, fly towards each other.

The main scene depicts individuals in a medical clinic. A youth wearing a himation, seated on a klismos, reaches to the arm of a bearded man, wearing a chlamys over his left arm, who leans on a staff in his left hand, and stretches his right hand towards the youth; a shallow bronze bowl sits below him. A seated man, wearing a himation around his lower body, sits on a diphros, profile to left, rests his left hand on his lap, and holds a staff in his upraised right hand. A bearded man, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a himation, raises his right hand in a speaking gesture. Another bearded man, standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation, and leaning profile to the right, on a staff under his left arm, looks down at a nude, bearded dwarf. The dwarf stands in a near frontal view, with his head profile to the left, and a hare draped over his left shoulder. A light-haired, bearded man, wearing a short himation, advances to the right, with his left hand on his hip (?), and his right hand on a staff.
artifact.shape_description: Round aryballos

artifact.name: Louvre CA 1947
artifact.summary: Side A: Satyrs demolishing a tomb<lb>Side B: Athletes with a flute player
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A nude, spotted satyr, with a long beard, stands 3/4-view to the right, holding an axe (?) above his head, with which he attacks a grave mound, upon which sits a sphinx. Another nude, spotted satyr, with a long beard, stands 3/4-view to the left, similarly holding an axe above his head.

Side B: A nude, youthful athlete runs toward the left, with his arms outstretched; his body is shown in 3/4-back view, although his head is turned profile to the right, and tilted down. He seems to run around narrow poles. A youthful male musician, in the center, stands profile to the right, wearing a long himation draped around his shoulders, and playing a double flute. On his right is another nude, youthful athlete, running profile to the left, with his left foot advanced, although he tilts his upper body back; he holds halteres (jumping weights) in both hands, at waist level.
artifact.shape_description: Column krater

artifact.decoration_description: A continouous figural frieze decorates the outside of the pyxis. Between two columns stands a woman, reaching to (kneeling before?) an altar; a wreath is hung on the wall behind her. In the next intercolumniation flies a winged Nike, with a wreath, toward a low altar. A woman, swathed in a himation, is seated profile to the right on a stool, between the last column and a door, to the right of which runs another woman, shown in 3/4-view to the right, toward a basin, although she turns her head profile to the left, toward the door.
