Red stripe around mouth of vessel. Black stripe around foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.9
artifact.summary: Cock and running fox.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: A cock stands on an exergue to right. In background are two lotus blossoms. In the exergue a fox runs to the right. There are chevrons on the ground line. There is a band of dicing between lines and a band of tongues around the outer rim. On the bottom are concentric circles.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.89
artifact.summary: Side A: seated man with staff and two standing youths. Side B: two seated males
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: man sits to the right on a klismos, flanked by two youths. All wear himations, and the two youths also wear red fillets. The man's head is restored from the lips up. The man holds a staff in his left hand and a fruit (fig?) in his right. Facing him at right, one youth leans on a staff. Behind him at left, a second youth sits on a stool. In front of this youth, hanging on the wall, is a pair of sandals.

Side B: man seated on a block between two standing youths. All wear himations. The man and youth at left wear red fillets. The man holds a staff in his left hand and twists around to gesture at the youth behind him, who leans on his staff to the right. A second youth stands before the man to right; his face is badly damaged. Between them a pouch or purse tied with red string hangs in field. Between the man and the other youth hangs a cross-shaped object, probably the top of a torch.

Under the handles are palmettes and coiling tendrils. There is a black circle under the foot.

Tondo: a youth sits on a klismos to right. His body between knees and shoulder is missing. There is a reserved exergue. In the field at right hangs a tortoise shell lyre with a hanging red cord. A meander frame also appears.

School scenes may be intended.
artifact.shape_description: Kylix Type B.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.88
artifact.summary: Two men and a woman.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Hirsch.
artifact.decoration_description: An old man with white hair and a beard stands to left in conversation with a figure whose left hand holds a staff. The old man gestures with his right hand. At right, facing away, upper body of a woman is visible, wearing a peplos, a necklace, earrings, and a broad band in her hair.
artifact.shape_description: Probably Type B.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.87
artifact.summary: Side A: komasts. Side B: same. Tondo: youth.
artifact.other_bibliography: Noble 1965, pp. 21, 69, figs. 130, 229.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Misfired, circular band, especially on Side B.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: three komasts. At left, nude youth wearing a red fillet has a himation over left shoulder. He dances to right while playing auloi, his cheeks puffed. His penis is infibulated. His staff leans in background. In center, nude komast with a himation over both arms dances to right. His staff is in his right hand and a kylix in his left. All three have red wreaths. At right a bearded man cloaked in a himation walks right looking back to left, a staff in his right hand.

Side B: three komasts. At left, a nude man dances to right with body turned frontal, head to left. He wears a red wreath, has a cloak over his shoulder, and a staff in his hand. At center, a nude bearded man, with a cloak over his shoulders, plays a barbiton, his head thrown back in song. At right, a youth in himation wearing a red wreath walks right, and bends over, a staff in his right hand.

Below the handles is a single palmette flanked by tendrils. An ivy leaf appears on either side of each handle.

Tondo: a youth in a himation and red fillet stands to right holding a knotty red staff in both arms. His incipient beard is shown in dilute glaze. Behind at left is a stepped structure with stripes in dilute glaze (rock?). Hanging behind from a peg is an aryballos with trailing cords. The frame is made of groups of three meanders to right alternating with cross squares.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: &epig-rough;*O *P*A*I*S ("the boy"). Side B: same.
artifact.shape_description: Type C with offset rim.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.86
artifact.summary: Side A: men with woman holding shield. Side B: two men and a woman. Tondo: departing warrior.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: a man is seated at left on a klismos holding a staff or sceptre upright in both hands. He wears a red radiate fillet. Before him at right, a woman stands wearing a peplos and a sphendone with upright elements. She holds a shield with a star device and gestures toward the man. To her right, looking left, stands a youth in a himation and a red radiate fillet holding a tall staff. At right is a man in a himation with a fillet.

Side B: a departing warrior stands at center facing a youth in a himation; the youth is holding a staff. The nude warrior carries a large fore-shortened shield and a spear. His face is largely destroyed. A woman at left pours a libation. She wears a peplos and holds a phiale in her left hand and an oinochoe in her lowered right hand. To right of the warrior facing left, a woman in a chiton, himation, and a radiate stephane gestures toward the warrior. There are palmettes under the handles.

Tondo: departing warrior. A nude young warrior faces left, his torso frontal. He holds a long spear and a shield with a star device, a sword hangs at his left hip, and he wears an Attic helmet with a low crest and upturned cheek flaps. Facing him, a long-haired woman in a chiton, himation and sphendone with three upright elements gestures to him. Meanders and cross-squares surround the tondo.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.85
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and Nemean lion. Side B: Herakles and Cretan bull. Tondo: archer
artifact.other_bibliography: Boardman 1975, p. XX, fig. 104 (A).
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Exterior by Euergides Painter, interior by a lesser artist.

Side A: Herakles kneels to right over the top of the crouching lion, which raises its left hind leg. Herakles wears a red wreath. The lion's mouth is open and snarling. In the background is a tree with red leaves from which hang a cloak and a sword. At right, another cloak hangs. At left, two nude youths run up, both with red fillets, gesturing emphatically. At right, a third nude youth runs up with a cloak over his extended left arm, and a club in his lowered right hand. Behind him is a palm tree. He wears a red wreath, and is possibly identified as Iolaos.

Side B: Herakles and the Cretan bull. Herakles stands with his back to the viewer and ties up the bull with a rope. Behind is a tree with red leaves from which hangs a cloak. Two youths run up on either side, and two youths run away at either edge. Herakles and all youths wear fillets. The youth at far right has a cloak. Second youth from left wears a wreath. There is a large ivy leaf below each handle.

Tondo: nude archer to right firing an arrow to right, drawing back his bow. Added red is used for the string, arrow, and wreath.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: nonsense inscription *N*O*L*B*O (??). Side B: nonsense inscription illegible. Interior: nonsense inscription *M*O*L*L*I*T (?) *L
artifact.shape_description: Type B. Large.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.84
artifact.summary: Side A: man. Side B: running youth with lyre.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Hirsch.
artifact.condit: Surface gouging and erosion.
artifact.decoration_description: Side A: a man leans to the right on a staff, wearing a himation. He holds a cup or rhyton in his right hand. Side B: a boy in a himation running to right, looks back to left. He holds a lyre in his left hand. On shoulder are simple black tongues. There is a band below the shoulder, and below the scene, a dotted ovulo pattern. Vertical groups of meanders alternate with cross-squares at the sides.
artifact.shape_description: Offset shoulder.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.81
artifact.summary: Woman with oinochoe and phiale.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Heavily pitted surface.
artifact.decoration_description:
Woman stands with her head turned to the left, and wears a chiton embroidered with tiny stars, a himation, and earrings. Her hair is tied in a krobylos with a red fillet. In her extended right hand she holds an oinochoe from which she pours a wine libation. In her left hand she holds a phiale. On the ground beside her is a kalathos full of red yarn. On the shoulder, a mirror, a pair of krotala, and a sakkos are visible.

An ovulo appears around the lower neck. The base line consists of meanders to the right.
artifact.inscriptions: *K*A*L*E on phiale.
artifact.shape_description: Big lekythos.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.80
artifact.summary: Woman and youth at tomb.
artifact.other_bibliography: Noble 1965, p. 52, figs. 198, 199
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: A tomb is shown with a square top and a three-stepped base, tied with three red fillets and three in faded colors. A woman stands at left in a chiton and himation, wearing a sakkos. She holds a phiale in her extended right hand. At right is a youth in a himation. There are meanders above the scene, and a palmette and tendril and ovulo pattern on neck.
artifact.shape_description: Lekythos has a false body (only small reservoir for fluid).

artifact.name: Tampa 86.79
artifact.summary: Youth and woman at tomb.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Searles.
artifact.decoration_description:
A youth (shade of the dead?) approaches from left with a tortoise shell lyre, with a plektron hanging from the lyre. He leans on a staff and wears a himation. At center is a tomb with pyramidal top and a four-stepped base. The outline of a tumulus is visible behind the tomb. At right, a woman in chiton and himation faces the tomb and carries a lekythos with a white ground scene in her raised right hand and a possibly a fruit or cake (or fig?) in her outstretched left hand. She wears a stephane in her hair.

Above the scene are meanders, saltiered squares and checkerboards. On the shoulder are palmettes and tendrils. There is an ovulo on the neck.
artifact.shape_description: Lekythos has a false body (only small reservoir for fluid). There is a vent hole on shoulder between handle and neck.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.78
artifact.summary: Wedding scene: bride, groom and winged Nike.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Misfired, surface condition poor.
artifact.decoration_description: Side A: at left, the bride wears a chiton embroidered with crosses, draped over head. She wears a crown with six upright leaves. Under the chiton she holds the hand of the groom facing her. To far left, the head of a woman is preserved wearing a crown and carrying a torch. The groom wears a himation, a wreath of laurel or myrtle and a fillet. Between them, flying to the right and looking back to the bride is a small winged Eros who carries a wreath. At right, behind the groom, stands a winged Nike holding two torches in her right hand and wearing a chiton, himation, necklace, earrings, and a headband with ovulo pattern. The shoulder has tongues and a band of ovulos.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.77
artifact.summary: Head of woman.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Acquired from Pietro Anti, Grottaglie, Italy.
artifact.condit: Excellent.
artifact.decoration_description: Upper body of a woman, head to left. She wears a peplos pinned on the right shoulder only. She wears an earring. Her hair is held by a checkered wrap. On the interior is a reserved stripe below the rim.
artifact.inscriptions: *B*A*X*X*H
artifact.shape_description: Bell krater.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.76
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos with satyr and maenad. Side B: satyr and maenad
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Misfiring on Side B.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos at center with a cloak over his shoulder and radiate crowns on his head. He holds a thyrsos in his right hand and grasps a maenad holding a tympanum in his left hand. The maenad has a nude torso with a himation around lower body and shoulders. Both figures stride to the right. At left, a satyr holds a basket in his outstretched left hand. The satyr has a fillet tied to his left wrist. Bunches of grapes and vines are seen in the background. There is a stump at right. The tympanum and maenad skin are white.

Side B: altar above at far left. A satyr at left puts his left foot on a short stump. A maenad at right runs to the right with a basket of offerings and a tympanum with a star device. She wears a peplos and a kekryphalos. In front of her at right is a stele.

Meanders and one cross square occur on each side below the scene. There is a laurel band under the rim.
artifact.shape_description: Rim warped in drying and cracked. Repaired with wet clay before glazing and firing.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.75
artifact.summary: Side A: three maenads. Side B: two men and a woman.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: three maenads in procession to right. The first, at right, looks back and wears a chiton, himation, and red fillet. She holds a flaming torch in her left hand. The center maenad, in a peplos, plays the barbiton, with the plektron in her right hand. Her hair is in a krobylos secured by a stephane with leaves. The last maenad at left wears a chiton, himation and ivy wreath, and holds a kantharos and a thyrsos.

Side B: a woman stands to the left between a man and a youth. The males wear himations. Both men hold staffs. The woman wears a himation, chiton and a fillet.

Slanted and addorsed palmettes are seen at the mouth. The base lines are meanders to left.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.74
artifact.summary: Aphrodite, Eros, and woman.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Excellent.
artifact.decoration_description: Seated Aphrodite faces to right, wearing a chiton embroidered with palmettes and stars. To right, Eros in added white wears a fillet, his left foot propped up. At right, a woman runs to right, looking back wearing a peplos. Her hair is in a kekryphalos. There is a palmette under the handle; it has coiling tendrils extending to the sides. Tongues appear on the shoulder, and an ovulo below the scene.
artifact.shape_description: Rayet Class. Rare miniature shape with tapering carinated body, deep flat shoulder, trefoil mouth, and high-swung handle.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.73
artifact.summary: Youth with hoop and tray of food
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art. Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.graffiti: *A*G (gamma retrograde) on underside of base
artifact.decoration_description:
Boy in a red wreath runs to right, looks left, and rolls a hoop with a stick in his right hand. He carries on his left shoulder a tray of food including a mesomphalos loaf.

The base line is a labyrinthine meander.
artifact.shape_description: Type 1.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.72
artifact.summary: Youth with oinochoe and ladle
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.graffiti: *A*G(gamma retrograde) on underside of base
artifact.decoration_description:
Nude boy with a red wreath and hair in dilute glaze runs to right and carries a ladle in his left hand and a jug in his right.

There are tongues on the shoulder. The base line is a labyrinthine meander. The rotelles are painted red.
artifact.shape_description: Type 1.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.71
artifact.summary: Nike with torches.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Milnassian.
artifact.condit: Excellent surface.
artifact.decoration_description: Nike, walking to the right, carries a pair of torches. She wears a chiton with embroidered edges. Her hair is in a bun. The ground line is composed of groups of two meanders to left alternating with saltire squares.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.70
artifact.summary: Body: seated woman in porch with youth and two men<lb>Shoulder: fighting hoplites
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: a woman sits on a stool (diphros) at left and holds a mirror. She wears a chiton, a himation, and a sakkos. In front of her to right is a mantled youth wearing a red fillet. Behind hangs an alabastron on cords. These two figures are in a porch supported by an Aeolic column and topped with a Doric frieze (metopes and triglyphs) above mutules with pronounced guttae. Outside approach two males; the nearest is bearded and wears a himation and red wreath. He leans on a staff and holds a purse. Behind him is a draped youth, also facing left. Between the men hangs a sponge, strigil, and aryballos with red cord.

Shoulder: three fighting hoplites. At left, a hoplite runs right, carrying a spear and shield with three dotted circles as a device. At the center, a hoplite (attacked by others) lunges to the right and looks back to left with his sword and shield. At right, a hoplite runs to left with a spear and shield whose device is three circles with central dots. Attic helmets, cuirasses and short chitons are seen here.

There are black tongues at the shoulder. Below the body scene are meanders and cross squares. At the sides is a net pattern. Between the body and shoulder scenes are running esses.
artifact.inscriptions: On shield of hoplite at right on shoulder: *K*O*A*O*N*S
artifact.shape_description: High swung vertical handle, upturned side handles, and ogival foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.68
artifact.summary: Side A: athlete and trainer. Side B: youth.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Hirsch.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: a trainer in himation and white fillet stands to right holding a forked staff. Facing him is a youth with white fillet taking off his himation.

Side B: a youth in a himation leans to left on a staff.

There is an ovulo base line on Side A, a reserved line on Side B.
artifact.shape_description: small.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.67
artifact.summary: Side A: satyr and girl. Side B: satyr and maenad.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex colls. Earl Fitzwilliam, Hearst.
artifact.primary_citation: <bibl>ARV2, 581, discussed in connection with no. 2, p. 1659</bibl>
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A satyr at right, runs to left, chasing a girl/nymph in a chiton and himation who runs to left. The satyr's penis is infibulated.

Side B: A satyr is chasing a maenad with thyrsos, sakkos and holding castanets (krotala).

There is an ovulo above the scenes, as well as palmettes at the bottom of the handles.
artifact.painter: Class of Small Pelikai by Pan Painter

artifact.name: Tampa 86.66
artifact.summary: Side A: satyr, goat, and maenad<lb>Side B: same
artifact.sources_used: Tampa Museum of Art records, J.V. Noble files, and description by Dr. Michael Padgett, Curator of Ancient Art, Tampa Museum of Art.
artifact.other_bibliography: Noble 1965, p. 52, figs. 198, 199.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.graffiti: A ligature of *D and *E.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: satyr (mid-body restored) dances to right, gesturing at a goat facing him which rears up on its hind legs. The satyr wears a red wreath and looks at a maenad who advances toward him from the right, a flaming torch in each hand, the right hand outstretched, the left lowered. The maenad wears a chiton, himation, earrings, and a reserved fillet that ties her hair in a krobylos.

Side B: nearly identical; the satyr's left hand touches the goat. The maenad's left shoulder and the bottom of the left torch are restored.

The upper frame is made of lotus buds, the side frames of net pattern. A red stripe circles the lower body.
artifact.shape_description: Large pelike.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.65
artifact.summary: Side A: hoplitodromoi and trainer. Side B: man and youths.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Surface pocking form lime inclusion expansion and pitting on lower body.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: at the center, a bearded trainer stands between two nude youths identified as hoplitodromoi by the shield and helmet on the ground at right. The helmet is Attic and the shield device is encircled dots. The trainer holds a wand in his right hand, only the butt of which is left reserved, the rest accidentally glazed over behind the youth at left. The youth at left has clenched fists. The youth at right walks to the right with his right hand clenched.

Side B: at left, a youth in a himation is leaning on a staff to the right, gesturing at a mantled boy and offering him a purse. The boy at center gestures with his hand and pulls his mantle taut. At right, a bearded man in a himation leans on a staff and strokes his beard.

Above each scene are three linked black palmettes flanked by animals in black silhouette. On side A are a boar and a lion. On side B are a lion and a leopard. The side frames on both sides are dot bands. There is a pair of red stripes around the mid-body.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.64
artifact.summary: Side A: horse and rider. Side B: woman.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection
artifact.condit: Misfired on Side A. Abrasion on handles and hard encrustation inside.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: a horse and young rider in chlamys and petasos gallop to the right. The rider's spear is leveled. The horse bit is spotted.

Side B: a woman in a himation, chiton and sakkos to left holds a flaming torch in her right hand.

On Side A above scene, groups of two meanders alternate with saltiered squares. Below both scenes is a meander. Palmettes are seen below the handles.
artifact.shape_description: Ridged handles.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.63
artifact.summary: Side A: flying Nike. Side B: youth.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Marquis Aldisio di Torreforte.
artifact.graffiti: *B and four vertical slashes, the third is offset.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Nike, pouring a libation of wine, flies right over a flaming altar. In her right hand she holds an oinochoe, and in her left a phiale. She wears a belted chiton. Her hair is in a krobylos, secured by a sphendone. The altar is decorated with volutes and ovulo. The flames and wine are in added red.

Side B: youth in a himation standing to left with a phiale in his lowered right hand. He wears a red fillet. The base lines are meanders to the right.
artifact.inscriptions: Nonsense inscription in front of Nike's face. Lambda's.
artifact.shape_description: Nolan amphora with triple handles, tall neck, and disc foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.62
artifact.summary: Octopi and ships.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Encrustation on one octopus.
artifact.decoration_description: Interior: sailing around the rim on opposite sides are the prows of two warships in added white, lacking interior details but with clearly defined ram, vertical bowsprit, and oarlocks on the deck. Between are two red octopi. Around the omphalos are red tongues. Exterior: there is a broad black band below the lip.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.61
artifact.summary: Cocks.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Misfired in red.
artifact.decoration_description: Side A: cock in added red standing to right between two palmettes. Side B: same.
artifact.shape_description: Miniature. Added clay on foot to repair hole at base, before firing.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.55
artifact.summary: Dionysos, satyrs and donkey.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Minor erosion on one satyr.
artifact.decoration_description: At front center, Dionysos (but with pointed ears) rides an ithyphallic donkey to right. He wears a white chitoniskos and a red-striped cloak. Grape vines emanate from Dionysos. The reins on the donkey are rendered as grape vines. Before him at right, a satyr dances to right with upraised arms. At left, another satyr approaches the donkey from behind and lays his left hand on his rump, an amorous gesture. On either side of cup are white eyes with black outlines and pronounced tear ducts. Iris and pupils are rendered by three concentric circles, middle ring is red. Behind the eyes flanking the handle are two nude komasts wearing boots and each holding a kantharos. The one to the left of the handle is missing his head and left arm. The one to the right has lost a forearm. The one to the right has satyr ears but no tail. All beards are red.
artifact.shape_description: Body slightly convex; snail-shaped finial on handle; relief ridge on handle ending in spade-shaped design.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.54
artifact.summary: Herakles and lion; men and woman.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Some surface damage from encrustation.
artifact.decoration_description: Herakles attacks a lion to right, holding the lion in his left hand and with his club in his right hand swung back. He wears a short belted chiton, and a sword hangs at his left side. He is beardless and has red hair. The lion rears on one leg; his right paw touches Herakles' left arm. The lion looks away from Herakles, his mouth open. Two figures flank the main scene on either side. At right, a nude youth (Iolaos?) walks to right and looks back to the lion. The youth has a sword and holds a club. He wears a red fillet. Beyond the youth to right, stands a man facing right, wearing a himation and holding a staff, probably a trainer. Behind Herakles at left a woman stands to right wearing a peplos and red fillet. The upper part of her peplos is red. To the left of the woman, a nude youth runs to right and looks back to left, and carries a javelin. Red stripes appear above and below scene.
artifact.shape_description: Handleless cup.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.53
artifact.summary: Horses' heads.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Moderate abrasion on surface.
artifact.decoration_description: Six horse heads to left in a band around the body. Three have red manes, one has a red face, one has a red chest, and one a red face and chest. All have reins. Above and below are bands of ivy leaves, alternating red and black. The top of the rim has black zigzags. A red stripe runs around the outer rim. Two thin red circles appear under the base.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.52
artifact.summary: Side A: procession to sacrifice. Side B: same.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble. Ex coll. Dr. Alfred E. Mirsky.
artifact.condit: Surface eroded in many areas.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: a man leading a bull to right to sacrifice, preceded by a pair of nude men carrying an amphora, slung from a pole. The men wear wreaths and across their chests are garlands of ivy. Grape vines grow in the background.

Side B: a youth carrying a basin of offerings on his left shoulder. In his left hand he holds a pair of grape vines. He wears a grape wreath on his head. In the center, a nude male drags a pig to the right by its hind leg. At right, a man walking right carries a bale on his back which he holds in his left hand. He holds a pair a grape vines in his right hand.

Under each handle, a white heron is seen to right. Many details are in added white, largely effaced: the beards of the first two men on Side A and the rightmost man on Side B, all wreaths and fillets, the ribbons on the bull, the mouth and body band on the amphora, and the herons. There is an ivy vine around the rim, with black and red tongues around the lower body. In the interior is a reserved circle with a smaller black circle at the bottom.
artifact.shape_description: Heron class.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.51
artifact.summary: Eye cup. Tondo: gorgoneion.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Said to be found in Vulci in 1955.
artifact.decoration_description:
Eye cup. Sides A and B: white eyes with pronounced tear ducts; the iris and pupil are indicated by concentric incised circles filled with black and red. Curved lines represent eyebrows. There is a stylized nose from which tendrils coil out to lotus buds doubling as satyr ears. Palmettes of red and black leaves decorate either side of the handle. Black tongues run around the pedestal.

Tondo: gorgoneion with red tongue and pupils.
artifact.shape_description: Chalcidizing, tall spreading ring foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.50
artifact.summary: Side A: siren and sphinx. Side B: same.
artifact.other_bibliography: Ohnefalsch-Richter, 11, pl. 109.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Found at Marion, Cyprus. Ex colls. Ohnefalsch-Richter, Branteghem.
artifact.condit: Some flaking of white on Side B.
artifact.decoration_description:
Lip cup. Side A: a siren stands at left with upraised wings, and faces a sphinx with its right paw in the air. Both have white female faces and white breasts. There are touches of added white and red on the wings. Both wear red fillets. Side B: same.

In the handle zone are palmettes linked by tendrils to the handle bases.

Tondo: reserved circle with black circle.
artifact.inscriptions: *X*A*I*R*E *K*A*I *P*I*E*I*E*N on both sides in handle zone.
artifact.shape_description: Lip cup.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.49
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos and satyr. Side B: satyr. Tondo: armed dancer and Hippalektryon
artifact.other_bibliography: B. Cohen 1978, pl. 53.3-5 (I,A,B)
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Hirsch.
artifact.decoration_description:
Bilingual eye cup. Tondo: a small Pyrrhic dancer on the back of a Hippalektryon to the right. Added white feathers are seen on the creature's tail. The feet are lost. The dancer wears greaves, a short chiton, and has a sword on his hip, a round shield on his left arm, and a spear in his right hand. He seems to be beating on his shield with the spear.

Side A: Dionysos reclining to left, served by a satyr at far left who holds out a jug in his left hand. The satyr has a dotted body and a red beard and forelock. Dionysos has a red beard. Dionysos wears a himation and an ivy wreath. In the background is a grape vine. Part of a large eye appears at right.

Side B: head of a satyr with a dotted body leaning to the right beneath a grape vine.
artifact.inscriptions: On interior, at left: *I*E (from *E*P*O*I*E,"he made"?) On interior, at right ...*O*S.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.47
artifact.summary: Youths fleeing from sphinx.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Minor surface pitting.
artifact.decoration_description: Three nude Theban youths with red hair run to the right, the leader looking back to the left. They are fleeing the sphinx who attacks from the left, her forepaws raised. She has a white face and breast, and red and white stripes on her wings. She wears a red fillet. Lotus buds appear on the shoulder.
artifact.shape_description: Small lekythos, broad swelling body.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.46
artifact.summary: Herakles and Greeks fight Amazons.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Purchased in Athens.
artifact.decoration_description:
Herakles, striding right, wearing his lion skin, attacks an Amazon. His quiver hangs from his back held by a white strap. His left hand (hidden) clutches the Amazon and his right holds his club. The Amazon has fallen to her left knee and turns her head to the right with a spear in her right hand. She bears a Theban shield (device: white snake) on her left arm. She wears a tunic and an Attic helmet with a stilted crest. On either side, armored Greeks slay two other Amazons. At left, a Greek warrior wears a stilted helmet with a cross-bandolier on chest. He plunges his sword into an Amazon who lies flat on the ground. The Amazon wears a short chiton and Scythian hat. At right, a Greek warrior in a Corinthian helmet wears a tunic, and his sword hangs in a white baldric. He holds a red-rimmed shield (device: white dots and circle) on his left arm. With his sword in his right hand he stabs an Amazon who falls to her left knee. She wears a short belted chiton and a Scythian cap. She holds an ax in her left hand. The object at her hip may be a quiver. All three Amazons wear greaves.

On the shoulder are lotus buds. Simple black tongues appear below the neck. A red stripe runs around the top of the mouth. Red and reserved bands are below scene. There is a net pattern above the scene.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.44
artifact.summary: Wedding of Peleus and Thetis.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Marquess of Sligo.
artifact.condit: Spalling on Apollo's lower body filled with plaster.
artifact.decoration_description:
Wedding chariot of Peleus and Thetis. A quadriga is seen to the right with the bridal couple in a box. Peleus holds the reins and a goad. He wears a tunic and himation, the latter with red stripes and white rosettes. He has a red beard and a red fillet. Thetis wears a peplos and a himation which goes behind her head; she holds the himation with her left hand. She has white skin and a red pupil. The near trace horse has a red chest band and red mane. The near pole horse is white with a red mane and tail. Behind the chariot at left stands Dionysos holding a drinking horn (keros) and a long staff. He wears a red fillet, a himation with red stripes and white rosettes, and has a red beard. Apollo stands behind the horses playing the kithara. He wears a tunic, himation with red stripes and white rosettes, and a red fillet. To the right of Apollo stands Hermes who walks to right and looks back to left. He wears a petasos and a chlamys with red stripes and red and white rosettes. His boots have long red tongues. At the head of the horses at right, standing to the left is a goddess, probably Aphrodite. She has white skin and wears a peplos, red fillet, necklace, and himation with red stripes and white rosettes. She holds a wreath in her lowered right hand. At the head of the procession, walking right but looking left, is a red-haired youth holding a long staff and wearing a himation with red stripes and white rosettes.

There is a red fillet below the neck and simple black tongues on the upper shoulder. Above are bands of lotus buds.
artifact.shape_description: Large and voluminous lekythos with broad cup-like mouth.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.43
artifact.summary: Octopus, dolphins between youths.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Pitting on back and on left youth.
artifact.decoration_description: On front is a large octopus, with four arms extended on either side and the head painted red. Below and on either side of the head are dolphins. Running toward octopus on either side is a nude red-haired youth with a red-spotted cloak over one arm and holding a spear. The youth at left carries a spear, while the spear of the right youth is largely effaced. Shoulder: a siren with red and black feathers stands between two males cloaked in himations.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.41
artifact.summary: Mounted warriors trample Scythian archer.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Excavated by Lucien Bonaparte in Vulci.
artifact.decoration_description:
A Scythian archer is ridden down by two mounted warriors. The archer falls backwards with only his feet on the ground. He wears a tall pointed cap with red flap, short belted tunic and carries a sword scabbard and quiver with a red lid. He has a red beard. The horses have red manes and white dotted bridles. The horseman at left holds two spears, and wears a Corinthian helmet with low crest, greaves, short tunic and Thracian cloak. The horseman at right wears the same but has a white crest and the designs on his cloak are faded. Nonsense inscriptions.

Ivy vines appear on either side of scene.

Above is a row of black tongues and a net pattern.
artifact.inscriptions: On base *S*O.
artifact.shape_description: Trefoil mouth, slight collar, globular body and echinus foot. Low handle.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.40
artifact.summary: Hoplites fighting.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.graffiti: *P on bottom of foot.
artifact.decoration_description:
Fighting hoplites. The standing warrior at left faces right and wears a cuirass, greaves, a short chiton with white rosettes, and a stilted helmet with a white crest. He carries a spear in his right hand; his chest strap is white as is the tip of the scabbbard. The warrior at right faces left and wears a short tunic with white dots at edge and white rosettes. The helmet crest, chest band, and scabbard tip are white. His shield device is a white vertical line with two horizontal crosses and there are red dots around the rim. The fallen warrior wears a helmet with white dots on the crest, greaves and a cuirass. His shield device is a white feline head (?) between white dots. His eyes are closed. White palmettes on the shield strap are visible on the fallen and left-hand warriors' shields.

A checkerboard pattern at the mouth, a band of five palmettes and a meander band below further decorate the vessel. At the sides of the scene are ivy leaf bands. There is a double red band below the scene.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.39
artifact.summary: Herakles and Amazons
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex colls. Durand, Magnoncourt.
artifact.graffiti: Ligature under foot. *G*A*M?
artifact.decoration_description:
Herakles fights three Amazons, one to left, two to right. The Amazon at left, running left and turning back to right, wears a stilted helmet, tunic and cuirass. Her shield has a red rim and white dots as a device. Herakles, facing right, wears a tunic and lion skin, and wields a sword (or club?). The kneeling Amazon to the right of Herakles wears a stilted helmet, tunic and cloak. Her shield has a red rim and white dots as a device. The Amazon at right moves to left and wears a stilted helmet, cloak and tunic, and carries a shield with a white tripod as a device.

At the mouth is a checkerboard pattern, with a row of dots below, a band of lotus buds, and a meander pattern above scene. A red band runs around the lower body at the base of the scene.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.38
artifact.summary: Athena mounting chariot, Herakles.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
From a scene of Herakles' departure for Mt. Olympos. Athena mounts a chariot facing right; part of the tail of one horse remains. Athena's right foot, right upper arm and all of her head except her chin, lips, and nose are missing. She wears a peplos with a checkered pattern filled with red dots and crosses. The scale pattern and panel of dots on her aegis are framed by snakes. Circles at the shoulders are filled with dotted crosses. She holds the reins in her left hand and a spear in her right. Herakles walks toward her from right with his bow in his right hand and his club in his left. At his hips hang a sword and a quiver. He has a red beard. There are touches of red on the quiver and chariot.

Ivy leaves appear at the side.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.37
artifact.summary: Departure of warrior with chariot.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Acquired from Paul Manship. Ex coll. Woodyat.
artifact.condit: Some erosion of figures and added white.
artifact.decoration_description:
Departure of a warrior. A charioteer in a long white chiton holds reins taut as he stands in the box of a quadriga facing right. His Theban shield, decorated with dotted circles in white, hangs on his back. Behind the horses stands a hoplite, his body pointing right, his head turned to the left. He wears a Corinthian helmet with a stilted crest over which is a red fillet. His shield decorated with white dots is on his left arm. A white sword baldric passes over his shoulder. At right, a nude boy stands facing left. The near trace horse has a red mane and red chest band. The near horses nod their heads, the far horses raise their heads. The near pole horse has a red tail. A pair of fillets hangs in the background.

Shoulder: a pair of lions attack a deer at center. On either side galloping away are young horsemen in Thracian cloaks.

Below the neck are black and red tongues. Framing the main scene are ivy vines. Double red stripes circle the body below the panel and above the zone of rays on the lower body.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.36
artifact.summary: Theseus and the Minotaur.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Minor repainting of figures. Surface is flaky.
artifact.graffiti: *X*O on underside of base.
artifact.decoration_description:
Black figure on white ground on the body panel. Theseus advances to right plunging his sword into the Minotaur which falls to right while looking back at Theseus. With his right hand, the Minotaur holds up a red rock which Theseus parries with his left hand. The Minotaur holds another red rock in his lowered left hand. The monster's body is covered with red circles and he has a red snarling mouth. The horned head has an almost lionine appearance. The nude Theseus wears a red fillet and a red sword baldric. The tip of the scabbard is also red. Flanking the action is a pair of women, possibly Pasiphae and Ariadne. The woman at left gestures with both hands and has a pointed nose and chin; she wears a peplos and himation, both with red dots, and a red fillet. The woman at right, whose hand and face are missing, is mantled in a red-striped himation, and wears a red fillet. In the background at left and right are sinuous grape vines.

In panel on shoulder (red ground) are linked black palmettes framed above by a band of net pattern and below by a key pattern. Bands of dicing on a white ground frame the scene on sides. The ground line is a double red stripe encircling the vase. Red stripes also surround the exterior and interior of the mouth, and the foot.
artifact.shape_description: Small kalpis with somewhat angular shoulder.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.35
artifact.summary: A chariot race
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Ex coll. Marquand.
artifact.graffiti: *H*R ligature.
artifact.decoration_description:
On shoulder: chariot race proceeding to right. Both teams of horses have their forelegs in the air and the rear team has all legs in the air. Below the leading team a dog runs to right. The horses have red manes and tails. The nearer trace horses have manes and chest bands. Both charioteers have red forelocks and wear long white chitons. Both charioteers hold a goad and reins. The losing charioteer has a red sash. In the background are grape vines.

Above, a band of lotus buds is seen, and at the sides, a band of net pattern. Below is a key pattern to left. A red stripe runs around the neck.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.34
artifact.summary: Side A: two racing chariots<lb>Side B: two men and two women. Shoulders: symposium scenes
artifact.other_bibliography: Philippaki 1967, pp. 18, 21, pls. 9:4, 13:1.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.graffiti: Large *K on base.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: two racing four-horse chariots or quadrigas. At left, charioteers in a chariot are looking at each other, with the lead charioteer looking back. Both hold reins and a goad. They wear long white chitons and have red hair. The charioteer at left has his body bisected by the handle. The horses are at full gallop, with their forelegs raised in the air. Below the lead horses runs a dog, also with forepaws in the air. The lead chariot is met at right by two eagles. Another eagle flies above the lead team, and a fourth is at the left. Eagles are seen also above and under the handle. The trace horses have red dots on their chest straps. Five of the eight horses have red manes. One of the pole horses in lead team is white. Shoulder: symposium scene with reclining man and woman. The man has a red beard and wears a red-spotted himation. There are white stripes on his mattress. The woman, with white skin, wears a sakkos, tunic, and himation with red dots and white rosettes. Two cloths hang in the field above.

Side B: Two groups, each composed of a standing man holding a staff and a seated woman. The men have red beards and ivy wreaths. They gesture towards the women with their left hands. The women have white skin and wear red fillets. All four wear himations decorated with red spots and white rosettes. The women also wear peploi and sit on stools. The women look down and hold up their cloaks in their right hands. The man at right leans over farther and reaches out farther than the one at left. Grape vines branch out from the hands and bodies of the women. Shoulder: symposium scene with woman reclining between two reclining men. The men wear wreaths and himations with red spots and white rosettes. The man at right looks right and gestures with his right hand. The woman has white skin and a red fillet. She wears a tunic and a cloak like the men. In the field above hang three fillets and a wreath.

There is a red fillet below the neck and simple black tongues around the upper shoulder. Over each handle are five linked palmettes. There are dot bands below the scene above a tall zone of rays.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.33
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena Promachos<lb>Side B: youth seated on rock
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Purchased in Athens.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Athena Promachos to left.

Side B: seated youth to right on rock.

Framed white tongues appear on the shoulder.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.32
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena Promachos<lb>Side B: running hoplite
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection. Purchased in Athens.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Athena Promachos with round shield to left, very schematic and without detail.

Side B: running hoplitodromos.

White and black tongues run around shoulder. Black stripes extend down the sides.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.30
artifact.summary: Side A: boxers. Side B: same.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Black figure on white ground. Side A: pair of boxers with wrapped fists are wearing red wreaths and sparring. To the left a trainer or judge leaning on a staff wears a red-striped himation and a red wreath. Side B: same.

Under each handle is a large alert dog with red collar.

A neck lotus and palmette chains with no incision also appear. Simple black tongues are seen on the shoulder. There are rays on the lower body.
artifact.shape_description: Light- Make Class. Dent on Side B.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.29
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and Antaios. Side B: youth and horse.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.graffiti: Griffito under base, line with two perpendicular lines, one on each side.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles wrestles Antaios. Herakles bends over fallen Antaios, clutching his left arm in his right hand and his head with his left hand. Antaios looks to left and has a shaggy red beard. Herakles wears a red fillet. Hanging above are Herakles' club, bow and what may be arrows. Doric colonnades in background on either side. Nonsense inscription above hanging weapons.

Side B: Groom currying a horse. Horse stands to right; the groom stands behind facing left with his hand on horse's flank. His cheeks are puffed out as if to blow hair off brush. Red used for fillet, mane and tail. Horse is tethered by red rope attached to neck of vase. A Doric colonnade to left.

Palmettes on neck. Black tongues on shoulder. Lotus and palmette quatrefoil under each handle. Band of double dots above zone of rays. Circular incisions inside neck.

Dot-band Class, formerly Group of Brussels R312.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: *O*O*I*N*O*S*I
artifact.shape_description: Dot Band Class.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.28a, b
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos<lb>Side B: same
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Surface pitting on Side B. Partial restoration of eye on Side A.
artifact.graffiti: On bottom of foot.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos reclining on his left elbow, looking right, on a kline with its legs below the ground line. His himation has fallen to his waist and covers his legs. He wears a wreath. Eyes appear to either side with two concentric white circles at the centers. Behind are grapevines.

Side B: Dionysos, wearing himation, sits to right on a folding stool. He holds a keros, or drinking horn, in his left hand. His right arm is hidden. Behind are grapevines. There are eyes, as on Side A.

Below the neck on the shoulder are black tongues. On the neck are three linked black palmettes on each side. A zone of rays is seen on the lower body.

Lid: a black knob with reserved bands; at the edge is an ivy vine with red stem and black leaves.

On the class of neck amphorae with pictures on the shoulder, see ABV, 276.
artifact.shape_description: Amphora with lid. Triple handles, rolled fillet between neck and body. Lid: pomegranate knob.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.27
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos on donkey and satyr playing lyre. Side B: same.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection
artifact.graffiti: *L*A (?) on underside of base.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos rides to right on an ithyphallic donkey, the latter with red mane and white muzzle. Its head rears back while braying. Dionysos wears a white tunic and himation with red stripes and white rosettes, and a red ivy wreath. He carries a grape vine in his right hand and other vines issue from the donkey and his shoulder. Dionysos has a red beard. The donkey has a red wreath around his chest. In front at right is a satyr with a white dotted tortoise shell lyre in his left hand and a grape vine in his right. His mouth is open in song. He has a red tail, beard and forelocks, and a white wreath around one shoulder. A red fillet hangs from his lyre.

Side B: a nearly identical Dionysos and donkey, but the god's tunic is not white, and in his right hand he holds a drinking horn (keros). Facing them at right are a dancing satyr playing a lyre and singing. The satyr has a red tail, beard and forelock.

Lotus buds are on the neck. Black and red tongues are on the shoulder. Double red stripes are below panel and above the zone of rays on the lower body. Red stripes run around the foot and mouth.
artifact.shape_description: Rare melon-shaped amphora with concave handles and echinus foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.26
artifact.summary: Side A: quadriga and charioteer. Side B: warrior donning greaves, men and youths
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: frontal quadriga, the horses' bodies foreshortened. All the horses have red manes and tails and red breast bands with white rosettes. The pole horses look toward one another, their faces overlapping. The trace horses look away to left and right. A red square is on the front of the chariot box. The charioteer with red hair and beard wears a long white chiton. He holds the reins and looks to the right.

Side B: nude warrior dons greaves flanked by a man and a youth on each side. The warrior has red hair and a red beard. On the ground below him rests a Corinthian helmet with a stilted white crest. Behind the warrior at left, a man gestures with his raised left hand. The man wears a himation with red stripes and white rosettes. Behind the man at far left stands a nude youth with red hair. His clenched fists are drawn up at his waist. In front of the warrior to the right stands a man with red hair and a red beard, wearing a himation with red stripes and white rosettes. At far right, walking right, is a nude youth holding a red staff in his left hand.

Above the scene on Side A is a lotus and palmette festoon. Above the scene on Side B is a band of lotus buds. There are two red stripes on the neck, on the edge of the mouth, below the scenes, and above the zone of rays on the lower body. There are single stripes around the mouth and lip, on the neck and on the foot.
artifact.inscriptions: Traces of a red dipinto now illegible on bottom of foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.25
artifact.summary: Side A: departing warrior. Side B: Athena and combatant (giant?)
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A departing warrior walks to left at the center. The warrior wears a cuirass, a red fillet over his helmet, and one red and one white greave, and he holds a spear in his right hand. His shield device is a white dog with a red eye. There is an old man with a white beard at left, facing right. He wears a red tunic and a red-striped cloak and carries a red cane. A man at right is facing left. He wears a red-striped himation.

Side B: giant (or Ajax?) in the center walking left has a shield with a white dog as device. He wears a bell cuirass, a short chiton, one red and one white greave, a helmet with a red fillet and white stripe on the crest. In his right hand he holds a spear. On his shield is a device of a white line. Athena wears an Attic helmet and in her raised hand there is a spear in dilute paint. Added red is used on her peplos and aegis. Her shield device is a chariot box. The scene may be interpreted possibly as Ajax and a statue of Athena.

A lotus and palmette band rings the neck. There are black and red tongues on shoulder. Palmettes and tendrils are seen under the handles. The lower body is decorated with zones of lotus buds, a meander, and rays near the foot.
artifact.shape_description: Triple handles.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.24
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena. Side B: two riders.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.condit: Some misfiring, particularly on Side B; partial erosion of shield device on Side A.
artifact.graffiti: Ligature on base.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Athena Promachos striding to left with shield and upraised spear. The shield device is a white tripod. She wears a peplos with red panels, scale pattern on lower skirt, and a panel of white rosettes. Her stippled aegis is framed with snakes. Her long hair falls in a pointed tress. Her helmet has a stilted crest. There are red curls on her brow.

Side B: horse race. Two young horsemen are galloping to the right. The forelegs of the horses are in the air. The winner holds his goad up high. The loser holds his low. Both horses have red manes. Both riders wear red tunics.

On neck is a lotus and palmette quatrefoil. A red fillet appears between the neck and the body. Above each scene is a band of red and black tongues. Double red stripes circle the lower body above the zone of rays on the lower body. There are red stripes also on the foot, lip, and the inside of the mouth.
artifact.shape_description: Pseudo-Panathenaic.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.23
artifact.summary: Side A: two couples and animals. Side B: Amazon, warrior, and animals.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: two couples consisting of a man and a woman between sphinxes at either end. The two women have long black hair, wear black chitons with red mantles, and hold a black wreath in their right hands. The women have white skin. Both men have red hair with a fillet, and wear black mantles over short white chitons. The chiton of the man in the left pair has incised folds, and a himation with incised stars. Below, two cocks between two sirens.

Side B: at center, an Amazon runs to right looking back to left. She carries a spear and a red shield with white dots at edge. Her red helmet has a black crest, and she wears a short black chiton decorated with stars. On the lower part of the chiton are three rows of white sirens or birds. To either side of her, a sphinx and a cock. Below, a warrior runs to left looking back to right with red shield and helmet with red crest. To the right is a ram and to the left, a panther.

On the neck are lotus and palmette festoons. On the shoulders are red and black tongues, on the central zone of the body, lotus and palmette festoons. At the base are rays.

The style of the scene is "Tyrrhenian".

artifact.name: Tampa 86.221
artifact.summary: Side A: herm between maenad and satyr. Side B: three youths.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: herm between a maenad and a satyr. Maenad wears a chiton, a himation, and a sakkos, and holds a thyrsos. The satyr advances from right offering a bunch of grapes and cradling a thyrsos in his arm. He wears a fillet and has black hair and beard. He is ithyphallic. A caduceus is on the side of the herm.

Side B: three youths in himatia. The youths at left and right hold staffs in their right hands.

The base line is composed of groups of meanders alternating with cross squares. There is a laurel wreath under the rim.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.15
artifact.summary: Wine-making scene with satyrs, maenad, and Dionysos.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Wine-making scene. A satyr at left stands on a table crushing grapes in a basket, one handle of which he holds. Juice flows out to right into a kylix. Below the table grows a lotus bud. A maenad with white skin dances to right in red-striped peplos. She holds a drinking horn (keros) in her right hand and balances a kantharos on her left. She wears a red fillet. On her head to left is a tiny ithyphallic satyr, defecating and playing the aulos. He has a red tail and, like the first satyr, red hair and beard. At right, Dionysos stands below a vine in a red-striped himation with red hair. He holds a drinking horn (keros). This bearded man is presumably Dionysos, but is shorter than the maenad. There is pseudo-inscription in the field behind the maenad.

Red and black tongues are seen on the shoulder.
artifact.inscriptions: Nonsense inscription.
artifact.shape_description: Deianeira type lekythos with pronounced collar and echinus foot.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.130
artifact.summary: Satyr.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: A satyr seated on a pointed amphora wears a white fillet. A filleted thyrsos is seen. The tondo border is made of meanders and saltiered squares. There are concentric circles on the bottom. The style is"Faliscan". The vessel belongs to the Cauliflower Class.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.13
artifact.summary: Side A: sphinx<lb>Side B: youth on horse
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: sphinx seated to right looking left. There is a broad red stripe on its wing, a double red fillet in its hair, and a coiling tendril emerging from top of its head. The face and breasts in added white are flaked off. A rosette appears in the field.

Side B: youth mounted on horse walking to right. The youth holds the reins in both hands and a stick in one hand. He has red hair and a red circle around his nipple. The horse has a red mane and tail. A tendril is seen below the horse and a rosette above.

There are lotus buds on the neck and rays at the base. Two red stripes run around the lower body, and one inside the mouth.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.129
artifact.summary: Satyr.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: A standing satyr appears with a basket. A hanging fillet and phiale are in the field. The satyr wears shoes; he has his left foot on a dotted rock. The tondo border is made of meanders and saltiered squares. There are concentric circles on the bottom. The style is"Faliscan". The vessel belongs to the Cauliflower Class.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.128
artifact.summary: Water fowl.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: Side A: lotus palmette quatrefoil between water fowl. Side B: same. "Pontic" style.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.12
artifact.summary: Lion, swan, eagle.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: lion to right. The lion's left forepaw is raised and his mouth is open. Below the lion's legs stands a swan. Flying to the left above is an eagle. In the field is a dotted circle and palmette.

There are palmettes by the handle bases. Black and red stripes, a band of rays, and a band of dots around the foot-body juncture complete the vessel's decoration.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.104
artifact.summary: Pegasos and Bellerophon
artifact.other_bibliography: Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 2.505, no. 89, pl. 131, 4. Oxford, 1983.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: Pegasos flies to right, above a built structure representing Peirene Spring. The figure at left is of Bellerophon holding a tether. The added white of the wings is eroded.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.102
artifact.summary:
Side A: Oscan warriors, woman, and boy
Side B: Dionysos, maenad, and satyr
artifact.other_bibliography: RVAp
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: departing or returning warriors in Oscan garb. At right, a mounted warrior rides to left holding a small round shield and a pair of spears in his left hand. He wears a short tunic with a wave pattern around the neck and other embroidered patterns. He also wears a Phrygian helmet with white crest with two tall feathers and boots. A star device decorates his shield. There are white dots on the horse's bridle and chest strap. Advancing toward him at center is a woman in a diaphanous belted chiton, earrings, a radiate stephane, bracelets, and shoes. In her left arm is a large nestoris (trozzella) with yellow handles, possibly meant to be metal because of its chased decor. With her right hand, she offers a wreath to the rider. Between the figures is a tree with leaves and fruit in white and red. At left stands a warrior in a patterned short tunic with cloak over both shoulders, boots, a tall pointed hat of Oscan type, and pair of spears. With his right hand he reaches for the hand of the boy, who seems to point at his hand but doesn't hold anything. All males wear wide belts. The boy wears boots, stephane, and holds a yellow jug. Above the boy, flying toward the standing warrior is a small winged Nike in a belted chiton, boots, necklace, and bracelets. She carries a fillet. There is a wreath at upper left, and in upper right a rosette.

Side B: Dionysos, maenad, and satyr. At center, Dionysos, nude except for shoes, fillet, and cloak, looks to left. In his right hand is a phiale, a thyrsos in his left. Running toward him from left is a maenad in a belted chiton with a cloak over her arms, wearing shoes, kekryphalos, and bracelets. She carries a thyrsos and proffers a wreath. Between, a stylized plant is growing. At right is a young satyr with white fillet and shoes, with a flaming torch in his left hand and a situla in his right. In the field are two rosettes. A laurel plant is at right.

Meanders and dotted cross squares are used as a ground line. On teh neckis a broad reserved band with an ivy wreath and dotted berries. On one side of the rim is a laurel wreath, on the other a wave pattern. Palmettes appear on the sides of the handle plates. Each scene is framed above by tongues and at the side by degenerate ivy.

artifact.name: Tampa 86.100.1.2
artifact.summary: Youth on a stool.
artifact.collection_history: Tampa Museum of Art, Joseph Veach Noble Collection.
artifact.decoration_description: Tondo: youth seated to right on a stool. He wears a red fillet, and a himation hangs from his leg. He rests his hand on his knotty staff. In the field at right hangs a sponge, strigil, and aryballos.
artifact.inscriptions: *E[*L*P*I*N*I*K*O*S *K*A]*L*O*S

artifact.name: Tampa 85.12
artifact.summary: Swans.
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Keith and Linda Rounsaville.
artifact.decoration_description: Frieze of three standing swans alternating with large rosettes. A large rosette on bottom and top, dots around side of mouth. "Italo-corinthian" style.

artifact.name: Tampa 84.14
artifact.summary: Lions, waterbird, siren.
artifact.decoration_description: Side A: lion and waterbird facing to left. Side B: lion and siren facing to left. On either handle a row of seven palmettes. Details in red and white.

artifact.name: Tampa 82.14.1
artifact.summary: Woman and youth
artifact.decoration_description: A woman appears in a chiton with a fillet in her right hand, a ball of wool in her left. She wears a necklace. To the left is a low pillar. A nude youth (athlete?) stands with a staff holding a strigil and aryballos in his left hand. Below the handle are stacked palmettes flanked by coiling tendrils. There is a wave pattern around the base of the neck. There is red wash under the base.

artifact.name: Tampa 82.11.1
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles battling Amazons<lb>Side B: fighting warriors
artifact.graffiti: Two signs under foot. A rough diamond divided into quadrants and a line with cross strokes at ends.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles battles two Amazons. Herakles attacks to the right, his club in his upraised right arm, his left leg raised, his left arm clutching the right arm of a fallen Amazon. He wears a lion skin knotted at the throat with red-dotted fur. A sword hangs from a white baldric on his hip. On his back hangs an open quiver with red stripes. There are red dots on his tunic and beard. The Amazon has fallen to one knee, supported by the Theban shield on her left arm. She wears a short chiton and an Attic helmet with low crest. She carries a spear in her right hand and wears a sword on her right hip. Her tunic has red dots and white rosettes. A wrapped element at her waist may represent the prized girdle. A second Amazon attacks from the right, her spear in her lowered right hand, a round shield on her left arm. The shield has white balls for a device and red dots on shield edge. She wears a short chiton, a cloak over both shoulders, and an Attic helmet with stilted crest. A red fillet circles the helmet; a sword hangs at her hip. Red dots and a white rosette appear on both cloak and chiton.

Side B: two warriors fight over a third. At left, a warrior wears greaves, a short tunic, and a low-crested Corinthian helmet. A sword hangs at his hip. He has a spear in his right hand and a Theban shield in his left. The porpax is affixed with white palmettes. He grasps the handle on the inside. The warrior at right wears greaves, a Corinthian helmet with stilted crest, and carries a spear in his right hand. He also has a sword and baldric. His shield device is a chariot box. There are red dots on the tunics of both warriors. All shields have red dots on the edges. The fallen warrior has greaves, a short chiton, bell cuirass, and a Corinthian helmet with low crest. He has a spear in his right hand, and a shield on his left with two white balls for a device. His face is obscured by warrior at right. His back is visible. Perhaps the scene shows Ajax and Hector fighting over the body of Antilochos.

There is a lotus and palmette chain on the neck (no incision). A red fillet appears below the neck, black and red tongues above each scene. Lotus and palmette quatrefoils are seen below the handles. On the lower body there is a zone of rays with a band of lotus buds above.
artifact.shape_description: Triple handles. Vase leans to one side slightly.

artifact.name: Tampa 81.5.1
artifact.summary: Side A: wedding of Peleus and Thetis. Side B: warriors departing.
artifact.collection_history: Purchased with funds from Friends of The Arts.
artifact.condit: Misfired red on Side B.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: standing behind wedding pair at left, a goddess in peplos, red-striped himation, and red fillet. To right, a quadriga proceeds right with Peleus and Thetis riding. Peleus holds the reins and a goad. Peleus wears a tunic and red-striped himation; Thetis wears a peplos, himation and red fillet. Behind the chariot Dionysos stands to the right wearing a red-striped himation and ivy wreath and holding a kantharos in his left hand. In front of him, Apollo stands to the right playing the kithara and wearing a tunic and red fillet. At the head of the horses, restraining them with his left hand hidden, stands a groom in a chiton and himation, his head hidden behind the horses. At far right facing left, a goddess (Artemis?) wearing a peplos and red fillet holds a torch aloft in each hand. Added white is eroded from the faces of all three women and the kithara. The horses have red manes and tails. Red details are seen on the chariot box.

Side B: at center a youth in a tunic holds a pair of spears and stands behind a horse facing right, which he restrains with his hidden right hand. At left behind the horse, standing to right are two youths, the one at far left wrapped in a himation with white rosettes and holding a spear, the other nude and gesturing toward the warriors with his left hand. At right facing the horse, a hoplite stands to the left in greaves, Corinthian helmet with stilted crest, and holding a spear and shield in his left hand. There is no device on the shield; its rim is red. Behind at right standing to left, a man is wrapped in a himation with white rosettes; he is wearing a red fillet.

Lotus buds appear on the top of the rim, and lotus and palmette quatrefoils are on the handle plates. Both scenes are framed above by red and black tongues, and at the sides by ivy vines. There is a band of rays on the lower body.

artifact.name: Tampa 1991.13
artifact.summary: Griffin.
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Dr. and Mrs. Jerome M. Eisenberg.
artifact.decoration_description: Griffin bird with outspread wings, knobs on head, tall pointed ears, and numerous details in added red and white. Blob rosettes as filling ornament. Rosettes on bottom, and top of mouth.

artifact.name: St. Louis WU 3284
artifact.summary: Lower portion: shape of negro woman's head.
artifact.essay_text:
Class G: London Class of Head VasesEarly Fifth Century B.C.Lent by the Washington University Gallery of Art; gift of Messers. Brookings and Parsons, donated after the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair (WU 3284).

The Vase: h. 17.5 cm; d. of mouth 12.5 cm. Mended and restored, small repairs. Portions of cup and right side of head restored. Surface worn and chipped in several places, particularly on the foot.

Decoration: This vase is formed of a wheel-made lip attached to a mold-formed lower portion in the shape of the head of a black female. She is depicted with her mouth partially open and her hair, wrapped in a sakkos, protrudes in a roll over her forehead. The whole vase is covered with a shiny black glaze of good quality, with the exception of the lips which are reserved. Incision was used to indicate the pupils of the eyes, the ears, and, by parallel undulating lines, the forehead hair. Added white: now mostly faded or partially missing, was used for the whites of the eyes, the outline of the sakkos behind the forehead hair and the teeth. The lip is encircled by a white wreath made of long leaves (perhaps a myrtle wreath shown tied in front). Added red: preserved only in traces on the tongue between the teeth, and probably applied in the nostrils as well. Although no traces survive, the lips may also have been red.

Attic plastic head-vases of the sixth and fifth centuries have been classified by Beazley on the basis of their molded portions. This example belongs to the London Class, named after a kantharos in London in the form of white women's heads. The class also includes oinochoai and mugs. Dionysos is a common subject, as well as both black and white women, sometimes arranged back to back (janiform).

The significance of the subjects chosen by the artist for a head-vase is still unclear despite numerous suggestions. The religious significance of the vessel type is now generally de-emphasized and the popularity of Dionysos and his female followers is seen as appropriate rather than cultic. There were relatively few head-vases and they were no doubt novelty and luxury items, probably of some snob value. The use of the head of a black for the body of many of these plastic vessels may be have no more significance than that of a topical reference, as souvenir-mugs in the form of human faces have today. There is no doubt, however, that, as Beazley pointed out, the nature of the Attic black glaze was particularly suited to the rendering of this subject.

Head-vases represent a marriage of the technique of the potter to that of the clay modeller, or coroplast. Although apparently never a truly successful union, it was tried out in this form throughout history in many different cultures.

Bibliography: FR, 243; Beardsley 1929, 28, no. 48; J. D. Beazley, "Charinos," JHS 49 (1929) 49, no. 11; Mylonas 1940, 202, fig. 18; ARV2, 1534, no. 19; K. Herbert & S. Symeonoglou, Ancient Collections in Washington University (St. Louis 1973) 24, fig. 31.

William Biers, University of Missouri-Columbia

artifact.name: St. Louis WU 3283
artifact.summary: Maenad walking to the right.
artifact.essay_text:
Probably by the Terpaulos Painterca. 500-490 B.C.Lent by the Washington University Gallery of Art; donated by Messrs. Robert Brookings and Charles Parsons, 1904 (WU 3283). Exhibited: World's Fair, St. Louis, 1904; Archaeological Institute of America Convention, St. Louis Art Museum, 1973.

The Vase: h. to rim 20.5 cm; h. to top of handle 24.4 cm; max. d. 11.6 cm at 11.0 cm from base; d. of base 8.1 cm; h. of base 0.7 cm. Broken into many pieces and mended. Some small missing pieces restored with plaster. Some relief lines restored, as on the underpart of the right chiton sleeve, and parts on the right hand. The glaze is good, but thin in places, and discolored, especially to right of figure; the wash over the reserved areas fired very red. The oinochoe is of shape 1, with trefoil lip, a ring molding articulating join of short neck with plump body, a narrow collar joining body to flat disk foot of two narrow degrees. Inside of mouth to neck is black; surface and upper edge of foot are black, sides and underneath reserved; the handle is all black. The vase is all curves: sections of various curvature compose handle, lip, neck and foot, which, with the larger curves of the body, are echoed in the floral decoration around the handle and sides of the vase.

Decoration: Just above the join of neck and body is a band of egg decoration, just below, tongues, which are broken by a reserved area on the body between handle-root and neck. Below the figure, extending only to the floral pattern is a key pattern, running left. The floral: below the handle a pendent palmette with ribbed, angled, central leaf springs from two volutes from which tendrils branch out to each side, each giving off and encircling a large palmette before terminating in another palmette which flanks the handle one. The circling tendrils each further branch to give off and encircle two more large palmettes on each side, ending in elaborate double-blossomed lotus-buds which flank the figure on the front. There are slight variations in the composition of the lotuses, but a black palmette is painted in the middle of each bud.

The single figure on the vase is a maenad. She walks right, looking back over her shoulder, in the crook of her right arm a thyrsos held at a slight angle. Over her chiton she wears a fawn-skin, the leg of which, from behind her left side, just about parallels the angle of her thyrsos. The vase is all curves, but straight lines dominate the figure; the fawn-skin in front hangs straight, the groups of chiton-pleats below her waist hang straight.

She moves calmly but holds up her left arm, the chiton wrapped around her hand in a gesture known from the so-called "wing-dance." Perhaps she is giving the signal to the thiasos, the crowd of Dionysos' followers, to start the dance. The branches and leaves of the thyrsos are painted in, in red; wound twice about her head is a painted band, tied in a bow at the back; on her right arm is a bracelet. The staff of the thyrsos is colored with thin glaze, as is the fawn skin and some of its spots, some parts of the hair, and the narrow pleats of the chiton. There is relief outline everywhere, except perhaps the tip of the chiton over the left hand. The thickness of the relief line varies wildly. Sketch lines are visible for some palmette leaves and for lines indicating legs under the skirt.

An inscription, *K*A*L*O*S, in red paint, runs from left of thyrsos over the head of the maenad. Under the left arm, just below a small restored patch, is another painted mark, probably a letter but without any obvious meaning or connection.

This vase, itself not without charm, demonstrates rather nicely the information which can be garnered from the often dull minutiae of scholarship. With detail such as floral patterns, rendering of drapery, vase-shape (as also, for instance, in the case of the Syleus Painter, Kansas City 30.13, or the Painter of Palermo 4, Madison 1976.143) the net is drawn tighter and tighter until a fairly clear idea of the working organization of Athenian craftsmen takes shape. The Terpaulos Painter is late-found, and not himself of particular interest. Although certain of his few vases were known and published earlier, he first seems to have been given his name, from the flute-playing satyr on an oinochoe in Rome (ARV2, 308, no. 1), in a short note by Beazley on his inscriptions (AJA 61 [1957] 6, no. X11).
