Nike stands on the right, her body facing front, her head in profile turned to the left. She faces Hera who stands on the left. With her hair drawn up in a sakkos or snood, Nike wears a long, Ionic style chiton with a dot pattern at the bottom and loose, transparent elbow sleeves which cover a generous breast. Over her left shoulder is draped a himation with a decorative stripe on the selvage at the gathered overfold; behind her left shoulder rise her wings. With her right hand extended towards Hera, she prepares to pour out a libation from a small oinochoe. In her left hand she holds a kerykeion. She wears earrings and, on each wrist, bangle bracelets. Her left foot points to the left, while her right is frontal. To the left Hera stands in profile, ready to receive the libation. She is dressed in a long, transparent Ionic style chiton with elbow sleeves and a dot pattern at the bottom; a himation is draped over her right arm and shoulder, leaving her left arm exposed. In her extended right hand she holds a phiale out to receive Nike's libation. Her left hand holds her striped scepter of authority, the finial of which is obscured by the oinochoe. On her head she wears earrings and a diadem which binds her hair; on her arms bangle bracelets. Both her breasts and her feet are in profile, facing Nike. Both himations end in teardrop terminations.

An egg-and-dot border marks the junction between neck and shoulder. On the shoulder is an elaborate palmette and bud pattern.

artifact.name: RISD 35.013
artifact.summary: Tondo: lion. Sides A and B: departure of a warrior.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design (1935.013)

Height: 5 1/16 in. (12.9 cm.); Diameter: 10 7/8 in. (27.6 cm.)

Broken and repaired; worn especially on side B. At one handle evidence of ancient repair; a small piece of bronze rivet remains.

Interior: lion. His head is turned back with mouth opened as if roaring. A border of framed tongues alternating red and black circles the tondo.

Exterior, side A: departure of a warrior. A youth dressed in chitoniskos and holding a javelin rides a horse moving to the right. In front, a gesticulating nude youth and a youth wrapped in a mantle; behind, a gesticulating nude youth and a youth wrapped in a mantle and holding a javelin. At the handles, two sphinxes. Behind the rider, a bird.

Side B: the same. However, the nude youth behind the rider carries a javelin, and neither of the draped figures is armed. Below the scene, a reserved line; at the handles, inverted lotus buds; at the base, rays.

Red: the lion's mane, fillets and parts of the wings of the sphinxes, parts of the drapery, hair of three youths.

White: parts of the drapery, chiton of central rider, sphinxes' flesh, horses' manes and tails (much worn).

Unattributed ca. 550 - 540 B. C.

Siana cups, so named because two well-known examples were found at Siana on Rhodes, are the dominant type of kylix in the second quarter of the sixth century. The shape is a continuation of the Komast cup (Yale 1913.102), but the foot and lip are longer. Unlike the Komast cup, the inside of the Siana cup is also decorated, beginning the long tradition of tondo pictures. The decoration on this cup is of the overlap type with the scene extending into the offset lip. J. Frel suggested a comparison with a Siana cup in Prague (Prague 18,52 K 1241; ABV, 682) by the Civico Painter which shows a similar scene.

Bibliography:Luce 1936, no. 3, p. 36, fig. 1.

artifact.name: RISD 34.858
artifact.summary: Side A: winged lion between two men. Side B: Man between dog and sphinx.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design; gift of Mrs. Murray S. Danforth (1934.858)

Height: 3 3/16 in. (8.1 cm.); diameter of lip: 4 3/4 in. (12.1 cm.)

One handle broken and repaired; glaze flaking in places.

Interior: small reserved disk with a black dot and circle.

Exterior, on the lip, side A: winged lion between two men. One man is hard to make out as the glaze has worn off. The other, with chlamys over one shoulder, attacks a winged lion with stones. The lion, which has a partially obliterated head, turns backwards toward the man attacking from its rear.

On the lip, side B: man between dog and sphinx. A man, nude except for a chlamys draped over one shoulder, defends himself against a sphinx at whom he seems to throw a rock. Behind him is a dog who is either helping or attacking the man.

Handle zone, on both sides: an inscription, xaire kai pi' thnde (welcome and drink this); beside the handles, small upright palmettes supported by volute tendrils which develop from the base of the handles.

Red: details of wings, breasts, hair, and tail of the sphinxes; ruff and anatomical articulation of the dog; chlamys and hair of the men; details of the palmettes.

White: breasts and faces of the sphinxes, details of their wings; traces of white on the chlamides of the men; details of the palmettes.

Unattributed ca. 540 - 530 B. C.

The decoration corresponds to one of the usual formulas for lip cups (see Beazley, JHS 52 [1932] 167 ff). The inscription in the handle zone is often a welcoming toast as here; it may also tell us who the potter or painter was. Little Master cups, so called because of their miniature style of drawing, were the dominant cup form in the middle through the third quarter of the sixth century. The Attic Siana cup is their forerunner (see No. 4), and their descendants are the great red-figure cups of the fifth century.

Bibliography:Luce 1936, no. 3, p. 36, fig. 2.

artifact.name: RISD 34.1374a and b
artifact.summary: Body: symposion. Lid: hunt.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design (34.1374 a and b)

Height with lid: 7 1/16 in. (17.9 cm.)

Height without lid: 3 5/8 in. (9.2 cm.)

Chipped at rim of base; lid broken and repaired with some plaster restoration. Glazed inside.

Body: symposion. Five bearded men recline on cushions and mattresses placed on the ground. One holds a kylix, and the other four play musical instruments, flutes and lyres. Behind, a leafless spray of ivy with only the berries (korymboi) depicted. The white of the cushions and dots of the drapery are mostly worn off.

On the lid: hunt. A youth with club and chlamys over one arm hunts a hare with the aid of three large dogs.

The scene on the body is framed above and below by a double row of dots between lines. The outer rim of the lid has a similar double row of black and white dots between lines; at the base of the knob, ray-like tongues. The edge of the lid is glazed.

Attributed to the Manner of the Haimon Painter [Bothmer]ca. 500 - 474 B. C.

This pyxis is similar to two in Berlin (Berlin F 2034 and Berlin F 2035; ABV, 556, no. 442 bis and 442 ter) ascribed to the Manner of the Haimon Painter. They are distinct from a number of pyxides of the Haimon Painter group which are variants of the Nicosthenic form with a black bowl and the picture confined to the lid (Para., 284). The scanty incision on the vague figures of the pyxis is characteristic of the Haimon Painter (Haspels 1936, 131).

Bibliography:Luce 1936, no. 2, p. 40, fig. 5; C. A. Robinson, Jr., "Greek and Roman Vases," BullRhode 27 (1939, reprinted 1951) no. 3, p. 7, fig 7.

artifact.name: RISD 30.082
artifact.summary: Cocks and sphinxes
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1 Pl. 7:1; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, p.48, Pl. 56: a-e.
artifact.dimensions: H. including handle 0.272 m., H. top of lip 0.258 m., D. base 0.096 m., D. body 0.179 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly of the Forman collection, sold at Sotheby's on 6/19/99 p. 63 no.326. Purchased by RISD from the Dikran Kelekian collection (NY), 1930.
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Cocks and sphinxes. In the center two roosters are confronted. Added red is used for combs, wattles, and there are red stripes near the base of the wings and red dots on the wings and tails. The wing and tail feathers are incised, as are the beaks, eyes, and outlines of the two cocks. White is also used on the tails. Between them is an addorsed palmette-lotus with a red base, black petals, red bud, and incised detail. Long lotus tendrils spiral up from behind the cocks. On either side of the vase in back of the cocks is a sphinx with frontal face in added white and red, and incised details. Seated on their hind legs with forelegs straight, they have red and black wings and long manes. Their tails are s-shaped. Incised details of anatomy are rare, although incisions occur for heavy eyebrows and neck wrinkles. Red dots are used to accent eyeballs, cheeks, and mouths over added white and over black glaze, two red strokes show the beginning of the breasts. In the field above the sphinxes are rosettes. At the junction of body and foot, a continuous band of rays.

Design in a large panel covers 70% of vase. The back is left in black glaze except for the junction of body and foot which is decorated with a continuous band of rays. On the shoulder tongues articulate the junction with the neck. The main decoration on the shoulder is an ivy vine with leaves and berries in groups of threes, unconnected to the main stem.
artifact.painter: Painter of the Phineus cup in Würzburg
artifact.shape_description: Ovoid with broad flat shoulder. Slightly flattened below left side of handle where it rested against another in the kiln. Trefoil lip, reeded handle.

artifact.name: RISD 29.140
artifact.summary: A: Apotheosis of Herakles; B: Theseus and the Minotaur
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce RISD Bulletin XVIII (1930) p.49; Uhlenbrock Herakles: Passage of the Hero through 1000 years of Classical Art, cat.no.11
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.323 m., Max. D. (at handles) 0.370 m., D. body 0.303 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Purchased in Rome, 1929.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Apotheosis of Herakles. In the center is a quadriga, facing right. Herakles in profile, facing right, steps into the chariot. He wears the lion's skin over a short chiton, his quiver strapped on his back and his sword at his side. He grasps the reins in both hands and holds a long spear in his left hand as well. To the extreme left, behind Herakles, stands Iolaos. Beardless to indicate youth, he wears a short chiton and has a red fillet in his hair. His sword hangs at his side. He carries the hero's club in his right hand and a bow in his left. Behind the horses, in the center, Athena stands in profile facing left, but with her feet pointing to the right. Her gender indicated by her white flesh, she wears the aegis over a long, sleeveless chiton, decorated with rosettes, and an Attic helmet with a high crest. She carries a spear in her right hand. Beside her Dionysos stands, wearing a long chiton and himation, the bottom of the chiton is decorated with a meander band. He has a red beard and a garland of ivy leaves on his head. At the right of the design stands Apollo, facing right, in front of the horses. Beardless and with a wreath of laurel on his head, he wears a long white chiton and a red-spotted himation. In his left hand he holds the kithara which he plays with his right. In the field there is conventional foliage.

Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur. In the center Theseus attacks the Minotaur, who seeks to escape. Theseus strides to the right, his head, hips, and legs shown in profile, his chest frontal. With his left arm, he holds the Minotaur's head and with his right, he grasps his drawn sword and aims it at the Minotaur's breast. Theseus wears a short spotted chiton with a meander band at the selvage, and his scabbard at his side. In imitation of Herakles, he wears an animal skin over this. With his hair worn in a long loop, gathered up with a fillet, he is shown beardless to indicate his youth. In this action pose the arm and foot of the Minotaur overlap with Theseus's body and incision is used to indicate important anatomical details. On either side two figures witness the action. At the left, Ariadne stands in profile, directly behind Theseus. She wears a long spotted chiton and a himation lined in red. Her hair falls in a long corkscrew curl just behind her ear. With her right hand at her side, she sniffs a flower held in her left. Behind her to the left, in profile facing right, stands a youth, in chiton and himation, holding a long spear and watching the action. Two similar youths frame the action on the right and stand in profile, facing left. These are probably the Athenian youths rescued by Theseus after he slaughtered the Minotaur.

There are many decorative patterns used. Lotus buds decorate the lip. There are palmettes above the handles, from which spring tendrils ending in lotuses. On the shoulder at the junction with the neck there is a tongue pattern (alternating in red and black), extending the width of the design panels. Along the side of the lip, from handle to handle, and along the sides of the panels there is an ivy leak pattern. On the body, where it joins the foot, are rays. The neck, handles, lower body, and foot are black.

artifact.name: RISD 28.020
artifact.summary: Body: A: Woman stands between youths; B: Mistress and maids; Foot: A: Poseidon pursues a woman; B: Youth pursues woman
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.51
artifact.dimensions: H. with lid 0.380 m., Max D. 0.160 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1928.
artifact.condit: Glaze on lid and neck worn off.
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Side A: Woman stands between youths. In the center stands a woman in profile, facing right. She wears a long chiton and a himation, and her hair is done up in a sakkos or snood. She gesticulates with her right hand and holds out her garment with her left. At the right, facing her, is a youth, draped in a himation which covers the back of his head. While leaning forward on a staff, he has his right hand on his hip and he points downward with his left. To the left, behind the woman, another youth stands to the right, his head turned to the left, away from the central scene. He is similarly clad with his himation draped over the back of his head. Also leaning on a staff, he holds a wreath in his right hand.

Side B: Mistress and maids. In the center a woman sits in profile, facing right, on a stool with a dotted cushion. She wears a long Ionic style chiton with loose elbow sleeves and decorated with two broad stripes; over her left shoulder is draped a himation. On her head she wears a sakkos or snood and earrings. She leans forward, gesturing with her right hand, palm up. On the right, and facing her, a woman stands in profile, similarly clad, with a kalathos in her right hand. Behind the seated woman, to the left, another woman stands in profile, facing left. She gestures with her left arm raised, similarly clad, but without the snood.

The knob is black. Where it joins the lid, there are rays. On the upper surface at the edge of the lid there are rosettes. The neck and handles are black. Below the handles are sphinxes. Above the design is tongue pattern where the neck joins the shoulder. Below the design is a reserved band and broad black stripe. Below this are rays which terminate in a black ridge where the body joins the foot.

Foot: Side A: Poseidon pursues a woman. Bearded Poseidon, partially clad in a himation, is identified by the trident which is placed obliquely beside him. He rushes to the left in hot pursuit of a young woman. He extends his left arm to catch her and holds together his garment with his left hand. The young woman flees to the left, her head turning back to the right to check on the sea god's advances. She gestures with her left hand as if to push him away. With her right, she holds up her garment so as to be able to run faster. With her hair gathered up in a sakkos or snood, she wears a long Ionic style chiton with loose elbow sleeves and a row of dots above the selvage. Perhaps the scene above is related in theme with the woman trying to evade the clear interests of the young men.

Side B: Youth pursues woman. To the left is a youth draped in a himation. Striding to the right, he pursues a young woman. With his right hand raised as if to catch her, he holds onto his garment with his left. Daintily, she holds up her dotted chiton with her right hand and carries her kalathos off with her left.

Beneath the ridge which joins the body to the foot, there is a band of vertical zigzags; below the design is a reserved band and rays.
artifact.shape_description: Lid has high knob

artifact.name: RISD 26.166
artifact.summary: Bull's head rhyton
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p.39, Pl.28: 3; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, pp. 51-52 pl.60
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52 and p.49, fig.12 a.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Purchased, 1926.
artifact.condit: Some flaking of glaze on head.
artifact.comparanda: For shape: Naples Stg.65; Verona 142 (Trendall & Cambitoglou 1978, p. 618, 109 and 112); Hoffmann 1966, p.16, no.47, Pl.12, 1-2
artifact.decoration_description: Bowl: A youthful satyr wears a yellow dotted garland on his yellow-haired head. With a yellowish-white tail he strides to the right towards a large red, yellow, and white flowering plant. He carries a yellow-tipped thyrsos in his right hand and a yellow-dotted tympanon or tambourine in his left. On either side is a large encircled palmette with a reserved leaf at three corners. Above is an egg and dot pattern; below a reserved band. Bull's head: The eyeballs are reserved with pupils and iris in black with the forelock accented in white, the eyes in red and black, and the insides of the ears and nostrils in red. A white star appears on his forehead.
artifact.shape_description: Bull's head. The bowl is Shape I (Hoffmann TR p.2), not aligned with head, but set at an obtuse angle to it

artifact.name: RISD 25.110
artifact.summary: Flying Nike
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Warren collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.comparanda: For subject: Metropolitan Museum 13.227.16
artifact.decoration_description:
Flying Nike. She flies to the right with outstretched frontal wings. In her right hand she holds a phiale, in her left a long incense-stand. She wears a long Ionic chiton, broken into many folds and with elbow sleeves, the right sleeve billowing with the breeze just before her descent. A himation falls down in heavy folds from her shoulder and ends in swallow-tail plaits. Her hair is covered with a netted sakkos or snood, curling up to a point at the back. In her ears are drop earrings, and on her right arm is a bracelet. On top of the sakkos is a diadem.

Where the neck joins the shoulder there is an egg-and-dot band, beneath which are elaborate ribbed palmettes and buds, joined by tendrils. Above and below the design panel is a band of meanders punctuated by squares with dotted crosses.

artifact.name: RISD 25.109
artifact.summary: Potter at work
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52; AJA 82 (1978) 397, fig.5
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the possession of E.P. Warren. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.condit: Body scratched
artifact.comparanda: for shape: ARV2, 676, 1-22
artifact.decoration_description:
Potter at work. The older, balding potter stands at the center of the design, his right arm outstretched, his left bent at the elbow. He wears a garment which is caught up about the waist and reaches the knees; otherwise he is nude. The loose muscles below the breast are indicated by faint dilute glaze. He has a long beard and mustache (in strokes of dilute glaze), a rather snub nose, round eyes, and a high skull, perhaps to indicate a barbarian. At the left is a solid seat, on which hangs drapery, perhaps the potter's himation. At the right is the oven, built of brick, in which a large pot is being fired. At his feet is a block on which to sit when at work.

At the junction of the neck and shoulder, there are rays/tongues. On the shoulder, a running palmette design in black-figured technique is seen. Above and below the design is a simple running meander.
artifact.shape_description: Class PL: neat make, broad body tapers strongly.

artifact.name: RISD 25.091
artifact.summary: Frieze of alternating goats and panthers
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1 p.16, Pl.5: 11; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, pp. 18, 19, fig.13: a-c
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks, RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p. 48; Hopper, BSA 44 (1949) p. 229, no.1; Benson, GKV (1953) p. 54 list 91 no. 5; Amyx BABesch 38 (1963) p.89 no.3.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Bought by E.P. Warren in London and formerly in his collection, where it had a round label in ink BB 243, below 8 (G). Purchased, 1925.
artifact.condit: Thick, brownish glaze for animals and boss is well-preserved. The brownish-black glaze used for the rest of the vessel is elusive with some decoration almost disappeared. Crazing and splintering around incised lines.
artifact.comparanda: For shape and plan of decoration Rhodes Tomb 5, no.3 (12.098)
artifact.decoration_description: Interior: In the center is the black omphalos or boss. Around this is a frieze of four animals, alternating between two goats and two panthers. In the field are dots and small, incised rosettes. There is a copious use of incised lines for details. The design is rendered in black only. The exterior is undecorated.
artifact.shape_description: Phiale with central boss. Two small holes for hanging at one end of lip.

artifact.name: RISD 25.090
artifact.summary: Arrival of young horseman before a seated man
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.date_description: belongs to the period of the Meidias Painter, but probably not by his hand
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Warren collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.comparanda: Boston 00.352; Boston 01.8085 For style: Athens, Vlasto (ARV2, 1215, 1)
artifact.decoration_description:
Arrival of young horseman before a seated man. At the left a bearded man sits in a chair, facing right. His upper body is nude, the lower part draped in a himation. He wears a white fillet in his hair. In his right hand he holds a long staff. In front of, and facing him, is a youth in a three-quarters view, wearing a chlamys, fastened by a clasp about his neck, and a petasos strapped to his back. The front of his body is nude; beardless, he wears only a fillet. His left hand is on his hip and he holds two spears in his right. Behind him is his horse, head down, as if grazing. Beside, and in back of the horse, is a rectangular tomb stele, surmounted by an offering, and drawn with an attempt at foreshortening. Perhaps this represents the warrior's own monument.

The design occurs in a framed panel. Above there is an egg-and-dart border; below are meanders and saltire squares, and at the sides, a pointed reed pattern between vertical lines.

artifact.name: RISD 25.089
artifact.summary:
Side A: Eros and Woman playing ephisdremos
Side B: Youth and woman
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p..38, Pl.28: 2 a-c; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, pp. 50-51, fig.59
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52 and p.49, fig.12a.
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.115 m., D. rim 0.135 m., W. from handle to handle 0.220 m., D. of foot 0.065 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.date_description: (Trendall)
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Warren collection, and purchased by him in Paris (Warren's no. BB 300.3. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.condit: glaze flaking off on handles.
artifact.comparanda: For ephisdremos: Malibu 71.AE.444; Von Bothmer, Ancient Art from NY Private Colls. (1961) no.233, Pl.89; Munich 8743. For shape, egg and dot motif and sub-handle palmettes: Altenburg 323 and Bari (private coll. (Melaguzzi-Valeri no.57). For palmette: Lecce 622.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A game of ephisdremos is shown (Pollux IX, 119: "...they put down a stone and throw at it from a distance with balls or pebbles. The one who fails to overturn the stone carries the other, having his eyes blindfolded by the rider, until, if he does not go astray, he reaches the stone, which is called the dioros." The woman, draped in a long sleeveless chiton, moves swiftly to the right. She makes a step, reaching her arms around behind her and clasping them together to support the left knee of the nude, youthful winged Eros, who is mounting on her back. Blindfolded by his hands, she stumbles towards the target, the dioros, a peculiarly contoured rock or pile of stones. In the field hangs a fillet or scarf. In front of the woman on the ground lies a white object, perhaps an incense burner. Besides her drapery the woman wears a necklace and bracelets of white beads.

Side B: Seated woman and draped youth. At the right is a seated woman, facing left. She wears a long, sleeveless chiton, a necklace and bracelets of white beads. On her right hand perches a bird. The contour of the rock on which she sits is suggested by a line of white dots. In the field over her head is a circular object, a ball(?). Before her stands a youth with a chlamys draped shawl-fashion over his arm, but otherwise nude. He wears a white fillet around his head and holds a strigil in his left hand.

On the lip from handle to handle on both sides an egg-and-dot pattern occurs. Under the handles there are elaborate palmettes and blossoms linked by tendrils.
artifact.shape_description: Broad body narrows steeply to a disk foot. The upper surface of the foot slopes downward.

artifact.name: RISD 25.087
artifact.summary: Standing woman and youth
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.51; Allentown Art Museum, Aspects 80-81, no.37.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Warren collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.condit: Glaze eroded on lip and lugs
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Standing woman. Adorned with a v-shaped necklace, she stands, facing front, dressed in a long transparent Ionic style chiton with loose elbow sleeves and overhang (kolpos), broken up into many folds. Her hair is bunched up on either side of her head and gathered in a fillet. With her right hand she holds up a long tasseled fillet and grasps the same in her left hand. Her feet are shown in profile, pointing to the right where there is a basket full of wool or fillets, indicated in red.

Side B: Youth. Draped in a himation which comes up over the back of his head, he faces left. He stretches out his right hand to the basket on Side A, and holds a branch. With his left, he leans on a staff, the top of which is concealed in the folds of his garment. Since the alabastron is a funerary offering, perhaps the woman is bringing the fillets to decorate a tomb as on RISD 69.142.1. Fillets were a token of remembrance and were frequently shown tied to the tomb stele.
artifact.shape_description: High, flaring mouth, wide bottom, two small pierced lugs for suspension.

artifact.name: RISD 25.086
artifact.summary: Tongues and geometric motifs
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p.42, Pl. 29:4; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, pp. 53-54, Pls.66: a, b
artifact.dimensions: H. with lid 0.133 m., H. lid 0.053 m., H. bowl 0.082 m., D. body 0.110 m., D. body 0.079 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Warren collection; Warren's no. BB 282.2. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.comparanda: Dot pattern: Moscow 505, 510; Karlsruhe B 252, B 236.
artifact.decoration_description: There are tongues/rays in black on buff on the shoulder of the lid, at its junction with the handle, and at the junction of the body with the foot. On the lid and body, where they join, there are broad buff stripes, each with three rows of black dots which slip into diagonal rows when aligned. The rest of the vase is covered with a good black glaze. Concentric circles and dot patterns on a buff ground complete the decoration.
artifact.shape_description: Bulbous pyxis with raised torus knob and ring foot. The top of the lid ends in a handle which can serve as a foot if inverted.

artifact.name: RISD 25.084
artifact.summary: Danae and Perseus in chest
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52; AK 13 (1970) 42, fig.4
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Warren collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.decoration_description:
Danae and Perseus in chest. Danae, drawn in outline, rises from the chest, clad in a chiton and himation; the latter worn over the back of her head. She faces right. In front of her is her son Perseus (whose head and neck alone appear) with long black hair. The chest is decorated with dots and rays and has claw feet. Against the white of the raised chest lid fly four sea birds.

On the shoulder where the shoulder meets the neck are rays/tongues. On the body above the design is a running meander band broken up with squares with reserved crosses.

artifact.name: RISD 25.083
artifact.summary: Side A: Triptolemos, in chair holding wheat with two women (Kore and Demeter?) Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.49
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the collection of E.P. Warren, who bought it from a Greek in London. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Triptolemos, in chair holding wheat with two women (Kore and Demeter?). Triptolemos in his chariot is facing right. He wears a long chiton and a himation decorated with red and white spots, the upper part of which is red. He wears a red garland or fillet and a red beard. In his right hand he holds a long winged scepter; in his left, four spears of wheat. The back of the seat ends in the head of a bird. Behind him facing right is Persephone, her flesh rendered in white. She wears a long chiton decorated with white spots and a black himation with white spots, lined with red. She wears her hair in a long mass down along the nape of her neck, bound with a red fillet or garland. She gesticulates with her hands, her left hand to her mouth and her right hand down. On the right, facing Triptolemos, is Demeter, crowned, looking left. Her flesh is white, her garments and gesticulating arms similar to those of Persephone.

Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur. Theseus, facing right, thrusts his sword into the neck of the Minotaur. He wears a short chiton decorated with red and white spots and a spiral band above the selvage. From a red belt around his waist hangs his scabbard. With his left hand he grasps the left arm of the Minotaur, who has been forced down on one knee. The back of the Minotaur's neck is decorated with red stripes and his nipples are in red. He grasps a white object in his right hand. On the right facing left is Ariadne, draped in a red-spotted chiton with an incised spiral border and a white-spotted himation lined with red. Her flesh is in white, her black hair bound with a red fillet. In her right hand she holds the wreath of light. Behind Theseus, at left facing right, is the hero's companion, nude and beardless, holding a garland in his left hand.

The lip, handles, and base are black. On the neck there is an incised double palmette-lotus chain. Beneath this there is an alternating red and black tongue pattern on the shoulder at the junction between shoulder and neck. Below the handles there are palmettes and small lotuses springing from tendrils. Below the design panel between alternating reserved and black glaze lines, there is a band of lotus buds. Below this at the junction of the lower body and base there are rays on the lower body.
artifact.shape_description: Small amphora; triple ribbed handles, "red-bodied" type.

artifact.name: RISD 25.082
artifact.summary: Charon in boat.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design; museum appropriation and special gift (Mrs. Gustav Radeke) (25.082)

Height: 9 1/2 in. (24.1 cm.)

Broken and repaired at neck; upper neck and mouth foreign. ?? From Greece.

Charon. At the left Charon, the ferryman, prepares to ferry a soul across the River Styx to Hades. He wears a red tunic (exomis) and conical hat (pilos). In one hand he holds an oar, and with the other he steadies himself on the stern of his boat. On the right is his passenger, a woman wearing a black chiton, much faded, and a white himation with red border and belt. Her hair is brown. She holds an aryballos in her right hand. Between the two figures are the tall reeds of the river bank with a red fillet draped in them. Above, meanders, much worn; on the shoulder, red palmettes, black egg and dot pattern, also worn.

??considerable repaint in design areas.

Attributed to the Reed Painter [Beazley] ca. 420 - 400 B. C.

The Reed Painter and the dependent R Group form one of the last major white lekythos workshops. The favored subject is Charon, who had appeared by the middle of the fifth century, but who became popular towards the end of the century. The chalky slip and varied polychromy, now much faded, place this lekythos in the late fifth century. Although the style has changed considerably, such late lekythoi still employ the same basic design (black mouth and neck, palmette motif on shoulder, meander pattern above scene) that was established by the Achilles Painter.

Bibliography: Banks 1928, 51, fig. 15; S. B. Luce, "Attic White-Ground Vases," BullRhode 20 (1932) 63, fig. 4; CVA, USA 2, p. 34, pl. 25, 5, pl. 25 a; C. A. Robinson, Jr., "Greek and Roman Vases," BullRhode 27 (1939) 35, fig. 16; ARV2, 1376, no. 5.

artifact.name: RISD 25.079
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena; Side B: Draped Youth
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI 1928 p.45, fig.9 (Side A) and p.51
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Warren collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Goddess Athena faces right. Unhelmeted, she wears the aegis over a long spotted chiton of Ionic style with full elbow sleeves and a himation with decorative stripe over her arms. Her right arm is outstretched as if exhorting a hero to action while her left hand carries a spear, point down. Her hair is bound in a fillet with long streamers and falls to the nape of her neck. One foot faces front while the other is turned to the right. Below is a band of meanders.

Side B: A crudely drawn youth, draped in himation, facing right, leans heavily on a staff. Below is a band of meanders.
artifact.inscriptions: *T*I*M*O*X*S*E*N*O*S *K*A*L*O*S, "Timoxsenos is beautiful", running vertically downward beside Athena.

artifact.name: RISD 25.078
artifact.summary: Hera seated
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p.26, Pl.19: 1 a-b; Beazley 1925, p.474, no.24
artifact.other_bibliography: D.M. Robinson, AJA XXXII (1928) pp. 53-55, figs.18,19; Studies von Blanckenhagen Pls. 10: 3-4, 12: 1-2, 13: 3-4
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Warren collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.decoration_description:
Shoulder: An egg-and-dot frieze marks the junction between neck and shoulder with the latter being decorated by an elaborate ribbed palmette and bud pattern.

Body: Hera. The goddess sits, facing right, on a high-backed throne with armrests. In her left hand she holds a scepter, ending in a lotus-bud, and in her right a phiale. She wears a long Ionic chiton with loose elbow-sleeves and a himation over her left shoulder. The chiton is broken up into many fine folds and has a dot pattern above the selvage; the folds of the himation are heavier. Her hair is folded up at the back and bound by a loosely knotted fillet, the ends of which fall down the back of the goddess. The throne has claw feet. Its back ends in a palmette on which is perched a falcon, with wings outspread. (This bird's association with Hera is rare, consisting only of this vase.) The goddess sits on a gaily decorated cushion which rests on the seat of the throne.

On the shoulder there are three palmettes. At the junction of body and shoulder and below the design, there are continuous bands of meanders broken by squares with dotted crosses.
artifact.inscriptions: on foot *A

artifact.name: RISD 25.077
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos with satyrs and maenads. Side B: satyrs and maenads.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design; museum appropriation and special gift (Mrs. Gustav Radeke) (25.077)

Approximate diameter: 11 3/4 in. (29.8 cm.)

Interior: satyr and maenad. Only the feet and tail of the satyr remain. Inscribed at the right, *O [*P]*A*I*S (the boy) and at the left, *K*A*L*O[*S] (beautiful). The tondo is framed by two reserved lines.

Side A: satyrs and maenads. At the left a maenad in chiton, himation, and sakkos brandishes her thyrsos, her head turned backwards. In front of her a satyr with a wineskin and drinking horn moves to the right. Between the two is inscribed *K*A*L*O*S (beautiful). In the center was the figure of Dionysos. Only the right arm, holding a drinking horn, and the right foot remain. Behind are sprays of vine. The figure after the gap to the right is missing except for one hand holding a drinking horn. At the far right is a satyr dancing towards the left, his back turned outwards as he circles around.

Side B: at the left an ithyphallic satyr follows a maenad who turns to attack him. She is dressed in chiton, himation, and sakkos and carries a thyrsos. In the center is a satyr with a leopard skin cape on his shoulders and a drinking horn in one hand. At the right is another maenad with chiton and leopard skin cape, followed by a satyr. To the left of the central satyr is inscribed *P*A*I*S *K*A*L*O*S (boy is beautiful) and to the right, *K*A*L*O*S (beautiful).

Dilute glaze: one maenad's hair, folds of the chitons.

Red: inscriptions, ivy wreaths, vine sprays.

Attributed to Epiktetos [Beazley] ca. 520 - 500 B. C.

The name of Epiktetos is known from forty signed vases. On a plate in Athens (Athens, Acr. 6; ARV2, 78, no. 102) he signs with both *E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N (made it) and *E*G*R*A*F*S*E*N (painted it), so we know he was both potter and painter. One can compare this kylix with one by Oltos (see Mount Holyoke 1967.BS.II.11) which is slightly earlier. The figures drawn by Epiktetos are more elegant and move with a lighter grace. This cup must belong in his early period.

Bibliography: Banks 1928, 50; S. B. Luce, "Two Kylikes in Providence," AJA 32 (1928) 442-444; S. B. Luce, "What Can Be Learned from Greek Vases," BullRhode 16 (1928) 46; Kraiger 1929, 198, no. 55; C. Dugas, "Céramique. Peinture. Mosaique." Revue des Etudes grecques 43 (1930) 123; CVA, USA 2, pp. 23-24, pl. 14; ARV2, 73, no. 34.

artifact.name: RISD 25.075
artifact.summary: Woman looking back
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley Attische Vasenmaler des rotfiguren Stils (1925) p.321, no.17 ter; Luce RISD Bulletin XX (1932) 58-63.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Warren Collection. Purchased, 1925.
artifact.comparanda: This vase falls into A. Fairbank's Group A, Class III, c (Fairbanks 1907, pp. 80-90) than to any other group, and the same shoulder palmettes appear in his fig.23 (p.52, no.19). An almost identical design is found on a lekythos from the Metropolitan Museum (New York 06.1021.126). Of inferior quality, this one is probably not by the same painter.
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Woman looking back. In the main panel a woman moves swiftly to the right. In her left hand she holds a twig with black leaves; in her right she holds a fruit, perhaps a pomegranate. She is dressed in a Doric chiton with kolpos or overfold, bordered with red. On her head she wears a sakkos or snood and earrings. Her head is turned back to the left towards what she is fleeing from.

The lip and bottom are black. The neck and shoulder are red. The white slip is of a brownish type. On the shoulder, four crude palmettes are connected by tendrils with short rays/tongues at the junction with the neck. Above the design is a running black meander.
artifact.shape_description: Shape ATL (AWLp.82).

artifact.name: RISD 25.074
artifact.summary: Both sides: reclining maenads.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design; museum appropriation and special gift (Mrs. Gustav Radeke) (25.074)

Height: 2 3/16 in. (5.6 cm.); Diameter: 2 7/8 in. (7.2 cm.)

Missing handle; minor abrasions on one side.

On both sides, reclining maenads. Both wear chitons with a kolpos overfold. They have ivy wreaths in their hair and recline against gaily colored cushions. Behind one of the maenads is a thyrsos; the other holds a skyphos.

Red: wreaths, tassels of belts, rim of skyphos.

Attributed to Makron [Beazley] ca. 490 - 480 B. C.

The abrupt transition between frontal and profile views on the maenads, as on the Erotes of the Bowdoin askos, helps place both askoi within the early work of Makron. The subjects (reclining maenads, flying Erotes) are both well suited to the narrow fields of decoration provided by the vessel.

Bibliography: BullRhode 16 (1928) 50 passim; S. B. Luce, "Four Red-Figured Vases in Providence," AJA 35 (1931) 298 ff; CVA, USA 2, p. 26, pl. 17, 4; ARV2, 480, no. 338.

artifact.name: RISD 25.067
artifact.summary: Child riding a stag
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52
artifact.dimensions: H. to top of handle 0.089 m., D. 0.058 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Purchased, 1925.
artifact.condit: The black glaze is eroded on the lip.
artifact.decoration_description: Child riding a stag. The group moves to the right. The child is nude, with its flesh rendered in added white, its arms pudgy and infantile in form, decorated with white bracelets in relief on the right wrist and ankle. Its hair is brown, bound with a white fillet. Below the lip and in the field are white heart-shaped flowers; on either side are plants with leaves and white berries. Below the design is an egg-and-dart pattern.
artifact.shape_description: Trefoil lip

artifact.name: RISD 23.356
artifact.summary: Woman with bird
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.52
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Purchased, 1923.
artifact.decoration_description:
Woman with bird. The woman stands in profile, facing right and holding a large striped bird in both arms. She wears a long Ionic style chiton with loose elbow sleeves and a himation over her left shoulder. Her hair is gathered up into a bandeau. Behind her is a stool with a decorated cushion, in front a small chest.

Where the neck and shoulder join there is an egg-and-dot band. Beneath this on the shoulder, there are three elaborate palmettes and blossoms. On front of the vase only, above and below the panel runs a band of running meanders.
artifact.inscriptions: to the right of the figure, *P*A*I *K*A*L*H?, "beautiful boy".

artifact.name: RISD 23.324
artifact.summary: Side A: Satyrs and maenads with Eros/Pothos<lb>Side B: Three youths
artifact.other_bibliography: BCH (1984) 128, fig.7a
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Hamilton and Hope collections. Purchased at Hope Sale, 1917. Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1923.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Satyrs and maenads with Eros/Pothos. A nude silen, bearded and with a garland in added white moves from left to right. In his raised left hand is a fillet in added white on his head. With his right forearm he grasps the right forearm of a Maenad who staggers forward, her head with short unbound tresses, thrown back in ecstasy. She wears a long Doric chiton with an overfold. In her right hand is a thyrsos, on her left arm a skin with a herringbone design in red on it. At this point, the ground, which is indicated by a black line, rises into a small mound on which is a plant. Above and to the right of this mound flies a nude, youthful winged boy, beardless, and with a garland of ivy leaves in his hair. He plays the double flute and, like the other figures, moves right. The quiet pose of this flying figure serves to bring out more plainly the frenzy of the others, while his name, Pothos or Desire as opposed to Eros or Love, serves to accentuate the orgiastic quality of the scene. At his right a second Maenad is reeling forward in a drunken frenzy. She wears a skin over a Doric chiton, tied with a ribbon beneath the breast, and fastened at the left shoulder. Her right arm is raised and her left lowered, and in each she holds an ivy branch with leaves and berries. Finally to the right, a nude, bearded silen dances to the right. Looking around at the Maenad, he holds a flaming torch in his right hand, his left arm raised over his garlanded head.

Side B: Three youths. Most of this side is missing, only the figure at the right is complete. Beardless, he faces left, dressed in a himation and has a fillet around his head. In his right hand he holds a strigil. Of the central figure only a part of the drapery is left. Of the figure at the left, only the feet, lower part of the drapery and a small bit of the upper part remain. From the name of the winged boy, Beazley calls the painter of this vase The Pothos Painter, and lists a number of works by his hand.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: Over the nude silen's head runs the inscription *K*O*M*O*S, "komos". Over the maenad's head is her name *Q*A*L*I*A, "Thalia"; at her right is the inscription *K*O*L*O*S, "kolos" for kalos, "beautiful". Over the head of the winged boy is his name *P*O*Q*O*S, "pothos" or Desire. Over the head of the second maenad is her name, *E*U*D*I*A, "Eudia"? or perhaps *E*U[*O]*D*I*A, "Eu(o)dia"(?). Over the head of the bearded silen is his name, *O*I*N*O*S, Oinos, "wine".
artifact.shape_description: no.1, with lugs

artifact.name: RISD 23.323
artifact.summary: Side A: combat of two warriors (Achilles and Hector?).. Side B: warrior advancing.
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.51; Allentown Art Museum, Aspects 86-87, no.40 (A, B).
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Hope collection. Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1923.
artifact.comparanda: For figures: Villa Giulia psykter
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Combat of two warriors. On the left, the victorious one advances to the right, bearded, he wears a helmet with a long crest. On his left arm he carries a round shield (shown foreshortened) with a tripod device. He is nude except for greaves on his legs and a garment around his shoulders, the ends of which are folded, crossed in front and tucked under his sword belt. Blood streams from a wound in his right shoulder, at the base of the neck. He attacks and thrusts at his foe with a long-bladed sword. On the right his antagonist has fallen, twisted to the right, his back turned toward the spectator, his left leg doubled up in collapse. His helmet is thus seen from the rear, a rare example of this in Greek vase-painting. Nude, except for a loin-cloth, his hair falls in long ringlets down his back. He holds his sword in his right hand and a long spear in his left, his scabbard hanging by a red baldric from his right shoulder. He is dying from two wounds, one in the left breast, the other in the right thigh, from which blood streams in added red. Ribs, backbone, and calf muscles are shown in dilute glaze.

Side B: warrior advancing. Moving to the left, the warrior wears a tight-fitting helmet without crest and a short stiff chiton (of leather or linen?) decorated with dots and crosses. On his left arm he carries a round shield (shown foreshortened) with a tripod device, in his right hand a long spear.

Below the design there is an elaborate and beautiful horizontal band of palmettes, addorsed and enclosed with tendrils.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: Under the feet of the victorious warrior, *K*A*L*L*I*A*S, (Kallias) Between the heads of the two, *K*A*L*O*S, (is beautiful).
artifact.shape_description: Class L (The Providence Class)

artifact.name: RISD 23.303
artifact.summary: Two horsemen, lotus, and palmettes.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Castellani, Paravey and Darthes collections. Found in 1865. Purchased, 1923.
artifact.comparanda: The Group of Louvre F 110; ABV, 220, 35. Same graffito *S*O occurs on Louvre F 110 (Hoppin, Nikosthenes 33*).
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: On the shoulder, two horsemen move right. The one at right is nude; his horse has a mane and tail in added white. The left horseman wears a short white chiton; his horse's mane and tail are red. On either side of the horsemen are three male figures facing them. In each case the inner figure is nude, the outer two draped in himatia.

Side B: On the shoulder, the scene is the same as on Side A, except that both riders are clad in short white chitons and that there is a flying bird between them.

On the neck there is a continuous pattern of addorsed palmettes and rudimentary lotuses, connected by tangent rings. On the lip there is a single pattern of ivy leaves with dots between leaves, and a double pattern on the handles. Below, between the moldings, is a palmette cable band. Below the lower molding is a zigzag pattern in red on black. At the junction of the body and foot are rays. Accessories are rendered in red and white. There is a sparing, but telling use of incisions for details.
artifact.inscriptions: *N*I*K*O*S*Q*E*N*E*S *E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N, "Nikosthenes made" under one handle. On the foot a very faint graffito occurs : *S*O
artifact.shape_description: The vase has a bell-shaped foot.

artifact.name: RISD 23.300
artifact.summary: Panelled decoration with horses and birds
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p.18, pl.8: 1a-b; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, p.34, fig.40, Pl.40: a-g.
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.41, fig.4 (Side A) and p.48; Luce, AJA 38 (1924) p.73.
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.339 m., D. body 0.325 m., D. lip (handle to handle) 0.405 m., D. without handles 0.273 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.date_description: Dipylon style.
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in collection in Germany. Purchased, 1923.
artifact.material_description: Rosy brown clay with black and white particles
artifact.decoration_description:
Geometric with horses and birds.

Side A: Three metopes are filled with animals and separated from each other by vertical and criss-cross lines. In the left panel a horse faces right with a goose under him. In the right panel a similar horse and goose face left. They seem to be tethered to feed boxes, fixed to the stall walls. Both have field decoration of dotted rosettes and zigzags. In the center two dancing birds (Coldstream: cock and hen) with hatched bodies are confronted. The field decoration consists of cross-hatched inverted triangles and dotted rosettes.

Side B: Three metopes, similarly filled with animals, are separated from each other by vertical lines and bands of cross-hatching. The left and right panels are the same as on A. The central panel has a broad heavy vertical meander pattern.

Light and dark are well-balanced on this vase with the upper half of body and foot predominantly light. The top of the rim is organized by groups of short strokes, five on each side. The handles are decorated with horizontal stripes in black on buff. Below the main design, there is horizontal linear decoration. The lower body and lower foot are black; and at the junction of foot and body, there are rays on the upper foot in black on buff.
artifact.shape_description: Generally kraters mark the burials of aristocratic males. Much like "sub-Mycenaean" vases, this krater has a low, offset rim, vertical strap handles and a flaring pedestalled foot.

artifact.name: RISD 22.216
artifact.summary: Europa on the bull
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.48
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.date_description: Late in black figured-technique, but excellent execution.
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1922.
artifact.condit: Added white for female flesh has largely disappeared.
artifact.comparanda: Not very pronounced Leagran, not far from the Edinburgh Painter (Haspels 1936, p. 50).
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Europa on the bull. The bull moves to the right with Europa on his back. She holds on with her left hand and steadies herself with her right. She wears a chiton and himation, both decorated with red and white spots. She has a red fillet in her hair. On her feet and right hand are traces of white, apparently the color used for all exposed flesh, mostly disappeared. Behind her to the left is a girl in right profile with white flesh. Wearing a red fillet on her head, she is dressed in a long chiton and himation, decorated with red dots. To the right is a bearded Hermes, facing the bull, wearing a short chiton and chlamys, both decorated with red and white spots. He wears a petasos on his head and winged boots on his feet. In his right hand he holds a kerykeion. There is conventional foliage in the field.

On the shoulder there are running palmettes and at the junction of shoulder and neck, short vertical rays/tongues. Accessories are in added red and white.

artifact.name: RISD 22.215
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles fighting two centaurs<lb>Side B: Man and youth
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1 pp. 39-40, Pl.28: 1a-b; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, pp. 48-50, no.58, p.49, fig.58, Pl.58: a-i
artifact.other_bibliography: Moon, BSR XI (1929) p.35
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.316 m., D. rim 0.312 m., D. through handles 0.295 m., D. foot 0.155 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Hope Collection. Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1922. Excavated during the eighteenth century.
artifact.condit: Minor surface wear does not obscure figured areas.
artifact.comparanda: For Doric columns: Boston (APS p.6, no.5), Berlin2400, and Lecce 571. For subject matter: Louvre G 570 (Sisyphus Painter).
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles fighting two centaurs. To the left a statuesque Herakles is shown in heroic nudity, beardless and youthful, striding right and swinging his club behind his head against two centaurs. One centaur advances with furrowed brow to fight back, armed with a stone in his right hand and a chlamys or cloak tied around his neck and thrown over his left arm as a shield. The other flees to right with arms unusually twisted behind his back, as if to rub a bruise or pull out an arrow (von Bothmer). He grimaces in pain with his mouth open, as if howling. The Centaurs are bearded, with short, woolly hair, snub noses with flaring nostrils, large ears and African (?) profiles. Around their waists are girdles of hair to mark the change between human and equine bodies. The coarseness of the faces of the centaurs is in marked contrast to that of Herakles and those of the youth and man on Side B.

Side B: A youth and a man. In the center is a Doric column. To the left a youth draped in a himation faces right. To the right a bearded man similarly attired faces left. His right arm hangs at his side while he leans on a staff with his left. Both man and youth wear fillets of added white on their heads.

Above, on lip, continuous laurel-leaf pattern with a line down the center leaf decorates the exterior. Below, on each side, from handle to handle, a coarse meander and dotted square pattern occur. Grooves and fillets accent subdivisions of the krater and serve as discreet decorative elements.
artifact.painter: Painter of the Berlin Dancing Girl

artifact.name: RISD 22.214
artifact.summary: Satyr and maenad
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.49
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.076 m., D. 0.194 m., W. handle to handle 0.255 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1922.
artifact.comparanda: Copenhagen, Thorvaldsen Museum 25 (ABV, 631,2)
artifact.decoration_description:
Exterior: Side A: Between feminine eyes, a nude silen attacks a Maenad. She advances toward him, but turns her head away. Her flesh is white; she wears a garland of ivy leaves in her hair, and is draped in a chiton and himation, decorated with white dots arranged in triangles. The hair, beard, and tail of the silen are red. In the field there is conventional foliage.

Side B: Similar scene except that the Maenad flees from the silen, and looks back at him. In her hands she holds a pair of krotala. In the field there is conventional foliage. Under each handle there is a flying bird. There is no design on the interior.

artifact.name: RISD 22.213
artifact.summary: Oinochoe in form of woman's head
artifact.sources_used: Beazley Addenda 2, p. 387, no. 1538.1; CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p.35, Pl.26: 1a-b
artifact.other_bibliography: Banks RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.49, fig.12c; Allentown Art Museum, Aspects 140-141, no.68.
artifact.dimensions: H. to top of handle 0.24 m., H. lip 0.201 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in Hope collection. Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1922.
artifact.comparanda: New York 30.11.10; for shape: London 73.8-20.280 (ARV2, 1538, 2)
artifact.decoration_description:
The head is in red with a weakly-modeled neck. The lips curl slightly upward. The lower lip is cleft, and between the upper lip and the nasal septum, there is a deep vertical depression. The ends of the mouth are finished off with black arcs. The irises of the eyes are red, pupils black, and the iris is separated from the whites of the eyes by black circles. Eyebrows are indicated by broad black strokes. The hair on the forehead is raised and finished in dots, stopping in front of the ears. The rest of the head is covered with a black and red-checked scarf, held in place by a bandeau in front with a design of chevrons, and another horizontal bandeau with a design of squares. At the back are two bosses, which represent the ends of a large fibula.

Between the head and neck of the oinochoe is a cushion, the top of which is treated with a palmette-lotus design in red figure, while on the side there is an egg-and-dart pattern. At the bottom of the handle there is an addorsed palmette motive. Above the cushion is undecorated.
artifact.shape_description: trefoil lip oinochoe, woman's head, no.1, with mouth of oinochoe-shape 1; Class L (The Providence Class)

artifact.name: RISD 22.212
artifact.summary: A: Combat scene; B: Apotheosis of Herakles
artifact.other_bibliography: M. A. Banks, RISD Bulletin XVI (1928), p.49
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Purchased at Christie's, London. Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1922.
artifact.graffiti: under foot of vase
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Combat scene. A quadriga with two men moves from right to left. Traces of added color show that horses' manes and forelocks were white. The horses stand on their hind legs, their forelegs bent and pawing the air. The charioteer, bearded and bareheaded, has a Boeotian shield (shown foreshortened) and breastplate strapped to his back. The chariot's wheels are successfully foreshortened. The shield device-a tripod in added white- is largely gone. The other man is largely hidden behind the horses. He wears an Attic helmet with a high crest and a large Boeotian shield (device, white dots) and carries two long spears. Under the horses' hooves lies a dying warrior. He wears a cuirass over a short chiton, a Corinthian helmet with a high crest ending in white horsehair, greaves, and carries a round shield (device, bukranion). Two white straps cross on his chest to support his sword, which is sheathed. His left leg is bent beneath him, and he sinks back on his right arm.

Side B: Apotheosis of Herakles. Herakles, clad in the lion's skin, walks from left to right, carrying his club in his left hand and his bow in his right. On his shoulder is a quiver, at his side, a sword, fastened to his belt. In front of him, at the center, Athena (flesh white) moves to the right, her head turned back towards Herakles. She wears a long chiton with white dots, her aegis draped over her upper torso, and an Attic helmet with a high crest. In her right hand she holds a long spear. At the right is Hermes in a white-dotted chlamys, a petasos with a pointed crown, the brim decorated with dots, and winged boots. In his left hand he holds the kerykeion; his right hand extended downwards. He is shown in profile to the left, walking towards Athena. On both sides the figures' helmets extend into the tongue pattern above. On both sides the figures overlap the palmettes and tendrils beneath the handles.

On the neck is an incised double palmette-lotus chain. At the junction of neck and shoulder, red and black tongues alternate. Below the handles, tendrils dangle, ending in palmettes and lotuses. Below the main design runs a band of running meanders, then a band of lotus buds, and below this, rays. The lip, handles, and foot are black.
artifact.shape_description: neck amphora with triple reed handles.

artifact.name: RISD 22.114
artifact.summary: Woman seated at her toilet with four women
artifact.other_bibliography: M. A. Banks, RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p. 52
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.date_description: Period of Hermonax, or somewhat later (figures painted inside side handles suggests a late date
artifact.collection_history: Found in Athens before 1884. Formerly owned by W.J. Stillman, esq., sometime U.S. Consul in Crete. Purchased, 1922.
artifact.comparanda: London E 183; London E 188; London E 445; Gerhard 1840-1858, Pl.156
artifact.decoration_description:
Woman seated at her toilet with four women. In the center a woman sits, facing right, and wearing a long Ionic chiton and himation. She holds a mirror in her right hand. Her hair is bound with a fillet which holds her diadem in place. At her feet and behind her chair are tall baskets or kalathoi (for wool?). In the field over her head another fillet hangs. In front of and facing her stands another woman similarly clad, with a heavier himation that conceals her left arm and hand. In her right hand she holds a casket which she offers to the seated woman. The fillet in her hair holds no diadem. Behind her hangs a wreath. She is followed by a third woman almost identically clad, who stretches out her right hand, palm up. This woman is partly concealed by the right handle. Behind the seated woman a fourth advances towards her, draped in a long Ionic chiton and himation, her left arm bent at the elbow with a rather unconvincing attempt at foreshortening, her right arm at her side. Her hair is bound in a fillet. Behind her comes yet another, a fifth, similarly clad, holding in her right hand a branch with spiral tendrils. She is partly hidden by the left handle.

On the rim of the lip and at the junction of handles and body there are egg-and-dart patterns. There is a palmette-lotus at the foot of the neck in front only. Meanders and saltire-squares occur below the design.

artifact.name: RISD 1986.158
artifact.summary: Eros chasing a hare.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Acquired from Mrs. Kate Cohen, Ms. Andrea Toon, and Mr. Joel Cohen, 1986.
artifact.condit: Applied white and yellow are in pristine condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Eros chasing a hare. A panel is created by egg-and-dot borders on the shoulder and lower body; dot sprays dangle from the border above. Here a very feminine looking Eros with generous breasts, bangle bracelets, necklace, and beribboned tresses runs after a hare. Male genitalia lead one to speculate whether a distinctly feminine Eros or hermaphrodite is being shown. The figures are bracketed by wispy floral sprays, indicated by a row of dots. This androgynous portrayal of the youthful god of love is characteristic of the late fourth century. The hare is a traditional love gift brought by an older admirer to a youth. Since the lekythos often carries funerary subject matter and has generally been found in graves, perhaps one should consider the scene of Eros chasing the hare as referring to the provision of love gifts for the deceased loved one even in the face of death.

Vertical stripes decorate the neck. Beneath the egg-and-dot frieze below the panel is a reserved area, partially filled by two horizontal lines in black glaze and, beneath these, a wave pattern, again set off against a reserved background. The foot and spout are undecorated save for the black glaze.
artifact.shape_description: delicate and diminutive

artifact.name: RISD 16.040
artifact.summary: Tongue and gear patterns.
artifact.sources_used: Ashmead & Phillips 1976, pp. 21-22, fig.17 and Pl.17: a-c; CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, Pl.26, fig.2
artifact.dimensions: H. without lid 0.114 m., H. with lid 0.164 m., D. bowl 0.204 m., D. lid 0.114 m., D. foot 0.127 m.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Wilham S. Baker, 1916.
artifact.condit: The glaze is thinner especially above the foot, perhaps as a result of stacking in the kiln.
artifact.comparanda: CVA, Munich 2 (6) Pl.100 (296) fig.1; Copenhagen 4706; Capetown H4821bis
artifact.decoration_description: The shoulder and lid are elaborately decorated with standard tongue and gear patterns while the zone at the base of the knob and the thin foot rim are reserved for clarity and emphasis. The underside of the bowl, the resting surface of the foot, and the lid's rim and undersurface are unglazed.
artifact.shape_description: In Beazley, this shape is known as a Type A kothon, characterized by a deep body and broad, flaring foot with very sharp foot rim. Knob handle has straight contour.

artifact.name: RISD 15.005
artifact.summary: Side A: Apollo. Side B: woman.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.essay_text:
Lent by the Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design; museum appropriation and special gift (Mrs. Gustav Radeke) (15.005)

Height: 20 in. (50.8 cm.)

Broken and repaired; plaster restoration especially on B; one handle restored; part of foot restored; abrasions of glaze on B. Under foot, graffito.

From Vulci.

Side A: Apollo. The god stands with head turned to the left. He extends his right arm with phiale in hand and holds a kithara in the other arm. Over his chiton he wears a himation fastened at the shoulder with a brooch. His long curled hair is dressed with a fillet and laurel wreath. A dotted sash with a crenelated border and a fringe is attached to the lyre and provides a festive air.

Side B: woman (Artemis?). Only the lower part of her body is preserved. She holds an oinochoe, presumably to fill Apollo's phiale. She wears a chiton and himation. On A, the ground line consists of pairs of meanders alternating in direction and interrupted with cross-squares. On B, it consists of meanders only. At the base of the handles are tongues.

Dilute glaze: strands of hair, step pattern on the fillet attaching the lyre to Apollo's hand, design on the sash.

Red: Apollo's wreath, lyre strings on black background, string for the plectrum of the lyre.

Attributed to the Providence Painter; his name piece [Beazley] ca. 500 - 475 B.C.

The shape as well as the style of this amphora are derived from the Berlin Painter (Yale 1913.133), who must have been the Providence Painter's teacher (Beazley 1918, 76). Although there are no inscriptions, the heavy kithara, long hair, and serene pose all suggest Apollo. By implication, the figure on the reverse should be his sister Artemis (Beazley 1922, 70).

Bibliography: C. Lenormant and J. de Witte, Elite des monuments céramographiques 2 (Paris 1837-1861) 33-34, pl. XIII; Gerhard 1840-1858, 85-88, pl. 24; Reinach 1900, 27, nos. 1, 2; S. B. Luce, AJA 21 (1917) 411 passim; Beazley 1918, 76; Hoppin 1919, vol. 2, p. 394, no. 38; Beazley 1922, 70; S. B. Luce, AJA 28 (1924) 73 passim; BullRhode 16 (1928) 37, fig. 1, p. 50; BullRhode 19 (1931) 38; CVA, USA 2, p. 26, pl. 18; BullRhode 27 (1939) 32-33; Simon 1953, 43, no. 43; J. H. C. Kern, "Two Vases by the Providence Painter in Leyden," Oudheidkundige Medelingen vit het Rijksmuseum van Oudheden to Leiden 42 (1961); ARV2, 635, no. 1.

artifact.name: RISD 13.1479
artifact.summary: Homosexual courtship; side A: A youth with cocks and a man with a leashed dog; side B: A youth with two cocks and a man with a stag.
artifact.other_bibliography: AJA XXVIII (1924) p.73; M. A. Banks, "Greek vases in the RISD Museum," RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p.43, fig 6, and p.49; Shapiro, AJA 85 (1981) Pl.24: figs. 2-3: A, B; Allentown Art Museum, Aspects of Ancient Greece, G. F. Pinney and B. S. Ridgway, eds. (Allentown Art Museum, an Exhibition, Sept. 16-Dec. 30, 1979), pp. 34-35, no.14a.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1913 (C1813).
artifact.comparanda: Pattern style shows strong Chalcidian influence, but Luce (CVA, 19) believes it is Attic. Approaches some of the more old-fashioned vases in Group E (ABV, 133-138).
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Two nude men, confronted. The beardless youth on the left wears his hair long with a long forelock and holds two cocks in his hands. The bearded man on the right approaches, offerings a leashed dog. What is being shown is the presentation of love gifts by the erastes or older lover to the eromenos or youthful beloved. This is called by Beazley, Beta, the second stage of courtship as shown in Attic vase-painting.

Side B: Similar scene. The bearded man on the left strides forward and offers the youth a stag while he reaches up to caress the youth's forehead. The beardless youth wears his hair long with two long forelocks in front of his ears and stands on the right holding two cocks.

On the neck is an intertwining palmette lotus. Under the handles is a bold design of spirals with accessory palmettes and lotus buds. Below the designs is a band of lotus buds and rays at the junction of the foot. Accessories are in red; and incised lines are used sparingly for anatomical details.

artifact.name: RISD 11.018
artifact.summary: Satyrs and maenads, three youths
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, probably in 1911.
artifact.comparanda: Athens 12255; Athens 12250
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Satyrs and Maenads. At the left a Maenad dances to the left. She wears a long Doric chiton, with a border of palmettes at the bottom. Around her neck is a necklace of white beads, and her hair is bound with a garland of white berries. She holds a thyrsos in her left hand and a large white tympanon or tambourine in her right. Behind her is a nude silen in an ecstatic pose with his right arm bent behind his head and his left stretched downwards, perhaps to the drinking horn at his feet. In the center, behind the silen, a Maenad dances, her white flesh showing through long, transparent drapery. She wears a necklace of small beads and a garland in her disheveled hair. With her head thrown back she sings and dances ecstatically to the accompaniment of the tambourine which she plays with both hands. She glides to the right while below and to the right, a nude silen moves to the right in a violent pose, his right leg straight, his left sharply bent. His hair, beard, and tail are rendered in added white. In his right hand he holds an unidentifiable object and in his left, a white tambourine. Above him and to the right is another silen in repose, facing left. He is nude and holds a horn in his right hand; his left is on his hip. In the field between the two silens are bunches of grapes.

Side B: Three youths. In the center is a nude youth in right profile, with his body in three-quarters view. His right hand rests on his hip, and his left holds a strigil. On either side of him there is a youth in himation facing him. The youth on the left holds out a strigil in his left hand, the one at the right extends his right arm. In the field hang two round vessels and two triangular objects, perhaps leather cases. Under each handle there is an altar.

artifact.name: RISD 11.015
artifact.summary: Cock
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 2, RISD 1, p.15, Pl.5: 1 a-b; Ashmead & Phillips 1976, p.15, 73, Pl. 6
artifact.other_bibliography: M. A. Banks, "Greek vases in the RISD Museum," RISD Bulletin XVI (1928) p. 48
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1911 (C1483).
artifact.condit: Some of the glaze has disappeared from the decoration below the handle.
artifact.comparanda: Payne 1931, p.282 nos. 267-279; Mannheim Cg 159; Brunswick AT 337; Louvre CA 1059; Brussels R 209; and Copenhagen (no #).
artifact.decoration_description:
A profile cock, facing right, left wing raised and flapping, right wing at side. Two of his tail feathers stretch around in back almost as far as the tip of his left wing. The comb, wattles, and parts of the wings are in added red. In the field there are large and small incised rosettes and small incised blobs. The rosette above his left wing has both interior incision and an incised contour. Rays or tongues occur at the top of lip, on the neck, and on the bottom. There are dots around the edge of the lip.

Accessories are rendered in added red. Firm, hasty incisions are used for details.
artifact.shape_description: Payne, Group A. The base has an indented navel.

artifact.name: RISD 11.013
artifact.summary: Iris (?) facing toward altar
artifact.other_bibliography: S. B Luce, RISD Bulletin XX (1932) 58-63.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1911. (C1497)
artifact.condit: There are traces of a chalky white slip laid over the cream slip. The surface of the shoulder is chipped and the black glaze on the foot is eroded.
artifact.comparanda: This seems to be closer to A. Fairbank's Group A, Class II, series 2 (Athenian White Lekythoi I (1907) pp. 36-58) than to any other group, and the same shoulder palmettes appear in his fig.23 (p.52, no.19).
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Iris (?) facing toward altar. Iris (?) flies towards an altar with a volute superstructure and dotted molding. She holds in both hands a large casket, decorated in black squares and wavy vertical lines at top and bottom, with a horizontal running meander pattern in the center. Fugitive lines around her shoulders show that although ostensibly nude, she was clothed with a transparent garment, probably chiton and himation. Her black hair is simply arranged.

On the shoulder there are five palmettes connected by tendrils. A running meander decorates the top of the body where it joins the shoulder.

artifact.name: RISD 06.050
artifact.summary: Woman facing stele brings funerary offerings
artifact.other_bibliography: S. B. Luce, RISD Bulletin XX (1932) 58-63.
artifact.collection: Museum of Art, Rhode Island School of Design
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mrs. Gustav Radeke, 1906 (C794).
artifact.condit: White slip and black glaze on body are somewhat chipped.
artifact.comparanda: Svres 3084.1; ARV2, 759, 20. This seems to belong to Fairbank's Group D, Class VII, series 2 (Athenian White Lekythoi I pp. 302-317).
artifact.decoration_description:
Body: Woman facing stele brings funerary offerings. A woman stands, facing right, in front of a stele which has a fillet tied around its center. She is dressed in an Ionic chiton, which is broken up into many rippling folds. With both hands outstretched she supports a huge basket of offerings, including a black lekythos and numerous hanging fillets. In the field hangs another long fillet, caught up in two places.

Neck and handle are red. There are traces of black on the lip; and the foot and lower body are black. On the shoulder there are four black-figured palmettes connected by tendrils and at the junction of the neck, short rays. On the white slip, above the design, there is a simple running meander.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS739
artifact.summary: Footrace
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1942, 79-80, n. 20 and pl. 41.
artifact.collection_history: The piece was excavated by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society in 1896/1897. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations was provided by Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst. From Tomb 65M.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is somewhat worn and pitted.
artifact.decoration_description: Footrace. Two nude youths are racing while two men watch. In the center of the scene, the two nude youths run toward the right. They have fillets around their hair. On either side stands a cloaked spectator looking toward them. Their chitons are black and their himations red, they wear little red caps, and they are clean shaven.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS715
artifact.summary: Body divided into zones and decorative bands.
artifact.other_bibliography: Pinney & Ridgway 1979, 16-17, no. 4
artifact.collection_history: The vase was recovered in 1896-1897 in excavations at Vulci sponsored by the American Exploration Society. The olpe subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: The surface is covered with small chips but shows little wear of the glaze.
artifact.decoration_description: The body is almost entirely covered by glaze, with the exception of a reserved zone decorated with black rays above the foot and the edge of the rim. The zones of black glaze on the body are delineated by fine horizontal lines in added purple bordered by white. The shoulder is separated from the neck by a fine raised band. Below this band on the shoulder is an incised tongue pattern. The tongues beside the lower handle attachment are painted white, three to one side, two to the other.
