The other tongues are alternately painted purple, black or yellow in sets of threes. Three rotelles decorated with white dot rosettes are placed where the handle is attached to the rim of the vase.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS649
artifact.summary: Four figures in front of a Doric porch.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was recovered in excavations conducted under the auspices of the American Exploration Society in 1896 and 1897, from Tomb 72, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contributions to the excavations came from Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: The preserved fragments are worn and somewhat discolored.
artifact.decoration_description: Four figures in front of a Doric porch, possibly courting. A man and woman stand talking to one another on the left, and a man speaks to a seated woman on the right. The column and entablature of a Doric porch are visible behind the seated woman. The bearded man on the far left is leaning on a staff and gesturing toward his mouth with his right hand. The woman to whom he is speaking is holding a mirror in her left hand while her right hand imitates the gesture of the man. Both figures are wrapped in plain, black mantles. The couple on the right reach toward one another. The man, standing on the right, leans forward to reach toward the woman with his right arm, while the woman, seated on a folding stool, reaches out with both arms, palms upward. The man is wrapped in a mantle, while the woman wears a chiton and himation. The women's skin and the abacus of the column were painted white. White paint is also preserved on the upper edge of the entablature.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5706
artifact.summary: Maenad.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1928, 72-74; ARV2, 141, 160.
artifact.collection_history: The University Museum, Philadelphia, received the vase from Joseph Brummer.
artifact.condit: The lekythos is in good condition; there is some chipping of the surface along the mends.
artifact.decoration_description: Maenad. A maenad strides to the right carrying a snake and a thyrsos. She is looking back over her shoulder to the left. The snake in her left hand has wrapped itself around her lower arm. Her right hand, extended behind her, holds the thyrsos. She is barefoot and dressed in chiton and himation. On her head she wears a diadem with a large flower at the back.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5693
artifact.summary: Side A: Nike between two youths. Side B: Nike between a boy and a bearded man. Tondo: a pair of athletes leave the palaestra.
artifact.sources_used: Ashmead & Phillips 1976. CVA, U.S.A., University Museum, Philadelphia (forthcoming)
artifact.collection_history: The kylix was given to the University Museum by Henry C. Lea in 1931.
artifact.condit: All reserved areas are scratched and worn.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Nike between a youth and a bearded man. The Nike in the center may be arriving to announce a victory, judging by her running pose. She is moving to the right, wings extended, and looks back over her shoulder to the left. She wears a long chiton with elbow length sleeves, girdled to form a long overfall. Her lower legs are visible beneath the chiton. The Nike is carrying a narrow piece of cloth draped over each of her forearms and passing behind her back. In her spread hands are pairs of sticks (obeloi?) bound together; the bindings are faintly visible at intervals down their length. The youth on the left gestures spread-fingered toward the Nike. He is wrapped in a knee length cloak and is leaning on a staff. The bearded man on the right moves away from the Nike, turning back to look at her and extending his right arm toward her with flat palm, in greeting or in awe. He leans on a knobby staff tucked under his left armpit, and is wrapped in a long cloak which leaves his right shoulder free. All the figures have their heads slightly bowed to better fit on the side of the kylix.

Side B: Nike between two youths. The Nike flies in between the two youths, moving to the right. She looks over her shoulder to the left and holds up the edge of her chiton with her right hand, as if to lend her more speed. She is wearing a long soft chiton and a himation draped loosely over her left shoulder. She also wears a headband and an earring. The youth on the left looks toward the Nike, leaning on a knobby staff with his right hand, his left arm tucked under his robe. On the right the lower legs of a man are preserved. He faces the Nike, draped in a cloak and holding a staff.

Interior: a pair of athletes leave the palaestra. The youth on the left is moving to the left with his head turned back to the right toward his companion. He is carrying a garment over his left forearm, and has his right arm extended at his side. The athlete on the right is shown in profile to the left, and is carrying a diskos in a diskos bag in his left hand. He holds a strigil in his raised right hand. An aryballos hangs on the wall behind him, on the far right side of the scene.
artifact.shape_description: A Type B kylix with a very shallow bowl.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5688
artifact.summary: Side A: naked youth carrying an amphora. Side B: naked woman holding a ladle and skyphos.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1932-33b, 31, fig. 8, 9; ARV2, 170, 24
artifact.collection_history: The vase was given to the University Museum by Henry C. Lea.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is mottled, with much red showing on Side B and around the handles.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: naked youth carrying an amphora. The youth advances to the right, carrying a large storage amphora in his outstretched hands. The amphora is decorated with a garland of ivy leaves.

Side B: naked woman holding a ladle and skyphos. The woman is standing with her lower body facing right, her upper body twisted to frontal view and her head in profile to the left. Her right arm is behind her, the ladle held in her hand. She raises the skyphos to the right in her left hand. She wears a pendant necklace around her neck.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5682
artifact.summary: Side A: four youths. Side B: three boys.
artifact.other_bibliography: Burlington 1903, pl. 99, no. 85; Amyx 1958, pl. 52e; Bull. Vereen, 38, 61; Beazley 1927, 351; Dohan 1928, 72-73, figs. 82 and 83; Cook 1960, pl. 48a; Johnston 1979, 161, Type 14F no. 5; Anderson 1985, fig. 16; Beazley Addenda 2, 336.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by the University Museum, Philadelphia, from Sprink & Son, London.
artifact.condit: The krater is in excellent condition.
artifact.graffiti: A graffito inscribed on the bottom of the vase reads: *P*E*L*L*I*N*I*A *D*P*I *O*C*I*D*E*S *P*I *I *K*R*A*T*E*R*E*S *P*I, "16 pellenia, one drachma; six oxides, one obol; six kraters, four drachmae, three obols." Interpoints are composed of circles or arcs.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: four youths. The youths, all hunters carrying knobby sticks, are standing in various positions conversing. The youth on the left faces forward, but is looking toward the right where the others stand. His legs are crossed at the ankles and he supports his weight on the knobby stick in his left hand, his right hand on his hip. He is wearing a chlamys and a hat hangs behind his back; it is visible above his right shoulder. The youth second from the left stands facing the first youth but turns his head and leans back to the right to talk to the third youth. He holds his stick in his right hand and gestures with his left. He is wearing a chlamys and a soft pointed hat with a brim, a pilos. The third youth faces the youth in the pilos. He holds his stick in his lowered right hand and in his left hand holds a longer stick to which he has tied his catch, a rabbit. He wears a chlamys and a petasos. On the far right, the fourth youth stands on one leg, lifting his other leg with bent knee. He holds a stick in his right hand; his other hand is hidden under his chlamys. All the youths are barefoot and have hair falling to the top of their shoulders.

Side B: three boys conversing. The central boy and the boy on the right face one another, mouths parted as they speak. The central boy is completely wrapped in his mantle which bulges in back as if covering a pack. The boy on the right gestures with open palm toward his companion, his eyes closed. He is also wrapped in a mantle. The boy on the left faces forward but turns his head toward the other two, gesturing with his right hand which is covered by his mantle. All three wear white fillets in their hair.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS553
artifact.summary: Three friezes. Top: Gorgon's head between sphinxes and a lion. Middle: tripod between a pair of horsemen with panthers and a padded dancer. Bottom: eagle with displayed wings flanked by lions and a grazing stag.
artifact.other_bibliography: Payne 1931, 86 no 457, fig. 24B, pl. 20, 1-2; Dohan 1942, 99 no. 6, 101, pl. 53; Buschor 1943, 17; Benson 1953, 36, list 49.1, 120.469.; Kleinbauer 1964, 361 n. 42, 389; Banti EEA, 1214; Seeberg 1965, 7 no. 3; Sidorova 1967; Seeberg 1971, 16 no 12; Hopper 1974, 166, 197 (1)
artifact.collection_history: The alabastron was recovered in excavations conducted under the auspices of the American Exploration Society from 1896-97, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst. From Chamber Tomb 5.
artifact.condit: The glaze on the front of the vessel is badly flaked and worn, and there are chips on the rim and body and cracks on the underside of the disk. A small hole through the left ear of the gorgoneion may be ancient.
artifact.decoration_description:
Three friezes. Top: gorgoneion between sphinxes and a lion. The gorgoneion has incised locks, dots around the eyes and on the cheeks, spiral curls on the forehead and a red circle on the bottom lip of the grinning mouth. She is flanked by seated sphinxes with curled wings and tails. The maned lion, his mouth open, stands left behind the sphinx on the right (under the handle).

Middle: tripod between a pair of horsemen with panthers and a padded dancer. A small tripod with ring handles, situated beneath the gorgoneion in the top frieze, is flanked by mounted horsemen dressed in short, red chitons. The horses' manes are drawn with alternating red and black locks. A lion, its head turned frontal face, stands behind each horseman. A padded dancer follows the one on the right, facing left. He dances with his knees bent and one arm up and one arm down. He is bearded and has shoulder-length hair.

Bottom: eagle with displayed wings flanked by lions and a grazing stag. The eagle stands to the left, his head and neck stretched to the left. The lions stand open-mouthed, the one on the right followed by a grazing stag.

Rosettes incised with arcs at the edges and crossed blobs fill the space around the figures in these friezes.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5482
artifact.summary: A single frieze of animals between ornamental bands.
artifact.other_bibliography: Rambo 1919a, 8-9; Payne 1931, 61-64 no. 868, 156. 339. 341, pl. 28, 5; GVK 57, list 99.5a, 124.832; Loporto 1959/60, 164, no. 3; Amyx 1962, 6, no. 24; Amyx 1971, 30, no. 2.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1918.
artifact.condit: There are small chips in the rim and the lower half of the body. There are some salt deposits on the surface, and the surface of the handle is worn.
artifact.decoration_description: Continuous animal frieze. A siren with wings spread forms the focus of the frieze on one side, since all the animals turn towards her. The siren faces right and is shown with body and wings in three-quarters profile, head and tail in profile. Added red decorates her wings, tail and breast. She is flanked by griffin birds with curled wings. Panthers stand behind each of the birds. Opposite the siren is a lotus-palmette with an attached upright bud on each side. It is flanked by griffin birds with raised wings. Filling motifs of dots, blobs and small and large incised rosettes cover the field.
artifact.shape_description: A convex handleless pyxis with lid, having a depressed globular body on a wide conical foot.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS548
artifact.summary: Three animal friezes.
artifact.other_bibliography: Rambo 1919a, 8-9, fig. 2; Payne 1931, 298 no. 731; UPMB 1933, 163, pl. 7; Dohan 1942, 98, pl. 52 no. 3; Perachora II, 171
artifact.collection_history: The vase was recovered at Vulci in excavations sponsored by the American Exploration Society from 1896-97, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst. From Chamber Tomb 5
artifact.condit: The back of the vessel has lost most of its glaze. The rest is in fairly good condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Three animal friezes. Shoulder: duck flanked by lion, sphinxes, a panther and an owl. The duck, standing to the right, is flanked on the left by a lion and a sphinx, on the right by a panther, shown with its body in profile and its head frontal face, an owl and a sphinx.

Central: swan flanked by sphinxes, a lion and a panther. The swan stands with closed wings facing right, a sphinx with curled wings to either side. Behind the left sphinx is a lion, behind the right sphinx, a panther, its head turned frontal face. Under the handle is a feline flanked by a siren with displayed wings on the left and a grazing doe on the right.

Bottom: swan flanked by lion, grazing goat and grazing doe on the left, and by a panther, grazing goat and panther on the right. All the animals are shown in profile. The panthers are shown with heads frontal face.

Incised rosettes, dots, blobs and incised blobs fill the field in all the friezes. The bottom of the vase is reserved and painted with a black ray pattern. The neck and lip are glazed black. There are two white dot rosettes at the front of the trefoil mouth and one on the outer surface of the left rotelle. Six of the same are spaced evenly around the neck.
artifact.shape_description: Trefoil oinochoe with narrow foot.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5467
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles in combat with two Amazons<lb>Side B: combat between an Amazon and two warriors
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917b, 145-147; Borelli Bey 1913, pl. 19, Lot 221; von Bothmer 1957, pl. 38,2 and pl. 53.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora originally formed part of the Borelli Bey Collection. The University Museum, Philadelphia, purchased it from Canessa in 1916.
artifact.condit: The surface of the amphora is worn and pitted, with much erosion of the white paint.
artifact.comparanda: Compare the amphora New York 56.171.7 of the Bateman Group, and perhaps the shoulder-picture of the hydria Florence 3790 (no. 30).
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles in combat with two Amazons. Herakles, striding in from the left with drawn sword, has forced an Amazon to her knees. A second Amazon stands on the right behind her fallen friend, her shield up in a defensive position. Herakles, his left leg off the ground to show momentum, is gripping his sword in his right hand and appears to have grabbed the headpiece on the helmet of the fallen Amazon. The Amazon is down on her right knee facing right, with her upper body turned forward and her head turned toward Herakles on the left. She has raised her shield and spear, but the spear is pointed at Herakles' leg while his sword is very near her neck and breast. The second Amazon will not be able to help, since her spear is still held down at her side. The bearded Herakles is dressed in a short red chiton with a decorative border, over which is tied the lion's skin. Herakles wears the lion's head over his own head so that the upper jaw of the lion covers the top of his head and the mane falls around his neck. The lion's front paws are tied on Herakles' chest and the skin is held in place by a red belt around the waist. The Amazons, their skin painted white, are dressed similarly. Both wear short chitons and cuirasses with a spiral pattern over the breasts and helmets with long cheek pieces and high crescents on the top. Long locks of hair fall from beneath the helmets and there are fillets tied over them. A tripod decorates the shield of the fallen Amazon, and a meander pattern the shield of the second Amazon.

Side B: Combat between an Amazon and two warriors. An Amazon is being forced to her knees by the Greek warriors to her left and right. She has her head turned toward the warrior on the left and raises her shield on this side, but her weapon hand is empty. Both warriors, shields up, have raised their spears. The warrior on the left plunges his sword downward, his left knee up as he puts force behind the effort. The warrior on the right stands ready to back him up. Amazon and warriors are dressed almost identically in short chitons with wrapped, striped skirts over which is worn a black cuirass with spiral designs over the chest. Dagger sheaths project from their waists. Their helmets, with high crescent top pieces, are similar, with the cheek pieces on the warriors' helmets covering more of the face. The warriors also wear greaves. They carry oval shields decorated with star motifs, and the Amazon carries a round shield decorated with a tripod.
artifact.shape_description: Neck amphora. The amphora has quadruple handles.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5466
artifact.summary: Side A: Apollo and Artemis. Side B: Dionysos and a maenad.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917a, 20, 24-25; ARV2, 415, 39; Le Musee III, 432, pl. 63, 1; Farnsworth 1958, 169, pl. 36b; Farnsworth 1959, 248, fig. 9; Boardman 1979, 4, 35, fig. 4; Beazley Addenda 2, 265.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by the University Museum, Philadelphia, from Canessa in 1916.
artifact.condit: The vase is in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Apollo and Artemis. Apollo and Artemis stand on either side of a low altar, holding offerings. Artemis, on the left, faces the altar holding a bow and arrows in her left hand while she tips an oinochoe toward the altar with her right. She wears a chiton and himation and a diadem. Apollo stands to the right of the altar, facing forward but looking toward Artemis. His lyre is tucked under his arm and held against his body as he strums it with his left hand while pouring a libation from the phiale in his right. The pouring liquid has been painted with a thin white wash. Apollo wears a chiton and himation and has a laurel wreath around his head. The altar, topped with volutes, sits on a low base. There are eight strokes of thin red paint, some crossing one another, on the front of the altar.

Side B: Dionysos and a maenad. A maenad, carrying a snake and an oinochoe, rushes towards Dionysos, her long ringlets flying behind her. Dionysos stands facing her, holding a thyrsos in his left hand and a kantharos in his right. The maenad wears a long sleeved, low-belted chiton and a leopard skin, and has a headband over her hair. Her left arm, holding the snake, is held out toward Dionysos, while she swings the oinochoe behind her with her other hand. Dionysos faces the maenad, resting the thyrsos against his left shoulder and offering her the kantharos. He wears a wreath, chiton and mantle, and has long hair and a long beard. Both figures are barefoot.
artifact.shape_description: Neck amphora. The amphora has twisted handles.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5465
artifact.summary: Side A: Apollo at an altar. Side B: Artemis with quiver and oinochoe.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917a, 26-27; Matthews 1970, 6
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally belonged in the collection of Forman Taylor. In 1916 it was purchased from Canessa by the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase has suffered some discoloration, especially on Side B, where the reserved surface has also flaked and the glaze is mottled.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Apollo at an altar. Apollo is pouring a libation at the altar. He stands on the right. The altar is on the left. Although Apollo's body faces forward he has turned his head to the left. He holds a phiale over the altar in his outstretched right hand. His lyre is against his left shoulder, somehow supported as he fingers the strings. A fillet hangs from the side of the lyre. Apollo is dressed in a long chiton and a short mantle pinned at each shoulder. A fringed sash hangs down his left side, and he wears a crown of ivy. The low altar sits on a rectangular base and is decorated with Ionic volutes and a pattern of dentils.

Side B: Artemis with quiver and oinochoe. Artemis stands in three-quarters view to the left holding an oinochoe in her raised right hand. Her quiver projects above her left shoulder. She is wearing a chiton and himation and a sakkos.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5464
artifact.summary: Body: friezes of chariots and warriors. Neck, side A: six men mourning. Neck, side B: five women mourning.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917a, 15-28, fig. 2; Cook 1934-35, 167, 212; Cook 1947, 149, 153; Ahlberg 1971, pl. 58d; Tolle 1964, 19-20, no. 42; Betancourt 1969, 8-9, fig. 26 and 30; Fittschen 1969, pl. 1.; Wegner 1968a, 83 no. 134; Davison 1961, fig. 49; Rombos 1988, 99, 140, 374, no. 1, Table 15, 20 and 51
artifact.collection_history: The amphora originally formed part of the Borelli Bey Collection. It was purchased by the University Museum, Philadelphia, from Canessa in 1916.
artifact.condit: The surface of the amphora is worn, chipped and discolored.
artifact.decoration_description:
Mid-body: continuous frieze of chariots advancing to the right. Each chariot is pulled by a single horse and holds a bearded charioteer gripping the reins. There are six chariots represented.

Lower Body: continuous frieze of warriors. The warriors, wearing crested helmets, march to the right carrying round shields and two spears. Their torsos and arms are completely hidden by the shields.

Neck, side A: six men mourning. Six men move to the right, their right hands on their heads in a gesture of mourning, their left hands extended by their sides. They are dressed in chitoniskoi.

Neck, side B: five mourning women. The five women advance to the right, their hands on their heads in a gesture of mourning. They are dressed in long chitons and have the stylized, triangular torsos typical of Geometric figures.

Plastic snakes decorate the rim and handles of the vase.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5463
artifact.summary: Mistress and maid.
artifact.other_bibliography: Borelli Bey 1913, 23, no. 223; Luce 1917, 21-28; Luce 1919, 19-32; Beazley 1928a, 49; ARV2, 642, 118.
artifact.collection_history: The lekythos was part of the Borelli Bey Collection, which was dispersed in Paris in 1913. It was number 223 in the Borelli Bey sale catalogue. It was later purchased from Canessa in 1916 by the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The vase is worn; many of the details and much of the added white are now gone.
artifact.decoration_description: Mistress and maid. A woman is seated on a chair weaving a wreath while another woman stands holding a basket. The woman, or 'mistress,' on the left is shown in profile, sitting on a chair facing right. Her head is bent slightly as she concentrates on the unfinished wreath (or necklace) in her hands. She wears a chiton painted with white wash and a white himation, and has an additional piece of cloth wrapped under her bust and falling to mid-calf. She may also wear a wreath on her head. Her skin and himation are painted in added white. The woman, or 'maid,' on the right stands facing forward, her head turned toward the seated woman. Her right arm hangs at her side, and she holds a wide, flat basket in her left hand; white and black ribbons and fillets hang from the basket. The standing woman has short curly hair and wears a simple chiton which falls to mid-thigh. Beneath this she wears a crinkly, ankle-length tunic. Several objects hang on the wall behind the women. On the far left a pouch or sakkos hangs on the wall. A mirror hangs directly above the seated woman, and a lekythos hangs on the far right. There is a painted inscription above and between the two women.
artifact.inscriptions: The inscription above the figures reads: *D*I*F*I*L*O*S *K*A*L*O*S, Diphilos is beautiful.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5462
artifact.summary: Lid: marriage of Herakles and Hebe.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1916, 269-270; AJA 21, 1917, 455, fig. 1; Beazley 1928a, 6 n. 2; Schefold 1934, 59 no. 579
artifact.collection_history: The pyxis was purchased from Canessa in 1916.
artifact.condit: The surface of the pyxis is chipped and scratched, especially on the bottom and in the interior. The lid and exterior of the body are in good condition.
artifact.decoration_description: Marriage of Herakles and Hebe. The marriage is shown in a circular scene on the lid of the pyxis. The procession proceeds to the right, where Zeus is seated on a throne, Hera standing beside him. Beginning with the seated group, from right to left the characters are: an erotes, Zeus, Hera, Athena, a female torchbearer, an erotes, Herakles, Hebe, an erotes, and two female figures. Zeus and Hera face left, where the wedding procession approaches. Zeus is reclining with his left arm casually draped over the back of the throne, a long, striped staff held in his right hand. He wears a decorative mantle over his lower body. His upper body is bare. Hera stands beside him, leaning with her left arm resting on the other side of the throne back and holding a striped staff in her right hand. She wears a chiton with elaborate decoration on the hem and bodice. Both Hera and Zeus wear purple diadems. An erotes standing behind the throne also leans on its back, partially resting on Zeus' arm. A thymiaterion stands on the ground between the erotes and the throne. Athena is seated to the left of Zeus and Hera, her seat turned toward them but her head turned to watch the approach of the wedding procession. She wears a white bodice over her thin chiton, a crested helmet, bracelets, earrings and a bead necklace. She holds her spear resting against her left knee, and sits on a mantle draped over her seat. To her left stands a female figure facing left and holding two torches. She is wearing a thin chiton with a decorative bodice and a wide band around her hair. A large bird stands on the ground in front of her. The wedding party is led by an erotes carrying a torch. He lunges to the right but turns his head to watch Herakles and Hebe. Herakles is leading Hebe by the hand. He is naked but for a piece of cloth draped over his shoulders, and he carries his club in his left hand. Hebe walks beside him dressed in a white, ankle-length skirt and tunic with elaborate patterns done in added red-brown paint. She also wears a bracelet on each wrist and dangling earrings. An erotes flies behind her, lifting or adjusting her veil. A rectangular chest stands on the ground behind the erotes. Next come two girls, one carrying a box and a sash, the other a loutrophoros-hydria. Both wear thin chitons belted high, and turn to each other to chat as they walk. Behind the girl with the box stands another rectangular chest. The skin of Hebe and the three erotes is done in white paint.
artifact.shape_description: Type C pyxis. There is a bronze ring in the center of the lid.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS5409
artifact.summary: Head of a young woman.
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1929, 61-64; Dohan 1931c, 123-127, pl. 9; ARV2, 904, 113
artifact.collection_history: The vase was given to the University Museum, Philadelphia, by Mrs. Dillwyn Parrish.
artifact.condit: The vase is in very good condition. There are minor chips in the surface and some of the white paint has eroded.
artifact.decoration_description: Plastic head of a young woman. Her hair is glazed except for a fringe around her forehead and temples painted white and consisting of a quadruple row of tiny beading. An ivy garland is painted in added white over her hair. The woman's evenly arched eyebrows are painted black. Her eyes and irises are outlined in black and the whites of her eyes are painted white. Her pupils are reserved, as is the rest of her face.
artifact.shape_description: Plastic head of a young woman. The vessel neck and trefoil lip rise from the back of the woman's head. There is a high arched handle attached to the back.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4873
artifact.summary: Side A: warrior and grazing horse. Side B: archer and grazing horse.
artifact.other_bibliography: Hall 1913, 158-159; Beazley 1931-32, 2; Dohan 1933, 60, 66, 68; Technau 1936, 21 no. 6; Moore 1968, 358 no. 12; Korres 1970, pl. 13a; Robertson 1975, 132, pl. 36b and c; Bianchi 1976, 289; Boardman 1980a, fig. 297; Moon 1983, 128, fig. 9.3; Beazley 1986, pl. 69, 3-4; Beazley Addenda 2, 40.
artifact.collection_history: The vase fragments were excavated by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society in 1897, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The preserved pieces are in good condition, showing some loss of the added white paint. The horse on side A is scratched.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: warrior and grazing horse. The bearded warrior stands on the right, in profile to the left. He is partially hidden behind his shield, which is decorated at center with a large, black bird. He holds a spear in his left hand and a javelin in his right, and wears a garment mostly obscured by his shield, but decorated with rosettes, swastikas and red dots, and a helmet with a ram's head cheekpiece. The horse stands on delicate legs to the warrior's left, head down toward the center. His mane is incised.

Side B: archer and grazing horse. An archer and his horse stand facing one another. The archer stands in profile on the right while the horse grazes on the left. The archer is dressed in Scythian clothing—a pointed cap and a tight garment which covers him from neck to ankle. The garment is decorated with stripes, zig-zags, meanders, swastikas, stars, circles and rosettes. The archer has a pointed beard and is barefoot. His quiver hangs at his side, and he holds the horse's reins in one hand. The horse is poorly preserved. It stands facing right with head down as if grazing.
artifact.shape_description: Type A amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4862
artifact.summary: Main Panel: warrior mounting chariot and three onlookers. Shoulder: two horsemen, two women and a warrior. Predella: three horsemen and three warriors.
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1931-32, 9 n. 5.
artifact.collection_history: The hydria fragments were recovered in 1897 in excavations by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society, and became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: Portions of the vase are in excellent condition, while other fragments are worn, discolored and pitted.
artifact.decoration_description:
Main Panel: warrior mounting chariot and three onlookers. The two horses drawing the chariot occupied the central foreground of the scene. Most of this part of the vase is lost, and only the tails and part of the heads of the horses are preserved. The charioteer is mounting his chariot on the far left, his right toes just leaving the ground, and his hands holding the reins. He has short hair and wears a short chiton, a cuirass, and greaves, and is carrying his shield on his back. A second male figure stands almost beside him in the background. He is naked and stands in profile to the right, turning his head to the left to look at the charioteer and gesturing with his raised left hand. A woman stands in front of him facing right holding a flower in her raised right hand. She is dressed in a sleeveless peplos decorated with a dotted checkerboard pattern. On the far right, a third male figure stands at the horses' heads, facing left and holding a spear. He is only partially preserved, but appears to be naked.

Shoulder: two horsemen, two women, and a warrior. The horsemen ride in from each end of the scene carrying long spears. They are short-haired youths dressed in short, short-sleeved chitons with white bands or skirts around their hips. The athlete in the center of the scene is only partially preserved. He is standing with legs spread wide, his arms cocked. Young women stand on either side of him holding spears. Each wears a black peplos with red overfolds, and red fillets around their long, black hair.

Predella: three horsemen and three warriors. Two warriors are engaged in combat, their swords drawn, while a third strides in from the right, his spear and shield held ready. Each is dressed for battle, in greaves, cuirass and helmet. Youths on horseback again frame the scene, riding in from the right and left carrying spears (the rider on the left carries two spears). The tail and hindquarters of the horse of a third rider are preserved to the right of the horseman on the left. There is extensive use of added red and white on the vase.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4861
artifact.summary: Side A: mule and three satyrs. Side B: satyrs eating grapes.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was excavated by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The preserved portions of the vase are in good condition, with some discoloration occurring.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: mule and three satyrs. The beleaguered mule brays in distress as a satyr pushes down his head and two others sit astride his back. The standing satyr bends over, pushing at the mule's head with both hands. The satyr sitting astride the center of the mule's back, having had too much to drink, sits slumped forward, a kantharos in the hand hanging by his side. A third satyr sits astride the rump of the mule facing backward and leaning forward to hold on either side of the mule's tail. All three satyrs have long hair and beards and pointed ears, but appear to lack tails.

Side B: satyrs eating grapes. Much of this scene is missing, but parts of two satyrs are preserved in a vineyard. A tall grape vine grows from the ground left of center, the twisted vines extending to the right, where bunches of grapes hang. A satyr stands to the left of the vine, eating from a clump of grapes. A second satyr sitting or kneeling in the center of the scene is just about to put a grape in his mouth. The tail of a third satyr may be identified on the lower right.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora?

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4856
artifact.summary: Ray pattern and pomegranate chain.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1932-33b, 61-63, fig. 1; Kunze 1934, 100, n. 1; Lane 1933-34, 135, n. 4; Greenewalt 1966, 62-63, 66, pl. 1.Y; Stibbe 1972, 275, n. 116; Greenewalt 1973, pl. 13.1 right; Pinney & Ridgway 1979, 122-123, no. 58
artifact.collection_history: The vase was found in 1897 during excavations at Orvieto led by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society. It subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The preserved fragments are in good condition, having suffered minor discoloration.
artifact.decoration_description: Ray pattern and pomegranate chain. The belly of the vase is reserved, creating the effect of a wide red band. Fine, black double lines set this off on either side. The lower part of the vase to the foot is painted white with a black radiating ray pattern. The foot and base are black glaze. A white band has been painted at the top of the body extending part way over the shoulder. It is decorated with a pomegranate chain and is set off with thin black bands. A white band decorated with black vertical zig-zags and outlined with black lines decorates the bottom of the neck. The upper part of the neck is painted black and is outlined with white on the bottom edge.
artifact.shape_description: The vessel has a narrow foot set on a wide base, a round but slightly tapered body, and a short cylindrical neck ending in a flaring, flat rim.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4853
artifact.summary: Main panel: quadriga led by Hermes. Lower frieze: two pairs of confronted goats and panthers. Shoulder frieze: hoplites.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1920, 59, fig. 36
artifact.collection_history: The vase was excavated by A. L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society in 1897 and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: Some of the preserved fragments are discolored and chipping has occurred around the cracks.
artifact.decoration_description:
Main Panel: quadriga led by Hermes. The upper left portion of the panel is missing, so that only a small part of the charioteer is preserved. The bottom of his red chiton and white mantle can be seen just above the chariot wheels. He carries a spear. The two pairs of horses are drawn so close together that there almost appear to be two horses rather than four. A bearded male figure stands behind the horses. His shoulders and the lower part of his beard are preserved above the backs of the rear horses. Hermes stands at the heads of the horses and is partially hidden behind them. He is dressed in his winged boots and chlamys. His head is not preserved.

Lower Frieze: two pairs of confronted goats and panthers. In both pairs the panther stands on the left and the goat on the right, the goat with his head lowered.

Shoulder Frieze: hoplites. Most of the frieze is not preserved, but portions of four figures marching in the left can be seen on the far right. Two are armed hoplites, the third is a naked youth, and the last is a bearded man in a mantle.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4852
artifact.summary: Side A: horseman & onlookers. Neck: two male figures. Side B: five figures around a tripod. Neck: footrace. Under the handles: Pegasus and the Chimaera.
artifact.other_bibliography: Mommsen 1975, pls. 6. 578, no. 49; LIMC, III, pl. 206, Chimaira 89; Beazley Addenda 2, 62
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was recovered in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham in 1987, under the auspices of the American Exploration Society, and became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The amphora is worn and pitted.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: horseman and four standing men. A mounted rider occupies the center of the scene, with two male figures standing to either side. The horse and rider are at rest, facing toward the right. Only the right arm and the right side of the male rider are preserved. He wears a short-sleeved, short red chiton with a black border. Of the horse the hindquarters, the two front legs, the outline of the chest, and its face are preserved. It is painted black with red markings on the rump and incised details. To the left of the horse and rider stands an older man carrying a spear and gesturing toward the rider with one hand. He is bearded and wears his hair long and bound with a fillet, and he is dressed in a long red chiton and a black mantle decorated with red dots and white rosettes. On the far left stands a second man whose head is not preserved. He is dressed identically to the first man, carries a spear, and raises his left hand in the same gesture. A third man stands to the right of the horse and rider. His body faces forward, although he appears to be moving toward the right while looking back toward the rider on the left. His right arm is bent in an awkward downwards gesture and he carries a spear in his right hand. The man is bearded and has long hair bound with a fillet. He wears a long black chiton with red dots and a red mantle. The man on the far right is preserved from his abdomen downward. He stands facing right in a wide legged stance, balancing himself as he leans forward slightly. He holds a large ring, about the size of a diskos, in his right hand. His left hand is held up at chest height, palm downward. A bird flying to the left above the horse's hindquarters completes the scene.

Side B: five figures around a tripod. Three men stand to the right and two to the left of a large tripod vessel, of which only the three legs are preserved. Only the feet and lower legs of the two most central figures are preserved. The figure on the left faces the tripod, while the man on the right turns away. Both wear long chitons; the edge of a mantle on the left figure is also preserved. The figure on the far left is preserved from the chest up. He faces the center of the scene, carrying a staff and dressed in a chiton. He is bearded and wears his hair falling down his back and bound in a fillet. The figure second from the right runs toward the tripod. His forward arm is not preserved. He is bearded and has long hair bound in a fillet, and wears a short black chiton and a black mantle decorated with red dots. The man on the far right walks toward the center holding a spear. He is also bearded and has his long hair bound with a fillet, and he wears a long chiton and mantle. A bird flies to the left behind him.

Handles: under the handle to the right of Side A is the Chimaera. A Pegasus stands under the handle to the left.

Neck, Side A: the entire center of the neck is missing, but two male figures are partially preserved on the right and left sides next to the handles. The figure on the left stands in profile to the right, holding a spear in his right hand and gesturing with his raised left hand. He is bearded and has long hair, and is dressed in a long, red chiton and a black mantle decorated with red dots and white rosettes. The figure on the right is preserved from the knee down. He faces right and is dressed in a long red chiton and a black mantle.

Neck, Side B: footrace. Two bearded male figures dressed in chitons and mantles look on as two nude males race to the right. The two central figures are depicted with wide-spread, bent legs to show that they are running. The cape flying behind the right, central figure also indicates motion. The upper bodies of the runners are not preserved. The figures watching may be judges or spectators.
artifact.shape_description: Type I neck amphora. Ovoid in shape.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4851
artifact.summary: Sides A and B: eyes and grape clusters.
artifact.other_bibliography: Böhlau 1900, 56, fig. 16; Hall 1913, 155
artifact.collection_history: The kylix was recovered in 1897 in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society. It subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface is chipped and somewhat discolored. Most of the white paint is intact.
artifact.decoration_description:
Sides A and B: eyes and grape clusters. Large eyes topped by eyebrows decorate each side. Between them is a 'nose,' a vertical red slash (flame?) atop a double volute capital. Clusters of grapes hang on vines next to the handles. The stems of the vines on sides A and B cross under the handles.

Interior: the inside of the kylix is glazed black with a central reserved circular area.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4842
artifact.summary: Tondo: seated youth writing on a tablet.
artifact.sources_used: Ashmead & Phillips 1976; CVA, U.S.A., University Museum, Philadelphia (forthcoming).
artifact.other_bibliography: Hall 1913, 156-157 fig. 134; Beazley 1918, 46; Luce 1921, 81 no. 80; Beazley 1925, 96; ARV2, 157, 65; Boardman 1979, 34, fig. 3; Beazley Addenda 2, 200.
artifact.collection_history: The kylix was excavated/collected by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society in 1896-1897 and became part of the University Museum's collection in 1897. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavation came from John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The kylix has been reconstructed from numerous pieces. The reserved surface is worn, scraped, and chipped. Damage is more severe at the fractures.
artifact.decoration_description: Interior: seated youth writing on a tablet. The youth sits on a low stool facing right. He is shown in profile and is dressed in a himation which leaves his right arm and shoulder uncovered. A faded wreath rests on his head. The young man gingerly holds a stylus which he is using to write on the folding tablet on his lap. To his right is part of a chest which may be for storing scrolls. There are nonsense inscriptions, one of them retrograde, in the field around him.
artifact.inscriptions: A nonsense inscription in the field around the youth is composed of unrecognizable characters.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4841
artifact.summary: Side A: Kitharode and two seated men<lb>Side B: Kitharode
artifact.other_bibliography: Hall 1913, 152, fig. 2; Beazley 1931-32, 2, no. 1
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was found in excavations at the site of Orvieto in Italy in 1897. Excavations were conducted by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society. The vase became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The amphora is somewhat worn and pitted, with large sections missing.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: kitharode and two seated men. A man stands playing the kithara, while two men sit listening. The kitharode stands in profile to the right, holding his kithara upright against his shoulder, having just played or getting ready to play. He is dressed in a red chiton and wears a long, black, sleeveless tunic which drapes down his front and back, leaving the sides open. He is bearded and wears a red fillet over his hair. The man seated on a stool to the left is wrapped in a red and black striped mantle, his arms at his sides. He wears a red fillet and has a red beard. The second man is seated on a stool to the right, his hands resting on his knees. He is wrapped in a short black striped mantle and has a black beard. His face and the top of his head are missing. All three men are barefoot.

Side B: kitharode. A kitharode stands in profile to the right, playing his kithara, the fingers of his left hand splayed across the strings. He is bearded and barefoot, and wears a black chiton and a mantle with broad stripes of red and black. His head is crowned with a laurel wreath. The laurel wreath, the upper bridge of the kithara, the kitharode's beard and the red stripes of his mantle are painted in added red. The top part of the kithara is white. White is used on both sides A and B to outline the features and clothes of the figures.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4834
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos, maenad and goat. Side B: Athena arming.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was found in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham in 1897 under the auspices of the American Exploration Society, and became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The preserved portions of the vase are in good condition, with some pitting and wear, especially on the areas painted white.
artifact.comparanda: London B 70 (See CVA, British Museum 68, 3a)
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos, maenad and a goat. Dionysos and the maenad stand facing one another, the long-horned goat between them and partially hidden behind Dionysos' mantle. Dionysos, on the left, holds up a kyathos in his left hand and reaches toward the maenad with his right. She is leaning away, her weight on her back right foot, and her head bent forward. She holds an unidentified object in her right hand, and holds her left hand at her chest. Dionysos is bearded and has a fillet bound over his long hair, and he wears a long white chiton and a black mantle. The maenad is wearing a long black chiton, an animal skin draped diagonally, and a short cape. A wreath of grape leaves sits atop her head, and her long hair falls down her back. A grape vine springs from the ground by Dionysos' feet. It grows behind and around him and continues along the top of the scene, with some of the vines falling between the two figures.

Side B: Athena arming. Athena and a handmaiden stand facing one another. Athena, on the left, is helmeted and holds a long staff in her left hand. The rest of her body is not preserved, but a shield can be seen resting behind her on the left. The maid helping Athena holds her shield ready. She is wearing a black garment and wears her hair long, one tendril falling in front of her shoulder.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4833
artifact.summary: Side A: warrior leaving home. Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was recovered in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham in 1897 under the auspices of the American Exploration Society. It subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is worn, chipped and discolored.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: warrior leaving home. The partially preserved scene shows a two-horse chariot to the left, two warriors, a child and two women. At least three additional figures stand behind the chariot, the central one wearing greaves and turned to the right- possibly the departing warrior. The other two figures face him. The one on the left, probably a female, wears an ankle-length chiton. The man on the right wears a chiton and mantle which fall to mid-calf. There may be a fourth figure to the left of the woman. Better preserved are the figures on the far left and right. A woman stands at the horses' heads, her right hand on the shoulder of the boy standing in front of her, a flower(?) clasped in her left hand. A warrior wearing a short chiton, crested Corinthian helmet, cuirass and greaves stands on the far left. A similarly dressed warrior stands to the right of the chariot facing left. A woman stands beside him on the far left. Both she and the woman on the left wear fillets and ankle-length chitons decorated with a circle-filled checkerboard pattern, the same pattern found on the dress of the woman behind the chariot.

Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur. Theseus and the Minotaur struggle in the center of the scene, while a woman (Ariadne?) and four men stand by. Theseus, on the left, has the upper hand in the struggle. He has grabbed the Minotaur around the shoulders with his left arm and is forcing him to the ground. He may already have delivered the death blow. The Minotaur is dropping to one knee, his head against Theseus' chest. Theseus is bearded and wears a short chiton and a cuirass. The Minotaur is naked. The female figure, perhaps Ariadne, stands to the left of Theseus facing the combatants, arms at her sides. She is wearing a long, red and black short-sleeved chiton belted at the waist and a wreath over her hair. Behind her stands a young man wrapped in a red and black mantle. His arms are hidden under the mantle. Three more youths stand to the right of the Minotaur. The one nearest the struggle is almost identical to the youth on the left; he is wrapped in a red and black mantle which hides his arms. The partially preserved youth behind him wears a fillet over his hair. He is either naked or dressed in a short garment, for his legs are bare. The youth on the far right is again wrapped in a red and black mantle. All three draped youths appear to wear red caps. Theseus wears a black one.
artifact.shape_description: Type A amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4832
artifact.summary: Side A: concert. Side B: Amazonomachy with wheeling chariot.
artifact.other_bibliography: Hall 1913, 148, 150; von Bothmer 1957, pl. 57,4; Böhr 1982, pl. 178a-b; Beazley Addenda 2, 84.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was found in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham in 1897 under the auspices of the American Exploration Society and became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: Some of the fragments are discolored, while others are worn. A few of the fragments are in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: concert. Two standing musicians play for two seated men. The two musicians play facing one another in the center of the scene. The musician on the right is only partially preserved and his instrument in missing. He wears a long chiton and mantle. The fat musician on the left is playing a flute, standing with swayed back and bulging stomach. He wears a long, white, sleeveless chiton. The other two men sit on stools facing the concert. The man seated on the left is better preserved. He is leaning on a staff with his left hand while gesturing with his right, and is wearing a piece of striped fabric draped around his waist and over his lap, and a fillet over his hair. The seated man on the right appears to have echoed him in pose and dress. All four men have short hair.

Side B: Amazonomachy with wheeling chariot. A warrior in a four-horse chariot chases an Amazon. The chariot travels from the left, its driver on the far left. He is holding a spear and is bending forward at the waist so that his face is hidden behind the head of the first horse. He wears a short, sleeveless, white chiton with borders around the arm and neck holes, and a chlamys. A bird flies behind the warrior. The Amazon on the far right is running from the chariot carrying a small shield and looking back over her shoulder in fear. A dog runs with her, partially hidden behind her right, rear foot. She wears a helmet and greaves, and a short garment with a dotted skirt. She also has a piece of cloth wrapped around her shoulders and hanging free on her left side. Between the two figures the horses are spread out, each rearing up so that their front legs are off the ground. The horses on the left and right turn their heads to the right, while those in the center are shown frontal face.
artifact.inscriptions: There is a pot mark on the bottom of the amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS4082
artifact.summary: Girl with wool basket.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was excavated in 1893 from a tomb in Attica, near Athens. Dr. R.H. Lamborn purchased it in 1894, and subsequently gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: There is some chipping of the glaze on the lip and neck, and the black glaze used to draw the girl is somewhat worn.
artifact.decoration_description: A girl with a wool basket. A girl is seated in front of her wool basket holding out an ivy wreath which she may just have completed. She is on the left side of the scene, the basket on the right. She has long black hair and is dressed in a chiton and himation. Her chair has a high, slightly curved back. Two spindles and some wool protrude from the basket. There is an undulating snake above the scene.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS405
artifact.summary: Tongue pattern, black bands and rays.
artifact.other_bibliography: FR, 256 no. 12; Bates 1907, 155-157, pl. 40; Bates 1909, 209; Luce 1921, 62 no. 43; Webster 1928, 198, fig. 4; Price 1928, 34; Hemelrijk 1956, 75, 121; Langlotz 1975, pl. 61.3; Isler 1981, 235-236; Isler 1983, 16; Hemelrijk 1984, 59, 152, 182-183 no. A1, pls. 21a, 155.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was collected by Tewfik Pasha, Khedive of Egypt. After his death it was sold in Constantinople. It was purchased by H.V. Hilprecht for the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1896. It was reported to have come from the Greek islands, but this is not likely.
artifact.condit: The vase is in excellent condition, with only minor chipping and discoloration.
artifact.comparanda: There is a vase of the same type in the Sammlung Ludwig, now in Basel (Berger & Lullies 1979: 173-174 no. 65).
artifact.decoration_description: Tongue pattern, black bands and rays. The neck of the vase is glazed black with the rim reserved. A small, round molding separates the neck from the shoulder. Pendant rays decorate the shoulder of the vase. A series of wheel-painted black bands decorate the body of the vase, beginning just under the handles. There is a small, round molding at the juncture of the foot and body. A long tongue pattern covers the foot and base. The tongues are outlined in black glaze and alternately filled with purple and white.
artifact.shape_description: Neck amphora. Ovoid body with tall flaring foot, a tall narrow neck and vertical strap handles.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS403
artifact.summary: Side A: pentathalon scene with three figures<lb>Side B: boxing contest with four figures
artifact.date_description: Date was listed as "late 6th c."
artifact.collection_history: The vase was collected by Tewfik Pasha, Khedive of Egypt. After his death it was sold in Constantinople. In 1896 in was purchased by H.V. Hilprecht for the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: Irregular firing has left the black glazed areas red in spots; see the left figure on side B and the third figure from the left on side A. The vase shows some wear and small gouges; the white paint on the diskos is particularly worn.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: pentathalon scene with three figures. The naked and bearded athlete on the left, an acontist, faces right holding two javelins upright in his left hand, his right hand on his hip. The central athlete, who is also naked and bearded, again faces right, swinging a large, white diskos, his weight back on his right leg as he gets ready to throw. His left arm is raised in the air for balance. The right-hand figure, probably the trainer, is bearded and wears a long cloak which is fastened on his left shoulder, leaving his right arm and shoulder bare. He is facing the two athletes, and holds a long stick.

Side B: boxing contest with four figures. In the center of the scene are two naked, bearded men, fists raised against each other. Both men wear himantes around their fists and little caps. To their left is a bearded man, fully clothed, who faces right and holds a stick toward them; he may be their trainer. On the right, a nude, beardless youth faces left toward the contest; he is wearing a band around his head and holds a bunch of himantes in his right hand. The hair and beards of the figures are painted red.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS401
artifact.summary: Side A: lion<lb>Side B: grazing deer
artifact.other_bibliography: Hall 1914b, 218-222, figs. 109-110; Hall 1915b, 77; Luce 1921, 63 no. 42; Rumpf 1921, 166 no. 25, pl. 9A; Smith 1931, 105; Pinney & Ridgway 1979, 128-129 no. 61; Iozzo 1986, 15 no. 9
artifact.collection_history: The vase was collected by Tewfik Pasha, Khedive of Egypt. After his death it was sold in Constantinople. In 1896 it was purchased by H.V. Hilprecht for the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: Unpainted areas on the exterior of the vase are worn away leaving painted areas noticeably raised. Only a few small patches of original unpainted surface remain. The red paint has mostly flaked away.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: lion. The lion strides to the right open-mouthed. Its tail is curved in a figure eight above its back, and there is a small rosette under its belly.

Side B: grazing deer. A doe faces left, head to the ground. There is an incised rosette under its belly and one over its neck.

The neck of the vase is decorated with interlocked lotus buds and flowers.
artifact.shape_description: Small neck amphora with echinus foot. There are fillets at the join of base to body and shoulder to neck.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS398
artifact.summary: Side A: Body: doe mauled by panthers; shoulder: grazing rams and a waterbird<lb>Side B: Body: sphinxes to either side of a palmette floral complex; Shoulder: grazing goats and an owl
artifact.other_bibliography: FR, 256 no. 11; Furtwängler, Kleine-Schriften II, 497 no. 11; Hall 1914a, 226-229, figs. 114-115; Luce 1921, 59 no. 39; Rumpf 1921, 185; Smith 1931, 105.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was collected by Tewfik Pasha, Khedive of Egypt. After his death it was sold in Constantinople. In 1896 it was purchased by H.V. Hilprecht for the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is chipped and badly worn, and most of the red and white paints have flaked away.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A, body: doe mauled by panthers. A doe, standing to the right, is being attacked by panthers on either side. The panther on the left has attacked its hindquarters, biting and holding on with its front paws. The panther on the right attacks the front, grabbing the doe around the chest and biting at the back of its neck; shoulder: grazing rams and a waterbird. The waterbird, its wings spread, stands in the center facing left, its head turned to face forward. A ram stands to either side, head to the ground.

Side B, body: sphinxes to either side of a palmette floral complex. Seated sphinxes with curled wings flank a large palmette floral complex with lotus bud tendrils; shoulder: grazing goats and an owl. The owl stands in the center facing right, its head turned to face forward. It is flanked by bearded goats standing with heads to the ground.
artifact.painter: Group of the Amphora in Leipzig

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS3498
artifact.summary: Sides A and B: two frontal horsemen (Dioskouroi?)
artifact.other_bibliography: Furtwängler, Kleine-Schriften II, 498, no. 19; Hall 1913, 149-151; Schauenburg 1963a, 426 n. 42, 430, fig. 13
artifact.collection_history: Gift of John Wanamaker to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface is chipped and flaking, especially around the mends.
artifact.decoration_description: Sides A and B are virtually identical. The horses and horsemen stand side-by-side facing forward, their heads turned toward one another. The horsemen on Side A are young and unbearded. The youth on the right is crowned with a laurel wreath. His companion wears a simple red band over his hair, and his brow is furrowed. The preserved horseman on Side B is bearded and he wears a red fillet. Both men and youths wear short-sleeved tunics. The manes and tails of the horses are done in added red paint. They wear simple bridles.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS3497
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and the Nemean Lion<lb>Side B: Dionysos and Ariadne.
artifact.other_bibliography: FR, 257, no. 18; Hall 1915b, 85-90, figs. 65-66; Luce 1917b, 155, no. 4; Luce 1921, 98-99 no. 110; Beazley 1928a, 31; Clement 1955, 9 n. 15; Boardman 1978, 14 n. 17.
artifact.collection_history: Gift of John Wanamaker to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: Some of the fragments are in excellent condition. Others are very worn and discolored and have lost most of the added white paint.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles and the Nemean Lion. Herakles grapples with the lion while Athena and Iolaos look on. Herakles, shown naked on the left, has grabbed the upper jaw of the lion and is wrestling him to the ground. He is pushing forward and down on the lion's head so that his legs are bent and his body parallel to the ground. The lion's tongue hangs from his open mouth as his head is forced to the ground, and he can be reconstructed as pushing at Herakles' head with his left hind paw. Athena stands to the right behind Herakles holding her shield and spear. She is wearing a short-sleeved chiton decorated with a circle-filled criss-cross pattern with meander patterns and squiggles bordering sleeves, neck and hem. Her shield is decorated with a Gorgon's head. Iolaos is standing behind the lion on the right holding Herakles' club and gesturing in excitement with his left hand. He is facing right, but has turned his head to look back at Athena on the left. His upper body is naked (his lower body is not preserved) and he is shown with a full beard and short, curly hair.

Side B: Dionysos and Ariadne. Dionysos and Ariadne face one another in the center of the scene while a satyr and maenad dance. The satyr dances behind Ariadne and the maenad behind Dionysos. Ariadne, on the left, is shown in profile to the right holding her twins, Oinopion and Staphylos, the children of Dionysos. Although the upper part of the figure is missing, the dangling feet of the twins can be seen hanging by Ariadne's waist. Ariadne is wearing a chiton decorated with panels of red and black scale patterns on the side and a meander band on the hem. Dionysos, facing her on the right, wears a chiton and a full mantle colored red and black. He is holding a large grape vine in his left hand and a kantharos in his right. Only the lower legs and raised arms of the dancing satyr on the left are preserved. The maenad on the right is shown facing forward but with her head turned toward Dionysos on the left. She has one foot off the ground as she dances with arms bent and held out to either side of her body. Her clothing is almost identical to Athena's on Side A.
artifact.inscriptions:
The inscriptions on side A read, above Herakles: &epig-rough;*E*R*A*K[*L*E*S], Herakles; to the right of Athena: *A*Q*E[*N]*A*S, Athena; to the left of Athena in a vertical position written retrograde: [.......]*E*S*K*A*L*O*S, possibly Eskalos is beautiful; and to the right of the standing male in a vertical position: *I*O*L*E*O*S, Iolaos.

On side B the inscriptions read, to the right of the left-hand figure in a vertical position: [*O*I*N*O*P*I]*O*N, Oinopion, and to the right of Dionysos written vertically: *D*I*O[*N*U*S]*O*S, Dionysos.
artifact.shape_description: Type A amphora

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS3442
artifact.summary: Side A: death of Achilles. Side B: death of Antilochos.
artifact.other_bibliography: Bates 1904, 45-50, pl. 1 and 2; AA 1904, 225; Hall 1915b, 85-93; Rumpf 1927, 135; Beazley 1931-32, 1-22; Dohan 1935a, pl. 8; Technau 1936, 21 no. 5, pl. 23; Beazley 1951, 68-69, pl. 30; Scherer 1963, 100; Bugner 1976, 144, fig. 155; Schefold 1978, figs. 326-327; Moore 1980, pl. 53, fig. 12; LIMC, I, pl. 321, Aithiopes I, pl. 666, Antilochos I, 30; Moon 1983, 90 figs. 6.4a-b, 132, fig. 9.6a-b; von Bothmer 1985, 31, fig. 19; Beazley 1986, pl. 69, 1-2; Beazley Addenda 2, 40..
artifact.collection_history: The vase was excavated by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society and became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The vase is somewhat worn, and has lost much of the added red and white paint.
artifact.decoration_description:
The scenes on both the obverse and reverse depict episodes from the Aethiopis. Side A: the struggle over the body of the dead Achilles. The scene is enacted by four figures. The foreign Amasos struggles with Menelaos on the left, while a warrior attempts to lift the dead Achilles on the right. The warrior straddles the body of Achilles, his weight on his forward, right leg as he bends over to lift Achilles, supporting his neck with one arm while he pulls him up by one of his wrists. His cape, decorated with a snake and a panther, flies out behind him. He also wears greaves, a short tunic or chiton, and upper body armor decorated with spirals. Achilles lies in profile, face upward and head to the right. His head tips back as he is lifted, and his helmet falls behind him. He is dressed in greaves, spiral leggings, a short tunic decorated with meanders and stars in a checkerboard pattern, an undergarment with a pleated hip skirt decorated with incised stripes, and a black cape elaborately decorated with rosettes and a meander border. On the left, Amasos struggles with Menelaos, leaning away from him to the left, his legs already buckling under him as he bleeds from a chestwound. He holds a club in his right hand and is looking at Menelaos. Menelaos lunges at Amasos, legs spread wide, holding his spear in his raised right arm and his shield in his left. Amasos has Negroid hair and features, and is naked but for a small cape around his neck which is decorated with a zig-zag pattern. Menelaos is wearing greaves, spiral leggings, a short-sleeved tunic with a meander border and a helmet. His shield is white and is decorated with a dog at its center. Amasos, Menelaos and Achilles are labelled.

Side B: the rescue of the body of Antilochos. Large sections of this side are missing, but the scene appears to have involved five figures. The dead Antilochos lies along the bottom of the scene, his head to the left and his arms at his sides, palms down. He has a red beard and wears a white tunic, red greaves, and a short fringed garment. On the left, two naked male figures run away from the fallen Antilochos, their speed indicated by their wide spread legs and their forward feet, which are off the ground. They are pursued by two helmeted warriors carrying spears and shields. The shield of the foremost of the two superposed warriors is white with a bird in the center. The back shield is black with a red border. Antilochos is labelled, as is one of the figures on the right, Euphorbos.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: above the figure on the far left, *A*M*A*S*O*S, Amasos; above the third figure from the left, *M*E*N*E*L*A*O*S, Menelaos; above the fallen warrior, written retrograde, [*A*X]*I*L*E*O*S, Achilles. Side B: above the fallen warrior, written retrograde, *A*N*T*I*L*I*K*O*S, Antilochos; on the upper right, *E*U*F*O*R*B*O*S, Euphorbos.
artifact.shape_description: Type A amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS3441
artifact.summary: Side A: birth of Athena. Side B: assembly of gods; perhaps the introduction of Herakles to Olympos.
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1931-32, 10, no. 9; Clement 1955, 9-10, pl. 6; Korres 1970, pl. 81a; LIMC, II, pl. 746, Athena 367; Mertens 1983, figs. 7-8; Beazley Addenda 2, 77.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was excavated by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society and became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations was provided by John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The vase is in generally good condition; some of the white paint has eroded.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side ABirth of Athena. Athena, not yet full size, stands on Zeus' lap while five other deities gather around. Zeus, seated on a throne in the center of the scene, reaches toward Athena with one hand while holding a stylized thunderbolt in his other hand. He is shown in profile to the right, his feet resting on a low stool. Zeus is bearded and is dressed in a striped chiton, a plain red himation with a decorative border, and a short, black mantle decorated with rosettes and draped over both shoulders. He wears a headband over his long hair. The throne has a ram's head on the visible end of the backrest. There is a small, winged Nike beneath the throne; she raises her left arm palm upward. Athena is standing on Zeus' lap facing right. Although small in stature, she is fully dressed and is armed with helmet, shield and spear. A bird flies away from her to the right. Eileithyia stands in front of Athena, facing her and touching her right hand to her chin, her other hand held out toward Athena, palm upward. She is dressed in chiton and himation, and also wears a band around her head. Ares stands at the far right, facing the central figures. He is mostly hidden by the large shield which he holds. It is decorated with a star motif at its center and scales around the outside. Ares wears helmet and greaves. His dog hides behind his legs. Apollo stands behind Zeus' throne on the left, holding his kithara and dressed in a white chiton, over which he wears a striped himation. His kithara is held in his left arm while he plays with his right. His hair is long and is worn in a headband, with long, thin braids in front of his ears. Another male figure stands beside Apollo and is mostly hidden by him. He is dressed in chiton and himation, and holds his right hand, palm open, at his waist. A bird flies to the left above him. There are nonsense inscriptions between the figures.

Side BAssembly of gods, perhaps the introduction of Herakles to Olympos. Poseidon and Amphitrite stand together at the left. Amphitrite, on the far left, stands facing center, wearing a white(?) chiton with red dots under a black and red striped himation, the black stripes decorated with small white rosettes. She has white skin and long hair bound with a red band. Poseidon also faces to the right, holding his trident upright in his left hand. His right arm is bent at his side. He wears a red chiton and a black mantle decorated with rosettes. Zeus and Hera are seated side by side on stools in the center of the scene, facing toward the right; there is a small sphinx under Zeus' stool. Zeus holds a stylized thunderbolt in his right hand; his extended left arm has been damaged. He has a long beard and long hair, and wears a red chiton over which a black mantle has been draped to cover both shoulders. Hera is partially hidden behind Zeus and part of her head has been lost through damage to the vase. Her white face and one raised hand are preserved. She wears a black himation. Above and right, a bird flies left toward her. Four figures stand to the right of Zeus and Hera, all facing left. Immediately to the right stands a warrior, perhaps Herakles. His torso is hidden behind his shield with its lion head decoration. He wears greaves and has a red beard. To the right of him stands a female, dressed in a red chiton and a black himation decorated with rosettes; there are inscriptions above and between these two figures. On the far right are two overlapping figures, the one in front a naked male figure, beardless and with long red hair. Partially hidden behind him is a female wearing a simple red chiton or peplos with a black border.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A: nonsense inscriptions in the field between the male on the left and Apollo read: *E*I -- *I*O*D*E*I*O.*E*S; between Apollo and Zeus: *S *O*X*E*I*E *D*E*I*O; and between Zeus and Eileithyia: *E*I*O*X --. Side B: nonsense inscriptions above the figures on the left read: -- *P*I*E*L*S*O -- *A; between Poseidon and Zeus: *O*I*D*I*O; above Zeus: *N*S*I*O; and retrograde between the warrior and female figure on the right: -- *I*O*I*E*O --.
artifact.shape_description: Type A amphora.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS3440
artifact.summary: Side A: birth of Athena<lb>Side B: chariot, charioteer, warriors and others.
artifact.other_bibliography: Hall 1912, 68-75; Balmuth 1963, 69, pl. 15, 2
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was recovered in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The vase is very fragmentary, making it difficult to read the figural scene. The surface is worn and chipped, especially around the mends.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: birth of Athena. Athena springs from the head of Zeus, who is seated on a stool in the center of the scene facing right. Athena, about one-tenth the size of the other figures, is not quite free of Zeus. One foot still remains in his head. Although small, Athena is fully dressed and armed, her shield held at her left shoulder. Zeus is draped in a red and black, full-length mantle. His stool has a low back carved with a swan's head. A small creature, half man, half bird, crouches beneath it. Apollo stands to Zeus' left playing his lyre and dressed in a long chiton and himation. Poseidon, bearded and wearing a long chiton and a full-length mantle, stands to his left. The top of his triton can be seen at the crown of his head. A female figure stands to his left. She is wearing a long chiton and short jacket, and a fillet over her hair. Hermes stands on the far left in his petasos. He is bearded and has long hair, and he is dressed in a long chiton and mantle. He appears to be getting ready to leave the scene, perhaps to announce the birth, for his feet are turned to the left though he still looks to the right. Four more figures occupy the right side of the scene. Standing directly to the right of Zeus and Athena are two female figures, their right hands raised over their heads in a gesture of greeting or respect. Ares stands behind them in full panoply. He wears a crested Corinthian helmet and carries a round shield whose device is now lost. Dionysos stands on the far right, a wreath of grape leaves on his head. He is bearded and draped in a full-length mantle.

Side B: chariot, charioteer, warriors and others. The two-horse chariot and charioteer face right in the foreground of the scene, surrounded by six warriors, three female figures and three other males. The bearded charioteer is in his chariot holding the reins. He is dressed in a short-sleeved, ankle-length chiton belted at the waist. Most of the figures clustered around the chariot face to the right, although a number turn their heads to talk to their companions. There are two warriors to the left of the chariot, two behind it, and two to the right. All are dressed in short chitons decorated with scallops or checkerboard patterns, and wear cuirasses, greaves and crested Corinthian helmets. One of the warriors behind the chariot carries a round shield whose device is now lost. The warrior on the far right carries a round shield with a snake device. Most of the warriors carry one or two spears. A female figure in a long chiton stands with the two warriors on the left. A white-bearded male figure stands behind the charioteer facing left. Another white-haired and white-bearded male and a second female figure stand behind the horses with two of the warriors. Both face to the right. A bearded male stands facing them wearing a long sash over his head. The third female figure stands with the warriors on the right, facing right. A white dog stands looking up at the horses in the lower right corner in front of the last warrior.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora. A number of holes have been drilled in the bottom of the vase.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2515
artifact.summary: Interior: naked athlete.
artifact.sources_used: Ashmead & Phillips 1976; CVA, U.S.A., University Museum, Philadelphia (forthcoming)
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1918, 101 and 106, no. 95; Hoppin 1919, vol. 2, 107, no. 110; Luce 1921, 80, no. 81.; Beazley 1925, 220, no. 147; ARV2, 314, 236; DePuma 1968, pl. 63, figs. 3 and 4; von Bothmer 1982, 32; Beazley Addenda 2, 247.
artifact.collection_history: The kylix was originally part of the Coleman Collection. It was later purchased and given to the University Museum by Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: Some abrasion of the surface.
artifact.decoration_description: Interior: nude athlete. A naked youth runs to the right, legs wide. He swings a diskos behind him with his right hand; the diskos is just visible behind his right elbow. His left arm is extended in front of him for balance, his hand open-palmed.
