There is a pair of jumping weights on the ground between his legs. The edge of a couch or stool occupies the far left edge of the tondo, a folded cloak resting on its cushion.
artifact.shape_description: A small, delicate type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2495
artifact.summary: Side A: Nike between two youths. Side B: Nike alighting between two youths. Tondo: two standing boys.
artifact.other_bibliography: FR, 259, no. 23, 2; Bates 1907, 152-54; Bates 1909, 210; Swindler 1915, 406, no. 9.; Beazley 1918, 132; Hoppin 1919, 348 no. 45; Luce 1921, 91-92 no. 100; Beazley 1925, 275; Dohan 1935b, 76; ARV2, 584, 18
artifact.dimensions: H. at handle 0.097 m., H. at rim 0.092 m., D. rim 0.239 m., D. foot 0.093 m.
artifact.collection_history: The vases was excavated by A. L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The preserved portions of the vase are in good condition, with some chipping of the surface around the cracks.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Nike between two youths. A Nike hovers in the air between two youths, her wings spread, her knees bent and her toes almost touching the ground. She is holding a piece of cloth stretched between her outstretched arms, and looks to the right toward one of the youths. She is wearing a chiton and himation. The youth on the right faces the Nike, his right hand resting on a staff. He is wearing a mantle. The youth on the left stands facing forward, his head turned toward the Nike. He also wears a mantle.

Side B: Nike between two youths. A Nike, her wings spread, has landed and is walking toward the youth on the right with outstretched arms. She is dressed in a chiton, a short himation, and a sakkos. The youth on the right stands with his right arm resting on his staff, looking toward the Nike. The youth on the left stands facing forward, his head turned toward the two on the right. The fingers of his left hand, held at his side, are spread wide. Both youths wear mantles. A wide, open vessel on two tall legs sits on the ground between the Nike and the youth on the right.

Interior: two standing boys. Two boys wrapped in mantles stand facing one another, the boy on the left stepping forward as he speaks to the one on the right. The hands of both boys are hidden by their mantles. The boy on the left wears his pulled partially over his head, while the mantle of the boy on the right is knotted at the back of the neck.
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2489
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena with two draped males. Side B: three naked youths dancing.
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was recovered in excavations led by A.L. Frothingham under the auspices of the American Exploration Society, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from John Wanamaker.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is chipped and pock marked.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Athena with two draped males. Athena, in full panoply, strides to the left brandishing her spear in her left hand and carrying her shield on her right. A ring-handled tripod stands on the ground in front of her. A young man wrapped in a mantle stands on the left holding a spear. Another youth in a mantle stands on the right in an identical pose, here reversed. Athena wears a long chiton, her aegis and a crested helmet.

Side B: three naked youths dancing. The youth on the right dances facing left, one foot off the ground held up in a stylized position in front of his face. The other two dance facing right. The youth in the center has both feet on the ground but has raised his right hand to his shoulder and holds his left at his waist. The youth on the left also touches his shoulder with his left hand, and his raised knee with his right.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora with flaring mouth, round handles and echinus foot.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2464
artifact.summary: Side A: symposion with three bearded men<lb>Side B: two youths and a boy
artifact.other_bibliography: Levi 1963, 55; Young 1963, 5; Beazley Addenda 2, 207.
artifact.date_description: The date is listed in the museum records as "early 5th c."
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally belonged to the Coleman Collection. It was later acquired by Davis and Harvey, from whom Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst obtained it before giving it the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface of the base is worn and pitted, especially on side B. The black glaze is better preserved than are the red portions of the vase.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: symposion with three bearded men. Two men recline on couches on the left and right, while a third man in the center entertains them with a double flute which he plays with both hands. The musician faces toward the right and is wearing boots, a headband and a short garment which leaves his right shoulder and his genitals uncovered. The man on the left couch is leaning back on the pillow, resting on his left elbow while his right arm is held out to the left, fully extended. He turns his head to the right to talk to the man on the other couch. A kylix hangs on the wall over his feet. The man on the right faces left. He also leans back on his left elbow and gestures with his left hand as if talking. His right arm is extended to rest behind his raised right knee. Both men wear long cloaks and wreaths. A small table is placed beside each couch; the couches face toward the left, pillows on the right.

Side B: two youths and a boy. The scene involves three draped youths, apparently conversing. The youth on the left faces the two on the right, reaching toward them with his outstretched right arm. He wears a full cloak which leaves his right shoulder bare. The boy in the center faces the youth on the right. He is completely covered by his cloak, which is pulled up around his neck and which hides his hands. The youth on the right leans on a staff facing the boy, one arm akimbo. His cloak has been pulled up to partially cover his head.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2463
artifact.summary: Main Panel: three women with hydriae at a fountain. Shoulder scene: Herakles and the Nemean Lion.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917b, 153, 155; Dunkley 1935-36, 203
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally belonged in the Coleman Collection. It was later purchased through Davis & Harvey by Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst who gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.decoration_description:
Main Panel: three women with hydriae at a fountain. The fountain is on the far right. One of the women is at the fountain. Her foot is on the first step and she is about to fill her hydria or has just finished filling it. Water is gushing from the fountain's lion head spout. The central woman is leaving the fountain, walking away to the left, her hydria balanced on her head. She has raised one hand to steady it. A third woman approaches the fountain from the far left. Her hydria is empty, for she carries it horizontally on her head. Her arms hang at her sides. There is a low-flying bird between the central woman and the woman on the left. A second bird is perched on the top of the fountain. A tree at the far side of the fountain has spread its branches in the background of the scene.

Shoulder scene: Herakles and the Nemean Lion. Herakles and the lion wrestle on the ground while Athena and Iolaos watch. Herakles has forced the lion's head to the ground and the lion tries to push his head away with his left rear paw. Herakles' quiver hangs above him and his mantle hangs to his left. Athena is seated on a stool on the far left holding a spear, her shield resting on her left knee. She wears a chiton, aegis and a crested helmet. Iolaos is seated on a stool on the right. He is holding something in his right hand, possibly a club. He wears a short chiton and there is a sash draped over his right arm. His other arm is held akimbo.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2462A
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos and Athena, with Hermes, a maenad and a satyr<lb>Side B: four satyrs carrying maenads
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by Phoebe A. Hearst from Davis and Harvey, and was subsequently given to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The amphora is worn and some portions are discolored. In some places the paint has been worn off completely.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos and Athena, with Hermes, a maenad and a satyr. Dionysos stands in the center facing Athena on the right. He is followed by a maenad and a flute-playing satyr, while Hermes accompanies Athena. Dionysos is holding a kantharos in his raised left hand and has his right hand hidden under his mantle. He wears a wreath of grape leaves. Athena faces Dionysos holding two spears and a shield which hides her body from neck to hip. The shield has a central boss of five white leaves. Athena is helmeted and wears a long black gown with a decorative border. Behind Athena, Hermes, in winged boots, striped chlamys and petasos, walks to the right looking back toward Athena on the left. On the left, behind Dionysos, is a maenad dressed in a belted peplos and crowned with a wreath of grape leaves. She wears her long hair loose down her back. A satyr prances behind her on the far left playing the double flute, one knee raised almost to his chest. He is naked, bearded, and has pointed ears and a long tail. A grape vine surrounds Dionysos, the maenad and the satyr.

Side B: four satyrs carrying four maenads. Four ithyphallic satyrs dance to the right, carrying music-playing maenads. The satyr on the right leads the way, prancing with one leg off the ground as he lifts the maenad by her waist. She faces him and the rest of the procession, raising her right hand as if to cheer them on. The second couple follows close behind, the satyr crouching down with the maenad on his shoulder. He is looking back over his shoulder to the third couple on the left. The maenad is playing a double flute, her head bent forward as she plays. The third satyr stands with feet together and legs bent, carrying a maenad on his shoulder. She is playing a lyre and looks back toward the last couple on the far left. The fourth satyr prances to the right but looks left. His right arm hangs by his side and his left is draped over the thighs of the maenad sitting on his shoulder. Like the second maenad, she plays a double flute. All the maenads wear long, black, belted chitons and have long hair crowned by wreaths of grape leaves. The satyrs have long hair and beards, pointed ears, and long tails. There is a grape vine in the background.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora. A lid, MS2462B, was originally attributed to this amphora, but in June, 1965, von Bothmer gave his opinion that the lid did not belong with MS2462A.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2449
artifact.summary: Side A: three seated women<lb>Side B: two seated and one standing woman<lb>Interior: woman before a chest
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1921, 91 no. 102; ARV2, 540, 35.
artifact.collection_history: The cup originally belonged to the Coleman Collection (C215). It was purchased through Davis and Harvey by Phoebe A. Hearst who gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The cup has been mended from many fragments. There is some abrasion of the surface on the reserved areas.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: three seated women. Two women seated on klismoi make music while a third seated woman listens. All three are dressed in chiton and himation and sphendones. The central woman sits facing left holding a faded wreath in her raised hands. She wears her hair in a sakkos. The figure on the left, facing right, is an aulist. She has paused in her playing and holds the two pipes in her extended hands. Her long hair is pulled back and bound in a soft cloth knot behind her back. Around her head is a headband with a row of leaves and berries along its upper edge. One long strand of hair falls down the front of her arm. The third woman on the right holds two pair of krotala. She is seated facing left and has her hair in a decorative sakkos bound by black ties. She wears a large round earring with pendent dangles. A spotted skin aulos case hangs on the wall between the left-hand woman and the central woman.

Side B: two seated and one standing women. All three wear chitons, mantles and sakkoi bound by elaborate ties. The central woman is walking to the left holding a mirror and looking back at the woman on the right, her left hand swinging behind her. Her mantle has a wide black border. The other two women sit facing her on klismoi. The woman on the left holds a flower in each hand. Her blond hair shows beneath her sakkos. The woman on the right holds a leafy wreath. Krotala hang on the wall between the central woman and the woman seated on the right.

Interior: woman before a chest. An elegant woman stands facing left, opening a chest with her right hand, a flat box balanced on her left hand and forearm. She is clad in a finely pleated chiton and a heavier mantle, draped to pile in stiff, steeply stacked folds at the neck and into a crescent-shaped catenary below her left hand. Her hair is covered by a decorative cloth cap. She wears a necklace and a round, dangling earring. The wooden chest is located on the far left and is partially open. It is supported by animal paw feet resting on a low base. The rim of the chest is decorated with alternating dark and light rectangles, and the body with two sunburst motifs. The small box carried by the woman is decorated in the same manner. There is a retrograde inscription on the right.
artifact.inscriptions: There is a retrograde inscription on the interior.
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2448
artifact.summary: Tondo: a youth holds a small pig and a basket
artifact.sources_used: Ashmead & Phillips 1976; CVA, U.S.A., University Museum, Philadelphia (forthcoming).
artifact.other_bibliography: Bates 1907, 144-146 no. 3, pl. 36; Bates 1909, 210; Hall 1913, 162; Luce 1921, 80-81 no. 82; Beazley 1925, 235; ARV2, 231, 24; Durand 1986, 135, fig. 59; Beazley Addenda 2, 218.
artifact.collection_history: The kylix was originally part of the Coleman Collection. It was purchased by Davis and Harvey, sale no. 212, and was given to the University Museum by Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: Much of the glaze has flaked off on the exterior. The interior is somewhat worn, with fine scratches from previous mending. Fourteen ancient mend holes were counted during restoration of the kylix; most can be seen on either the interior and exterior.
artifact.graffiti: The inscription to the right of the youth reads: &epig-rough;*O *P*A*I*S. The inscription on his left reads: *K*A[*L]*O*S. (The boy is beautiful.)
artifact.decoration_description: Interior: a youth carrying a piglet and a basket. A slender youth is walking to the right, carrying a piglet to be sacrificed. He is wearing a wreath in his hair and a short garment around his waist which falls to about mid-thigh. The kicking piglet is dangling from the his right hand, while in his outstretched left hand he carries a kanoun, each of its 'horns' decorated with a branch. The youth walks with his left foot forward, his knees slightly bent and his head bowed. There are inscriptions below the basket and between the youth and the piglet.
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2445
artifact.summary: Interior: walking komast<lb>Side A: three singing and dancing figures<lb>Side B: three komasts
artifact.other_bibliography: Furtwängler 1905, 259 no. 22; Bates 1913, 479-486 figs. 1-3; Beazley 1918, 94, 96 no. 24; Hoppin 1919, 138 no. 92; Luce 1921, 94 no. 105; Beazley 1925, 191; ARV2, 276, 60; Mededelingenblad 34, 1985, 14, figs. 22-26; Beazley Addenda 2, 232.
artifact.collection_history: The cup was originally part of the collection of Prince Canino. It passed into the collection of James Jackson of Florence, thence into the Robert Coleman Collection, Philadelphia. In 1896 it was sold by Davis and Harvey to Phoebe A. Hearst who gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The vase has been mended from numerous fragments, and the surface is worn, especially on side B.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: three singing and dancing figures. The figures move to the right. A lyre player stands in the center, swaying backward, his face turned up, absorbed in the music. He plays a six-stringed lyre or barbatos, holding the bottom pressed into his side while he presses the strings with his left hand and plucks with his right. He is naked under the heavy cloak he wears draped over his shoulders. Behind him, on the left, a nude krotala dancer hops onto his left foot, drawing up the right. His arms swing out and his head is turned back. He carries krotala in both hands and a spotted pelt aulos case is hung over his forward, left forearm. His knobby staff is propped up beside the handle of the kylix. A second dancer on the right balances a banded skyphos in his left hand as he skips on his right foot, looking back toward his companions. He carries a knobby staff in his right hand which swings behind him. A short cloak hangs over his left forearm and behind his back. All three revelers wear fillets over their short, curly hair.

Side B: three komasts to the right. This side is damaged. The central figure is an older, bearded man with hair on his belly who is bent over holding pipes, though they are not raised to his lips. A heavy black-bordered cloak covers his left arm and swings in folds behind his back. He is followed by a dancer who carries a knobby staff in his right hand and a cloak in his forward extended left hand. He has just leapt onto his right foot and his left leg is bent at the knee. On the right another youth dances to the right looking toward the others on the left. He swings his arms, krotala in his hands. The lower half of his aulos case is preserved. His cloak is draped over both upper arms and he wears a fillet over his hair.

Tondo: walking komast. A komast holding a knobby staff is walking to the right, his head turned to face forward. A heavy cloak is draped over his extended left arm while his right arm, holding the staff, is held behind him. He is naked but wears soft leather shoes tied at the ankle. He has heavy thighs and a paunch, and his hair is short and curly.
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2444
artifact.summary: Side A: two athletes wrestling while a trainer watches. Side B: three athletes. Interior: nude athlete.
artifact.other_bibliography: Bates 1907, 140, pl. 35; Beazley 1918, 111; Luce 1921, 90-91 no. 103b; Beazley 1925, 232, no. 33; ARV2, 235, 36; Hyde 1921, 231, fig. 50; Gardiner 1910, 392; Jüthner 1968, 250, fig. 62; Beazley Addenda 2, 220
artifact.collection_history: The kylix was originally part of the Coleman Collection. It was purchased by Davis and Harvey, and was given to the University Museum by Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: The surface is pocked and deeply eroded on the interior. The exterior is worn, but is much better preserved.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: wrestlers and their trainer. Two nude athletes wrestle on the ground, two crossed javelins leaning behind them and a diskos bag and a pair of halteres hanging above them. The athlete on the left has the upper hand, and has grabbed the right elbow of the wrestler on the ground with one hand, while reaching with his other hand for his opponent's leg. The losing wrestler is on his hands and knees, his left knee still off the ground and his left foot pushing to keep him up. A low, fluted column without a capital occupies the far left of the scene, locating the wrestlers in the palaestra. Next to it stands a bearded man, the trainer, facing the wrestlers. He is wearing a long, heavy cloak and a red wreath, and is leaning on a staff while holding a long, forked stick over the wrestlers to his right.

Side B: Three nude athletes. The boxer on the left moves to the right, his head turned back to the left. He holds himantes in his extended left hand, and holds his right hand to his chest. More himantes hang on the wall immediately above and to his right. The central athlete is seated on the ground facing right with his right leg extended and his left knee up. He extends his hands straight-armed toward the ground to his left. On the wall above hangs a looped boxing cord. The acontist on the right is preparing for a throw. He stands facing right but turns his head to the left, holding a javelin behind him in this direction in his extended right hand. The thong wrapped around the shaft of the javelin has been looped around his extended fore and middle fingers. His left arm is bent, with his hand on his shoulder.

Interior: standing athlete. A nude athlete balances on his left foot, his right foot flexed and crossed behind, its toe brushing the ground. His right hand rests on his waist and his head is tipped down to his left. He wears a fillet around his short curly hair and holds a 'T'-handled staff in his left hand. A diskos in its bag hangs at the left; on the ground lie two jumping weights.
artifact.inscriptions: Written on the interior is the following: *K*A[*L*O*S] retrograde, and *L*U*K*O*S, "Lykos is beautiful." On sides A and B is written: *K*A*L*O*S, "beautiful."
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix. Ashmead and Phillips believe the potter to be Euphronios and the painter, Onesimos.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS2440
artifact.summary: Side A: two youths and a Nike. Side B: two youths and a Nike. Tondo: a youth adoring a herm.
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1918, 132; Hoppin 1919, 347 no. 44; Luce 1921, 89 no 104; ARV2, 602; Levi 1963, 407; von Bothmer 1971a, 41
artifact.collection_history: The cup originally belonged to the Coleman Collection. It was purchased through Davis and Harvey by Phoebe A. Hearst, who gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The cup has been restored from many fragments, with some loss of clay along the breaks. There are also some gouges on the surface.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: two youths and a Nike. A Nike alights between two youths to announce a victory. She lands facing left, her wings pressed together and her feet tucked up behind her. She wears a chiton and sakkos and is enveloped in a large mantle which hides her arms. The youth on the left, whom she faces, is stooped over, leaning on his staff. He appears to be raising his right arm, perhaps in a gesture of greeting; his forearm is not preserved. He is wearing a mantle which falls to mid-calf. Another youth moves away on the right as if frightened, but turns his head to look back. He holds his forearms outward, although his hands are hidden under his heavy mantle. Both youths wear wreaths.

Side B: two youths and a Nike. A Nike has landed between two youths, facing left. Her wings are extended behind her and she is dressed in a chiton and mantle. The youth on the left faces her wrapped in a mantle and leaning on a staff. The youth on the right is identical in pose and dress to the right-hand figure on Side A.

Interior: a youth adoring a herm. The youth stands left, facing the herm. He is hunched over slightly, leaning on his staff, and has extended his right arm toward the herm, palm outward. He wears a himation with his right shoulder left free and a vine wreath around his hair. The short, ithyphallic herm stands on a low base and is represented with very long hair, a long beard, sideburns and a mustache. His phallos is nearly one-third his height. Ribbons, rendered in dilute glaze, hang over its arm strut along with a wreath, now faded. Below the wreath is a kerykeion. There is an inscription written above his head, along the rim.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A to the left of the Nike's head: . . . [*K*A]*L*O*S, "(he is) beautiful." Above the herm on the interior: *K*A*L*O*S, "(he is) beautiful."
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS1753
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and the Nemean Lion. Side B: Hermes, Herakles and a female(?) figure.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917b, 154-155, fig. 62
artifact.collection_history: The vase was recovered in excavations conducted under the auspices of the American Exploration Society from 1896 through 1897, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from Mr. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: The preserved portions of Side A are in good condition. Side B is very badly damaged through erosion and encrustations.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles and the Nemean Lion. Herakles struggles with the lion while Athena looks on. Herakles, on the left, has wrapped his left arm around the lion's neck, pushing downward with all his strength, forcing the lion's head to the ground. Herakles' fingers are locked together and his head rests in the lion's mane. The lion mouth is open, his tongue hanging out, as he struggles with Herakles, trying to push his head away with his left rear foot. Athena stands behind the two facing right. She is holding her spear in her right hand and gestures with her left, and is shown dressed in a chiton and her aegis. Herakles is bearded and naked, his mantle hanging on the right and his quiver on the left

Side B: Hermes, Herakles and a female(?) figure. This side is badly damaged, but Hermes can be identified on the left by his winged boots, short mantle and staff. The lion skin identifies the figure on the right as Herakles. A third figure in the center is dressed in a long chiton with a meander pattern on the bottom border. This figure can probably be identified as female.

artifact.name: Philadelphia MS1752
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles in combat with two Amazons. Side B: two Amazons on horseback.
artifact.other_bibliography: Luce 1917b, 148-149; von Bothmer 1957, p. 49, no. 110, p. 101, no. 122
artifact.collection_history: The amphora was recovered in excavations conducted under the auspices of the American Exploration Society in 1896-1897, and subsequently became part of the collection of the University Museum, Philadelphia. Funding for the museum's contribution to the excavations came from Mrs. Phoebe A. Hearst.
artifact.condit: The amphora is in very good condition, with the exception of two deep gouges near the bottom of the figural scene on Side B and some loss of the added white paint.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles in combat with two Amazons. Herakles struggles with one Amazon as another runs in to join the fight. The Amazon in the center has been pulled down by Herakles. Having come in from the left, he has gripped the Amazon's helmet where the crescent top piece connects to the helmet itself, pulling her head back and forcing her closer to the ground. At the same time he swings his sword back getting ready to strike. The Amazon's right leg has buckled under her and her body is pulled back at a sharp angle. Although she still grips her shield and sword she is in a helpless position and her expression, eyes staring upward and lips parted, shows it. A second Amazon in oriental costume and armor rushes in from the right with raised spear and shield, but she will be too late. Herakles wears a short tunic and his lion's skin tied over his shoulders and belted. His dagger sheath can be seen behind his left hip. The fallen Amazon is dressed in a short black tunic and a black cuirass and helmet. A mantle is draped over her left spear arm and falls diagonally behind her back. Her round shield is decorated with a laurel wreath. The second Amazon wears a tight fitting, oriental 'body suit' decorated with lozenge shapes, a cuirass, and a red pointed cap with long tassels. There is a quiver at her side, and she carries a spear and a crescent-shaped shield.

Side B: two Amazons on horseback. Two Amazons ride to the right accompanied by their dogs. Their horses overlap slightly to show that the two ride side by side rather than one behind the other. Each Amazon carries two spears in her right hand and grips the reins with her left. The Amazon on the left is dressed in a short tunic, cuirass and helmet. The Amazon on the right is dressed in oriental garb—a full 'body suit' decorated with lozenge shapes and a pointed red cap with long tassels falling in front of her shoulders and behind her back. The animals are depicted in a lively manner. The horse on the right has tossed its head up and opened its mouth, while the horse on the left has tucked its head. The dogs are shown running with open mouths, as they naturally would.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-540
artifact.summary: Revelers dance to the music of flute and castanets.
artifact.other_bibliography: Eismer 1975, 81; Beazley Addenda 2, 129.
artifact.dimensions: H. at handle 0.143 m., H. at rim 0.074 m., D. 0.106 m.
artifact.collection_history: The cup was once part of the collection of Francis T. Sully Darley, who bequeathed it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1914. It is now on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.decoration_description: Revelers dancing to the music of flute and castanets. The procession of revelers moves to the right. It starts at the handle of the kyathos, where the procession is led by a woman playing a double flute. She is dressed in chiton and himation. She is followed by a naked man with a piece of cloth draped over his shoulders. He walks or dances with arms spread wide, looking back at a man carrying an amphora. The man with the amphora is naked, and is bent under the weight of the large amphora which he carries on his back. His stomach bulges slightly in this awkward position. He holds an unidentifiable object in his right hand. This man is followed by another man in a short chiton and mantle who holds a staff in his left hand. He is looking back over his shoulder at the woman behind him, who has one arm raised and is playing castanets. She is dressed in chiton and himation. Behind her is a naked youth in a short mantle walking or dancing with bent legs, holding a long projectile-like object. A man brings up the rear of the procession. He is wrapped in a mantle and is looking back over his shoulder to the left and holding his left arm akimbo. All the male figures are beardless. All the figures wear red wreaths.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-41
artifact.summary: Three women conversing.
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally belonged in the collection of William S. Vaux. It was bequeathed to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1882, and has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1935.
artifact.condit: The hydria is in very good condition. Portions of the red surface of the vase are slightly worn.
artifact.decoration_description: Three women conversing. The central woman stands facing forward, one hip thrust out, and turns her head to the left to converse with another woman. She holds a wide, flat-bottomed basket with three short legs at her right side. Her left hand is held limp-wristed at her waist. Her hair is wrapped in a sakkos, with short curls falling out in front of her ear. The woman on the left faces the central woman, holding a wreath in her left hand and gesturing with her close-fingered right hand. She has a short, curly hairstyle. The young girl on the right faces the two women, gesturing with her left hand which is hidden under her himation. She has long hair which falls down her back, and bangs and short curls in front of her ears. All the women are dressed in chiton and himation and are barefoot. A cushioned stool on the right of the central woman is partially hidden behind her.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-40
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena and a youth (Theseus?). Side B: man with a scepter.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1935b, 76, pl. 4; ARV2, 432, 18; DeVries 1973, 4, 34, fig. 1; Kunisch 1974, pl. 45,2; Beazley Addenda 2, 273
artifact.collection_history: The amphora originally belonged to the collection of William S. Vaux. It was bequeathed to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1882, and has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1935.
artifact.condit: The vase is in perfect condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Athena and a youth. Athena and the youth, possibly Theseus, stand facing one another, Athena on the left and the youth on the right. Athena holds a spear vertically in her left hand, her helmet held in her lowered right hand. The youth is reaching toward Athena with his open right hand, two spears held in his left hand, and a sword in the scabbard at his waist. Athena is dressed in a simple shift (a peplos?) under a low-belted chiton, and she has a short mantle draped over both shoulders. She wears a diadem over her long, wavy hair, and a round earring. The youth has short hair and is beardless. He wears a short chiton and has a short mantle draped over his arms, leaving his shoulders bare. A circular hat or rolled pack hangs behind his back. Both figures are barefoot.

Side B: man with a scepter. A solitary man is shown standing in profile to the right holding a tall staff. He has short hair and a long beard, and is dressed in a long chiton and wrapped in a mantle. His feet are bare. He holds his staff, which has a finial, upright in his right hand. It is taller than he is.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-39
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos in his chariot<lb>Side B: Dionysos with maenad, satyr and a male figure
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1935b, 72, pl. 3.
artifact.collection_history: The vase once belonged to William S. Vaux, who bequeathed it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art. It is presently on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos in his chariot. Dionysos, crowned with ivy and carrying a drinking cup, is shown stepping into his chariot. Dionysos stands on the left, facing the four-horse chariot on the right. Dionysos' right foot is already in the chariot, while the toes of his left foot are still on the ground. He holds the reins with both hands, a kyathos in his left hand as well. Dionysos has long hair and a long beard with a red stripe. He wears a white chiton and a black mantle draped over both shoulders. A large ivy wreath crowns his head. Vines sprout from the kyathos and extend over and behind the horses on the right. The four horses overlap; all have red stripes on their fetlocks and tails.

Side B: Dionysos with satyr, maenad and a male figure. Dionysos and a maenad stand facing one another at the center of the scene, while a satyr and a man look on. Dionysos is shown in profile to the right, handing a vine-sprouting drinking cup to a maenad. He is wrapped in a mantle which hides his right arm, and wears a large wreath on his head. He has long hair and a long beard. The maenad tips her head down to look into the drinking cup as she reaches for it with her left hand. She has white skin and wears a chiton and himation. There is a red headband around her long hair. On the far left, a nude satyr stands facing Dionysos and the maenad, his right arm bent at chest level and his left arm at his side. He has pointed ears, long hair, and a beard; both hair and beard have been painted with red stripes. On the far right, a man moves away from the other figures, but looks back at them over his shoulder. He has long hair and a beard, both red-striped, and wears a short chiton, a short mantle draped over both shoulders, and a pointed cap with a turned-up brim. The vines sprouting from Dionysos' drinking cup extend above and behind the figures on both sides.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-30
artifact.summary: Red brown wash and reserved stripes.
artifact.collection_history: The vase belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1932.
artifact.condit: The surface is somewhat worn.
artifact.decoration_description: The vase is covered with a red-brown wash leaving narrow reserved stripes. These are on the rim, at the juncture of the neck and body, and above the juncture of the foot and body where the body begins to flare.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-259
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos and Ariadne in a chariot<lb>Side B: Dionysos with satyrs and maenad
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1935b, 72, pl. 3
artifact.collection_history: The vase once belonged to the collection of Dr. Robert H. Lamborn, who bequeathed it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1903. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since the 1930's.
artifact.condit: The surface has suffered slight discoloration and chipping, especially in the areas of added red paint. A circular misfired red area on the breasts of the central horses on Side A perhaps indicates that this vase had contact with another during the firing process.
artifact.graffiti: A graffito was added before firing to the underside of the foot: *D*I.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos and Ariadne in a chariot. The four-horse chariot is depicted frontally, so that Dionysos and Ariadne are hidden behind the two central horses. Only the tops of their heads can be seen. They turn away from each other, Dionysos on the right and Ariadne on the left. Both wear vine wreaths, and vines laden with bunches of grapes spring from their shoulders and trail down the sides of the chariot. The two central horses turn their heads toward one another, their muzzles crossed. The two outside horses look to the outside.

Side B: Dionysos with satyrs and maenad. Dionysos stands in the center facing right, his head turned toward the satyr and maenad on the left. He wears a long white chiton and a black mantle draped over his left shoulder. He has a long beard and, like the maenad and satyrs, wears a wreath of vines on his head. A long-horned goat stands behind his legs facing right. A satyr and maenad approach from the left, the maenad nearest to Dionysos. She is holding fan-like objects in her raised hands. She wears a chiton and himation. The satyr approaches with head slightly bowed, his left hand raised in a gesture of greeting or respect. The satyr on the right plays the double flute, head tilted back. His flute pouch(?) hangs from his left arm.

There is a palmette lotus chain on the neck of the amphora, and palmettes and a pendant lotus under the handles.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-248
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos with satyrs and maenads. Side B: Dionysos riding a donkey.
artifact.collection_history: The vase once belonged to the collection of Dr. Robert H. Lamborn who bequeathed it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1903. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1935.
artifact.condit: The vase is in very good condition, showing only some discoloration and slight chipping of the surface.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Dionysos with satyrs and maenads. Dionysos stands in the center holding a rhyton. On each of his sides, there is a naked satyr and a maenad, with the maenads standing next to Dionysos. Dionysos stands in profile to the right. He has raised the rhyton he holds in his left hand, as if to drink, and he holds a grape vine in his right hand. His long beard is red, and he is dressed in a long chiton over which is draped a heavy mantle with a red border. There is a crown of grape leaves on his head. The satyr and maenad on the left are dancing. The maenad has thrown her right arm over the satyr's shoulders and prances so that her left knee is raised and her foot off the ground. She holds a cup in her left hand. The satyr moves more sedately. His left hand is held out at waist level and it looks as if the artist had made some attempt to show him holding the maenad's hand with his right. The satyr and maenad on the right are also dancing, their arms held bent with the right hand at chest level and the left hand at waist level. They are shown in three-quarters view, she to the left, he to the right. They turn their heads to look at one another. She has one foot off the ground. The maenads wear chitons belted at the waist. They are decorated with small rosettes and the skirt is gathered at the center to fall in folds painted red and black. The satyrs have long red beards and tails. The vine held by Dionysos spreads over most of the background.

Side B: Dionysos riding a donkey. Dionysos sits astride a donkey facing right, a naked satyr standing to either side. Dionysos, bearded and wearing a crown of grape leaves, is holding a rhyton in his right hand. He has hitched up his mantle to be able to mount the donkey, leaving his bare legs hanging. The donkey is ithyphallic. The satyr on the left walks behind the donkey and is gesturing with his left hand. The satyr on the right is leading the donkey forward with his right hand and has turned his head back to better watch its progress. He holds his left arm cocked with his hand held flat at waist level. Both satyrs have long red beards and tails and a fringe of red hair around their faces. A grape-laden vine extends over the background, apparently emanating from Dionysos.

There is a honeysuckle pattern on the neck of the vase.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-191
artifact.summary: Theseus and a boar.
artifact.collection_history: The askos originally was part of the collection of Dr. Francis W. Lewis. It was bequeathed(?) to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1899, and has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1935.
artifact.condit: There are small chips on the handle and lip, otherwise the surface is in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description: Theseus and a boar. Theseus is on one side of the handle and the boar is on the other. Theseus is running to the left with outstretched arms, and looks back to the right. He is holding a club or sling in his right hand. A garment is draped over his left arm. Theseus is naked but wears a hat with a hemi-spherical crown and a short brim. The boar is running to the left, toward Theseus, his teeth bared.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-19
artifact.summary: Front: an Eros between florals
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 22, Univ. Mus. I: 31-32, fig. 5, pl. 36
artifact.other_bibliography: The Pennsylvania Gazette 78 no. 7.; Schauenburg 1981, 344, 346 fig. 3
artifact.collection_history: William S. Vaux bequeathed the vase to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1882. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1935.
artifact.condit: The vase is in excellent condition, with only minor erosion of the added white paint.
artifact.decoration_description: Front: an Eros between florals. The winged Eros squats facing left, holding a small axe or hammer in his right hand and a bird-trap in his left. He is naked but wears slippers and a small, tight-fitting white cap from which his curly blond hair escapes in the front. A top knot protrudes at the crown of his head.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-185
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and the Nemean lion. Side B: Theseus and the bull.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1935a, 451-452; Dohan 1935b, 5, pl. 5; Herter 1941, 218; Dohan 1942, 90.(?) (1943); Dinsmoor 1944, 91 fig 12; Boardman 1979, 37 fig. 6; Beazley Addenda 2, 188.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was once in the possession of Joseph Buonaparte I, acquired when he was king of Naples. Buonaparte gave the vase to Dr. Nathaniel Chapman no later then 1835. After Dr. Chapman's death, it was bought by Mr. Edward S. Clarke and afterwards sold by him to Dr. F.W. Lewis. It was subsequently given to the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and is now on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The vase is in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles and the Nemean Lion. Herakles, on the left, faces the lion, his left arm around the lion's neck and grasping the lion's upper jaw with his right hand, forcing his head and chest to the ground. The exhausted lion's tongue hangs out; his haunches are raised as he struggles to stand. His left paw is stretched forward against Herakles' head as he tries to push him away. Herakles is naked and wears a headband. His club leans behind him on the left. A quiver hangs by a leather thong above him. A tree is placed centrally behind the struggling figures.

Side B: Theseus and the Marathon Bull. Theseus and the bull face each other, Theseus on the left and the bull on the right. Theseus, standing over the bull, pushes him down with his left arm, forcing the bull's chest to the ground while he holds him down with his left foot on the bull's head. Theseus is prepared to strike the bull, his club raised behind him in his extended right arm. The bull's front left leg is curled beneath him, and his hindquarters are raised as he struggles to stay up. Theseus is naked but wears his quiver. A short cloak hangs behind him on the left. There is a tree behind the bull.
artifact.inscriptions: Above Herakles on Side A, in reverse: *K*A*L*O*S*E. Above Theseus on Side B, in reverse: *K*A*L*O*S*E.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-174
artifact.summary: A continuous band of decoration depicts Dionysos, three satyrs and three panthers.
artifact.collection_history: The cup once belonged to the collection of Dr. Francis W. Lewis. It was given to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1935, and is now on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.decoration_description: A continuous band of decoration shows Dionysos with three satyrs and three panthers; all the figures face right. Dionysos is seated on a stool holding a torch in his left hand. He wears a white chiton and a black himation with red stripes. Vines appear to spring from him and extend over the rest of the frieze. There is a satyr to the right of Dionysos. He crouches as he moves to the right with hands stretched forward. In front of him, a panther moves to the right, his head turned so that he is shown frontal face. He follows another crouching satyr, who is preceded by another panther. A third satyr moves to the right, looking back to the left and raising his right arm. A third panther moves toward the right to come up behind the seated Dionysos. Details are rendered in purple and white paint.
artifact.shape_description: The handleless cup has an offset rim and a round body tapering to a narrow flat base.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-64-173
artifact.summary: Thin black lines.
artifact.other_bibliography: Greenewalt 1966, 45-48, 53, "Type A," no. 15, pl. I.T; Greenewalt 1973, pl. 13.1 bottom left
artifact.collection_history: Dr. Francis W. Lewis, who purchased the vase in Athens, gave it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1899. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum since 1935.
artifact.condit: There is minor chipping, but otherwise the vase is in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description: Thin black lines. The neck and foot of the vessel are glazed black and there is a wide black band around the belly. The rest of the vessel is covered with fine black lines, including the rim, which has been decorated with a single black line. The edge of the foot is reserved.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-637-1a & b
artifact.summary: Side A: departure of young horseman. Side B: departure of young horseman. Interior: youth pursuing a girl.
artifact.other_bibliography: <bibl>Swindler 1909, 142-150, figs. 1-7</bibl>; <bibl>Jacobsthal 1912, 20</bibl>; <bibl>Hoppin 1919, 348</bibl>; <bibl>Dohan 1935b, 76</bibl>; <bibl>Dinsmoor 1944, 90-91, fig. 13</bibl>; <bibl>Immerwahr 1984, 342 pl. 41</bibl>; <bibl>Keuls 1985, 70-72, fig. 56</bibl>; <bibl>Keuls 1986, 86 note 9</bibl>; <bibl>Sourvinou-Inwood 1987, 149</bibl>
artifact.collection_history: The cup was found at Vulci in 1828/1829 or 1831 on the estate of Lucien Bonaparte, Prince of Canino and younger brother of Napoleon. It was presented to the American Philosophical Society on June 17, 1836 by Joseph Bonaparte, ex-king of Spain and a member of the American Philosophical Society from 1823 to 1844. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1968.
artifact.condit: There is some discoloration and pitting of the surface.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: departure of young horseman. In the center, a stallion stands in profile to the right, a youth behind him. The youth, wearing a chlamys and with a petasos hanging behind his back, is leaning on his staff and looking toward a second youth and an older, bearded man standing to the left. Another youth and bearded man stand talking on the right. The youth on the left stands facing forward, but looks toward the horseman on the right, leaning on the staff in his right hand. The older man on the far left is leaning on a staff tucked under his left arm and gestures with that hand, his right hand on his hip. Both men wear short mantles. The bearded man to the right of the horse stands in profile to the right, his right arm held straight out at shoulder height. His staff is held off the ground in his left hand. The youth he addresses faces forward but turns his head to listen, his staff tucked behind one bent knee and his right hand on his hip. His left hand rests limp-wristed on his staff. A shield hangs on the far right in its shield case, a scabbard below it. A writing case hangs on the far left, a stylus tied underneath around its middle.

Side B: departure of young horseman. The horse and youth in the center are almost identical in pose and dress to those on side A, except that the youth leans on a spear rather than a staff. Again, another youth and an older, bearded man stand to the left. Two more youths are involved in a discussion on the right. These figures echo the poses of those on side A, with small differences. On side B, the youth to the left of the horseman has his staff tucked under his left arm and is gesturing toward the horseman with his right hand. He is draped in a calf-length mantle. The older man on the far left is virtually identical to the older man on side A. The youth standing to the right of the horse stands facing left talking to the third youth. He is leaning forward as he gestures with his left hand, his right arm held at his waist, and his staff resting at his side. His companion stands facing him leaning on his staff, his weight on one leg and one arm held out limp-wristed at waist level. Both youths wear knee-length mantles. Again, a shield in its shield case hangs on the far right with a scabbard below. A money purse hangs on the far left.

Interior: youth pursuing a girl to the right. A youth has surprised a young woman at an altar. He is running after the girl and has just grabbed her around the neck. He holds up his mantle with his left hand, baring his body. The girl, dressed in a chiton and himation, runs away, but has turned her head to look at the youth. She is holding her himation at her waist with one hand, while holding up the hem with her other hand. There is a white fillet tied around her head. On the far left, behind the youth, the edge of an altar is visible.
artifact.inscriptions: *N*I*K*O*S*Q*E*N*E*S *E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N, Nikosthenes made it (or me).
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix. The bowl is very large and flat. The alien foot is signed by Nikosthenes.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-29-40
artifact.summary: Side A: head of a bearded man<lb>Side B: horse protome
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1933b, 48-48, pls. 8-9; Dohan 1934, 526-527, pl. 33; Hopper 1974, 224 (5)
artifact.collection_history: The amphora originally belonged to H.V. Hilprecht who bequeathed it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1929. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1932.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is covered with small chips and has suffered some discoloration.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: head of a bearded man. The man is in profile to the left, and is shown from the shoulders up. His long hair is bound at the nape of his neck with a white band, and white fillets are tied around the crown of his head, crossing over his ear. His skin is painted with added red, although his stylized ear is black. His round eye is also done in black glaze, and he wears a simple black chiton.

Side B: horse protome. The horse is shown in profile to the left with one of his forelegs raised. He is predominantly black but his neck has been painted in added red and his mane is drawn with alternating black and red locks. He has a round, black eye.
artifact.shape_description: The amphora has an ovoid body with cylindrical handles to mid-neck.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-29-30
artifact.summary: Bands of geometric ornament.
artifact.other_bibliography: Greenewalt 1966, 9, 30
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally belonged to H.V. Hilprecht who bequeathed to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1929. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1932.
artifact.condit: There are several small chips on the rim and some discoloration of the surface has occurred.
artifact.decoration_description: Plain band and bands of geometric ornament decorate the vase. The widest band is situated just under the widest part of the vase and is decorated with a triple zig-zag pattern. Plain black bands and narrow bands decorated with rows of dots complete the decoration. The lid is decorated with black lines and bands, and one narrow band decorated with a row of black dots. The knob is striped with fine black lines.
artifact.shape_description: A "Fat-bellied" lydion.

artifact.name: Philadelphia L-29-2
artifact.summary: Reserved band under the rim decorated with birds and geometric motifs on each side of the vase.
artifact.other_bibliography: Brommer 1978b, 45
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally belonged to H.V. Hilprecht who bequeathed it to the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1929. It has been on extended loan to the University Museum, Philadelphia, since 1932.
artifact.condit: There is some erosion of the surface, but the vase is generally in very good condition.
artifact.decoration_description: The handle zone is left reserved, and has been divided on each side into three panels by four groups of three vertical lines. The two outside panels have cross-hatched lozenges in frames. The central panel holds a water bird with "X" filler above its back.
artifact.shape_description: East Greek bird skyphos

artifact.name: Philadelphia 75-10-1
artifact.summary: Maltese dog and grapes.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was a gift of the estate of Rodney S. Young to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1975. It is said to have been purchased in Athens.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is chipped and worn, especially on the handle and lip.
artifact.decoration_description: Maltese dog and grapes. A Maltese dog stands to the right, his right forepaw off the ground. A bunch of grapes hangs above him.
artifact.shape_description: The vessel has a trefoil lip.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 58-20-3
artifact.summary: Front: winged demon or boread flying right<lb>Under handle: standing bird
artifact.other_bibliography: Benson 1965, 4-5, 85, no. 4, pl. 11
artifact.collection_history: The Volunteers of America gave the alabastron to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1968. The early history of the vase is unknown.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is chipped and peeling and there is some encrustation. Especially large chips are missing from the rim.
artifact.decoration_description:
Front: winged demon or boread flying right. The boread rushes to the right in the bent-kneed, bent-armed running pose typical of gorgons. His body is shown frontally and his legs and head are in profile. He is bearded and has shoulder length hair, and is dressed in a chitoniskos with zig-zag bands along the lower edge, over the shoulders and down the center of the chest.

Under handle: standing bird. The large bird stands facing right, its head turned toward the left.

There is much incised detail in the figural decoration, and thick filling ornament covers the field, consisting mainly of incised rosettes.
artifact.shape_description: The shape can be found in Necrocorinthia 319:B.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 51-32-1
artifact.summary: Departure scene. On the shoulder: a boxing contest.
artifact.collection_history: The vase belonged to the collection of Thomas Clarke of New York from 1915 to 1920. It was acquired by Mrs. Randal Morgan who gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1951.
artifact.condit: The vase is in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Departure scene with three figures. A charioteer waits in his chariot while a hoplite and an old man look on. The scene is dominated by the quadriga in the foreground. The charioteer, dressed in a short-sleeved, long white robe, stands in the chariot holding the reins in one hand and two spears in the other. On his back is a quiver(?). A hoplite stands behind and is partially hidden by the hindquarters of the horses. He faces left, toward the charioteer, holding a shield and wearing helmet and greaves. An old man with long white hair and a white beard stands directly behind the hoplite, also facing left. He wears a long cloak and holds a staff.

Added red and white glaze are used liberally.

On the shoulder, six figures in a boxing scene. Two naked boxers fight on either side of the two stacked cauldrons in the center of the scene. They take the wide-legged boxing stance and have their fists raised. Next to the boxer on the left is a naked youth in a wide-legged stance, a cloak flung over his left shoulder and arms held bent, away from his sides, with clenched fists(?). On the far left stands another youth in profile, feet together and facing the boxers. He wears a long robe and holds his right hand to his chest, while his left arm is raised and bent, his hand in front of his face. Next to the boxer on the right is a youth wearing a diagonally draped garment which falls to his knees. He also takes a wide-legged stance and holds his arms bent and slightly away from his body, holding a stick in one hand. On the far right, a youth in profile stands facing left, his feet together and arms bent and held away from his body. All the figures are beardless. There is a great deal of added red and white.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-9-1
artifact.summary: Hoplite head wearing a Corinthian helmet.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1931c, 126, pl. 8; Edrich 1969, 11 no. K34
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by the University Museum, Philadelphia, from Segredakis, Paris, in 1931.
artifact.condit: Some lime accretions remain on the surface; otherwise it is in very good condition.
artifact.comparanda: The aryballos can be compared to those in the Richmond, Virginia Museum of Fine Arts (Richmond 62-1-12), Basel 2-208, and an aryballos from tomb 45 at Ialysos (Ducat CIRh III: 75 no. E17, fig. 66).
artifact.decoration_description: The aryballos is in the shape of a hoplite's head wearing a Corinthian helmet. The cheek pieces of the helmet cover almost the entire front of the lower face and are decorated with large rosettes painted white. The rest of the helmet is painted black except for the top of the rim and an incised palmette and tendrils at the front of the helmet which are painted red. The flesh of the face is reserved and the eyes and eyebrows are done in black and white.
artifact.shape_description: Helmeted head aryballos.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-36-17
artifact.summary: Side A: woman and a youth<lb>Side B: two draped youths
artifact.sources_used: CVA, USA 22, Univ. Mus. I: 1, fig. 1, pl. 1
artifact.other_bibliography: Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 34, no. 19; Trendall 1974, 52 no. B 134; RVAp, 46 n. 8
artifact.collection_history: Arthur H. Lea gave the amphora to the University Museum in 1931.
artifact.condit: There is some scratching and pitting of the surface, as well as some flaking of the glaze.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: woman with a youth. The woman stands on the left holding a hydria. The youth faces her holding out a sash over his right arm, his other hand on his hip. She is dressed in a peplos with overfall and black borders. The youth is naked but has a himation draped over his left arm and shoulder. A plant is on the ground between the two and a sash hangs in the field above.

Side B: two youths. The youth on the right balances a stick on the back of his right hand. The other youth stands watching, one hand on his hip. Both youths wear himatia draped over the left arm and shoulder, leaving the right shoulder bare. The himatia have black borders.
artifact.shape_description: A small amphora of Panathenaic shape.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-36-15
artifact.summary: Sides A and B: siren between two draped youths.
artifact.collection_history: Arthur H. Lea gave the vase to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1931.
artifact.condit: The surface is worn and discolored and Side B is pitted and chipped.
artifact.decoration_description: Sides A and B: siren between two draped youths. On each side a siren stands to the right, wings spread. She is flanked by beardless youths draped in ankle-length mantles. Each youth has raised his left hand to waist level, still hidden under the mantle. There are palmettes on either side of the handles.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-36-11
artifact.summary: Side A: Nike flying to the right. Side B: standing youth.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan, Mus. Journal 23, 26, fig. 5; Dohan 1931c, 53-54, pl. 53f and pl. I; ARV2, 132, 15; Isler-Kerényi 1971, pl. 8,; Boardman 1979, 39, 8; Kurtz and Beazley 1983, 22; Beazley Addenda 2, 95.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was given to the University Museum by Arthur H. Lea in 1931. Beazley writes (1936) that it was no. 53 in the Braun sale at Christie's on February 21, 1850, and no. 282 in his second sale there on May 18, 1853.
artifact.condit: Side A is in excellent condition except around the mends. Side B is much more worn. The central part of the figure appears to be smeared.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: winged Nike. The Nike flies to the right, her feet off the ground with toes dangling. Her head is turned toward the left, while her wings overlap above her right shoulder. Her arms are spread wide, and she holds a thymiaterion in her left hand and a flowering tendril in her right. She is dressed in a sheer, crinkly chiton, a heavy himation with a border of dots and crosses, and a sakkos. Short tresses fall around her face, with longer tresses falling on her shoulders. She has an earring in her visible left ear and wears a coil bracelet on each wrist. Her hair is rendered in dilute glaze.

Side B: standing youth. A youth stands facing left, his head turned to the right. He wears a wreath and a cloak which leaves his right shoulder bare. His right hand is raised to his left shoulder; he holds onto a staff in his left hand. Part of his face and chest have been obliterated.
artifact.shape_description: The amphora is of Panathenaic shape.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-19-3
artifact.summary: Interior: lyre-player. Side A: boy with hare between two youths. Side B: two youths and a bearded man.
artifact.collection_history: The kylix originally belonged in the collection of Henry C. Lea. His son, Arthur H. Lea, gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1931.
artifact.condit: The surface of the kylix is worn and scratched. Reserved surfaces are badly eroded, while the glazed areas are in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: lyre-player. The youth stands holding his lyre, body frontal and head turned to the left. The lyre is held horizontally in his lowered right hand. His left hand is tucked inside his tightly wrapped mantle. The mantle is wrapped to leave his right shoulder exposed. He wears a fillet over his short hair. To his right is a fluted column with echinus, abacus block, architrave and platform, representing a building.

Side A: boy with hare between two youths. The boy with the hare stands in the center facing the youth on the right. He is holding the hare at the base of the ears and holds it out to his companion. The hare is wriggling, holding out its left forepaw. The youth on the right is leaning on a crooked stick, staring at the youth with the hare. His right hand is on his hip. Behind the central youth is an unfluted column with a capital block, narrow architrave and base. The youth to the left of the column looks and gestures to the left. His right hand may once have held a fillet for there is a large loop preserved above his right forearm. He leans his left elbow on his staff.

Side B: two youths and a bearded man. The central youth and the bearded man look toward the youth on the left. The youth on the left faces right, and is holding a stick in his right hand. His other hand is hidden under his mantle. To his right, there is an unfluted column with capital block, architrave and base. The central youth stands with his body frontal and his head turned to the left. He is wrapped in a mantle which is pulled over his head and which he seems to be unwrapping with his right hand. To the right, facing left, is an older, bearded man carrying a staff on his right forearm. A writing case and stylus hangs on the wall between the two figures.

The six male figures on sides A and B all wear mantles wrapped to leave their right shoulders exposed.
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix with a very shallow bowl.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-19-2
artifact.summary: Interior: cup-bearer<lb>Side A: Centauromachy<lb>Side B: Combat between archer and hoplites
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1931b, 23 and 26, pl. 11; Dohan 1932-33b, 33-44, figs. 10-13, 16 and 18; Van Ingen 1935, 159-160; ARV2, 264, 21; Richter 1946b, 87; Beazley 1966, 53-60, pls. 13-14; Knauer 1987, 3 n. 6 and 8, 10, 23 n. 60, and n. 116
artifact.collection_history: The kylix originally belonged in the collection of Henry C. Lea. His son, Arthur H. Lea, gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1931.
artifact.condit: There is some chipping of the surface, especially along the mends.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: cup-bearer. A nude youth carrying a kylix in one hand, has stepped up to a column krater to pour out wine or water from the trefoil oinochoe he carries in his other hand. He looks behind himself as he does so as if summoned by someone. His hair is bound by a taenia sprigged with vine leaves. The krater is garlanded with vines. A nonsense inscription runs along the inner edge of the tondo from the krater to the youth's left heel.

Side A: centaur battling with two hoplites. The centaur gallops to the right. He is wielding a small tree and reaches out dramatically with his left arm which is covered with the panther skin tied over his shoulders. The hoplite he is attacking has fallen wounded to one knee. He now turns his body to face his attacker, protecting himself with his shield and aiming his spear at the centaur's chest. Blood pours from his left shoulder. A companion hoplite is fleeing in the other direction, but turns awkwardly, stabbing the centaur in the buttocks with his spear. Both hoplites are naked but wear greaves and Chalcidian helmets with long crest-tails and nose guards. The device on the shield of the wounded warrior is a bull's head. The shield device of the fleeing warrior is a scorpion. The fleeing warrior also carries a sword at his waist. The centaur has a heavy face and coarse features. Although balding on top, he has long hair and a beard. He wears a fillet looped twice around his head.

Side B: fight between an archer and two hoplites. On the left, a nude archer has set an arrow in his bow and is drawing back on it, both arms straight. In the center is a fallen warrior, his left leg buckled under and his right extended. Although dying from the wound in his chest, he still holds his sword and shield. A second warrior on the right confronts the archer, lunging forward and leaning on the spear he appears to have planted between the thighs of his companion. He also carries a shield and wears a sheathed sword hanging from a double baldric at his waist. His round shield is fitted with a fringed apron. Both hoplites wear greaves and Corinthian helmets. The fallen warrior sports a baldric and scabbard. The shield device on both their shields is a snake. The archer is naked but wears leather boots, a gorytos suspended from a leather strap, and a Scythian cap made of leather. His bow is also Scythian.
artifact.inscriptions: Nonsense inscriptions on both sides and in the tondo.
artifact.shape_description: Type B kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 31-19-1
artifact.summary: Interior: Black figure warrior<lb>Sides A and B: Red figure eyes and palmettes
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1932-33b, 23-25 figs. 1, 2 and 4; ARV2, 11; B. Cohen 1978, 287-290, 355, pl. 58 figs. 2-3; Beazley Addenda 2, 158
artifact.collection_history: The kylix originally belonged in the collection of Henry C. Lea. His son, Arthur H. Lea, gave it to the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1931.
artifact.condit: The surface is worn, chipped and scratched, and there is some discoloration.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: black figure representation of a warrior. A helmeted warrior advances to the right, his body turned forward and his head to the left. His legs are bent and his weight thrown back as he raises his sword above his head getting ready to strike. A shield covers his left side. He is naked but wears a short cloak tied over his shoulders and wears greaves. A red scabbard hangs on his right side. The pommel of the broad, curved sword may be in the shape of a bird or animal head. The warrior's helmet is Corinthian, and is circled by a fillet.

Sides A and B: red figure eyes and palmettes. Large eyes topped by thin eyebrows decorate each side. There is a small nose between the eyes. Palmettes are positioned on either side of the handles.
artifact.shape_description: Type A kylix.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 30-51-2
artifact.summary: Horseman.
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1932, 21, fig. 18; ARV2, 639; Langlotz 1930, pl. 25; Vermeule 1966, 128, fig. 6.
artifact.collection_history: The vase originally was part of the collection of Baron Heyl. Dr. Valentin Mueller purchased it at the Heyl Sale. In 1930, the University Museum, Philadelphia, purchased it from Dr. Mueller.
artifact.condit: Some of the lekythos fragments are in excellent condition, while others are worn and faded; the black glaze on one large fragment toward the back of the vase is completely worn away.
artifact.decoration_description: Horseman. A youth on horseback gallops to the right carrying two spears. The youth rides lightly, his spears resting on his thigh. He is barefoot and wears a chlamys, and a large, rounded pack hangs on his back. His hair is short and thick and he has thick, starlike sideburns. The horse is rearing up slightly, only his back right hoof on the ground, while he looks back at the rider with one eye.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 30-44-4
artifact.summary: Side A: the Departure of Hektor<lb>Side B: departure scene
artifact.other_bibliography: Dubois-Maisonneuve 1817, pl. 63; Tillyard 1923, no. 87, pl. 9; Dohan 1931a, 90-94, pls. 10 and 11; ARV2, 700, 81.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was originally part of the Hope Collection. It was purchased by George Nicole in 1930 for the University Museum.
artifact.condit: The vase is worn and lightly pitted, with the black areas better preserved. The best preserved figures are the messenger on side A and the mother on side B.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: The Departure of Hektor. Hektor bids farewell to Priam and Hecuba, while a man waits to conduct him to battle. Hektor, the focal point of the scene, stands third from the left. He faces forward in a contraposto pose looking to the left toward Priam. He is fully armed, with spear, shield and plumed helmet, and wears a short chiton and a girdle decorated with a zig-zag pattern. The outline of his legs is visible through the lower edge of his garment. Hektor's shield is held on his left side (covering his left shoulder), and he holds his spear upright in his right hand. Hecuba stands on the left side of the scene facing Hektor and holding an oinochoe in her right hand. She is dressed in a chiton and himation, and has her hair tied up with a wide band. Priam stands to Hecuba's right, his head turned toward Hektor. He is shown as a bald, white-haired and white-bearded old man leaning on a tall staff with a cross-piece on top. He wears a long mantle with a black border draped to leave his right arm and shoulder bare. His name is inscribed above his head. A man wearing a chlamys, striped stockings and a soft, pointed hat stands on the far right, holding a spear in an upright position. His wavy hair falls to his shoulders.

Side B: Departure scene. A youth bids farewell to his father and mother. The youth in the center faces forward but turns his head toward his mother on the left. He wears striped stockings, a black-bordered chlamys fastened on his right shoulder, and he holds a spear. A pack hangs behind his left shoulder. The mother occupies the left side of the scene and is wearing a chiton, himation, mantle and a sakkos. She is facing her son and holds a phiale toward him in her outstretched hands. The father, bald and bearded but not white-haired, is on the right and stands facing his son, holding a staff with a cross-piece on the top. He is dressed in a long mantle fastened on his left shoulder.
artifact.inscriptions: Above Priam's head is written: [*P]*I*A*M*O*S, "Priam."
artifact.shape_description: Neck amphora. The amphora has twisted handles.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 30-41-3
artifact.summary: Bands of geometric motifs.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by Georges Nicole for the University Museum, Philadelphia.
artifact.condit: The surface of the vase is worn, abraded and chipped in places.
artifact.decoration_description: Bands of geometric ornament. The very bottom of the kyathos is black and the rest of the body is decorated with bands of dotted circles, dotted diamonds, rows of dots and a checkerboard band, each band set off from the next by triple black lines. A wider band decorated with a meander pattern forms the focal point of the decoration and is located two-thirds of the way up the body. The handle of the kyathos is decorated with crosses separated by triple black lines. The inside rim is decorated with triple black lines.
artifact.shape_description: The kyathos has a high swung handle and tall neck typical of Late Geometric I workshops.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 30-41-2
artifact.summary: Geometric ornament on the body and two (originally three) plastic horses on the lid.
artifact.other_bibliography: Dohan 1930, 14
artifact.collection_history: The pyxis was purchased by Georges Nicole for the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1930.
artifact.condit: There is some wear and discoloration on the surface of the pyxis.
artifact.decoration_description: A band of geometric ornament on the body is divided into panels containing swastikas, meanders, a circle filled with dotted circles, diamonds with hatched outlines and filled with dotted circles, and quatrefoils with small triangles in the spaces created by the arms of the crosses. The bottom of the pyxis is decorated with a large rosette between radiating circles. There is a simple quatrefoil on the interior floor of the pyxis. The two remaining horses from the original three on the lid have black bodies and reserved heads and necks painted with stripes, dot-filled circles and, on either side of the head, a crossed circle.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 30-41-1
artifact.summary: Geometric ornament on the body and four plastic horses on the lid.
artifact.collection_history: The pyxis was purchased by Georges Nicole for the University Museum, Philadelphia, in 1930.
artifact.condit: The surface of the pyxis is worn and faded.
artifact.decoration_description: The body is divided into panels containing meanders, swastikas, checkerboard patterns, herringbone patterns and simple hatching. The bottom of the pyxis is decorated with an elaborate pattern—a curved swastika in the center of radiating circles filled with double lozenges. The effect is flame-like. Four horses stand side-by-side on the lid. They are painted black with reserved rectangular panels on their chests painted with dot-filled diamonds.

artifact.name: Philadelphia 30-4-1
artifact.summary: Upper Body: battle scene. Lower Body: funeral scene. Neck: young warrior and a man holding a sceptre.
artifact.other_bibliography: Univ. Mus. Bull. I, 1930, 15-18, pl. 6-7; Beazley 1932, 5, figs. 1-17; Cat. Sotheby May 27, 1929, pls. 5-6; Seltman 1933, pl. 34a; Felten 1971, 96, fig. 3; Folsom 1976, pl. 43; Beazley Addenda 2, 296, 311
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by the University Museum, Philadelphia, from Charles Seltman in January, 1930.
artifact.condit: The vase is restored from many pieces. The preserved fragments are worn and in some places discolored. There is some pitting of the surface.
artifact.decoration_description:
Upper Body: battle scene. Hoplites fight with cavalry. Two men on horseback gallop to the left, where each is met by a warrior on foot, and two more men fight one another on foot. The first horseman has raised his spear to his shoulder, grasping it in his right hand. He is bearded and wears a petasos and a short cloak. An unbearded warrior lunges at him with raised spear, his back turned toward the viewer. A cloak is flung over his left arm, which is extended behind him, and he wears a high, bulbous helmet. His shield strap can be seen crossing his back diagonally. The two combatants on foot fight in front of this warrior; he is visible between them. One of the warriors, wearing a brimmed helmet and a short cloak, is lunging away from the other warrior, having been pierced by his spear. He casts a last glance behind him before falling onto his knees. The other warrior, in a crested helmet with cheekpieces, stands over him, his right arm raised as he plunges the spear downward. The second horseman rides up behind the first. He has raised his spear to his shoulder, like the first horseman, and grips the reins low on his horse's neck. He is wearing a short cloak and a high, domed helmet and has a pointed beard and a mustache. A naked, bearded warrior moves to meet him, his spear held ready. He carries a shield on his left side, and the scabbard of his sword is visible above his left hip. His shoulder-length hair shows beneath the elaborate, crested helmet he is wearing. This scene is by the Achilles Painter.

Lower Body: funeral scene. Men and youths walk in procession with their right arms extended and palms held out in a gesture of respect or farewell to the dead. The procession begins at a small building with a projecting cornice and a door with riveted cross bars (the tomb?).
