artifact.decoration_description:
The tondo is framed by a labyrinth meander. Inside the frame, a man stands on the left in front of a seated youth. The man's left leg is set slightly behind his weight-bearing right, as he leans on a walking stick. The man, with dark hair and beard, is wearing a wrap that covers his left shoulder and upper arm, his front torso, buttocks and both legs to the calves. With his right hand on his hip, he appears to be talking to the youth, who slumps head down on a stool with rectangular legs. The youth is wrapped from the neck down in heavy drapery. His feet are propped on a foot stool. A piece of athletic equipment appears in the background on the left of the picture.

The lower border of the exterior scenes is marked by a band of palmettes just under the groundline. Side A depicts the archery contest from the story of Herakles and Eurytos. The lower bodies of eight figures are preserved. Herakles stands in an active pose on the far right, recognizable by his lionskin rendered in dilute glaze. On the far right is a draped woman, assumedly Iole, the prize of the contest. In between are six archers, all dressed in animalskin boots laced up around the legs, with spotted decoration at the tops. These men, the sons of Eurytos, wear short chitons and carry scaley quivers (visible on three figures) and bows (seen on two).

On side B, a different contest, probably a pankration, is depicted. Three watchers, preserved in lower body only, are seated on stools to the right, apparently the judges. All are draped to the ankles. The legs of five standing spectators, one a boy, are crowded in front of those on the stools. On the far left are the two naked contestants, seen from the waist down. The contestant on the right is kicking the lefthand figure, a recognized pankration maneuver, which resembled a karate stroke.
artifact.inscriptions: An inscription in the tondo reads *H*E*R*M*O*L*U*K*O*S *K*A*L*O*S (Hermolykos is beautiful). Following it is the signature of the painter, *D*O*R*I*S *E*G*R*A*F*S*E*N. On the foot the potter's signature is written, *K*L*E[*O]*F*R[*A*D*E*S *E*P*O]*I*E*S*E[*N].

artifact.name: Malibu 83.AE.10
artifact.summary: Side A: Judgment of Paris<lb>B: Two Amazons in combat with Greeks
artifact.sources_used: Karl Schefold, "Parisurteil der Zeit Alexanders des Grossen," Greek Vases in the J. Paul Getty Museum 2 (1985): 119-126.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.date_description: The vessel's slender shape argues for a late date.
artifact.decoration_description:
The outer edge of the lip is decorated with an egg-and-dart pattern between two reserved lines. The pattern is repeated as the lower boundary to the scenes on both sides. Above the scene on side A are, from the top, a narrow egg-and-dart pattern between reserved lines, a dot band with another line below it, a broken spiral pattern with dots in the center of each spiral, and the same reserved lines, egg-and-dart band, and dots as seen above the spirals. Above side B are from the top, an egg-and-dart pattern between reserved lines, a band of right-pointing lotuses between lines, the same egg-and-dart pattern, and a band of dots. Below both handles are two superposed palmettes surrounded by elaborate patterns of spiraling tendrils and smaller half palmettes. The base has three parallel grooves, each with a reserved band decorating its upper edge.

On side A, Paris is seated on a rock in the center of the scene with his body frontal and his face inclined toward Athena. He is wearing a belted chiton, arm- and leg-coverings, a mantle with added red color, and a Phrygian cap. He holds a stout club in his left hand, and tree cover is indicated behind him by the presence of a leafy stalk that rises from the ground parallel to the club and emerges from behind his left shoulder. Athena stands to the right and speaks to him in lively fashion, while her right hand gestures. Athena is wearing a chiton with a short peplos over it. The hem of the peplos is in added white; further color has largely worn away. Her skin is white. She has a brown aegis, once golden, decorated with scales. Her shield, with a flamelike device and raised dots around the border, is propped against her legs. Her Corinthian helmet, whose crest breaks through the upper scene border, has an added yellow edge and a metal attachment for the plume. In her left hand she holds a lance. To the left of Paris stands Hera, also posing frontally, with her face bent down at him, clearly already rejected. Like Athena's, her skin is white, and she wears a chiton and a mantle, fastened over her left shoulder. Some of the color is worn off her garments, but a gold stripe down the middle of the chiton remains apparent. Hera is holding a scepter, and she wears an added yellow polos. On the far left, with his face turned toward the other figures and his body frontal, stands a naked Hermes. He holds his kerykeion in both hands, and he has a chlamys fastened around his neck and falling to the back of his knees. On the far right of the scene, behind Athena, are Aphrodite and Eros. Aphrodite stands frontally with her head turned slightly downward to look at Eros, who is walking toward her from the left. She wears a chiton and mantle and an added yellow crown. Eros lifts his arms toward her as if wanting to be picked up.

On side B, a mounted Amazon in the center faces right, where a warrior awaits her offensive. Her horse rears slightly, and a shield with flamelike device lies on the ground beneath its forefeet. The Amazon's skin is white; details of her clothing are difficult to make out, since much of the surface color is obliterated. Her garment is long-sleeved, and a mantle flies out behind her back. Her hair is bound in the rear, and a hairband is visible above her forehead. In her raised right hand she wields a spear aimed at the opponent in front of her. The Greek soldier is depicted from the rear, with his legs planted apart on the ground, his left knee bent slightly to meet the Amazon's onslaught, and his face turned in her direction. He is naked except for a trailing wrap behind his left leg, wound over his shoulders. The top of his head and his shield are largely missing, with only faint traces visible from beneath. The end of his spear emerges on his right side, apparently gripped in his right hand. Behind the horse on the left, a second Amazon follows her leader into battle, stepping to the right with arms upraised. She is wearing a chiton covered by a long-sleeved peplos and spotted leggings. The hem of her chiton is decorated with two horizontal stripes. Her sleeves have a spotted pattern, while her trunk is covered with vertical stripes and waves. Her long curly hair emerges from her helmet, and a quiver is visible on her left side.

artifact.name: Malibu 82.AE.83
artifact.summary: Side A: Aristophanes' Birds. Side B: warrior with woman and old man.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.date_description: Shape and drawing style suggest a date in the later fifth century BC, probably shortly after the production of the Birds in 414 BC.
artifact.comparanda: The closest parallel is the Birds oinochoe, London B 509.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A bearded piper stands frontally between two dancing men dressed as birds. The piper is wearing a chiton decorated with pictures of a charioteer on his left chest, winged horses, deer and hares, crosses, dots, pi shapes and a meander around the skirt. He is playing his double pipes. The bird-men wear large spherical masks in dilute glaze with hooked beaks and combs or crests, tights and wings, spurs at the ankles, shoes, and attached erect phalloi and tails. Their costumes are decorated with circles filled with dots, and solid black circles with traces of added white. White was probably also added to the shoes of the righthand bird-man. Relief contour was used for the righthand man's phallos, face, beak, upper chest, shorts, right leg and spur, and one circle on his hip. For the piper relief contour appears on the left side of the chiton's overfall. Below the scene the pattern band includes two groups of three and one group of two meander squares, each separated by saltires.

Side B: A naked youth is standing, holding a spear in his left hand and Corinthian helmet in yellow brown wash in his right. He is facing an older man in a himation, who holds a curly stick in his right hand. His hair is straggly and long. To the left, a standing woman is wearing a chiton and himation. Her left hand is extended. The groundline for all three figures is a little above the pattern band that runs from handle to handle. The band is made of three groups of three meander squares separated by saltires. A laurel band runs around the whole vase above the scene, right under the lip. Added white was probably used for the laurel stems and relief contour for the back of the shoulders of the man on the right.

artifact.name: Malibu 82.AE.38
artifact.summary: Interior: Seated woman with Peitho and Eros. A: Women in conversation.
artifact.sources_used: Marion True, "A New Meidian Kylix," Greek Vases in the J. Paul Getty Museum 2 (1985): 79-88.
artifact.dimensions: H. 12.4-13 cm., d. 35.5 cm., width with handles 47.2 cm., d. of foot 13.5 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.condit: The remains of five bronze rivets are found in the bowl, as well as two empty holes connected by a deep channel, made for a different repair.
artifact.comparanda: The closest parallel for the floral decoration on this vessel appears on two fragments of a volute krater, Würzburg H4729, attributed to the Pronomos Painter and dated to the same period as the Getty vase. The figure of Demonassa appears on at least two other late red-figure vessels, Florence 81947 (ARV2, 1312, 2) and a fragment of a pyxis in the Agora (J. D. Beazley, "Some Inscriptions on Vases, V," AJA 54 (1950), 320). Both of these vases are dated to the end of the fifth century. The Florence vase is attributed to the Meidias Painter, the pyxis to the Jena Painter.
artifact.decoration_description:
Most of the footplate and underfoot are glazed in black. The tondo is framed by a lefthanded meander pattern between reserved lines. The pattern is broken every three squares by a checkered square with dotted reserved areas. The odd square lies in the upper left side of the circle, with half a meander missing. An empty exergue is separated by a relief line from the three figures sitting and standing above. Behind them fine lines, now mostly obliterated, in added red paint indicated a rocky landscape. A delicate three-branched plant reaches down as far as the exergue.

The woman on the left of the tondo stands in profile facing right, with her left foot raised. She bends forward and gestures with her right hand to the woman sitting in front of her. She is wearing a transparent belted chiton with dark stripes running down the sides. The stripes are oblivious to the folds of her skirt. Behind her back, an extra bunch of cloth appears above the cord that holds her bodice in place. She has a krobylos in her hair, a lozenge-patterned stephane, a necklace and a white earring. The seated central woman is in three-quarter view to the left, with her head slightly bowed. Her left foot is drawn up on a ledge, and her left hand supports her on her rocky seat. With her right hand resting quietly in her lap, she appears to be listening to the first woman's conversation. Like the first woman, she wears a belted chiton fastened with a cord at the shoulders, but hers has sleeves as well. Around her legs is wrapped a himation of thicker, star-patterned material. The lower edge of her chiton has a stripe woven into it, and a second stripe extends irregularly across her midsection. Her hair is bound at the nape of her neck, although part of the back of her head is damaged and not visible. A sort of bun appears on her left temple, and she wears an apicate stephane with a meander decoration, a necklace, bracelet and earring. The third figure is Eros, who stands behind the seated woman on the far right, resting his right hand on her shoulder. He is naked and stands frontally, but both his spread wings and his head are turned toward the two women. The presence of Eros makes it probable that the identity of the standing woman is Peitho, the goddess of Persuasion, advising the seated woman about love. The central woman is identified as Demonassa by an inscription above her head.

The exterior of the vase offers similar scenes on each side, with an interrupted meander, like that of the tondo, running around the bottom of both scenes. Both handle regions are decorated with dense floral patterns--addorsed acanthus-like lotus buds, acanthus leaves, spiraling volutes, ribbed fronds, single fronds, and miniature bulls' eyes--all appearing to grow in natural luxuriance.

On side A six women are depicted, conversing and adorning themselves. Five are standing, while the third from the left is sitting on a klismos. The woman on the far left stands in profile to the right, holding a now faded, added red or white laurel wreath in front of her. The second woman on the left stands facing right as well, with her body frontal and a mirror in her left hand. The next woman sits on the klismos, with her legs and torso facing the two on the left, but her head turned back toward the three women on the right. Her left hand is raised in an empty gesture; her left elbow leans on the chair back. The next two women face each other with their arms raised in conversation, while the woman on the far right stands frontally with her head looking back at the others and her hands outspread, holding a long painted cord, now mostly gone, with tasseled ends. The seated woman and the second woman from the right are wearing transparent chitons wrapped with heavier himatia, while the other four women wear Doric peploi, some girded and some ungirded. The second and third women from the left wear bracelets, while the first on the left has her hair in a sakkos, the third a white painted apicate stephane, and the fourth a series of narrow bands tied around the head, and decorated with little leaves. The fifth woman once had a long fillet in added red tied around her krobylos.

On side B, a similar scene appears. Here the seated woman is third from the right. The first two women on the left are turned frontally, and their heads are turned to face each other in conversation. The first woman places her left hand on the second's shoulder and her right hand on her own hip. The second woman raises her left hand to hold a painted flower, now faded. The third woman faces right and bends over the seated fourth, who faces away from her and gestures with her left hand at the fifth. This figure and the woman on the far right are turned frontally with their heads in profile facing back toward the seated woman. As on side A, four women wear Doric peploi, while the seated woman and the woman on the far right have transparent chitons covered with himatia. The far lefthand woman once had a fillet in her hair, similar to that on side A; the seated woman wears a sakkos, while the far righthand woman has a stephane decorated with a cyma pattern.
artifact.inscriptions: In the tondo appears the neatly lettered name inscription, *D*E*M*W*N*A*S*A*S?. Above the seated woman on side A is an inscription in added red, *K*A*L*H (beautiful). A fragmentary inscription also appears over the heads of the two righthand women on side B, *E *D*A, perhaps referring to the painter, Meidias.

artifact.name: Malibu 82.AE.16
artifact.summary:
Side A: Niobe
Side B: Funerary lekythos within a naiskos surrounded by women making offerings
artifact.other_bibliography: RVAp, 100, no. 20/278a; A. D. Trendall, "An Apulian Loutrophoros representing the Tantalidae," Greek Vases in the Getty 2 (1985), pp. 129-144
artifact.dimensions: H. 98.0 cm., h. to bottom of picture 18.0 cm., h. to joins of handles on shoulder 58.0 cm., h. of neck 37.2 cm., h. of picture 36.5 cm., d. of mouth 21.9 cm., min. d. of body 23.3. cm., d. of foot 16.5 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.condit: There has been some restoration, especially on the reverse and handles. Inside, a plastic tube runs from the foot to the lower neck to strengthen the reconstruction. The foot is pierced.
artifact.comparanda: Other vases representing Niobe include Bonn 99 (Trendall & Cambitoglou 1978, p. 338, no. 13/3) a hydria by the Ganymede Painter (Trendall 1989, ill., 242), and three other vessels--Naples 3246 (Trendall & Cambitoglou 1978, 341, no. 13/22), Taranto 8928 (Trendall & Cambitoglou 1982, 926, no. 28/97, pl. 363,1), and Sydney 71.01 (A. D. Trendall, The Red-figured Vases of Lucania, Campania, and Sicily, Second Supplement (Supplement to the Bulletin of the Institute of Classical Studies of the University of London, 31), London, 1973, p. 223, no. 3/340a, pl. 38, 4).
artifact.decoration_description:
The edge of the lip has an egg and dot pattern between narrow reserved stripes, with yellowish white centers. The underside of the mouth on side A is decorated with laurel and dot clusters and a central rosette; on side B there are rosettes with white tipped petals and dot clusters.

The neck on side A has an egg and dot pattern, with yellowish white centers between narrow reserved relief bands. Under this there are alternating white, yellow and black lozenges, a white scroll on a black band between four narrow reserved stripes, a yellow zigzag against a black background, a yellow bead and reel on a black relief band, the same egg and dot pattern as above, a white swastika meander interspersed with yellow hollow squares with central dots on a black band between reserved stripes, white rays against black between two pairs of reserved stripes, white-centered rosettes with white-tipped petals, dot clusters above two narrow reserved stripes, a winged female figure (to be described below), and eggs between reserved stripes.

The neck on side B has the same egg pattern as on side A, Eros depicted between two reserved stripes (to be described below), a yellow meander on a narrow black band, white dots on a black relief band, a white zigzag on a black band, white-centered eggs between two pairs of reserved stripes, tongues, rosettes and dot clusters between two pairs of reserved stripes, the head of a woman looking left (to be described below) appearing from a campanula in an elaborate leaf setting, tendril spirals, and rosettes above reserved bands and black lines.

The shoulder is decorated with black gadroons. On both sides of the body, above the scenes is an egg and dot pattern, and beneath are a meander interrupted by crossed squares with dots and black gadroons. The handles are white bordered, with white diamonds in the center of the buds that form the handle terminations. Under both handles are two enclosed palmette fans superposed with a palmette fan above, as well as smaller palmette fans and side scrolls. A reserved band circles the vessel where the body and foot join. The underside of the foot is reserved.

On side A, a mourning Niobe is pictured in the upper register and Pelops and Hippodamia in the lower register. At the center of the upper register is a tomb monument; within it Niobe standing semi-frontally, in a mourning pose. Her head is inclined to the right, and she supports it with her left hand. She is wearing a peplos and a cloak pulled up over her and right arm. With her left hand she holds part of it. She has a necklace with a single white pendant and a bracelet. Her lower dress is in added white, typical of many scenes of Niobe before petrification. Four columns with white Ionic capitals support the tomb monument. The shafts are white with dilute glaze flutes, and the pediment has white floral akroteria and a black gable with a disk and a small floral pattern in white. The ceiling beams are reserved in white with white outlines. Niobe is standing between two white loutrophoroi with dilute glaze details. The lefthand vessel is of Type I with an ovoid body, while the righthand one is of Type II with a barrel shape. Both have lids and s-shaped handles. On either side of the monument two attendants wear short-sleeved chitons with single stripes down the front. They are also wearing mantles, stephanai, ribboned kekryphaloi, earrings, bracelets, double strand necklaces, and white shoes. The far lefthand woman is standing three-quarters right; her left hand reaches for the drapery on her shoulder, as does her neighbor, standing three-quarters left. The two women to the right of the monument stand facing each other, the first holding a phiale with spray and dot cluster. The second has a wreath in her right hand. Above them on a white dotted ground line are a white lyre and tall kalathos with a ball of wool on top.

In the lower register, Pelops and Hippodamia are riding left in a quadriga. Pelops is in Oriental dress, with long white-dotted purple sleeves and circles and rays as decoration, a Phrygian cap decorated in added white, two shoulder cords and a white-studded belt. Hippodamia wears the same jewelry as the others, a tall crown with a row of white beads on top and yellow and white bands and black dots on the bottom. Her sleeveless, beltless chiton has white dot-clusters as decoration, and she is holding part of her cloak in her left hand. The horses' lower hind legs and hoofs are white, as are the forelegs of the righthand trace horse. The bridles are dotted with white, and the reins are in added red, also used for the chariot rail and body. The chariot wheels and axle are white.

The neck on side A has the upper half of a winged female in added white and yellow. She emerges from an elaborate floral setting, wearing a crown with a row of white beads at the top, a necklace, a dilute glazed double bandolier, and bracelets. Her hair is in shades of dilute glaze, as are her facial features, and her wing details. She is holding the ends of the tendrils of the flower that is under her.

On side B, both upper and lower register belong to the same scene, five women at a shrine. Each woman wears a short-sleeved chiton with a ribbon and a single stripe down the front, a stephane, a ribboned kekryphalos, a double-stranded bead necklace, a double-coil bracelet on each arm, and shoes. The upper righthand woman also has a himation diagonally draped. In the upper register are two women standing on either side of a naiskos. Inside it are a white marble lekythos and two fillets. The upper lefthand woman holds a mirror in her right hand and leans her elbow on a dotted support. The righthand woman is holding a patera in her left hand and a cista in her right, decorated with white zigzag and meander patterns and a small spray on top. In the lower register are the other three women. The one on the left is holding an open box in her right hand. Her body is seated pointing left, but her head looks right at the center woman who looks back at the lefthand one, and rests her right hand on her shoulder. She is holding a mirror in her left hand. On the right, the woman stands facing left, leaning forward with raised right leg and right foot resting on a rock. In her right hand is a wreath, and a ball of wool hangs by a ribbon from her left. On either side of the naiskos above are two ribboned fillets with white edges, while below is an open box, phiale, and flowering plant.

On the neck of side B, Eros stands above facing left, with a mirror in his right hand and a white fillet in his left. He is wearing a stephane, a kekryphalos and hair ribbon, a double-stranded necklace, a bandolier, thigh and ankle bracelets, and shoes. The edges and other details on his wings are in added white. In front of him are a fillet, a rosette, a branch, and a small plant. Behind is a flowering plant. On the lower part of the neck is the head of a woman with a left profile. She is wearing a kekryphalos with a bunch of hair emerging, a white stephane, a white earring, and a white beaded necklace.
artifact.shape_description: The mouth is broad with an overhanging lip. The neck is long and narrow with a relief band less than halfway down. Relief gadroons appear on the shoulder. The cylindrical body is slightly concave, with relief gadroons at the bottom. The pedestal foot edge is in three degrees. The handles are elaborate s-shapes which end in scrolls and buds.

artifact.name: Malibu 82.AE.14
artifact.summary: Tondo: Reclining girl playing kottabos
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.decoration_description: Interior: A naked hetaira reclines facing right, while playing kottabos with a large skyphos. There is a kalos inscription in the field around her head. Side A: A reclining hetaira is playing castanets, while a youth in front of her holds a large skyphos, offering it to her. Another youth behind her is dancing. Side B: Three naked revelers dance; the central figure is playing castanets.
artifact.inscriptions: There is a kalos inscription on the interior.

artifact.name: Malibu 81.AE.83
artifact.summary: Shoulder: birds, quadrupeds, spirals. Body: antelope frieze above, deer frieze below, floral ornaments at base.
artifact.other_bibliography: Handbook of the Collections, 1986, p. 46
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.collection_history: Ex Miletos. Other pieces of the same lot were sold to Richmond.

artifact.name: Malibu 81.AE.78
artifact.summary: Side A: Europa on the bull<lb>Side B: Dionysos with satyrs and maenads.
artifact.other_bibliography: M. Jentoft-Nilsen, "A Krater by Asteas," Greek Vases in the Getty 1 (1983), pp. 139-148, figs. 1-4; O. Taplin, Greek Fire (London, 1989), p. 67, p. 66 (ill.); E. Zahn, Europa und der Stier (Würzburg, 1983), p. 122, no. 66; Trendall 1987, p. 85, no. 2/129, pls. 49-51a, and pp. 92-94; Trendall 1989, pp. 200-201, figs. 349-350; LIMC, III, s. v. "Eros," p. 933, no. 1013; LIMC, IV, s. v. "Europe I," p. 80, no. 74, pl. 38.
artifact.dimensions: H. 71.0 cm., d. of mouth 61.0 cm., h. of foot 21.0 cm., d. of foot 29.0 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.condit: Parts of the rim are restored.
artifact.comparanda: The krater most comparable to this in shape is in San Antonio (see Trendall 1987, pp. 84-85, 90-92, no. 128, pl. 48). The foot is close in shape and pattern to another, probably also by Asteas (see Trendall 1987, p. 92, 2/129A, pl. 51b). Other Dionysiac scenes by Asteas are seen on Naples 3412, Madrid 11094, San Antonio 275, and Naples 3226.
artifact.decoration_description:
The top of the rim is decorated with ivy leaves and white flowers, now flaked, on an incised stem. The side of the rim holds reserved ivy leaves running to the right, with veins showing up in dilute glaze, as well as dotted berry-like rosettes in added white on an incised stem. On side A below the main scene, alternating black and reserved squares form a metope pattern between reserved lines; the cul holds a floral pattern in applied yellow and white, now mostly obliterated, of tendrils, flowers and buds connected to a central palmette flanked by scrolls. To the right and left the floral pattern ends in an "Asteas flower." Beneath the floral pattern are eggs between two narrow reserved lines. On side B the cul is better preserved; between reserved lines, white ivy leaves and berry clusters on an incised stem face the center, where a campanula divides the righthand train from the left. The overhanging lip on the stem has tongues separated by black lines ending in a white dot. On the foot, on both sides, are griffins chasing horses to the left. Below, reserved ivy leaves and white berry-rosettes on an incised stem are mostly flaked off. The lower edge and underside of the foot are reserved.

On side A, vertical reserved bands and a white capital at the top define the edge of the main picture. Two diagonal bands, their lower edges white, separate the upper corners into triangular scenes and make the main scene pentagonal. In this area, Europa on the bull is depicted. Europa sits on its white back, as it flies left over the sea, shown by figures of Scylla, Triton, and several marine creatures. Europa is dressed in a chiton, held at the waist by a studded girdle, and with a row of white beads running down each sleeve. The chiton is decorated with palmettes, stars, meanders, and a checkerboard pattern at the lower edges. Europa holds a shawl in her left hand; it is wrapped over her right arm and blows out behind her with fine black dots in its design. Her shoulder-length hair, shown in relief with a dilute glaze, is in ringlet curls. She has an earring, a necklace of white pendants, a bracelet on each arm, and sandals. The bull is rendered in added white, with flaked-off patches. Its anatomical details are in shades of dilute glaze, and the pupil in its eye a large black dot.

To the left of the bull, Scylla is shading her eyes as she stares at it. Her hair resembles Europa's in dilute glaze. Her upper body is naked except for a white pendant bead necklace. Her lower body is a sea monster's, with two dogs in added white and dilute glaze, emerging from the front. The sea monster portion is covered in white scales with black outlines, as well as a row of sharp spines projecting along the upper edge. The lower edge has markings in dilute glaze. The rest of the body, with its forked tail, is decorated in black circles filled with white. Scylla holds a trident, whose prongs and shaft bottom are in added white.

Behind the bull, Triton is holding an oar in his left hand, while in his right is a small octopus in dilute glaze . Its eyes in white and black, it curls its tentacles around his forearm. Triton's body is covered with black circular scales; his other features are in added red and white. His tail is forked like Sylla's, but its top edge is red.

A naked Pothos, the personification of passionate desire, hovers over Europa. His wings are almost completely worn away, but were in added white with details in dilute glaze. Wearing a white wreath, a white beaded bandolier, white bracelets on wrist and left ankle, shoes, and a mantle in added red with white dots, he holds a small, mostly obliterated spray in his right hand and in his left a small circlet of white beads, also mostly gone now, and a phiale in white and metal-like dilute glaze. Seventeen marine animals, including an octopus, torpedoes, dogfish, and striped bass, fill the lower field. They are in added white with details in dark yellow.

Three figures gaze down from each triangular frame. To the left, a knee-length figure of Zeus and busts of Crete and Hermes fill the space. Zeus holds a scepter with a white palmette tip in his right hand, and he wears a cloak embroidered with stars, palmettes, circles and a checkerboard-pattern border. Crete, who represents the island where Europa will be taken, is wearing a bandeau in added red and a chiton decorated like Zeus's. Palmettes are added on the sleeves, as well as a studded white girdle. The back of her head is covered by a piece of drapery. She has a diadem, earring, necklace, and bracelets in added white. Hermes is wearing a wreath, a chlamys fastened at the throat by a brooch, and a petasos, mostly obliterated, behind his back. He is holding a kerykeion in his right hand. The brooch, wreath, and end of the kerykeion are white.

Looking down from the left triangle are busts of Eros and Adonis, as well as a knee-length figure of Aphrodite. Eros's wings were in added white, mostly lost now. A reddish brown drapery piece covers the lower part of his body, and in his right hand is an unidentified object. The effeminate Adonis has long curling tresses in dilute glaze, as well as a long-sleeved chiton with embroidered circles, stars, and palmettes. White beads and black dots between white lines run down the sleeves. A cloak with fine lines and a checkerboard border is seen over his left arm and lower body. With his left hand on his hip, he extends his right arm. Aphrodite, with added white flesh, has her right hand on his shoulder. Her chiton has stars and a broad added-red stripe down the front, while her himation is patterned with circles and a checkerboard edge. She also wears a white diadem, a headband in added red with a white dot pattern, an earring and a necklace of pendants in dilute glaze.

Side B is a Dionysiac scene. Horizontal and vertical reserved bands frame the picture, including a horizontal band about one third of the way down, dividing the scene into a main lower and a smaller upper panel. Capitals in added white adorn the upright bands, the left-hand side largely gone. In the main scene Dionysos in the center, a maenad and a satyr are all moving to the right. The maenad wears a short-sleeved chiton with dot-clusters and dot-stripes and an overfall, and with white beads down the sleeves, and a spotted fawn skin in dilute glaze. She has a white wreath, a white bead necklace, two white bracelets and shoes with white dots. She holds a yellow torch with a red flame in her left hand and a second wreath in her right. Dionysos is naked except for a mantle with dot-stripe edges, a fillet in dilute glaze, tied in a bow at the back and decorated with black dots and white ivy leaves, a bandolier of white beads and shoes with white dots. In his left hand he has two eggs in added white; in his right is a white thyrsos with a red fillet tied near the top. On the far right, in front of Dionysos, is a satyr wearing a white wreath, a white beaded bandolier, and shoes with white edges. His tail is drawn with thin stripes of black over a dilute glaze wash. From his left hand hangs a red fillet, while with that hand he holds a phiale with eggs. In his right hand is a thyrsos like Dionysos's.

In the smaller upper panel are five half-length figures: a papposilen in the center with two maenads to one side and a third maenad and Pan on the other. The three maenads are dressed identically to the maenad in the main scene, except that the far left maenad's chiton is sleeveless. This one looks to the right and holds a bell in her left hand and a phiale in her right. The next maenad turns her head back toward the first and holds a flaming yellow torch in her left hand. The papposilen, with white dots suggesting hair tufts on his body, wears a fawn skin and fillet in added red. His hair, beard, and the white of his eye are white. In his left hand he holds a red tambourine with a black center. The third maenad is looking toward him, with a thyrsos tied with a red fillet in her left hand and a bell in her right. Pan, leading the procession, has diluted glaze dots to show hair on his body; he is wearing a white wreath. In his left hand he holds white cymbals and in his right a white bead circlet. His hip is covered in a wash of dilute glaze.
artifact.inscriptions: On side A, Europa, Scylla, Triton, and Pothos are each labelled, *E*U*R*W*P*H, *S*K*U*L*A, *T*R*I*T*W*N, and *P*O*Q*O*S. In the triangular frames above the main scene, Zeus, Crete, and Hermes are labelled on the left--*Z*E*U*S, *K*R*H*T*H, and &epig-rough;*E*R*M*H*S--and Adonis and Aphrodite on the right--*A*D*O*N*I*S and *A*F*R*O*D*I*T*H.
artifact.shape_description: The vessel has a flaring mouth and overhanging lip. The elongated, slightly concave body has an offset band at the top. The handles are set high and curve upward, turning sharply in at the top. On the stem is a relief band between two thin reserved grooves. Where the stem meets the foot is a wide overhanging lip. Another relief band is seen between two reserved grooves on the stem's outward curve toward the foot. The foot has three portions, with a flange at the top. The upper most portion is reserved, as is the groove where it joins the edge of the stem.

artifact.name: Malibu 81.AE.220
artifact.summary: Peleus and Thetis.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.decoration_description: On the fragments, Peleus and Thetis are pictured.

artifact.name: Malibu 81.AE.213
artifact.summary: Fragments. Uncertain.
artifact.sources_used: M. Robertson, 1991, "A fragmentary phiale by Douris", in Greek Vases in the J. Paul Getty Museum 5: 75-98.
artifact.other_bibliography: H. Luschey, 1939, Die Phiale, Bleicherode; Perachora I, (chapter by T. J. Dunbabin); T. J. Dunbabin, 1951, in Papers presented to A. J. B. Wace, BSA 46: 61-71; B. Freyer-Schauenburg, E. Bouml;hr and W. Martini, eds., Studien zur Mythologie und Vasenmalerei: Festschrift für Konrad Schauenburg, Mainz, pp. 115-120; M. Robertson in Cambitoglou 1979, 131.
artifact.dimensions: Orig. d. ca. 42 cm., h. of bowl 4.5 cm. h. of omphalos 4.0 cm., d. of omphalos hollow 5.2 cm., interior h. 2.2 cm., h. of spiral frieze 1.5 cm., h. of figured frieze 9.9 cm., h. of rim band 2.2 cm.; exterior h. of broad frieze 4.0 cm., h. of narrow frieze 2.5 cm., h. of figured frieze 12.0 cm., h. of rim band 0.7 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.graffiti: A very small fragment of an interior scene shows a woman lifting her veil; its black exterior has the roughly scratched *U*T, from the Etruscan word SUTIL, apparently of a dedicatory nature.
artifact.decoration_description:
All the fragments' exteriors depict males in chitoniskoi. Each had a quiver, or gorytos, hanging on the thigh, and each was holding a Scythian bow. Two are clearly bearded, and none of the others is certainly clean-shaven. Two wear lionskins over their chitoniskoi and are taken to be Herakles in two separate, but related scenes. One of the Herakles figures is standing upright, while the other is squatting, with only his lower half preserved. The legs of two other squatters are also preserved, as well as the arms and hands of a figure who must have been in this position. The interior scenes on these fragments suggest that all of the squatters, thought to be drawing their bows, were concentrated in one area. By the same logic, the standing figures, taken to be stringing or reaching for their bows, should belong to a different scene. Frel has suggested that the two scenes are of the archery contest of Herakles with Eurytos and his sons, the first a preparation, the second the contest itself.

The interior is reconstructed into three scenes: an assembly of seated gods, a combat depiction, and running figures. The latter scene shows three figures hurrying to the right and overlapping one another. In the back is the lower half of a woman, her right leg stretched back, her left foot and hand forward and raised up. She is wearing a chiton, himation, and red bracelet. Just in front of her another woman is running, preserved except for the back of her hair, her right shoulder and upper arm, the fingers of her left hand and her left foot. Her dress and body position are identical to the first woman. She has a bracelet on each arm and a stephane on her light hair. Both her hands are raised. Overlapping her in front is a man wearing a himation. He is preserved from neck to waist, and his right foot is also visible, in the same position as the other runners. His arms, preserved below the elbows, are reaching forward, and his long fair hair hangs over his neck and back.

The righthand figure in the combat scene, stepping to the left, overlaps the rear figure of the scene just described. This figure wears a chiton and himation similar to those of the running women. The head and shoulders are not present, and nor is the left arm, but the wrist and hand are shown holding a bow. The bow is of Greek form. The right arm in its long chiton sleeve reaches forward, but the forearm and hand are missing. This figure is taken to be Apollo. The second figure is that of a collapsing warrior, with left foot and lower left leg bent sharply forward, part of the thigh, buttock and hip and some of the belly and back, left arm and hand holding a slipping shield. Red blood is visible on the belly. A spear is seen extending above the lower leg, its point touching Apollo's shin. Behind the warrior is Athena, preserved throughout much of her midsection in chiton, himation, and snake-fringed aegis, her right arm with its red bracelet raised forward, her left arm (also with red bracelet) reaching forward below the next figure's arm. In the black area behind Athena flies a miniature Nike, with traces of her chiton and arms preserved. The left arm is concealed by the right with its red bracelet, but both hands are shown, holding a red wreath for the victor of the fight. This last figure, the victorious warrior, is preserved frontally in his lower torso, left thigh forward and right knee back, and the elbow of his right arm raised for a spear thrust. Below his arm flies the crest of his helmet. An inscription fragment identifies this figure as Achilles. Parts of both his and the falling hero's helmets, as well as that belonging to Athena, are preserved on separate fragments. The falling hero apparently has a Corinthian helmet, while Achilles has only a bit of the front of his helmet crest present. Athena's helmet is Chalcidian.

In the assembly-of-deities scene, all surviving figures' knees and feet point to the right, but four heads turn back to the left. All figures are fragmentary, with the righthand end of the group preserved, but not the left. The far righthand figure is labelled Ares, and it is expected that Aphrodite accompanied him in the second position. All figures seem to have had names written beside them, except a child on one goddess's knees. Besides Ares and Aphrodite, the other deities are preserved in two groups, but there is no way to connect these to either end of the whole scene. The forehead of one black-haired deity in an ivy wreath is accompanied by an ivy branch and a fragmentary name identifying him as Dionysos. He looks to the right. A seated figure to his left, the only fully preserved figure, is a female with frontal torso and left hand placed on her right thigh. This is apparently Amphitrite, identified by a small inscription fragment that fits close to her. She is dark-haired, looking over her shoulder, with her left hand on her thigh and her right lifting a cloak from her shoulder in front of her face. Overlapping her to the left are the knees and hands of another figure holding a long staff, which slopes across its skirt. All deities in this scene wear similar long chitons and himations, but the females have red bracelets on either arm as well. Since this figure's arms are bare, it must be male. Since Amphitrite usually accompanies her husband in this kind of scene, the figure to her left is taken to be Poseidon. His staff probably ended in a trident head. Another separate fragment of the scene shows a head with blond hair and beard, looking left, accompanied by the name Plouton. Next to this inscription comes the head of a goddess looking left and part of her arm encased in a patterned garment. Across her arm are grain ears, apparently held in her left hand, and to her right is the name Demeter. A different fragment, paired with this one by its exterior scene, gives more of Plouton's arm and Demeter's garment spread over her stool seat. Yet a different fragment shows the head and torso of a blond goddess in transparent chiton, with accompanying inscription of Kore. Two small hands reach across her breast; evidently a child is seated in her lap. Although all of these fragments cannot be certainly fit together, the three Eleusinians should have sat together, accompanied to the right by Poseidon, Amphitrite, and Dionysos. Besides these deities and Ares and Aphrodite on the far right, there is no certain evidence for others, although several other tiny fragments of torsos, as well as a lion-footed stool, might still be fit into this scene, if not into the running figures scene.
artifact.inscriptions:
The exterior bears one fragmentary inscription, part of a name followed by *E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N.

On the interior of another fragment is the inscription *A*Q]*E*N*A*I*A. Behind Athena, in a blank area, is visible the end of a himation and the name *A*R*E[*S. Another inscription is seen between the hero's thighs in the combat scene, *D*O*R*I*S, and on a nearby fragment the verb *E*G*R*A*F*S]*E*N. In front of the same hero's helmet are the letters *A*X[*I*L*L*E*U*S, thus identifying this figure.

In the assembly-of-deities scene, a fragment of a dark-haired deity in a wreath bears the letters *D*I*O[*N*U*S*O*S, with more letters belonging to the goddess next to him, *A*M*F[*I*T*R*I*T*H. A fragment of a blond god shows the name *P*L*O*U*T*O*N, and to his right, the name *D*E*M[*E*T*E*R. A fragment of a goddess with a child on her lap is labelled *K]*O*R*E.

Two other fragments, with uncertain positions on the interior, show unidentified name segments. One contains only the letter *O, while another has the letters *D*E*S.

artifact.name: Malibu 77.AE.13
artifact.summary:
Side A: Orpheus playing in Hades
Side B: Deceased in Naiskos
artifact.other_bibliography: See CVA for extensive bibliography.
artifact.dimensions: H. restored 89.0 cm., d. of mouth 54 cm., d. of body 52.5 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.collection_history: Gift of Mr. Gordon McLendon.
artifact.comparanda: For representations of the underworld on Apulian vases, see M. Pensa, 1977, Rappresentazioni dell'oltretomba nella ceramica apula, Rome; K. Schauenburg, 1984, Unterweltsbilder aus Grossgriechenland, Römische Mitteilungen 91: 359-387. For the Herakleidai, see LIMC, IV, pp. 723-728.
artifact.decoration_description:
The side of the lip on side A is decorated with an egg pattern, the eggs with white centers. Under the lip is a band of palmettes and a reverse wave in black on white. The neck on side A has a berried laurel wreath with alternating added red and white leaves and a central rosette, and a white female head crowned with a polos emerging in three-quarter view from a campanula in an elaborate floral design. On the shoulder is a palmette and lotus pattern, with an egg pattern below. On side B, the side of the lip displays an egg pattern, and under the lip is a wave above a black band. On the neck is a laurel wreath to the right, while below are three palmette fans with half fans above between them. The shoulder on side B has a tongue pattern above and an egg pattern below. Below the main scene on both sides, part of a meander pattern is preserved, interrupted with quartered and dotted squares. Under each handle are superposed palmette fans with scrolls underneath and enclosed palmette fans above. Below the handle joins are half palmette fans. The blinkers on side A show added white, red and yellow floral scroll work; those on side B are missing.

Side A depicts an underworld scene. Persephone and Pluto are sitting in their palace on a white couch. The couch details and the footrest below it are in added red. Persephone is wearing a chiton, with an embroidered panel in front, and a cloak over her lower body. She holds in her right hand a cross bar torch with infibula. Her long hair is in ringlets over her shoulders, and a veil covers the back of her head. Pluto, with his head turned to the right, wears a longsleeved chiton, some of its details in added red. With his left arm he leans on a cushion, while in his right hand he holds an eagle-tipped scepter. From the ceiling beams, greaves, a helmet, a shield, and a cuirass are hanging. These objects are all in added white and yellow, the cuirass with added red flaps and interior lining. On the upper left, Hermes is seated on a rock pile, wearing a cloak fastened at the throat by a brooch, a petasos, and high-laced sandals with open toes. In his right hand he is holding his caduceus, its top missing, and in his left he has an M-handled hydria with a flowering plant below it. Hekate stands below, holding a flaming torch with attached infibula in each hand. A panther skin is knotted around her shoulders, its interior in added red and its exterior white with spots in dilute glaze. In addition, she is wearing a longsleeved garment in added red, red pants, and a diadem. On the upper right, Megara sits on a pile of rocks, flanked by two Herakleidai. The one on the left is naked with a white fillet around his head and a white bandage around his thigh. The one on the right is partly draped, with a white belt and fillet. Megara is dressed like Persephone. Below the trio stands Orpheus, wearing a longsleeved garment with an embroidered panel in front, a mantle, and a Phrygian cap. In his left hand he holds a kithara, and in his right is the plektron. In front of the palace three draped women are seated, wearing white saccoi. Next to each one is an M-handled hydria. The one on the left is holding a phiale in her right hand and a fan in her left, while the central figure holds a fan in her left hand, and the righthand figure has a dish in her right hand. Phialai are visible in the fields between Megara and Orpheus. In the field above Megara is a phiale with looped infibula and an ivy leaf.

On side B, a youth in added white is seated on a piece of drapery in a naiskos to the right. He is looking over his shoulder to the left. In his left hand he is holding a phiale with offerings. A petasos is hanging down his back. There is a shield behind him, a window and a ball to the upper left, two fillets to the right, and two flowers below. To either side of the naiskos are two draped women, the one on the left holding a phiale and fillets, the other with a fan and a bunch of grapes. In the field to the left is a phiale, to the right a fillet, and in the corner above, a bunch of grapes. The base of the naiskos shows a band of white vine leaves on a red background, with a row of white dots on black above it.
artifact.shape_description: The flanged parts of the handles have blinkers.

artifact.name: Malibu 77.AE.11
artifact.summary: On neck: Side A: Herakles and Amazons; Labors of Herakles. Side B: arming scene
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.collection_history: Previously in the collection of Gordon McLendon. Four fragments of this vase are in the Louvre, formerly in collection of the Marquis Campana, acquired in 1869.
artifact.decoration_description:
The body of the krater is black. On both sides of the neck are miniaturist friezes in two registers.

Side A, upper register: Amazonomachy, of which only the right and central parts are preserved. To right, three pairs of Amazons (two archers and four hoplites) defend a fallen Amazon against Herakles. Herakles grasps the hair of the fallen Amazon and prepares to stab her with his sword. He wears a lion skin and carries a sword in his right hand. The Amazons are dressed as Greek hoplites, with round shields (devices include a centaur), spears, cuirass, and crested helmets. They stride to left towards the hero, spears and bows upraised. To the left, Telamon fights a group of Amazons, one of whom is on her knees before him, raising her spear and shield. Telamon lifts his shield (device: a horse) and sword to strike the fallen Amazon. The left side of the frieze is hardly preserved; an Amazon carrying a wounded companion is preserved at the far left.

Side A, lower register: three labors of Herakles. At the far right, Atlas stands holding the heavens. Before him is the apple tree of the Hesperides, protected by the dragon Ladon. Herakles approaches from the left, wielding his club, to pluck the apple. He is naked except for his lionskin. Athena his protectress is partly preserved behind him, facing to the left toward his next labor. In the center of the frieze (a large part of which is missing), Herakles battles the triple-bodied Geryon (of whom only the three forward feet are preserved). Behind him, Herakles has already killed the double-bodied dog Orthos and shepherd Eurythion. At the left of the frieze, Herakles and Iolaos battle the Hydra. Only Herakles' foot is preserved, framing the register. Iolaos attacks the Hydra from the right, burning the severed stumps of its heads as Herakles cut them off. He carries a shield with a winged Pegasos as a device. On the rim is a maeander pattern.

Side B, upper register: Amazons preparing for battle. At the left side, five Amazons test their weapons and begin to arm themselves, holding greaves, shields, spears, and helmets; one tests an arrow with her finger, another prepares to put on a helmet, another puts on her greaves. Shield devices include a triskeles and a chimaera (?). At the center of the scene, three Amazons lead their horses to the right. The Amazons are armed and carry two spears. Four running Amazons to the right follow a trumpeter (at the far right, fragments preserved in the Louvre) into battle: they are on foot but a horse runs with them.

Side B, lower register: Peleus wrestling Thetis, with onlookers. The central part of the scene is poorly preserved, but Thetis has taken the form of a snake, and Peleus wrestles her. To the left, Chiron watches over his pupil Peleus; he will also be the teacher of Peleus' and Thetis' son Achilles. The centaur carries an elm branch over his shoulder. At the far left of the scene stands Doris, Thetis' mother (the fragment preserving Doris' head is in the Louvre). Two Nereids flee towards her; they wear long himations and mantles. The scene is framed on the right by Thetis' father Nereus, who sits on a stool, holding a staff in his right hand; two more Nereids, one holding a fish, flee towards him.

On the neck, a maeander pattern appears, slightly different from that on Side A. Under the handles are palmettes. On the volutes are linked spirals.

artifact.name: Malibu 77.AE.102
artifact.summary: Anakreon between eyes. Roosters by handle, plastic head on handle.
artifact.sources_used: Kurtz, D. C. and J. Boardman, 1986, "Booners," Greek Vases in the J. Paul Getty Museum, vol. 3, pp. 35-70
artifact.other_bibliography: Haspels 1936, 88-89, 173; B. Cohen 1978, 247, 250, 275; ABV, 697; Higgins 1967, 72
artifact.dimensions: H. to rim (restored) 6.88 cm., h. to handle (preserved) 9.63 cm., max. d. of bowl 9.5 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.condit: The foot has been restored in an inverted echinus shape.
artifact.comparanda: The embattlement pattern on the rim is closely paralleled on fragments of a white-ground kyathos, Heidelberg 263, almost certainly by the same artist. The eyes on this vessel, too, though very incompletely preserved, strongly resemble those on the Getty vase.
artifact.decoration_description:
The interior, handle, and lower portion of the bowl exterior are black. The outside of the rim has an unusual embattlement pattern with five small dots in the intervals, done in black on white ground between fine lines.

Large eyes separate the central figure from those at the handles. The eyes, though incompletely preserved, are relatively small and elongated, with the outer corners pointing upward and long, curving tear ducts. The strongly curved outlines of the eyes are executed in white paint, added over the white ground. The outer ring of the eye is red, while the next, equal in size is painted white. Probably there was a central black area with a small red pupil.

The cocks, while not completely preserved, are rendered in great detail. The eye and beak are incised, while comb and wattle are in added red, with carefully depicted points and blade of the comb. The throat has a strong convex curve, while the hackle bears white dots, its lower feathers indicated in incised points. Each wing feather has an incised outline and a dot of red paint. The long flight feathers probably appeared in two layers, set apart by a scalloped line of incision with added white paint. Four or five long saddle feathers were incised in outline, while two long sickle feathers were painted black. The tail feathers are rendered similarly to the flight feathers, with the same scalloped incision. The color of the two cocks' tail feathers differs; every other feather on the lefthand cock is red, those of the righthand cock white. Each cock faces the handle.

The komast in the center of the scene has an unusual costume that covers much of his body. The remaining parts are rendered in little anatomical detail. His head appears too large for his body, partly because of the mitra wrapped around it, and partly because of his extensive projecting hair and beard growth. The hair and beard are painted red. The komast's eye is large, low, and carefully incised, and his nose is straight. His short-sleeved chitoniskos has buttonholes drawn, but no buttons. Its collar is white, and its hem is dotted white. The skirt folds are broadly spaced, curvy incised lines. His boots are red, laced around the ankles and given prominent tongues. His upper and lower limbs have few details except the open incised loop of the kneecap. He is holding in both hands a lyre with swan-head terminals.

The face and neck of the molded female on the kyathos handle are painted white. A red band with white dots holds her long, red brown, wavy hair away from her face. Three tresses hang behind each ear, and her curly bangs are shown by a single row of raised dots. Her eyes and eyebrows have the same color as her hair. Her lips are undefined.
artifact.shape_description: The wall of the bowl is thin and gently curved, slightly similar to the calyx shape of kyathoi by Psiax. Generally, however, the bowl is lower and broader than those of Psiax, closer to vases by the Hanfmann Painter. Only the presence of the molded female head on the handle is atypical of the Hanfmann Painter.

artifact.name: Malibu 72.AE.128
artifact.summary: Transformation of Kallisto
artifact.other_bibliography: See CVA for extensive bibliography.
artifact.dimensions: H. with handle 16.8 cm., d. of mouth 8.4 cm., d. of body 12.8 cm., d. of foot 8.6 cm.
artifact.collection: Malibu, The J. Paul Getty Museum
artifact.date_description: The style is early "Ornate" Apulian.
artifact.condit: Black glaze on the interior has flaked off in places and worn away in others, so that the red wash beneath is visible. There is incrustation under the handles and on the underside of the foot.
artifact.comparanda: For the subject of Kallisto's transformation, see A. Stenico, 1977, Kallisto, in Numismatica e antichità classiche: Quaderni ticinesi 6: 73-86; R. Arena, 1979, Considerazioni sul mito di Kallisto, Acme. Annali della Facoltà di Filosofia e Lettere dell'Università Statale 32: 5-26; L. Rossi, 1981, Ceramiche apule nel Museo di Cremona, Bari, p. 31, no. 43, pls. 15-17; Trendall & Cambitoglou 1983, p. 21; LIMC, II, s. v. "Arkas," with bibliography; LIMC, forthcoming, s. v. "Kallisto". Also see P. Shepard and B. Sandars, 1985, The Sacred Paw, New York, chap. 5.
artifact.decoration_description:
Around the neck extends a band of enclosed, upright palmettes between two reserved lines, all discontinued under the handle. Below the handle are superposed palmettes emerging from an acanthus-leaf base and palmette fans enclosed by side scrolls. Added white is used for some leaves on saplings in the palmette design, as well as for terminals on the scrolls. Beneath the picture zone, a meander pattern is interrupted by squares with different saltire types and a star pattern. The underside of the foot is reserved.

On the body, the transformation of Kallisto is pictured. Kallisto, with star-spangled drapery covering her legs is seated on a skin-covered rock to the right, with two trees and smaller saplings growing behind her. Kallisto is wearing hunting boots, and her right leg is bent beneath her. Her right hand is resting on the rock, with two spears placed next to it. Both her hands are in the process of changing into paws, and fur appears on her face and arms. To the right Hermes is lifting up the naked infant Arcas. Hermes is wearing a chlamys and petasos, and his caduceus leans against a stele behind him. Behind Kallisto, a young hunter is striding to the left, while looking at her. He is naked except for a chlamys over his shoulders and wrapped around his arms, and a pilos on his head. He is carrying a spear.

This depiction refers to the myth of the nymph Kallisto, a friend of Artemis and beloved by Zeus. In one version of the story, she bore him the infant Arcas, the father of the Arcadians. In a different version, a jealous Hera changed her into a bear, while in a third version, Zeus changed her into a bear to protect her from Hera's jealous ire. Later accidentally killed by Artemis, she was placed by Zeus among the constellations.
artifact.shape_description: The handle is low and ridged, the body bulbous with a trefoil mouth, and the base echinoid.

artifact.name: Louvre G 416
artifact.summary: Death of Orpheus
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Thracian women, with characteristic tattoos on their arms, and dressed in chitons, run toward Orpheus with a variety of weapons. The left figure is armed with a rock and drapes her himation over her arm, the central one deals the death blow to Orpheus with a spear. The hero falls, holding his lyre up, his himation slipping off and wound bleeding (in added purple). The woman at right is about to hurl a large rock at him.

Side B: A woman runs left with one arm covered by a himation the other wielding a spear. Her hair is bound up with a fillet. Two others run right, one with a curved knife or sickle, the other with an axe and arm draped with a himation. Her hair is up and tied with a fillet. All of the figures run continuously without interruption by the handles around the vase. The rim ornament is an egg and dart band, at the base of the neck is a tongue pattern, and the ground line is a band of two stopt maeanders (alternating directions) alternating with upper/lower dotted X's.

The artist is a follower of the Berlin Painter and mainly a painter of large vases. He fills space with figures with spread drapery leaving little background free, and likes to do pursuit scenes.

artifact.name: Louvre G 402
artifact.summary: Youth sacrificing at an altar
artifact.decoration_description:
At the left, a youth wearing a wreath and draped in a himation leans on his staff while viewing the sacrifice made by a similarly clad youth in the center. He pours a libation from a cup onto an altar with added white flames and an object. At the right, a nude youth seen from the back wearing a wreath holds a spit with meat on the end to be cooked over the flames. The ornament around the neck is an egg and dart band, the picture frames have a vertical flame pattern, and the ground line is a band of checkerboards alternating with three stopt maeanders.

In this period, several painters specialized in such small oinochoe. The youthful figures attending the sacrifice are typical of the late fifth century, unlike older figures seen previously.
artifact.inscriptions: Above the figure making the sacrifice: <foreign lang="Greek">*P*U*Q*O*D*E*L*O*S *K*A*L*O*S</foreign>, Pythodelos is beautiful.
artifact.shape_description: Shape 3, choes

artifact.name: Louvre G 367
artifact.summary: Side A: Centauromachy. Side B: Three youths.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: At the left, a Lapith wearing chlamys, striped boots, and petasos at the back, struggles with the centaur whom he will strike with his axe. The centaur is drawn in an unusual three-quarter back view. At the right, another Lapith, similarly clad but wearing the petasos on his head, is about to stab a centaur with his spear. The centaur wields a branch with added purple leaves held above his head. Dilute glaze is used for the tails and cursorily drawn centaur musculature. The picture frame is two rows of dots. The ornament on the top of the rim is a ray pattern, on the rim edge two rows of dots, on the neck a network of pendant buds (side A only), and on the shoulder a tongue pattern.

Side B: Three youths draped in himatia stand around chatting. The outer two extend arms to the center figure who leans on his staff. All the figures' upper eyelids are clearly drawn.

Robertson 1992, 215-216The artist paints bell kraters and column kraters in the Polygnotan style, the dominant style of the period.
artifact.shape_description: Column krater

artifact.name: Louvre G 355
artifact.summary: Side A: Symposium<lb>Side B: Komos
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A male figure reclines on one couch with scrolled headrest and striped cushions; a table is under the bed. He is draped in a himation from the waist down and holds up a cup while gesturing to the party at the right. A double pipe (aulos) player (dressed in chiton, himation, and added purple fillet) performs for two figures reclining on another couch of the same sort with striped cushions and table below. The left male figure wearing a himation below the waist and fillet, holds a cup in the direction of the second bearded male figure dressed similarly and wearing an added purple wreath. A dog, wearing an added purple collar, waits in anticipation below the table. The scene is framed along the shoulder with a tongue pattern and along the sides with double rows of ivy leaves. The ornament around the rim of the krater consists of two rows of ivy leaves, on the neck (on side A only) pendant buds, and rays above the foot in two degrees.

Side B: Three male figures fully draped in himatia, revel with a cup on the left, and skyphos at the right. The middle figure sways with his staff. The ornament frame is the same as on side A.

Mannerists mainly paint column kraters, hydriai, and pelikai (Boardman 1985b, 180). The painter is a rather dull draughtsman according to Robertson 1992, 149.
artifact.shape_description: Column krater with framed pictures

artifact.name: Louvre G 332
artifact.summary: Interior: Woman in doorway, holding out a sakkos.
artifact.date_description: Very close in style and quality to the late phase of the Painter of Munich 2676 (who coarsely imitated the late Brygan style).
artifact.decoration_description: <hi rend="ital">Interior:</hi> A woman at a door, dressed in Ionic chiton and himation, holds a sakkos out over a stool. A handled mirror hangs on the wall. The tondo ornament is a stopt maeander moving right.
artifact.shape_description: Type B cup. Among many cups decorated on the inside only, forming the majority of the painter's oeuvre.

artifact.name: Louvre G 3
artifact.summary: Side A: Menelaos and Helen<lb>Side B: Chiron with the infant Achilles<lb>On the neck, sides A and B: Nereids<lb>Handles: helmeted runners
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>Simon & Hirmer 1976, p. 94, no. 91 right</bibl> (with previous bibliography)
artifact.decoration_description:
The neck on both sides shows a running Nereid wearing a short chiton and sakkos and carrying a dolphin in each hand. They are the sisters of Thetis, the mother of Achilles. On each handle a helmeted warrior is shown, without shield.

The two sides of the main panel are separated at the handle zones by palmette designs. On side A, the child Achilles is held in the right of hand of Chiron the centaur. Chiron is depicted as a man in front with the back and hind legs of a horse projecting out behind. His human form is wearing a himation and mantle that leave his right shoulder and arm bare. In his left hand he holds a young tree trunk against his shoulder; from its branches a dead hare hangs. In his right hand sits Achilles, dressed identically to Chiron.

On side B, Menelaos is shown grasping Helen by the left hand. Menelaos is wearing a short chiton, helmet and greaves. In his right hand he brandishes his sword, whose scabbard hangs from a baldric over his right shoulder. Helen wears a long chiton and bracelet and moves away from Menelaos, heading right.

The scenes are bordered above by a band of tongues. Below, projecting up from the base is a flame pattern.
artifact.inscriptions: On side B the names of Menelaos and Helen are inscribed, *M*E*N*E*L*A*O*S and &epig-rough;*E*L*E*N.
artifact.shape_description: Nikosthenic amphora

artifact.name: Louvre G 291
artifact.summary: Interior: Athlete<lb>Side A: Athletes at a well<lb>Side B: Athletes at a louterion
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: An athlete with frontal face stands over a louter or laver (with tongue pattern on the base) holding a sponge (?) in his hands. Dilute glaze is used to articulate some of the musculature. At the left, his staff rests against the wall along with a strigil with duck head finial and an aryballos tied with added red. Sandals hang on the wall at the right. The tondo ornament is a broken meander running left.

Side A: An athlete seen from the back scrapes himself with a strigil. At the left, an aryballos tied with added purple and a sponge (?) hang on the wall. To the right, a staff rests against the wall and a vessel is probably lifted by the athlete intending to fill a laver. A strigil and sandals with added purple straps hang on the wall above another athlete holding out a strigil in his hand. Jumping weights (halteres) appear in the background near a staff.

Side B: A staff rests on the wall to the left of an athlete in three-quarter back view scraping himself with a strigil, He wears an added purple fillet and bracelet. An aryballos and sponge hang on the wall and another athlete in back view, wearing an added purple fillet and anklet, draws a vessel of water from a well with a rope. A third athlete in three-quarter back view scrapes himself with a strigil. His aryballos tied with added purple and a sponge hang on the wall along with his sandals with added purple straps. A staff closes the scene.

The artist favors varied poses for his figures, especially the twisted back view with distinctive broken shoulder blades (Boardman 1985b, 134).
artifact.inscriptions: On the interior, <foreign lang="Greek">*K*A*L*O*S</foreign>, beautiful.
artifact.shape_description: Type B cup

artifact.name: Louvre G 278
artifact.summary: Interior: Man embracing boy<lb>Sides A and B: Nike and youths.
artifact.dimensions: H. 0.12 m; Diam. (lip) 0.26 m; W. (max.) 0.34 m
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: In an interior scene with a column and chair (with striped cushion), a man embraces a boy. The man wears a chiton, himation, and short laced boots; he leans on a staff. The boy is draped in a himation. The tondo ornament is a stopt meander running left.

Side A: A figure wearing a chiton and short laced boots looks on at two Nikes dressed in Ionic chitons flying to a youth and about to present him with fillets. The Nike at right has an added red belt. An altar is near the youth. At the right a male figure with stippled beard wearing a fillet (in added red) and short laced boots, leans on a walking stick and looks on.

Side B: A male figure at left draped in a himation raises his hand in greeting as two Nikes dressed in Ionic chitons do the same as on side A. The left one has an added purple fillet. At the right a figure dressed in a himation and added purple fillet, holding a spear looks on. A double reserve band serves as the ground line.
artifact.shape_description: Type B cup

artifact.name: Louvre G 265
artifact.summary: Interior: Youth leading a woman away (wedding of Menelaos and Helen?)<lb>Sides A-B: Deeds of Theseus
artifact.comparanda: For the deeds of Theseus cf. <rs type="vase">Louvre G 104</rs>.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: A youth wearing a chitoniskos, chlamys, and fillet and carrying a staff leads a woman away. She is dressed in chiton and himation which is draped over her head and wears earrings. She stands before a doorway, representing a house. The tondo ornament consists of meanders running left interrupted by crosses.

Side A: In a rocky landscape, Theseus dressed in chitoniskos and fillet with petasos at the back, runs to the right with his club, approaching the bull of Marathon, which is being held back by a satyr. To the right, Theseus appears again, wielding an axe is about to attack Procrustes who falls in a rocky landscape with tree.

Side B: Theseus wrapped in a chlamys, wearing a cap and striped boots, and holding a spear (?) is about to club the Grey Sow of Krommyon in a rocky landscape. A figure draped in a chiton and wearing shoes stands behind the animal. Next, Theseus faces Sinis seated on a rock holding a club or staff who extends his arm to the hero. A tree is between them. Theseus' sword in its scabbard hangs in the background.
artifact.shape_description: Type C cup

artifact.name: Louvre G 204
artifact.summary: Gigantomachy: Side A, Zeus; Side B, Giant
artifact.date_description: Late period, with mechanical drawing style
artifact.collection_history: Once in the Pourtalis collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Zeus strides to the right while holding a bird in his outstretched hand and brandishing a thunderbolt in the other hand at the back. He wears a chiton, himation, and fillet (in added purple). Some of the musculature and bird feathers are outlined in dilute glaze. The groundline is a decorated band with stopt key pattern.

Side B: A Giant in hoplite garb walks to the left wearing a helmet and carrying a spear and round shield with a device of a flying eagle with snake in its beak. He stands on a groundline decorated with ivy leaves.
artifact.shape_description: Nolan amphora with triple handles

artifact.name: Louvre G 201
artifact.summary: Symposium. Side A: Dionysos and satyr reclining. Side B: Satyr drawing wine.
artifact.date_description: Early period
artifact.graffiti: Sign(s) incised on base of foot
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A satyr reclines on a striped cushion while playing the double pipes (aulos). He wears an added purple wreath and his musculature is articulated in dilute glaze. Behind him, Dionysos reclines on a similar cushion wearing an Ionic chiton (with dilute glaze folds), himation wrapped around his waist, and added purple wreath. He hold a large skyphos and reaches out with one arm.

Side B: A satyr, squatting, stretches and reaches in a three-quarter pose with a ladle into a lugged vat and is about to fill a large skyphos with wine. He wears a wreath in added purple and has horse ears. A decorated band with linked slanting pairs of palmettes serves as the ground line.

Under each handle is an ivy leaf.

The hastily executed anatomical details suggest an "early" date (Kurtz 1983, pp. 78-79).
artifact.shape_description: Nolan amphora with triple handles

artifact.name: Louvre G 2
artifact.summary: Body: Side A, satyr and maenad; Side B, the like<lb>Neck: Side A, naked woman doing up her sandal; Side B, the like<lb>On each handle, a victor
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>Simon & Hirmer 1976, p. 94, no. 91 left.</bibl> (with previous bibliography)
artifact.decoration_description:
On each side of the neck, a naked hetaira laces up her sandal. On one side, the woman is crouched over to reach her foot, while on the other side she sits on a small cushion and raises her foot to reach her hands. Each wears a sakkos and a wreath. On each handle a victorious athlete is depicted.

The two sides of the main panel are separated at each handle zone by large palmette designs. On each side a maenad is struggling with a silen. On one side both are on their feet, the maenad covered to her feet in a long chiton and mantle, with bracelets and earrings, the silen naked and ithyphallic. The silen holds a young tree as a staff and grasps the maenad's left arm in an attempt to push her down. On the second side, the maenad stands taller than the crouching silen, grabs his hair with her right hand and pushes, while he holds her arm. She wields a black snake in her left hand and points it toward her attacker as well. The silen is naked, with a wreath in his hair, while the maenad wears a chiton, mantle, leopardskin, and cap. The scenes are bordered above by a leaf pattern. Below, a band of rays projects up from the base.

The rim is covered with a palmette design.
artifact.inscriptions: The signature of the potter appears in the background of side B: *F*A*M*F*I*O*S *E*P*O*I*S*E*N (Pamphaios made it).
artifact.shape_description: Nikosthenic amphora

artifact.name: Louvre G 198
artifact.summary: Side A: Nike. Side B: Youth.
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>Kurtz 1983, pp. 69-70, no. 10, plates IV, XL a-c</bibl>; <bibl>Boardman 1985b, 94-95</bibl>
artifact.date_description: Middle period with conventional drawing style
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A winged Nike flies above a groundline with a continuous maeander broken and running right. She is dressed in Ionic chiton and himation, wears bracelets and necklace in added red, earring, and stephane, and carries a thymiaterion (incense burner) and phiale. Her legs are visible through the folds of the chiton, and dilute glaze is used for the top of her hair and the bangs.

Side B: A youth draped in himation with black selvage and leaning on a staff reaches out with his arm. The details of musculature are done in dilute glaze. The drapery is like that on the painter's earlier mantled figures with peaks at the shoulder and bulk at the waist. The flat, two-dimensional drapery and angular body contours with inner details are characteristic of his "Middle" period (Kurtz 1983, p. 70). He stands on a groundline with stopt key pattern.

A double palmette decorates each handle and below.
artifact.shape_description: Large with ridged handles; foot in two degrees

artifact.name: Louvre G 192
artifact.summary: Side A: Infant Herakles and snakes. Side B: Zeus sending forth Hermes and Iris.
artifact.date_description: Middle period with conventional drawing style
artifact.collection_history: Once in the Durand collection.
artifact.graffiti: Incised sign on the base of the foot.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: At the left, a female figure draped in chiton, wearing a stephane and bracelets, makes a gesture of conspiracy with two bent fingers (CVA, France 1, Louvre 1, pp. 41-42). She stands behind Athena who is dressed in Ionic chiton, himation and aegis, holding a spear. She raises a hand protectively over the infant Herakles who grapples with two snakes on an elaborately decorated bed with striped cushion. A himation is draped over him and his twin brother Iphicles who jumps into the arms of Alkmene. She wears a chiton, bracelets, earring, and a sakkos. At the right stands Amphitryon who raises a hand in consternation; he is draped in a himation, wears a fillet, and leans on a knurled staff. Dilute glaze is used for his musculature as well as Herakles', Alkmene's, some of Athena's and Amphitryon's blonde hair plus his beard; added red for bracelets, Amphitryon's fillet, and the ribbon around Athena's chignon.

Side B: Hermes departs to the left wearing his winged boots, chitoniskos patterned in dilute glaze, chlamys, petasos (tied on with added red), and holding his kerykeion; his musculature and long hair is done partly in dilute glaze. Zeus standing in the center is dressed in Ionic chiton (with dilute glaze folds) and himation, wears an added red fillet, and holds his long scepter and thunderbolt (with added red). He dispatches both Hermes and Iris. Winged Iris runs to the right wearing Ionic chiton (with dilute glaze pleats) and himation, added red bracelets, and stephane. Her chignon is tied in added red. She is winged and carries a kerykeion.

The border below the reserve groundline has two joined meanders alternating left and right with crosses. A tongue pattern encircles the bases of the handles and the rim. Palmettes and buds are above and below handles.
artifact.shape_description: Special long-necked shape. Displayed with a lid.

artifact.name: Louvre G 186
artifact.summary: Side A: Peleus bringing Achilles to Chiron<lb>Side B: Man and two youths.
