Much anatomical detail is added in dilute glaze.

The Pioneers are known as a clique of artists who challenged each other in their works of art, writing messages to one another on their pots and labeling figures with their friends' names. Furthermore, they often signed their own works as Phintias did here.
artifact.inscriptions: Upper scene: in the field *F*I[*N]*T*I*A*S *E*G*R*A*F*S*E*N, "Phi(n)tias made (me)." Lower scene: in the field *M*E*G*A*K*L*E*S *K*A*L*O*S, "Megakles (is) beautiful."
artifact.shape_description: older Black figure form

artifact.name: London E 157
artifact.summary: Amazonomachies<lb>Side A: Theseus and Andromache; Side B: Phorbas and Alexandre
artifact.other_bibliography: Von Bothmer 1957, 186, no. 100 and 189-190; Salzmann Necropole de Camire pl. 59; Kretschmer, Vaseninschriften 105 and 183
artifact.collection_history: Biliotti, 1864. From Tomb 56 at Kameiros
artifact.decoration_description:
Exterior: Side A: Theseus and Andromache. On the left Theseus, clad only in a helmet, lunges forward on his left leg with his sword hanging at his side. Holding his shield up to protect himself with his left arm, with his right he aims his spear at Andromache's breast. She flees to the right with her bow in her left hand, but turns to face him and with her right arm raised above her head she strikes at him with her battle axe. She is armed with bow and quiver and clad in cuirass and short chiton with a kidaris (eastern head-dress), spotted to indicate animal hide. Both are named by inscriptions, *Q*E*S*E*U*S, Theseus and *A*N*D*R*O*M*A*X*E, Andromache.

Side B: Phorbas and Alexandre. From the right the Greek hero Phorbas attacks the figure of an Amazon on the left. He runs over a small rise and lunges forward on his left leg, thereby giving the viewer a rear view. Helmeted and sword at his side, he wears a mantle loosely draped across his shoulders and caught by the rushing breeze. He protects himself with his shield on the left arm and attacks with a spear held high in his right hand. The shield device is a lion, drawn in black outline with only the hind part to be seen. Alexandre backs off to the left with her shield on her right arm to cover her retreat and her spear raised in her left. She wears a helmet rather than the kidaris (eastern head-dress), a jerkin decorated with dots and wavy lines, a short girt chiton with broad double vertical lines at center, and anaxyrides (eastern pants) decorated with alternating rows of large and small dots. Both are named by inscriptions, *A[*L]*E*C[*A]*N*D*R*E, A(l)ex(a)ndre *F*O*R*B*A*S, Phorbas.

On the exterior curve of the rim there is an egg pattern. The same runs in a frieze just below the main design at the point of carination. Around the foot is a reserved band.
artifact.inscriptions: Beside each figure their name is inscribed. Side A: *Q*E*S*E*U*S, Theseus. *A*N*D*R*O*M*A*X*E, Andromache. Side B: *A[*L]*E*C[*A]*N*D*R*E, A(l)ex(a)ndre *F*O*R*B*A*S, Phorbas.

artifact.name: London E 140
artifact.summary: Side A: Demeter, Triptolemos, Persephone, Eleusis, and Eumolpos. Side B: Zeus, Dionysos, Amphitrite and Poseidon.
artifact.sources_used: Smith 1896, 137-139; Haspels 1936, 14 n., 72 n.2; CVA, 5, 3-4, pl. 28,2; Boardman 1975, fig. 309; Kurtz 1989, 95-96, pls. 78, 79; Williams 1991, 106, fig. 42; Barber 1992, 115, fig. 73
artifact.collection_history: Castellani, 1873
artifact.decoration_description:
Exterior: Side A: Triptolemos in his winged car is about to set off and bring wheat to humankind. He holds a bunch of grains in his left hand and an elaborately decorated phiale in his right. He wears a long, sleeved chiton and himation draped over his left shoulder. His wreathed hair is worn long with dangling curls in front of his ears and framing his face. Over him runs his name, *T*R*I*P*P*T*O*L*E*M*O*S, Triptolemos. The car itself is magnificently decorated with great spreading wings and arching serpents hissing on either side, as well as Ionic columns supporting the seat itself. Persephone stands on the right, looking center. She holds a blazing torch in her left hand and pours a farewell wine libation from an oinochoe with her right into the phiale of Triptolemos. She wears a radiated diadem and earrings on her head and a long, sleeved chiton with an elaborately bordered himation. Her name is inscribed, *F*E*R*O*F*A*T*T*A, Pherophatta. On the extreme right is a young nymph, Eleusis, a personification of the locality. She is dressed like Persephone in a long, sleeved chiton and himation which she wears modestly draped over her crowned head. With her right hand she holds up a flower and her left lifts the edge of her chiton. Her name is also inscribed *E*L*E*U*S*I*S, Eleusis. Behind the chariot is the goddess of grains, Persephone's mother, Demeter, who holds grains in her left hand and a flaming torch in her right. She wears an embattled diadem, earrings, and long, sleeved chiton. Her himation is richly embroidered with small winged figures, dolphins, eagles and other birds, panthers, chariot races, foot races, pegasoi, and humans in black silhouette. The borders consist of spirals and upright palmettes. Her name is inscribed, *D*E*M*E*T*R*E, Demeter. Beneath the right handle and to the right of the nymph Eleusis, is the king Eumolpos who originated the rites of Demeter at Eleusis. He is seated to the right, facing left, holding his scepter in his left hand. The bearded king has his hair long and wears a sleeveless chiton and a bordered himation draped over his left shoulder. His name is inscribed, *E*U*M*O*L*P*P*O*S, Eumolpos. Beneath the other handle, seated to the left but facing right, towards Demeter, is the god Poseidon, identified by the scepter of authority which he holds in his right hand and the dolphin which he holds in his left. He is bearded and wears a sleeveless chiton and himation which is draped over his left shoulder. His name is inscribed beside him, *P*O*S*E*I*D*O*N, Poseidon.

Side B: At the feet of Eumolpos is a swan which follows Zeus, who walks to the right. He carries his attribute, the thunderbolt, in his right hand, and his scepter of authority in his left. He has his wreathed hair short, with a long curl behind his ear, and wears a mustache and long beard. The god wears a long, sleeved chiton and a bordered himation over his left shoulder. He is further identified by his name, *Z*E*U*S, Zeus. The central figure on this side is the god Dionysos, who stands facing right and holding a sprouting staff in his left hand. He has his hair long in back, a mustache, and beard, and wears a bordered himation over his long chiton. In his hair he wears an ivy wreath. His name, too, is inscribed, *D*I*O*N*U*S*O*S, Dionysos. The scene is related to that on Side A since the female figure furthest right, Amphitrite, wife of Poseidon, looks off right in his direction. She is identified by her attribute, the dolphin, which she holds in her left hand, and her name which is inscribed, *A[*N]*F*I*T*R*I*T*E, Amphitrite. She moves to the left, wearing a fillet, earrings, a necklace, and a chiton with overfold. With her right hand she holds up her himation for her husband in a gesture which is associated with brides and wives. The figures walk on a reserved double line which runs round the entire exterior.

The event on Side A takes place at Eleusis. The torches held by Persephone and Demeter are typical of the equipment of the Eleusinian mysteries, held in their honor. They also indicate that the action is taking place at night.
artifact.inscriptions: All figures are identified,*T*R*I*P*P*T*O*L*E*M*O*S, *F*E*R*O*F*F*A*T*T*A, *E*L*E*U*S*I*S, *D*E*M*E*T*R*E, *E*U*M*O*L*P*P*O*S, *P*O*S*E*I*D*O*N, *Z*E*U*S, *D*I*O*N*U*S*O*S, and *A[*N]*F*I*T*R*I*T*E. On the left handle appears &epig-rough;*I*E*R*O*N *E*P*O*I*S*E*N, "Hieron made (me)."

artifact.name: London E 137
artifact.summary: Two komasts
artifact.other_bibliography: Burlington Magazine 1921, 231, b; Langlotz G.V. pl. 2, 4
artifact.collection_history: ex Blacas Collection. Canino Collection no. 175. Smith 1896, 136: from Nola (?)
artifact.decoration_description: Two komasts, wreathed, walk to the left, side by side. At center one takes short steps with knees slightly bent. Facing left, he plays the double flute. He is nude and carries a sybene (flute-case) on his left shoulder. In it are two spare flutes. Attached to it by a thinner cord in a glottokomeion (reed case). Behind him is a bearded man who stoops forward to lift with both hands a large kotyle which has been sitting on the ground. He wears a mantle thrown over his shoulders and high boots. Arranged in an arc around the figures is the inscription *E*P*I*K*T*E*T*O*S *E*G*R*A*S*F*E*N (sic), "Epikitetos made (me)."
artifact.inscriptions: In an arc around the figures runs the inscription *E*P*I*K*T*E*T*O*S *E*G*R*A*S*F*E*N (sic), "Epiktetos made (me)".

artifact.name: London E 134.2
artifact.summary: Youth reclining
artifact.other_bibliography: JHS 52, 202
artifact.graffiti: On the exterior is a roughly engraved inscription in large characters*A*I*T*I, perhaps part of a dedication *O *D*E*I*N*A *M*E *A*N*E*Q*H*K*E *K]*A*I *T[*H*N *P*R*O*X*O*U*N, cf. Naukratis, i, pl. 32, 1.
artifact.decoration_description:
Exterior: unpainted, except for a thin black line at the lower edge. On the exterior is a roughly engraved inscription in large characters *A*I*T*I, perhaps part of a dedication *O *D*E*I*N*A *M*E *A*N*E*Q*H*K*E *K]*A*I *T[*H*N *P*R*O*X*O*U*N, cf. Naukratis, i, pl. 32, 1.

Interior: Symposium. A male figure reclines to the right on a cushion. He looks right and extends his left arm in the same direction as if engaged in conversation with a missing symposiast on the right. Sporting a wreath in added red he holds a dotted phiale in his right hand. With frontal chest and profile face and hips, he wears a himation decorated with crosses, tied about his waist.
artifact.shape_description: Fragment

artifact.name: London E 129
artifact.summary: Interior: Dionysos, Ariadne, and Eros. Exterior: Side A: Dionysos and thiasos. Side B: Same as A.
artifact.other_bibliography: Corbett 1960, 52-60, pls. 5-7 and 4.2; Jahrbuch 25 129-130, pl. 4
artifact.date_description: The date of ca. 400 BC was modified downward based on associated objects in the tomb.
artifact.collection_history: Blacas Collection. Found in the Blacas Tomb, by the elder Duc de Blacas.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: Tondo: Looking drunk, Dionysos staggers to the right, his head (in three-quarter view) thrown back as if he were singing. One arm, holding a chelys (lyre) hangs at his side; the other is flung around the neck of Ariadne who supports him with her right arm around his waist. The youthful god has long, wavy hair with a radiated stephane and a fillet over his ears. The full-bodied figure wears a mantle hanging from his left shoulder and twisted round his right leg. On the right Ariadne looks back at him, holding a tympanon on her left, decorated with a central star. She wears a long chiton, a bordered himation, draped over her left arm, and a jacket open down the front and embroidered with rosettes and a spiraliform border. Her hair is looped up with a fillet in added red and she wears a radiated stephane, earrings, bracelet, and necklace. On the left Eros flies behind them, his head thrown back as if singing and striking on an uplifted tympanon with his right hand.

Between the lip and tondo runs a wreath of vine-leaves alternating with bunches of grapes. The tondo design is set within a circle of sets of four meanders separated by checker squares.

Exterior: Side A: Here a youthful nude Dionysos wears only a fillet in his short hair. He is seated to the right on a mantle spread over the rising ground. Ground lines are indicated in added red. He leans on his right elbow and holds a thyrsos in his left hand as he turns left to look at a nymph who brings a phiale to him. On his right another nymph brings s kantharos. Both are dressed in chitons girt at the waist with their hair tied back in a knot. They wear gilded earrings, necklace, bracelets and a stephane. On the far right a full-bearded silen dances into the scene with his right arm and left leg raised. He wears only a fillet.

Exterior: Side B: The scene is the same as is depicted on Side A. But here the nymph on the right has no kantharos and turns away from Dionysos to face the right. Her right hand rests rather on her hip and her left gestures toward the silen. She stands to the right facing the dancing ithyphallic silen, as he reaches out to grab her.

The exterior scenes fall into two horizontal bands. On the broad lip is a wreath composed of myrtle flowers and alternating groups of three myrtle leaves. Beneath and beside each handle is a triple fifteen-leafed palmette ornament with bristling acanthus leaves. The area above the handles is reserved.

artifact.name: London E 104
artifact.summary: Interior: Herakles and the Nemean Lion. Exterior: Side A: Herakles driving off the cattle of Geryon. Side B: Herakles (?) and the Cretan Bull
artifact.collection_history: Durand Collection, no. 298
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: Tondo: Herakles, youthful and beardless, bends forward to the right. He has locked both arms from above around the neck of the Nemean lion. With his head pressed downwards against its mane, compresses the throat so that its jaws are open and its tongue protruding. The lion's forepaws are planted firmly on the thighs of Herakles, whose club has fallen behind him. The contest takes place on rocky ground, indicated by an irregularly shaped space left red. The tondo is encircled within a band of single meanders interspersed with six red cross squares.

Exterior: Side A: Herakles moves to the right behind three bulls, the foremost of which, drawn almost in a frontal pose, turns back to look at Herakles. The hero is bearded and wears the lion's skin over his head and girt at the waist. He holds his club in his right hand and a cornucopia(?) in his left. In the background beside the hindmost bull is a leafless tree with six branches.

Exterior: Side B: Herakles, bending forward to the right, has caught the bull by both horns as it springs forward and seems to be forcing it backward. His head passes under that of the bull so that the bull's muzzle rests on the shoulders of Herakles. The hero is youthful here as in the tondo, distinguishable by the club which has dropped to his feet. In the background beside the bull, a bearded man stands looking on and raises his right hand as if in surprise. He is wearing a mantle and leans forward on his staff. On the right another bearded spectator carries a club on his left shoulder and raises his right hand in surprise. He wears a short girt chiton, the lower part of which is decorated with a border of vertical black rays, and a skin (a nebris?).

Beneath and beside the handles there is a quadruple palmette ornament.

artifact.name: London D 71
artifact.summary: Woman seated at a tomb
artifact.sources_used: Smith 1896, 134-135; Fairbanks 1907, XIV, no. 24, 174 pl. 28, 2; Kurtz 1975, 59 n.13, 60, 61 and n.4, 62 nn. 9, 14, 63 n.9, 65 and n.11, 66 n.8, 222 and pl. 49,4; Williams 1985, 52, fig. 56; L. Burn 1991, 127-128, fig. 51
artifact.decoration_description:
To the right a woman sits at a broad monument draped with taeniae (ribbons) and laden with offerings (probably her husband's tomb). She looks left, her arms folded, as she sadly contemplates her future as well as the past. She wears a long chiton, himation, sandals, and a necklace of beads. A white-ground lekythos sits on the step beside her, two alabastra, and a black loutrophoros on the finial above her head. There appears to be a secondary monument — a shaft with a triangular pediment — surmounting the primary one. Beside the shaft there is a strigil, suspended in the field. A woman stands to the right holding a basket of ribbons in her left hand and places a large lekythos on the upper plinth with her left. She advances, wearing a long chiton. On the left is a figure, almost completely worn away, whose feet show that it was once seated on a mound to the left of the tomb with its left hand on its knees and feet resting on the plinth.

Figures "seated at the tomb on Group R lekythoi are regularly taken for the dead, even though (they) can in no way be distinguished from the other 'visitors' to the tomb." (Kurtz 1975, 223). This example tends to disprove this assumption for if the woman is dead, then why does a strigil hang down from her tomb (an object associated with male athletes)? Williams (Williams 1985, 52) believes she rather mourns the loss of her husband. Burn (Burn 1991, 128) holds to the idea that the woman herself is the deceased, but she does not explain the strigil.

The style of drawing shows quick broken lines which indicate volume. The technique recalls the descriptions of the work of Parrhasios, a painter at work from 431-404 B.C. who was said to have achieved volume without shading. This work also reflects interest in perspective in the treatment of the alabastra on the tomb and in the strong foreshortening of the body.

artifact.name: London D 7
artifact.summary: Man and snake: the death of Opheltes?
artifact.sources_used: Smith 1896, 392; Murray & Smith 1896, pl. 18, b; Pfuhl 1923 pl. 200, no. 528; Robertson 1992, 10-11, fig. 3
artifact.other_bibliography: Frîhner von Branteghem Collection, no. 165, pl. 40; H. Hoffmann, "Aletheia: the iconography of death/rebirth in three cups by the Sotades Painter," Res 17-18 (1989) 67-88; L. Burn, "Honey Pots: Three White-ground Cups by the Sotades Painter,"Antike Kunst 28 (1985) 93-105; A. Griffiths, "'What Leaf-Fringed Legend...?' A Cup by the Sotades Painter," JHS 106 (1986) 58-70
artifact.collection_history: Found in a grave in Athens together with cups London D 5 and London D 6, phialai London D 8 and Boston 98.886, two mastoi London D 9 and London D 10, and stemless cups Brussels A 891 and Brussels A 890.
artifact.decoration_description:
On the left is a spring indicated by a bunch of tall, growing reeds; behind the reeds on the right rises a large serpent. With its body in one large coil, it draws back its head as if to strike. From its open jaws issue flames and smoke, partly concealing the reeds. The hunter stands opposite, wearing a skin tied about his neck and a tall conical fur cap. He has a stubbly beard and his lips part as if in surprise. Over his left shoulder he carries a short hunter's club. As he moves away to the left, he glances to the right, raising his right hand as if to hurl a rock at the snake. Further left the lower part of young girl in a chiton is visible. She seems to have fallen on her knees while fleeing. Beside her on the right is the outstretched arm of another figure, the remainder of whose body is missing. L. Burn has recently suggested an identification with Eurydice and Aristaios.

The surface is covered with a white slip, on which the design is drawn in brown outline within a tondo, described by a thin brown circle. The flames from the serpent's mouth are rendered in a thick added white pigment.
artifact.shape_description: delicate make

artifact.name: London D 61
artifact.summary: Charon in his boat
artifact.sources_used: Smith 1896, 406; Fairbanks 1907, II, no. 137; Kurtz 1975, 60 n.3, 62, 63 and n.11, 205, 221, 223, pl. 47, 3, pl. 49,4; Murray & Smith 1896, pl. 12
artifact.comparanda: Group R lekythos with Charon (ARV2, 1384)
artifact.decoration_description:
On the right just projecting from tall red and black reeds is the prow of Charon's boat. He sits inside, a bearded figure in a short chiton and a rough cap with a tall arching piece in the center of the crown. He leans forward on his oar, one end on the bank and the other held in his left hand against his left shoulder. He extends his right hand as if to welcome the woman advancing on the left. She holds in each hand a basket containing taeniae (fillets) and wears a long bordered chiton with apoptygma (overfold). The Reed Painter devotes much attention to Charon whose depiction is rare in the work of other painters. The reeds, too, are a signature of the painter, as is the prominence of the fillets.

The body is covered with a white slip, on which the design is drawn in red outline. Above the design is a band of meanders broken by dotted cross squares. On the shoulder is a pattern of three palmettes, painted in matt black on white. The petals of the palmettes are alternately red and black. Vermilion is used for hair, beard, and dress of Charon as well as for the border of the woman's chiton.
artifact.shape_description: standard shape

artifact.name: London D 60
artifact.summary: Hare hunt beside a stele.
artifact.sources_used: Smith 1896, 405-406; Kurtz 1975, 39 n.11, 40 n.1, 41 n.3, 69 n.5, 211, pl. 32, 3; Murray & Smith 1896, pl. 6; Fairbanks 1907, VI, 1, no. 1, 256-257; Schnapp 1989, 81-82, fig. 111
artifact.collection_history: Found in 1876 at Ampelokepoi, near Athens.
artifact.comparanda: For highly unusual scene another vase by same painter, Bonn 1011, ARV2, 1230, 37
artifact.decoration_description:
A youth chases a hare in the vicinity of a tomb. The locale indicated is a rocky hill slope, rising to the upper border on the left. At the foot of the hill is a plain stele, surmounted by a cornice and resting on a quadruple plinth. Around it is tied a taenia, another is laid on the top, and two more rest on the plinth and rocks below. A hare runs up the hill past the stele, closely pursued by a large hound which is urged on by a nude youth on the right. He carries a mantle on his left arm and a club over his shoulder and extends his right towards the hare. On the left, under the hill, a second youth strides forward with his left foot raised on a rock. He hurls a stone at the hare with his right hand and grasps a club in his left. He wears a mantle over his left shoulder.

There is a quite unusual conflation of two scenes: the tomb and the hare hunt. What resulted is a personal vision of a funerary scene appropriate to a deceased youth who had enjoyed hunting hares.

The body is covered with a white slip, on which the design is drawn in brown outline. Above the design is a band of unbroken meanders. On the shoulder is a pattern of three palmettes, painted in matt brown on white. Above is an egg pattern. Preliminary sketch is visible in transparent, shiny lines.
artifact.shape_description: standard shape

artifact.name: London D 6
artifact.summary: Women or nymphs picking apples: the Hesperides?
artifact.other_bibliography: H. Hoffmann, "Aletheia: the iconography of death/rebirth in three cups by the Sotades Painter," Res 17-18 (1989) 67-88; Frîhner von Branteghem Collection, no. 164, pl. 39
artifact.collection_history: Found in a grave in Athens together with cup London D 5, phialai London D 8 and Boston 98.886, two mastoi London D 9 and London D 10, and stemless cups London D 7, Brussels A 891 and Brussels A 890. Von Branteghem Collection, no. 164
artifact.condit: Fragmentary. The left side of the design is partly broken away.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: In the center is an apple tree, its branches extending to the top of the tondo and spreading rather lower of the left than on the right. On the right a girl stands on tiptoe, stretching to reach up with her right hand to pluck an apple from the highest branch and holding her skirt aside with her left. She wears a long, undergirt chiton with apoptygma (overfold) and her hair is confined with a sphendone. Above her is her name, of which only three letters remain, ...*L*D*O. The figure on the left is completely lost, except perhaps for the outline of the back. Judging from the space, it must have been either seated or shorter than the other. Above the second figure runs the name *M*E*L*I*S*I. Below the design between the border and the lip, is inscribed [*S*O*T]*A*D*E*S *E*P*O*I*S*E*N, "(Sot)ades made (me)." The tondo is defined with a broad yellow band within a black band.

The inner surface is covered with a white slip, on which the design is drawn in brown outline. The fruit is painted in added white so thick as to look like relief. Coral red used.
artifact.inscriptions: Above the woman is her name, of which only three letters remain, ...]*L*D*O. Above the second figure runs the name *M*E*L*I*S*I. Below the design between the border and the lip, is inscribed [*S*O*T]*A*D*E*S *E*P*O*I*S*E*N, "(Sot)ades made (me)".
artifact.shape_description: Of delicate make, with Merrythought handles

artifact.name: London D 51
artifact.summary: Woman says farewell to an arming warrior
artifact.other_bibliography: JHS 12 315, pl. 14
artifact.collection_history: Presented by the Cyprus Exploration Fund; found in 1890.
artifact.decoration_description:
On the left a woman stands, holding the edge of her garment with her left hand and the soldier's helmet in her right. She is modestly dressed in a sakkos and a long, sleeved chiton with a deep overfold. Opposite her stands a nude bearded man in a frontal pose. He turns his head to look at her, holding his right hand out to receive his helmet and holding his spear in his left. Between them a goose with ruffled neck feathers pecks at the ground. Behind the woman, partly hidden is a diphros (stool). Above it a small jug hangs in the field. Here is a domestic scene within the woman's quarters or perhaps in the courtyard.

The body is covered with a fine white slip, on which the design is drawn in brown outline. Above the design is a band of reversing meanders broken by squares with dotted oblique crosses. On the shoulder is a pattern of three palmettes, brown on white. Above this there is an egg pattern.

artifact.name: London D 4
artifact.summary: Interior: The making of Pandora<lb>Exterior (both sides): Palaistra scene.
artifact.collection_history: Found at Nola in 1828 or 1829, ex Hope Collection. Purchased in 1881, from sale of Bale Collection.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: Tondo: In the center Pandora (or Anesidora) stands in a frontal pose, stiff as an Archaic kore or xoanon with her feet together and hands at her sides. She looks to the left and raises the edge of her drapery slightly with each hand. Above her is her name [*A]*N*E*S*I*D*O*R*A. She is wearing a long, sleeved chiton undergirt and decorated with stars; her hair streams down loosely about her shoulders, confined with a fillet, apparently just placed there by Hephaistos. Athena appears to be fastening Pandora's chiton on her shoulders. Both deities stand taller than the mortal woman. Athena on the left wears a long chiton girt at the waist with a girdle, the ends of which fall in front under the upper fold of the chiton. Around her shoulders she wears the aegis fringed with snakes and set with the gorgoneion. It is decorated with a diaper pattern rather than scales. Over her is her name, *A*Q*E*N*A*A. Hephaistos on the right wears a rather scanty himation and holds his hammer at his side in his left hand. His short hair is confined with a golden fillet. The scene recalls Hesiod's Theogony (Hes. Th. 573-580).

The inner face is covered with a white slip and has a thin, brown circle drawn within one inch of the lip, forming the border of the design. The figures are drawn in black outline with inner details in brown with accents in purple and white. The head-dresses and head of the hammer are molded and gilt on a raised ground.

Exterior: Side A: A horse stands to the right in the center. It is approached by two ephebes. The first holds the halter in his right hand and a spear in his left. He wears a chlamys, fillet, and petasos, hanging at his back. The second is closely draped in a himation and carries a crutched staff on his left arm. He too wears a fillet. Beside the horse in the foreground a woman stands to the left and holds a honeysuckle flower in her right hand. She wears a long, sleeved himation, sakkos, and stephane. Confronting her is a bearded man who rests on his staff with his right hand on his hip and offers her a purse with his left. He is dressed in himation and fillet.

Side B: In this scene the central horse turns to the left. Beside it in the background is an ephebe standing in a frontal pose, but looking left at another youth. The first wears a himation and fillet and holds a staff in his right hand. The second youth moves away, looking back and leading the horse by the halter with his left hand. He carries a spear and wears a chlamys, fillet and petasos at his back. On the left is a woman who raises a flower to her face with her right hand. She wears a long chiton and himation, with her hair knotted with a fillet. To the right of the horse are two figures. The first is a woman in a long, sleeved chiton, himation and radiated sphendone, who holds out a phiale in her left hand and pours wine onto the ground from a jug in her right. Facing her on the right is an old man in a long chiton, himation, and fillet, who stands in a frontal pose, looking left toward the woman. He leans with his right shoulder against a crutched staff. From the gesture of his left hand and his open mouth he seems to be addressing her.

The exterior is executed in red figure with fillets, wine and cords in added red and the old man's hair and beard in added white. Below is a band of meanders broken by red cross squares. Below each handle is a double palmette ornament.
artifact.inscriptions: Above Pandora is her name [*A]*N*E*S*I*D*O*R*A. Above Athena is her name, *A*Q*E*N*A*A.

artifact.name: London D 20
artifact.summary: Seated woman
artifact.other_bibliography: Lane pl. 90a
artifact.decoration_description:
A woman sits on a diphros or stool to the right. She holds up a wreath with both hands, grasping it with the thumb and finger of the left hand above and the right below. She wears a long, sleeved chiton, with himation around her legs, earrings, and bracelets and her hair is looped up with rows of curls over her forehead. On the right a sakkos hangs from the upper border; on the left an alabastron hangs from an oblong object. Behind her hangs a large basket. In the field is inscribed, *K*A*L*E, "(she is) beautiful."

Above the design, there is a strip of meander on white. On the shoulder is a pattern of three red figure palmettes and two lotus buds. Above this is an egg pattern in red figure. The body is covered with a warm yellow slip, on which the design is drawn in black outline. A second white was used for the flesh, sakkos, and alabastron and spoils the drawing. Her hair and himation are black with details added in pink. The chiton is pink with brown detailing.
artifact.inscriptions: In the field, *K*A*L*E, "(she is) beautiful."

artifact.name: London D 13
artifact.summary: Woman spinning
artifact.collection_history: Castellani, 1873.
artifact.decoration_description:
A woman stands to the right, wearing a long, sleeved, dotted chiton, a bordered himation, and sandals and further adorned with earrings and bracelets. Her hair is wound up in a ball on her neck and fastened with a fillet. She twists between the thumb and forefinger of her right hand a thread from a hank of wool on a distaff which she holds up with her left. To the right runs an inscription, &epig-rough;*E *P*A*I*S *K*A*L*E, "the girl (is) beautiful." This vase celebrates women's work within the domestic sphere, the production of all woven materials for the oikos.

The neck, handle, and foot are of black glaze. The edge of the lip is colored purple. At the base of the handle is an inverted palmette. Below the molding on the shoulder is a band of tongue pattern, red on black. The body is covered with a white slip, on which the design is drawn in black outline. Purple is used for the fillet, bracelets, sandals, wool, and spindle. Inner markings of the drapery and inscription are drawn in light brown.

Attributed to the Brygos Painter in Barber, in Neils 1992, p. 105 fig. 64.
artifact.inscriptions: On the right, &epig-rough;*E *P*A*I*S *K*A*L*E, "the girl (is) beautiful."

artifact.name: London B 89
artifact.summary: Four swans
artifact.collection_history: ex Calvert Collection, 1877
artifact.decoration_description: Design is in black on a pale red ground.

artifact.name: London B 76
artifact.summary: Hector's chariot
artifact.decoration_description: At center is Hector's quadriga facing front. The charioteer, Kebrione, named in inscription, faces right. He wears a long chiton and holds the reins. The two inner horses face each other, the outer ones look away. They have incised tails and decorative breast bands. Hector stands to the left looking on at the central scene. He holds a spear in his right hand. The bearded hero of Troy wears a fillet in his long hair and is dressed soberly in a long black chiton and himation in added red. Behind him a nude soldier stands ready, holding a shield on his left arm and grasping a spear. He wears only a helmet. On the right of center Glaukos, named, stands looking left. He, too, wears a long chiton and himation in added red. He holds his spear with his left hand. At the far right is another man at arms, helmeted and carrying a shield and spear, he faces left. There are lotus as filling ornaments growing up from the ground line. Below the main design is a frieze of intertwined lotuses in red and black. The inscriptions naming the central figures are painted in red.&epig-rough;*E*K*T*O*R, *K*E*B*R*I*O*N*E, [*G]*L*A*U*K*O*S.
artifact.inscriptions: The inscriptions naming the central figures are painted in red: &epig-rough;*E*K*T*O*R, *K*E*B*R*I*O*N*E, [*G]*L*A*U*K*O*S.
artifact.shape_description: Strap handles

artifact.name: London B 693
artifact.summary: Dionysos seated
artifact.comparanda: Decoration can be compared to that on the early red figure lekythos in Oxford, Oxford 1949.751, ARV2, 9,1.
artifact.decoration_description: The decoration is done in Six's technique.

artifact.name: London B 675
artifact.summary: Chariot in battle
artifact.collection_history: Found in 1864
artifact.decoration_description:
A quadriga half-turned to the left carries a warrior with high-crested helmet and shield. The shield has a device three white pellets. The quadriga is shown in three-quarter view as it turns. The warrior is pursuing another who retreats to the left, looking back. He is fully armed with a chlamys over his shoulders and a shield. His shield device is a bull's head. In the field there are imitation inscriptions.

The design is in black on a drab ground with added red. Above the design there are palmettes. On either side of the vase are ears.
artifact.inscriptions: In the field there are imitation inscriptions.

artifact.name: London B 674
artifact.summary: Black archer and palm tree
artifact.other_bibliography: C. Smith Naukratis I p. 51
artifact.collection_history: Found in 1875
artifact.decoration_description: An Ethiopian walks to the right, but faces left. His short curly hair is rendered in crude stippling, his skin is black. Dressed like an archer, he wears a sleeved jerkin with a fringe on the bottom and anaxyrides (trousers). Both are embroidered with stripes and dots. Over his left arm he has a garment with a meander border and fringe. In his right hand he wields a double axe. On the left is a table and on the right, a palm tree. The painting is in thick lines on a drab ground.

artifact.name: London B 668
artifact.summary: Bacchic revel
artifact.collection_history: Found in 1887
artifact.comparanda: For polychromatic washes, Athens 15002, ARV, 98, 2, Para, 330, 1
artifact.decoration_description:
On the left stands a maenad facing right and extending a phiale in her left hand. She wears her hair tied up in a bun with a yellow plume or comb. She is dressed in a long yellow chiton with a white himation over her shoulders. Before her a black crane with yellow feathers on its head and breast stands quietly facing right. A maenad rushes from the right to the center, her drapery billowing out behind her. She faces the other maenad and waves laurel branches with both hands. She wears a sphendone and cap over her hair and a chiton and himation like the other, but is further attired in sandals and a nebris or fawn skin of the cult of Dionysos. Above the scene is inscribed [*P]*A*S*I*A*D*E*S *E*P*O*I*S*E*N, (P)asiades made (me)." On the top of the vase is inscribed &epig-rough;*O *P*A*I*S *K*A*L*O*S, "The boy (is) beautiful."

Above and below the design there is a circumscribed tongue pattern in black. On the bottom there is a rosette in red on black. On either side of the vase is an ear in red. The figures are painted in black outline on a white ground. In the main design, polychromy in black and yellow is achieved through the use of dilute glaze washes. There is a little round rosette on the bottom.
artifact.inscriptions: Above the scene is inscribed [*P]*A*S*I*A*D*E*S *E*P*O*I*S*E*N, (P)asiades made (me)." On the top of the vase is inscribed &epig-rough;*O *P*A*I*S *K*A*L*O*S, "The boy (is) beautiful."
artifact.painter: Group of the Paidikos Alabastra and the Pasiades Painter
artifact.shape_description: ovoid without shoulder, short neck

artifact.name: London B 658
artifact.summary: Three warriors carry severed heads
artifact.other_bibliography: Arch. Anz 1942, 74, figs. 6-8
artifact.collection_history: ex Burgon Collection
artifact.decoration_description:
Three warriors move to the right, carrying severed heads in their left hands and drawn swords in their right. The severed heads still wear their helmets, grisly trophies for the victors. They all wear high-crested helmets, short chitons girt at the waist, and greaves with volutes. Perhaps this may represent a three-fold repetition of Amphiaraos with the head of Melanippos (Haspels 1936, 179).

The upper part of the neck is black as are the lower body and handle. The shoulder has rows of black pendants on a reserved ground. The body has a white ground. Above the panel a meander runs to the right.
artifact.shape_description: Chimney mouth with sharp shoulders and a high, blunt, foot.

artifact.name: London B 323
artifact.summary: Body: Hero (Achilles?) carrying the body of an Amazon (Penthesilea?<lb>Shoulder: Arming
artifact.other_bibliography: JHS 85 pl. 11a
artifact.collection_history: ex Durand Collection
artifact.graffiti: Underneath the foot is incised *D*F.
artifact.decoration_description:
Shoulder: Soldiers arming: At center a beardless warrior faces right, fastening a greave onto his left leg which rests on his helmet. He wears his hair long and filleted with a short chiton and sword, and his right greave already on. Confronting him is a female figure (his wife or mother?). She stands facing left and holding his spear with her right hand. She wears her filleted hair long and is dressed in a peplos. Behind her a warrior fully armed with helmet, shield (with a bent white leg as device) chlamys, short chiton, and greaves, faces left and holds the young man's shield (with a white tripod as device). Behind him, an archer walks to the right, turning back with his left hand raised and carrying an unidentified object in his right. He wears a peaked Phrygian cap, short chiton, and quiver. At the far right a fully armed warrior looks on. His shield bears the device of three pellets. With his back to the young warrior another fully armed warrior faces left, away from center. He, too, has the shield device of three white pellets. Confronting him further left is another beardless archer who holds a in his raised left hand and a in his right. He is dressed like the first. At the far left a beardless man looks right, standing quietly and watching the preparations. He wears a long chiton and himation and holds a staff in his left hand.

Body: At center a bearded warrior walks right, carrying on his left shoulder the dead body of an Amazon off the battlefield. He wears his filleted hair long with front locks and is dressed in a cuirass short chiton, and greaves, holding his two throwing spears in his right hand. A shield with an ivy wreath device rests against his leg. She, limp and lifeless, her eyes closed in death, wears a wreath in her long hair, a short chiton, cuirass, an arm bracelet, anklet, and sword. Is it Troy, Achilles, and Penthesilea? These names are not inscribed. To the right a warrior and archer depart to the right. The warrior looks back at the central scene. He is fully armed and his shield bears a triskeles device in white. The archer, wearing a peaked Phrygian cap, short chiton, quiver, and greaves, carries an axe in his left hand. On the left, behind the central group, an Amazon has fallen to the ground with her left leg drawn up under her. She protects herself with her shield on the left arm and holds her spear in her right hand. She wears a high-crested helmet, cuirass, short chiton, and greaves. Over her a fully armed warrior strides to the left with a shield device of a bull's head and with his right hand transfixes her with a spear. Above the last warrior is inscribed *K*A*L*O*S, "(he is) beautiful." In front of Achilles, *K*R*I*T*I[*A*S].

A circumscribed tongue pattern runs above the shoulder panel, around the base of the neck. Borders of ivy run down the sides of the panels. A palmette frieze runs across the bottom. On the lower body there is a band of rays.
artifact.inscriptions: Above the last warrior is inscribed *K*A*L*O*S, "(he is) beautiful." In front of Achilles, *K*R*I*T*I[*A*S].

artifact.name: London B 304
artifact.summary: Shoulder: Battle scene<lb>Main Panel: Harnessing horses to a quadriga<lb>Predella: Boar hunt
artifact.collection_history: ex Canino Collection, 1764.
artifact.decoration_description:
Shoulder: A quadriga on the right races toward the center with the horses straining to move ahead. Beneath their hooves lies a dead warrior on his stomach, his beardless face down in the dust and his body stripped of armor. Another seems to fall in front of them stumbling to his knees, as he tries to run to the left, and looking back at the horses. In vain he tries to protect himself with his shield as he holds his spear with his right hand. Behind him another foot soldier tries to defend him, holding his shield with his left arm and his spear raised in his right hand. At the far left another soldier strides vigorously to the right with his spear ready and his shield up. Beside and behind the horses a soldier runs to attack the man falling on the left. He carries a shield with a white dolphin device and a spear. The bearded charioteer is next to the right, bending far forward over the horses and keeping a tight grip on the reins. He wears a long white chiton and his shield is strapped to his back. Following him is an archer at the far right who stoops to aim his bow. He wears a peaked Phrygian cap, jerkin, anaxyrides (tight trousers), and high boots. All of the foot soldiers are fully armed with helmets, cuirasses, short chitons, greaves, spears, and shields. Above the panel is a circumscribed tongue pattern in red and black. Below the panel is meander frieze, running to the left.

The main design shows the harnessing of horses to a quadriga, much quieter in spirit than the shoulder composition. The moment before the battle is shown here with the nude, long-haired groom on the far right, quieting the horses, the bearded charioteer with fillet and long white chiton beside their girths making adjustments to the harness, and the nude young youth hopping up into the chariot itself with a goad in his right hand. A third horse, the paraseiros, of pie-bald color, is being brought up on the left by a male figure who is barely visible because of overlapping. The fourth horse has not yet arrived. On the sides of the scene are vertical ivy borders.

Predella: A boar hunt is shown here with nude mounted hunters attacking a central boar with spears from both sides. The one on the left is beardless, the other wears a peaked Phrygian cap. The animal lowers its snout. Three spears stick in the boar's back while hunters on foot rush in from both ends.

At the bases of the handles are circumscribed tongues.

artifact.name: London B 300
artifact.summary: Shoulder: Chariot Race<lb>Main Panel: Dionysos, satyrs, and maenads<lb>Predella: Lion and boar.
artifact.collection_history: ex Durand Collection, no. 91. Found in 1849
artifact.decoration_description:
Shoulder: Horseman and charioteer with a quadriga race at a gallop to the right. The bearded charioteer leans forward over the horses, holding his reins with his left hand and his whip with his right. He wears a long white chiton. Behind comes the horseman with his long hair flowing, wearing a short white chiton, holding the reins with his left hand and plying his whip with his right. Behind the horseman is the meta (starting point). On the far right is a bearded brabeus (judge), facing left and watching the race as he leans on a staff with his right hand gesturing at the participants. He wears a striped himation. Above this panel is a frieze of circumscribed tongues. On the sides is a crenellated pattern. Chariot scenes occur frequently in the repertoire of the Euphiletos Painter.

On the main panel a Dionysiac thiasos is depicted with the god in the center, facing right, holding his kantharos in his right hand and a branching vine in his left. Behind him a bearded satyr plays the double flute as he walks to the right. At the far right another bearded satyr plays the kithara which is edged with added white to simulate ivory. Between this satyr and Dionysos, a maenad dances wildly to the right, while looking back toward the god. She plays krotala (clappers) with both hands and wears a wreath over her long hair, a long striped chiton, and a pardalis (leopard skin) knotted at her throat. At the far left is the other maenad who also dances, facing right. She wears her long hair with an ivy wreath, a peplos, and a short garment round her middle, embroidered and bordered with a meander, from which issues a snake. She carries a deer on her shoulders, holding the legs close with both arms. Across upper edge of the main panel runs the inscription, *P*A*N*F*A*I*O*S *M*E*P*O*I*S*E*N, "Pamphaios made me." Along the sides of the panels there are borders of embattled pattern.

Predella: A lion, moving to the right confronts a boar, facing left. Behind each of them is a palmette.
artifact.inscriptions: Across upper edge of the main panel runs the inscription, *P*A*N*F*A*I*O*S *M*E*P*O*I*S*E*N, "Pamphaios made me."

artifact.name: London B 298
artifact.summary: Side A: Wedding Procession. Side B: Five female figures. Stand A: Peleus wrestling with Thetis. Stand B: Dionysos and maenads.
artifact.collection_history: ex Blacas Collection, 1867.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: The bride and groom stand to the left, facing right in a quadriga, pulled by black and white horses. The bride holds her veil away from her face with a gesture typical of brides and wives (Hague 1988, 32-37). They are accompanied by a male figure who strums the kithara with a plektron (Apollo?) and the wreathed god Dionysos, holding a branching vine. At the far right female figure (Artemis?) holds a torch to lead the way. A fawn follows her. The bearded groom may be Zeus who holds the reins with both hands. Both he and his bride (Hera?) are dressed in long chitons and himatia, as are Apollo, Dionysos, and Artemis at the right.

Side B: Five female figures face the right. Two of them stand side by side. They all wear long embroidered chitons and himatia. The first and third hold out wreaths in their left hands, the second is veiled in a himation, the fourth and fifth have fillets and raise their left hands.

Lid: The finial is glazed in black. Below this there is a frieze of pendants, followed by a frieze of circumscribed lotus buds, and finally by an ivy chain.

On the lebes at the top of the shoulder, above the main design is a band of tongue pattern. The design is enclosed in a panel. On the lower body is a band of rays.

Stand: Side A: Peleus attacks from the left and grabs Thetis, his future bride, around the waist and buttocks. To do this he uses a standard wrestling hold. The muscular young hero wears a fillet, cuirass, and short chiton. She clearly resists his advances, her arms flying akimbo as she looks to the right for help. She has long wreathed hair and wears a long sleeveless chiton and an embroidered himation. Behind her are flames or wings emerging from her back, indicating that she is about to transform herself into another shape in order to be free of him. The women (Nereids?) on either side of her run away, although the one on the right looks back at her. They both wear long chitons and embroidered himatia.

Stand: Side B: At center Dionysos stands, facing right with a kantharos in his left hand. He is bearded with long wreathed hair and wears a long white chiton and embroidered himation. On either side maenads face him wearing long embroidered chitons and himatia over their heads. The maenad on the right runs to the left, looking back at and holding out her left hand to another, who holds out her hand to the first. She has long wreathed hair, and wears a long chiton and himation.

On the stand there is a double honeysuckle pattern above the design. Below the design is a frieze of pendants.
artifact.shape_description: The lebes is on a stand with its cover and two handles, each formed of two loops. Since the shape had ritual connections, the old black-figure technique was retained for this shape and for loutrophoroi.

artifact.name: London B 280
artifact.summary: Side A: Aeneas and Anchises<lb>Side B: fight
artifact.collection_history: ex Durand Collection, no. 414
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Aeneas is in the center, facing right as he carries his aged father Anchises out of Troy. The hero's body is bent over with the weight of the old man whose leg the son holds up with his right arm while he protects them with the Boeotian shield on his left. Aeneas wears a helmet, cuirass, and short chiton, with spears strapped to his back. The father Anchises has long hair and a beard, wears a long embroidered chiton and carries a scepter. He is framed by women running away on both sides, but looking back at the central scene. They wear long chitons bordered with stripes of added red and embroidered himatia. The one on the right has drawn hers up as a veil over her head. Could this be Kreusa, Aeneas' wife whom he forgets and leaves behind to perish at Troy? The other woman might possibly be Aphrodite, Aeneas' mother. Their gender is indicated also by their white flesh. On the left a beardless archer runs in clad in a high-peaked cap, cuirass, short chiton in added red and quiver. On the far right a balding, bearded elderly man stands absolutely still witnessing the pious act and holding onto his staff. He wears a long chiton and himation. The hair of both elderly males is depicted in added white.

Side B: On the left is a bearded warrior, fully armed, with short white chiton and embroidered chlamys, thrusting a spear with his raised left hand at an opponent who retreats before him. The first soldier protects himself with a shield on his right arm. The retreating soldier who runs to the right glances back at his assailant. He defends himself with a shield on his right arm and his spear with his left. He has two white plumes on his helmet and wears a short chiton in added red. His Boeotian shield has a thunderbolt device. Behind him is a third fully armed warrior in a short chiton in added red. He defends the man in front of him, by preparing to hurl his spear with his raised right hand while defending himself with a shield on his left. His shield has a dolphin in added white as device.

On the neck there is a double honeysuckle chain. Above the main figured design is a tongue pattern. Below the design are circumscribed lotus buds. Below that are rays on the lower body. Beneath the handles are palmettes.

artifact.name: London B 215
artifact.summary: Side A: Peleus and Thetis between a male and female eye siren. Shoulder: confronted lions and goats<lb>Side B: Apollo Kitharoidos, between a male and female eye siren. Shoulder: same as A. Below goat between lions and panther; panthers and goats<lb>Under handles: Hermes and Artemis.
artifact.collection_history: ex Canino Collection, 1523.
artifact.comparanda: for shape with rounded mouth, Northwick, Group of Bologna 33, 1.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: lunging from the right, Peleus wrestles with his future bride Thetis. He bends forward to lift her up, placing his shoulder beneath her waist and grasping her there with his left hand and pulling at her clothes with his left. The bearded hero wears a short embroidered chiton. She walks right, but turns back to the left, caught off guard by his advances. Thetis, her long hair wreathed, wears a long embroidered chiton and himation. Her right arm is around Peleus' body. Her changeability is hinted at by two simultaneously occurring transformations: a lion's head with open jaws and flowing mane emerging from her shoulder and by the panther which has leapt upon Peleus' back with its forepaws digging into his shoulder. On either side are sirens — human-headed bird-figures whose bodies are formed by great eyes. That on the right is a female siren, on the left, a bird with a bearded head. Both have long hair and myrtle wreaths. It is a rare occurrence when the male gender is shown with white flesh. The eyes themselves are formed of concentric circles with black pupils, surrounded by added red and white rings and black outlines against a reserved ground. This use recalls the conceit by the Amasis Painter. Shoulder: There are two occurrences of lions, facing right and confronting goats.

Side B: Apollo Kitharoidos faces right, holding his kithara with his left hand and sweeping across its strings with the plektron in his right. The beardless god has long hair with curls falling in front of his ears, and wears a long chiton and embroidered himation. The kithara is edged with white to simulate ivory ornaments. A deer stands by his side, facing right and nibbling on grass. As on Side A, on either side are sirens, human-headed bird-figures, whose bodies are formed by great eyes. That on the right is a female siren, on the left, a bird with a bearded head. Both have long hair and myrtle wreaths. It is a rare occurrence when the male gender is shown with white flesh. The eyes themselves are formed of concentric circles with black pupils, surrounded by added red and white rings and black outlines against a reserved ground. Shoulder: Just as on A, there are two occurrences of lions, facing right and confronting goats.

Under the handles: Hermes moves to the right, looking back at Apollo. The bearded god wears his hair looped up under a fillet, a petasos, embroidered chlamys, short chiton, and endromides (winged boots). He carries his caduceus and ivy branches in his right hand and raises his left. Beneath the second handle, Artemis moves to the left, looking back at Peleus and Thetis. She has long hair, confined in a mitra (crown), and wears an embroidered chiton and himation. She carries a bow in her raised left hand. Her flesh is in added white as is customary for females. There are ivy branches in the field beside both figures.

Predella: There is a frieze of confronted animals. Panthers and goats occur twice and there is a lion confronting a panther with a goat facing to the left between the animals.

On the neck there is the usual double palmette pattern, but on a white ground.
artifact.shape_description: The mouth is of unusual form — rounded above.

artifact.name: London B 174
artifact.summary: Side A: wedded pair in chariot<lb>Side B: Theseus and Minotaur
artifact.collection_history: presented by S. Addington, esq., 1868. ex Collection of Samuel Rogers.
artifact.condit: Intact
artifact.graffiti: Underneath is incised q, three times.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A:

A quadriga moves to the right. In it stand the bridal pair; the beardless bridegroom holding the reins, the bride veiled. Both wear embroidered himatia. Behind them is the beardless parochos, facing right in a long chiton and embroidered himation. To the right of the horse walk three women in single file, with embroidered peploi carrying objects, such as a liknon (a winnowing fan used to clean wheat and having connotations of fertility and plenty) or a vannus, for carrying offerings at sacrifices and used in the worship of Iacchos. The middle one carries either a basket or a sieve. They all wear embroidered peploi. In front of the horses is a bearded male figure, probably the proegetes walking to the right and looking back at the pair. He wears a petasos, an embroidered chlamys, and endromides (high boots).

R. Hague (Hague 1988, 32-37) believes the anachronistic touch of the bridal couple riding in a chariot was intended to elevate the proceedings to the level of the epic or divine.

Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur are in the center with Theseus attacking from the left. He leans forward and with his left arm forces the Minotaur to his knees, grasping him by the neck with one hand and burying the sword in his throat with the other. The hero wears a fillet on his close-cropped hair and a short embroidered chiton, girt at the waist. He has beginnings of a beard. The Minotaur, with a bull's head on a man's body, struggles to get free, clutching at Theseus with his right hand and trying to aim a white stone at him with his raised left hand. Behind each figure there are two standing figures framing the action. Are these Athenian youths and maidens anxiously awaiting their moment of freedom? Both girls have white skin, a peplos and embroidered himation. The beardless youths wear long chitons and embroidered himatia.

There is a double border of entwined honeysuckle at the top of the design panel. On the lower body there are rays.

artifact.name: London B 163
artifact.summary: Side A: Herakles and the Stymphalian birds<lb>Side B: Two Maenads dancing in one mantle and three satyrs
artifact.other_bibliography: Gerhard Auserlene Vasenbilder iv, pl. 324
artifact.collection_history: Canino Collection
artifact.comparanda: For Side A: Boulogne 420, side A.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Herakles and the Stymphalian birds. Herakles stands on the left facing right. He holds his sling shot with his left hand and aims with his right. He wears the lion's skin over his head and body with the forepaws tied about his neck and a girdle around his waist, his quiver hangs on his shoulder. Beneath this he wears a short bordered chiton in added red. Eleven birds are flying this way and that in great confusion while five remain on the ground.

Side B: In the center two maenads are confronted, gesturing with their hands as if speaking to one another. They are wrapped in the same chlaina, embroidered with white rosettes (Soph. Trach. 540). Both wear a fillet and a peplos with overfold. Between them on the ground is a small bird facing right. Behind one at the far left a bearded satyr with a full goatskin on his back dances to the right. On the right are two bearded satyrs dancing back to back.

There is a lotus palmette border at the top of the panel on Side A. On Side B the frieze above the design panel bears entwined honeysuckle flowers.

artifact.name: London B 150
artifact.summary: Side A: a youth setting out. Side B: the same.
artifact.collection_history: ex Blacas Collection, 1867.
artifact.graffiti: Underneath the foot is incised *M*X*L.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: At center a male figure stands, facing right and carrying a spear in his left hand. He is bearded with long hair and wears a fillet, long chiton in added red, and a himation embroidered with white rosettes. In front of him is a bearded male figure running to the right and looking back to the left. He holds up a wreath in his right hand to the first figure and grasps a spear in his left. His long hair is bound with a fillet and tied back. He wears a chlamys embroidered with white rosettes. A similar male figure stands to the extreme left. On the right is a bearded male figure facing left and holding a spear in his right hand and a wreath in his left. He has long hair confined in a beaded fillet and wears a long chiton in added red and a himation embroidered with white rosettes.

Side B: Similar scene. At center a male figure stands, facing right and carrying a spear in his left hand. He is bearded with long hair and wears a fillet, long chiton with dots in added red, and an embroidered himation. Behind him is a bearded male figure facing right with a staff in his right hand and his left raised. His long hair is bound with a beaded fillet and he wears a long chiton in added red and an embroidered himation. In front of the first figure is a beardless male figure advancing to the right, but looking back to the left with his right hand raised. He wears his long hair tied back and confined with a fillet and an embroidered chlamys. On the right is a bearded male standing to the left and holding a spear in his right hand and a wreath in his left. He has long hair confined in a fillet and wears a long chiton in added red and an embroidered himation.

Over the design panel is a frieze of lotus buds. 'Affected' style.
artifact.shape_description: Type C with rolled lip

artifact.name: London B 148
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysiac throng. Side B: Theseus and the Minotaur.
artifact.collection_history: ex Basseggio Collection, 1848
artifact.condit: There are chips from the rim and the vase is much faded.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: The composition is made up of Dionysos, a Maenad, four satyrs and a hare. On the left two hirsute satyrs dance around a maenad. She stands facing right with her long hair tied back. She wears a nebris or fawn skin over her long bordered chiton. Underneath the spout a hairless satyr crouches, facing left and bending over to pet a hare which faces left. Further to the right the god Dionysos stands formally with his drinking horn in his left hand. He wears a long bordered chiton, ornamented with rosettes dotted in added red, and a himation draped over his shoulders. His hair is long and wreathed in ivy. Further right another hirsute satyr raises his left arm, and prances off to the right. All of the satyrs have long, thick hair and beards as well as horses' tails. In addition, three have hairy bodies shown by a stippled pattern. This Dionysiac iconography was a popular choice in the painter's repertoire.

Side B: The central scene shows Theseus killing the Minotaur. A long-haired Theseus on the left strides right. He holds the Minotaur's left arm in his left hand and plunges his sword into the monster's neck with his right. He wears a fillet, cuirass, and short chiton on which there is a large dot rosette in added red on his hip. Beneath his legs is a conical stone on which he has laid his chlamys. The Minotaur, right of center, has a bull's head and mane and the hirsute (stippled) body of a man. He has fallen on his left knee, grabbing Theseus from behind with his right hand and clutching a stone in his left. On each side of the central group are two beardless male figures. Can these youths represent Athenian victims? The one on the right and the one behind Theseus wear striped bordered himatia. The one on the left is nude. The one behind the Minotaur has an embroidered chlamys over his shoulders and his hair tied back. Can these different garments be marks of status? All of the youths have a lock of hair in front twisted over a fillet.

There is a lotus-palmette frieze above the main design. Around the spout are rays. On the flattened lip of the spout there are zigzags. Beneath each handle is a palmette. On the lower body there are two levels of rays. A reserved band runs around the foot.
artifact.shape_description: This is a vase within a vase with outer part resembling an amphora, accessible through the spout only, and the inner part, accessible through the top. It was used for cooling wine. The cold water was poured into the outer chamber through the spout and the wine was poured into the inner chamber. The Dionysiac iconography on Side A emphasizes the vase's function.

artifact.name: London B 144
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena with Hermes and unidentified man. Side B: The winner in a horse race.
artifact.other_bibliography: Gerhard Auserlene Vasenbilder iv, 247
artifact.collection_history: Found at Vulci in 1849.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: At center stands Athena, facing left between two male figures, Hermes and Zeus(?). Her head, waist, and feet are shown in profile, while her shoulders are frontal. She holds her shield with her right hand and raises a spear high with her left. She wears a helmet, the high crest of which overlaps the tongue frieze on the upper border of the panel. Her shield bears the device of a ten-point star in added white. She wears a peplos, the upper part of which has borders in added red, the lower part with scales, girt at the waist, over which hangs her aegis decorated with a fringe of snakes in the front. Her face and arms are in added white for female flesh. Hermes on the left faces right, holding his caduceus in his right hand and raising his left to greet the goddess. He wears a petasos, a short chiton, an embroidered chlamys, and endromides (high boots). On the right stands the other male figure (Zeus?), facing left. He is bearded and wears a long chiton and himation. He carries a scepter of authority in his right hand.

Side B: A youthful male figure is shown on horseback at center, facing right. He reins in his magnificent horse with both hands and leans back slightly. He wears a short chiton bordered with dots. Behind him is a nude youth, facing right and carrying a tripod on his head and a wreath in his left hand. Both objects symbolize the victory. In front of the horseman a bearded figure walks to the right. This man, perhaps a herald, wears a long chiton, and white and red himation, and fillet. His head is raised slightly as if speaking the words inscribed before him, *D*U[*S]*N*E*I*K*E*T[*O]*U *H*I[*P]*P*O*S *N*I*K*A*I.

On the neck there is a lotus-palmette chain. Beneath a raised fillet at the junction of neck and shoulder is a circumscribed tongue pattern in black and added red. On the lower body above the foot is a band of rays.
artifact.inscriptions: Inscribed before the herald are the words, *D*U[*S]*N*E*I*K*E*T[*O]*U *H*I[*P]*P*O*S *N*I*K*A*I.

artifact.name: London B 134
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena. Side B: Pentathlon.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: At center stands Athena, facing left between two Doric columns surmounted by cocks. Her head, waist, and feet are shown in profile, while her shoulders are frontal. She holds her shield with her right hand and raises a spear high above her head with her left. She wears a helmet, the high crest of which overlaps the tongue frieze on the upper border of the panel, the shield bears the device of a wheel in added white. She wears a long, sleeveless chiton embroidered with patterns of stars and spirals, girt at the waist, over which hangs her aegis decorated with a scale pattern and inner and outer fringes of snakes. Rapid movement is indicated by the folds of her chiton. Her face and arms are in added white for female flesh. In front of Athena is inscribed *T*O*N*A*Q*E*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L*O*N, "(I am) one of the prizes from Athens." On the shield is inscribed, *E*U*F*I*L*E*T*O*S *K*A*L*O*S, "Euphiletos is beautiful."

Side B: There are four bearded nude athletes, competing in the pentathlon. They proceed from left to right. On the left is one with both arms raised, holding halteres (jumping weights) painted in added white, and about to leap. The next is about to hurl a spear which he holds by the amentum (throwing strap) in his right hand. His left hand is raised for balance. His left knee is also raised, about to lunge forward. The next walks, carrying his discus in his right hand, his left hand raised. On the right another figure, walking right, turns his head to the left. He gets ready to throw his spear with his right hand. He holds the spear by the amentum (throwing strap) with the point down and keeps his left hand raised and out of the way of the javelin.

On the neck there is a lotus-palmette chain. Beneath a raised fillet at the junction of neck and shoulder is a circumscribed tongue pattern in black and added red. On the lower body above the foot is a band of rays.
artifact.inscriptions: In front of Athena is inscribed *T*O*N*A*Q*E*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L*O*N, "(I am) one of the prizes from Athens." On the shield is inscribed, *E*U*F*I*L*E*T*O*S *K*A*L*O*S, "Euphiletos is beautiful."

artifact.name: London B 130
artifact.summary: Body, side A: Athena striding; side B: Chariot race<lb>Neck, side A: siren; side B: owl
artifact.sources_used: Walters 1893, 98; Haspels 1936, 7; CVA, 1, 3, pl. 1 a,b; Beazley 1986, 106 n. 7; Corbett 1960, 52-60; Boardman 1974, 168, fig. 296, 1 and 2; Williams 1985, 30, fig. 34; J. Neils, in Neils 1992, 30, fig. 19; Kyle 1992, 93 fig. 59
artifact.other_bibliography: JHS 80 11, pls. 1 and 2
artifact.collection_history: Found in the Burgon Tomb, discovered by Thomas Burgon near the Acharnian (northern city Gate) in 1813, ex Burgon Collection, 1842
artifact.condit: Side B is much repaired.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Athena stands to the right, facing left. Her head, waist, and feet are shown in profile, while her shoulders are frontal. She holds her shield with her left hand and raises a spear high above her head with her right. She wears a helmet, the high crest of which overlaps the upper border of the panel, the shield bears the device of a dolphin, facing left. She wears a peplos in added red with incised meanders, girt at the waist with a broad girdle, over which hangs an overfold with meander borders, and an aegis with a fringe of snakes. Her face and arms are in added white for female flesh. In front of her is inscribed in retrograde, *T*O*N *A*Q*E*N*E*Q[*E]*N *A*Q*L*O*N *E*M*I, "I am one of the prizes from Athens." On the neck of Side A is a siren which faces right with its left wing advanced and its right wing stretched out behind.

Side B: The synoris, a cart race with a team of two horses or mules, indicates the event for which the winner won the prize. A beardless driver in a light cart on the left drives on a pair of horses on the right in a race to the right. The driver sits with his feet resting on a foot board in the front of the car. He wears a sleeveless chiton in added red. He holds a goad in his right hand and a kalaurops (a long rod from which hang two pointed metal objects to incite the horses with their jingling). The horses are yoked to a transverse bar fastened to the pole; their yokes are those customarily used for mules. The wheels are those of cart not a chariot with no spokes, but a diametrical bar crossed by two at right angles. On the neck of side B is an owl with frontal face, facing right, its right wing stretched out, its left wing down. on the lower body is a band of rays.

Inside it were found cremated bones and six small vases: a black-figure lekythos, a plain hand-made jug, and four black glaze vessels, funerary offerings for the man who had presumably won one of the most prestigious games at the Panathenaic festival. This is the earliest known Panathenaic amphora.
artifact.inscriptions: In front of Athena is inscribed *T*O*N *A*Q*E*N*E*Q*N *A*Q*L*O*N *E*M*I (retr.), "I am one of the prizes from Athens."

artifact.name: London 1977.12-11.9
artifact.summary: Horses.
artifact.condit: The lid is in excellent condition.
artifact.decoration_description: Horses. Four grazing horses follow each other to the right around the perimeter of the lid. Their eyes and manes are executed in a sort of outline, their bodies in silhouette. Between two of the horses stands a foal, executed in pure Geometric silhouette. A heron stands feeding between the forelegs of one of the horses. A stylized plant is drawn between the forelegs of another. Beneath the belly of each horse is a diamond motif with a point coming out of each side, its interior divided into four squares. Multiple chevrons and dotted lozenges fill the rest of the available space.

artifact.name: London 1964.4-15.1
artifact.summary: Side A: head of a horse. Side B: head of a horse.
artifact.other_bibliography: Cat. Sotheby, 24 February 1964 no. 94, and pl. at p. 30; The Times, 16 April 1964; AR 1966-7, 47, fig. 1.
artifact.dimensions: H 31.1; W with handles 23.7; D of mouth 15.5; D of foot 12.2
artifact.collection_history: The British Museum purchased the amphora at a Sotheby's sale in 1964. The provenance and history of the amphora before it reached the London market are unknown.
artifact.condit: The glaze is uneven and has fired orange-brown in parts, especially on the reverse. The glaze has also flaked and peeled in places.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: head of horse. The head and neck of a haltered horse is drawn in profile to the right. Its mane is divided into eight locks which fall over its neck. The forelock is divided into two locks and falls between the horse's ears. Added red is used for the mane, and deep incision marks the halter and facial features of the horse.

Side B: head of a horse. The horse on side B differs only slightly from that on side A; the mane is here rendered in seven locks rather than eight.
artifact.shape_description: Type B amphora.

artifact.name: London 1961.7-10.1
artifact.summary: Side A: warriors leaving home. Side B: komos.
artifact.other_bibliography: Cat. Sotheby 19 June 1961, frontispiece; Daily Telegraph 12 July 1961; ILN 22 July 1961, 135; AR 1962-3, 52-53; Corbett 1965, pl. 4; LIMC, I, pl. 233, Aias I 16; Beazley Addenda 2, 264.
artifact.dimensions: H 40.2; D of rim 46.7; W at handles 48.5
artifact.collection_history: The vase was purchased by the museum at a Sotheby sale in June, 1961.
artifact.condit: The vase is in very good condition.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: warrior leaving home. A young warrior takes his departure while an older warrior, a bearded man and a woman bid him farewell. The young, unbearded warrior (Teucer?) walks to the left, his head turned back toward the older warrior on the right and his right hand raised in a farewell gesture. He wears a short chiton, cuirass and a helmet of Attic type. A sword and quiver hang from his belt, and he carries a shield whose shield device is a scorpion. The cheek pieces of his helmet are turned up. The bearded older warrior (Ajax?) has stretched out a braceleted arm, palm up as if in entreaty; in his other hand he holds a long stick and a shield. The shield device is a snake, and the fringed shield apron is decorated with a large eye. He is dressed similarly to the younger man, but his helmet is Thracian and he wears it with cheek pieces down. His chiton appears to be pleated rather than plain. A woman stands to the left of the scene holding a phiale toward the youth, her left hand raised, palm facing inward. In her left hand she holds a flower which was once white but has now faded. She wears a long chiton and a thin fillet around her head. A bearded man stands on the right wrapped in a long mantle, his right hand lifted but hidden behind the older warrior's shield.

Side B: komos. A flute-girl plays between two dancing youths. She steps to the right playing a double-flute. She has short hair crowned by a wreath and wears a long, simple chiton through which the outline of her legs can be seen. The youth on the left is shown in profile to the right, his outstretched left arm holding one part of a garment that is flung over his left shoulder. The youth on the right is infibulated. He faces right with his head turned toward the left, his weight supported by his bent left leg. He holds a garment in both hands which passes behind his back and falls over his raised right arm. Both youths wear wreaths and chaplets, like the flute-girl.
artifact.inscriptions: Written vertically between the woman and the left-hand warrior on Side A is: *K*A*L*O*S, while the meaningless letters *L*O*N and *L*O*N*U appear in the spaces between the heads of the three men.

artifact.name: London 1929.11-11.1
artifact.summary: Interior: youth with spear (hunter?). Side A: Herakles and the Centaurs. Side B: battle.
artifact.other_bibliography: Bloesch 1940, pl. 36; Boardman 1975, 57-59, fig. 72; Antichità Altoadriatiche XII, 2, figs. 1,4,5,6; Beazley Addenda 2, 168.
artifact.condit: The vase in is excellent condition.
artifact.comparanda: For the shape see Bloesch, 134 no. I.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: youth with spear. A young man stands in combative attitude holding a spear in his right hand. He holds out his chlamys like a shield over his left arm.

A: Herakles and the Centaurs. Herakles battles three centaurs. Herakles, nude, has lunged forward brandishing a club against a centaur with spotted hide. The centaur turns round in an effort to hurl back a rock at Herakles; his front legs have buckled and he has fallen onto one knee. The centaur on the left makes ready to throw a large rock, and that on the right is armed with a small tree. The centaurs have long hair, beards and pointed ears. A sheathed sword and a quiver hang at Herakles' side.

B: battle. Five warriors armed with spear and shield engage in combat. The warrior in the center, in profile to the left, has fallen back onto his left knee, still holding onto his shield. Two companions rush to his rescue. The one in front thrusts his spear forward, his shield held up on his left arm. The man behind him runs alongside his horse, his spear and shield held ready. The first man's shield device is a running man. The warrior in the rear holds a shield with a lupin- or plane-leaf shield device. The shield device of the fallen warrior is the head of a bearded satyr. The two warriors attacking from the left are also accompanied by a horse. The man in front holds up his shield to fend off the spear thrust of the oncoming warrior, his own spear held at his side. His companion runs behind him, his horse running at his side. All five warriors wear the same type of high crested helmet but are otherwise naked. The fallen warrior wears a sheathed sword on a strap over his chest.
artifact.inscriptions: On the interior: *E*P*O*I*E*S*E, made me. On side B: *E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N, made me.
artifact.shape_description: For the shape see Bloesch: 134 no. 1. Note the off-set lip.

artifact.name: London 1928.7-19.3
artifact.summary: Side A: Paris and Helen<lb>Side B: youths
artifact.other_bibliography: Sotheby Sale Cat., 5 July 1928, no. 44; Beazley 1943, 72; Trendall 1952, 24 n. 5; Trendall 1967, 250, 2/148; Trendall 1976, pl. 11; Trendall 1989, fig. 275-6.
artifact.collection_history: The vase was formerly in the collection of the Misses Dillwyn Parrish. It was acquired by the British Museum at a Sotheby sale in July, 1928.
artifact.condit: The vase is in good condition, with some wear of the surface glaze.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Paris and Helen. Paris stands holding his horse as Helen approaches accompanied by a handmaiden. Helen occupies the approximate center of the scene. She stands with her head modestly tipped down. Both hands are raised as she pulls back her veil. She wears a transparent chiton, a thin mantle and sandals. Her maid stands with ankles crossed in a leaning pose, though there is nothing to lean against. She is pulling a piece of drapery forward to cover her head, and is naked but for a necklace and a wreath. Paris, on the left, wears a short cape knotted at his throat and a wreath over his hair, but is otherwise naked.
