Bibliography:Philippart 1928, 50; D. M. Robinson, AJA 21 (1917): 167, fig. 7; Beazley 1918, 7, 12, no. 51; Hoppin 1919, vol. II, 261, no. 47c; Beazley 1925, 17, no. 70; Beazley 1933a, pl. X; CVA, USA fasc. 6, Robinson fasc. 2, 11, pl. I.1; ARV2, 59, no. 55.

This fragment arrived at the university as part of the restored sections of the kylix by the Pistoxenos Painter (Baltimore, Hopkins AIA B12). Subsequently, Beazley recognized the Hopkins piece to be part of the exterior of a kylix to which fragments in Florence, Heidelberg, Braunschweig, Bowdoin, and the Villa Giulia also belong (see above, Beazley pl. X; and Bowdoin 1913.14).

For Oltos, see J. D. Beazley, JHS 58 (1938):267; Boardman 1975, 56-57; ARV2, 53-67; Para., 326-28; Beazley Addenda 2, 1933, 7, pls. I.21, 23; X. The Bowdoin fragment appears in Buitron 1972, 69, no. 30.

The maenad on our segment formed part of a procession of satyrs and maenads whose counterparts on the opposite side are a fleeing girl and two men. In the tondo was a representation of Pegasus, together with the signature of Kachrylion, the prominent Attic potter for whom Phintias (see Baltimore, Hopkins AIA B4) and the Kiss Painter (see Baltimore, Hopkins AIA B5) may also have worked.

Bloesch 1940, 45-50.

Oltos was one of the most skilled early artists of red-figure vasepainting.

E. Finkenstaedt, AJA 72 (1968): 383, pl. 129.

He signed two cups and is accredited with over one hundred fifty vessels in all. Although he primarily painted kylixes, he also worked on amphorae, psykters, stamnoi, and a kyathos. He was employed by the best potters of his age, including Kachrylion, Nikosthenes, Pamphaios, and Hischylos.

Bloesch 1940, 31, 33, 45-50, 64; ARV2, 53.

The artist's distinctive style can be recognized in the stumpy bodies and the square heads with long noses and narrow, elongated eyes. Also characteristic is the patterning of the extended figures. Oltos's use of relief line was extensive and particularly skilled.

artifact.name: Baltimore, Hopkins 9286
artifact.summary: Side A: three figures running. Side B: Youth addressing two other youths.
artifact.essay_text:
ca. 380-350 B.C.9286. Robinson Collection. "Tarentum." Ht, 34.8 cm; diam rim, 38 cm; diam foot, 19 cm. Intact.Side A

Three figures run in left profile. In front is bearded nude male with pail in left hand, torch in uplifted right hand, and cloak over shoulders. In center is woman dressed in chiton with overfold, her right hand uplifted, her left hand holding a tympanum. Behind her is nude youth carrying jug in right hand. His mantle is flung over the left arm and hand, in which he holds a spear. Relief contour for some details. Band of wave pattern above figures.

Side B

Bearded youth with short, curly hair stands in right profile and addresses two youths who turn toward him. All figures are enveloped in long mantles to ankles. Youth in center holds staff in right hand; in field behind his head is reserved disc.

Figures on both sides stand on narrow reserved band above band of leftward meander that terminates below handles in dotted cross-square, from which rises a scroll motif. Above pictures is leftward laurel band between reserved bands. Zone of tongues around roots of handles.

Bibliography: FR, 252, no. 4; CVA, USA fasc. 7, Robinson fasc. 3, 27, pl. XIX; Trendall 1938, 26 n. 41; Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 56, no. 2.

This krater is one of eleven vases attributed to the Hoppin Painter, who with five colleagues formed the Hoppin Group, painting in the Plain Apulian style.

Trendall 1966, 20; Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 55-56. Our vase is p. 56, no. 2.

The workshop was located in Tarentum and was active between about 380 and 350 B.C. The Hoppin Painter was probably trained by artists of the school of the Tarporley Painter (400-380 B.C.), a disciple of the Sisyphos Painter, who originated both the Plain and the Ornate Styles.

The Hoppin Painter worked mostly on bell kraters, although he also painted one pelike and one calyx krater. His vases are recognized by their tall, slim figures with flying drapery, the wrapped heads of the women, and the youths with white fillets and himatia draped over their arms.

Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 55.

The three figures on the reverse of our vase also appear on vases by the artist in Lecce

Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 56, no. 3, and Lecce 620, CVA, Italy fasc. 6, Lecce fasc. 2, pl. 12.

 and Cambridge.

Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 56, no. 1.

 The style of the Hoppin Painter is especially close to that of the Lecce Painter,

Cambitoglou & Trendall 1961, 62.

 who was active at about the same time, the second quarter of the fourth century.

artifact.name: Baltimore, Hopkins 9022
artifact.summary: Satyr and maenad
artifact.essay_text:
ca. 500 B.C.9022. Ht, 18.9 cm; diam mouth, 4 cm; diam foot, 5 cm. Mended from many pieces, with parts of handle and rim restored.

Rim and inside of neck glazed. Glazed handle, with underside reserved. On shoulder is chain of lotus buds, with stalks linking every three buds; band of tongues above.

Body:

Satyr strides in right profile, left leg advanced. Right outstretched hand grasps right wrist of a maenad, while left arm is outstretched toward her genitals. Maenad advances in left profile, left leg advanced and both arms outstretched. Contour and interior markings of satyr incised. Delicate incisions for maenad's eye, brow, hairline, arms, back left leg, and back of right thigh. Interior of maenad was painted white.

Two red lines above scene; one red line beneath figures as groundline. Foot in two degrees, glazed except for reserved side of top step and underside.

In Six technique the background is in black glaze, like the background in red-figure vasepainting, but the artist works the figures either by incising their contours through the black glaze or by applying white, red, or brown paint on top of the glaze before the vase is fired.

Boardman 1974, 178; J. Six, Gazette Archéologique 13 (1888): 193-294; Haspels 1936, 106ff.; P. E. Corbett, JHS 85 (1965):24; Kurtz 1975, 116-19.

The painter may, as in the case with our maenad, render a figure entirely or mostly in color, using incision only for details. Alternately, he may work a figure like our satyr in "outline Six," wherein all of the figure is incised and no color is added.

Kurtz 1975, 116, 119.

The Six technique originated during the first half of the sixth century, but at first was employed only for parts of figures. Not until around 530 B.C., in the experimental atmosphere that stimulated the introduction of red-figure vasepainting, did Nikosthenes and Psiax first work entire vases in Six technique.

Boardman 1974, 178.

In the later sixth century the technique was most popular in the workshops of the Sappho

ABV, 507-8; Haspels 1936, 94-130, 227-28; Para., 246-48.

 and Diosphos Painters,

ABV, 508-11; Haspels 1936, 94-130, 235-36; Para., 248-50. To the examples listed by Beazley, add: Hornbostel 1977, 298, no. 258; Kurtz 1975, pl. 6.4 in Columbia, Missouri. Another, surely by one of these two painters, is discussed by D. von Bothmer in Brommer Festschrift, 61, pl. 19 (New York 67.11.22).

 artists who were influenced, and perhaps trained, by the Edinburgh Painter. The Sappho and Diosphos Painters were primarily black-figure artists who painted a variety of shapes but specialized in lekythoi, which they executed in Six technique as well as in black-figure and white-ground. The Diosphos Painter is credited with over thirty-six lekythoi; the Sappho Painter is assigned only eleven lekythoi and one hydria.

Our vase is best paralleled by work of the Sappho Painter. Although both the Sappho and the Diosphos Painters used lekythoi of the DL type, those of the Sappho Painter have the shallow mouths and squat, full bodies with tapering profiles of the Hopkins vase, in contrast to the deeper mouths and straight-sided cylinders preferred by the Diosphos Painter.

Kurtz 1975, 80.

The stalks in the bud patterns of the Sappho Painter generally skip two buds, as on our example, while those of the Diosphos Painter usually skip only one, but occasionally two, and sometimes add white dots between the buds.

Haspels 1936, 94.

 The Six lekythoi of both painters have a red line beneath the scene, but the Sappho Painter almost always applies two red lines above, as on our vessel, while the Diosphos Painter may employ a checker or key pattern.

Haspels 1936, 95.

 While the Diosphos Painter often relies upon incision alone, the Sappho Painter also executes elements of his representation in added white.

Kurtz 1975, 119.

 Our vase is especially similar to a lekythos by the Sappho Painter in New York on which a satyr, worked entirely by incision, crouches amid an amphora, serpent, and rocks, all of which are rendered in white.

Haspels 1936, 228, no. 43, which is the same as Bulletin of the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1930):136, fig. 4. (17.8 cm; New York 23.160.87).

On the Hopkins vase the incisions for the maenad are so much lighter and more delicate than those for the satyr that they could not have been intended to be seen through the white paint and thus must be preliminary incisions intended as guidelines for the artist. On this lekythos the artist carefully respected these sketches in his final application of color, but on other Six vases the preliminary incisions are often disregarded.

P. Corbett, JHS 85 (1965):16-28, especially 24-25.

The Sappho Painter used Six technique early in his career, and certainly the heavy thighs and strict profile of the satyr support a date for our vase of ca. 500 B.C.

artifact.name: Austin 1980.63
artifact.summary: Flying Nike with kithara and phiale.
artifact.collection: Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, University of Texas at Austin
artifact.essay_text:
Collection of the Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, University of Texas, Austin (1980.63)Attributed to the Oionokles PainterCa. 470 B.C.Height: 36.5 cm.Flying Nike with kithara and phiale

This charming lekythos shows a winged Victory hovering in mid-flight. Her progress is to the left, but momentarily checked, as she looks back to the right. Her ornate wings and her drapery, a chiton and diagonal mantle, flutter out behind. She wears a diadem in her flaxen hair, which is rolled up in back. Lightsome as this Nike is, she is burdened with heavy equipment: in her outstretched right hand she holds a plain phiale; in her left is cradled a large kithara or lyre, the strings of which are facing her. A dotted strap with trailing ends attaches the instrument to her left hand, and a long, fringed, diamond-patterned scarf is draped over her forearm. There is a nonsense inscription in the field under the wings. The picture is framed above and below by zones of stopped meander, and as is common on lekythoi of this period, palmettes decorate the shoulder.

The figure of Nike, while known earlier in Attic vase-painting, becomes especially prevalent after ca. 480 B.C., especially on smaller vases like Nolan amphorae and lekythoi. The victory she alludes to is not always known, unless she is accompanied by other figures, like warriors or athletes, or carries a specific attribute. Here, the presence of the kithara implies a victory in a musical competition. A Nolan amphora formerly in Goluchow by the same hand (ARV2, 646, 10) details the narrative more fully: a Nike with kithara on one side is presenting the instrument to a young kitharode or lyre-player with outstretched hand on the other. While the musician is missing on the Austin lekythos, his presence is implied by the Nike's glance.

This painting represents an extremely fine work by the so-called Oionokles Painter, an early classic artist whose name derives from four kalos inscriptions. Beazley calls him a follower of the Providence Painter, who in turn was a pupil of the Berlin Painter (Shapiro 1981a, no. 63), and both predecessors produced many pictures of Nike. However, the high quality of this work singles it out, and perhaps the same can be said of it, as Beazley said of an earlier lekythos with a kithara-bearing Nike by the Pan Painter (Oxford 312; ARV2, 556, 102), "a triumph of technique — pot, figure, patternwork."

Bibliography: Unpublished. On Nike: Isler-Kerényi 1969. On kithara playing: Beazley 1922, 70-98. On the Oionokles Painter:ARV2, 646-649.

Jenifer Neils

artifact.name: Austin 1980.37
artifact.summary: Duel of warriors flanked by riders
artifact.collection: Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, University of Texas at Austin
artifact.essay_text:
Collection of the Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, the University of Texas, Austin, James R. Dougherty, Jr. Foundation and Archer M. Huntington Museum Fund Purchase (1980.37)Warrior GroupCa. 600 B.C.Height: 6.2 cm.Duel of warriors flanked by riders.

The incision and attention to detail are particularly careful on this miniature Corinthian perfume bottle. The two warriors on foot are heraldically posed, and the two squires who wait behind them are also perfectly symmetrical. Only the contrast between the two shields which occupy the center of the composition, one seen from the outside, the other from the inside, mitigates the rigid symmetry.

The combatants are dressed alike in low crested Corinthian helmets, short tunics with decorated border at top and bottom, and greaves. Subtle variations in the incised decoration of the helmet crests and the borders of the garments also enliven the composition. They fight with spears, though the right hand warrior's weapon is mostly obscured behind his body and shield. The other warrior's spear crosses behind his head, an impossible position, in order not to block our view of his profile. The one shield device we can see is a splendid frontal bull's head which fills the surface and even overlaps the rim. The horsemen also wear tunics, though undecorated, and fillets in their long flowing hair.

The rest of the vase's surface is almost covered with filling ornament, mostly plain blobs and rosettes whose incision is not always as careful as that of the figures. In addition there is a pattern of tongues on the shoulder and the lip, and an incised double palmette on the handle.

The footless round aryballos became a very popular shape rather suddenly in the Early Corinthian period, at the end of the seventh century, perhaps due to contact with the Near East, where the shape had long been known. By about 600, the animal style that had dominated earlier Corinthian vase-painting was starting to die out, and a figured style, favoring soldiers, horsemen, and padded dancers, was increasingly popular. The warrior Group comprises several dozen aryballoi of Payne's shape B1. Although the Austin vase is unattributed, according to D. A. Amyx the style recalls the Heraldic Riders Painter.

Bibliography: Amyx 1988, 309, 11 bis; CVA, Castle Ashby (Great Britain 15) 19 and pl. 30, 4-6; Christie's Sale Catalogue 1980, London, July 2, 1980, lot. 54ii, p. 95, ill. On the Warrior Group: Payne 1931, 288.

artifact.name: Austin 1980.33
artifact.summary: Herakles wrestling the Nemean Lion
artifact.collection: Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, University of Texas at Austin
artifact.essay_text:
Collection of the Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, the University of Texas, Austin, James R. Dougherty, Jr. Foundation and Archer M. Huntington Museum Fund Purchase (1980.33)Related to the Class of Vatican G47520-500 B.C.Height: 13.9 cm.Herakles wrestling the Nemean Lion

The first of Herakles' labors was the capture and killing of the lion which had ravaged the valley around Nemea, in the northeastern Peloponnesos. The lion's invulnerable pelt rendered all weapons useless and forced the hero to engage the beast in a wrestling match and finally strangle it. Herakles skinned the dead animal and thereafter wore the impervious hide for protection, and in vase-painting it is usually his distinguishing attribute (see for example New Orleans 16.38).

On this vase, the wrestling match is in full swing and the outcome is still in doubt. Herakles is entirely nude, but for a fillet around his head and a baldric worn diagonally around his chest, to support a sword. His bow, quiver, and sword all rest in the branches of a tree in the background. With his left hand the hero is grasping the lion's belly, while his right holds off a rear paw with which the lion tries to claw Herakles' head. He hunches over the lion's luxuriant mane, leaving his thigh and groin area exposed and dangerously close to the lion's open jaws. Behind Herakles stands Iolaos, his young nephew and frequent companion in his labors. He wears a corselet over a short chiton and holds Herakles' knotty club. His sword hangs from a baldric, and a second baldric crosses in an X pattern. He stretches out his left hand over the wrestling pair as a weak gesture of fright, or of encouragement for the hero.

In early black-figure, before about 540, Herakles and the lion regularly wrestle standing up. The great master Exekias apparently first showed them wrestling on the ground, as John Boardman has recently demonstrated, on a vase, fragments of which are at Ensérune. After that this version became increasingly popular in the last quarter of the sixth century, the period of the Austin oinochoe.

This vase is similar in shape to a large class of late sixth century oinochoai designated by Beazley the Class of Vatican G47. The term 'class' refers to shape and proportions, not to drawing style.

Bibliography: ABV, 431, 9; Brommer 1973, 136,40; CVA, Castle Ashby (Great Britain 15) 13-14 and pl. 22.5-7; Christie's Sale Catalogue, lot. 78, p. 119, ill. On Herakles and the Lion: Brommer 1974, 7-11; for the wrestling match on the ground and the Ensérune fragments: Boardman 1978, 14-15.

artifact.name: Austin 1980.32
artifact.summary: Side A: Athena. Side B: flute player between two judges.
artifact.collection: Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, University of Texas at Austin
artifact.essay_text:
Collection of the Archer M. Huntington Art Gallery, the University of Texas, Austin, James R. Dougherty, Jr. Foundation and Archer M. Huntington Museum Fund Purchase (1980.32)Ca. 540 B.C.Height: 27.5 cm.Diameter: 17.2 cm.Side A: Athena.Side B: Flute player between two judges.

The vase is of the same shape as those given to victors in the Panathenaic Games, and the pose of Athena on side A is similar to that on prize amphoras. But this is not a prize vase, for it is too small and lacks the inscription *T*O*N *A*Q*E*N*E*Q*E*N *A*Q*L*O*N ("From the Games at Athens") running alongside one of the columns that flank Athena.

On side A, Athena stands in the pose of the promachos ("who fights in the forefront"), fully armed; she held a spear in her upraised left hand. She wears an Attic helmet, with a high crest projecting from a simple cap, a necklet, long belted peplos, and her aegis slung crosswise so that three snake heads are visible behind. Her shield, with a wide rim painted in red, has as a device three large white balls. She stands between two slender Doric columns, on top of which perch owls, in place of the cocks which regularly stand atop the columns on Panathenaic prize amphoras. The owl is Athena's (hence Athens') bird.

On side B, a young flutist (auletes) stands on a three-stepped podium (bema) and plays, while two seated figures listen. The auletes wears a loose fitting chiton, a fillet around his head, and a phorbeia, or leather mouthpiece which helps hold the flutes in place. One of the listeners is beardless, the other bearded; both sit on folding stools and wear a striped himation over a chiton.

Because of the Panathenaic context - the vase's shape and the Athena of Side A - it seems likely that the seated listeners are judges and that the scene refers to musical competitions which took place at the Greater Panathenaea in Athens every four years. Literary and epigraphical sources do not confirm the existence of such musical contests before the fourth century, but this vase and several others suggest that in the sixth and early fifth centuries there may have been as many as four musical events: flute-playing and lyre-playing, either alone or accompanying a singer (a lyre player could accompany himself). These musical competitions, along with contests for rhapsodes, who recited passages from Homer, may have all been introduced with the major reorganization of the Panathenaea in 566 B.C. The earliest of the vases, about 560, is an amphora of Panathenaic shape in London (London B 141), on which a flute-player and a bearded man stand facing each other on a low platform, between a young athlete and a seated judge. Perhaps this scene represents the contest for aulodia, singing to the flute, while ours shows auletria, or unaccompanied flute-playing.

Bibliography: CVA, Castle Ashby (Great Britain 15) 8-9 and pl. 15, 5-6; Christie's Sale Catalog 1980, lot. 89, pp. 142-143, ill; E. Gerhard, in Archaeologische Zeitung 1846, 340, no. 2; A. Furtwängler, ibid. 1881, 303; H. Philippart, in L'Antiquité Classique 4 (1935) 212. On musical contests at the Panathenaia: J. A. Davison, in Journal of Hellenic Studies 78 (1958) 36-42.

artifact.name: Yale 1913.112
artifact.summary: Poseidon on a winged hippocamp.
artifact.other_bibliography: Baur 1922, pp. 77-8, pl. 6; Haspels 1936, p. 255, no. 26.
artifact.collection_history: Purchased for Yale by Rebecca Darlington Stoddard.
artifact.condit: The vase has been broken and repaired; all restoration is visible.
artifact.decoration_description: Poseidon astride a winged hippocamp. The hippocamp faces right while Poseidon looks back to the left. He brandishes his trident forward, above the hippocamp's forelegs. Two dolphins swim downward in the field behind the hippocamp's raised tail. Details of the hippocamp, including its bridle, harness, mane, facial stripe, dorsal and pectoral fins, and dots on the wings, are painted in added red. Poseidon's wreath and beard are also in added red. The belly of the hippocamp is in added white, as are dots on Poseidon's chiton. Five black palmettes are painted on the shoulder, with the middle one inverted. At the shoulder is a band of dotted zigzag framed with red stripes, into which the hippocamp's tail fins penetrate.

artifact.decoration_description:
A: Okeanos (labelled to the right of his head) (missing lower face and upper left arm), standing profile to the right, with his left foot advanced, wearing a himation draped over his left arm (missing) and around his lower body, over a medium-sleeved chiton with a patterned hem, and a taenia (his hair in a krobylos), holds a scepter with palmette finial upright in his slightly raised left hand, and holds his right hand at waist level; Ge Panteleia (labelled to the right of her head) seated 3/4-view to the right on a decorated stool, with her feet on a footstool, wearing a himation draped over her left arm and around her lower body, over a medium-, button-sleeved chiton with an overfold, and a rayed stephane, holds a scepter with a palmette finial upright in her slightly raised left hand, and a phiale at waist level, in her right hand; bearded Dionysos (labelled retrograde diagonally from his right elbow), standing profile to the left, with his left foot slightly advanced, wearing a himation draped over his left arm and around his lower body, over a medium-, button-sleeved, patterned chiton with an overfold (?), and an ivy wreath, holds an ivy branch in his slightly lowered left hand, and branch with fugitive white leaves/flowers in his extended right hand; a small panther (leopard?) behind him, standing profile to the left.

B: Bearded King Balos (labelled above his scepter), seated profile to the right on a stool, wearing a himation draped over his left shoulder, his hair in a short pony tail, holds both bent arms at waist level, spreads the fingers of his right hand (to receive the phiale from Themis?), and a scepter diagonally in his left hand; Themis (labelled to right), standing near frontal, with her head profile to the left, wearing a medium-, button-sleeved chiton, a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, and a red taenia, holds a phiale to Balos, in her outstretched right hand, and a trefoil-lipped oinochoe to Epaphos in her slightly upraised left hand (her left arm is bent); bearded Epaphos (labelled retrograde to the left of his head; missing body between hips and neck, and both arms, except right hand), standing profile to left, his right foot advanced, wearing a himation over a chiton, and a white wreath (fugitive), also holds a scepter upright in his slightly upraised right hand.
artifact.inscriptions: Signed in the field behind Dionysos' head: <Foreign lang=Greek>*S*U*R*I*S*K*O*S* E*G*R*A*F*S*E*N</Foreign>

artifact.dimensions: H. 0.60 m; H. (incl. lid) 0.675 m; Diam. (mouth) 0.25 m
artifact.collection_history: Ex Coll. Beugnot; acquired by the Louvre in 1866.
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Apollo and Artemis are alarmed at the abduction of their mother, Leto, by Tityos. Apollo, nude except a himation draped over his left arm, advancing profile to the right, reaches to Tityos. Tityos, bearded and nude, wearing a red wreath, standing profile to the right, lifts Leto, wearing a himation over a short-sleeved chiton, and a narrow stephane, shown profile to the right, with her head profile to the left. Artemis, advancing profile to the left, wearing a himation draped over her shoulders, a thin chiton with an overfold, a thin stephane and wreath in her hair, holds her right hand up (a gesture of horror?), and grasps her bow and arrow in her left hand.

Side B: A bearded trainer, wearing a himation draped over his left shoulder, holding a staff in his right hand, and his drapery in his left hand, directs a nude, youthful athlete standing in a nearly frontal stride, with his head profile to the left, holding a stick at a diagonal from the ground; another nude, bearded athlete (or trainer?), standing profile to the left, holds a stick at a diagonal in his left hand.
artifact.inscriptions:
In red dipinti, on side A: *X*A*I*R*E, *X*A*I*R*E, *A*P*O*L*L*O*N, *X*A*I*R*E, *L*E*T*O*U*S (retrograde), *A*I*D*O*S (next to Artemis).

On side B: *S*O*S*T*R*A*T*O*S *K*A*L*O*S, "Sostratos is beautiful"; *S*O*T*I*N*O*S, "Sotinos"; *X*A*R*E*S (retrograde), "Chares"; *D*E*M*O*S*T*R*A*T*E, "Demostrate" (the last six letters in retrograde); *X*A*I*R*E, "hail,"*S*O*S*I*A*S, "Sosias" (retrograde).

Side A: Presumably during the Calydonian boar hunt, the boar on the left is being speared by three hunters: a man wearing a fillet and carrying a wrap on his arm, and two youths, both naked except for the fillet one of them wears. The boar is also attacked by a black dog which digs his hind claws into the boar's flank. The scene is reconstructed with this dog also biting the boar's neck, though his head is not part of these fragments. There is another dog, this one white, biting and clawing at the boar's hindquarters. The boar is clearly fatally wounded, as there is blood pouring from all his wounds, and he collapses to the right.

Side B: A wounded stag with a spear embedded in his back is in the center between two hunters on horseback. Due to the fragmentary nature, little is left of the stag or rider confronting him.

Interior: Swan to the right.
artifact.inscriptions: <hi rend="bold">Side A:</hi> Meaningless inscriptions above and behind the dog on the boar's neck. <hi rend="bold">Side B:</hi> Meaningless inscriptions below the horse.

artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Odysseus and his men encounter Circe. Odysseus, in patterned chlamys, approaches the sorceress with his sword drawn. Circe stirs the contents of a cup she has just taken from the man next to her, who is in the process of being transformed, and has the head and neck of a boar. A dog sits on the ground between Circe and the transforming man, looking toward the sorceress. Other of Odysseus' companions surround Circe, each transformed: one has the head, neck, and forequarters of a boar; two on the right have have heads, necks, and forequarters of a ram and a wolf, respectively. A fifth man runs away at left, transformed with the head and neck of a lion. On the right end, a bearded man in patterned chlamys escapes, looking over his shoulder. Added red is used for Odysseus' hair and beard; Circe's hair; parts of the dog's coat; necks and chests of some of the transformed men; and for the rosettes on clothing. White is used for Circe's skin, Odysseus' sword hilt and baldric; the teeth, tusks, and horns of the transformed men; and for rosette petals.

Side B: Odysseus and his men in the cave of the Cyclops Polyphemos. At center, Polyphemos has collapsed onto one knee, drunk. Odysseus, in an elaborate chlamys and carrying an oinochoe in his right hand, hurries toward a companion, who brings a full wineskin. Athena appears at left, behind the hero, in peplos and high-crested Athenian helmet, spear, and round shield (with the device of a swan). To the left of the man with the wineskin, two bearded men wearing flowered chlamydes and scabbards on baldrics approach with drawn swords. At the far right, a fourth bearded man in a patterned chlamys flees to right, similarly to the fleeing figure on Side A. A bearded spectator in himation stands underneath each handle. Nonsense inscriptions. Added red for Polyphemos' genitals and belly; hair and beards of some of the men; Athena's peplos, helmet, crest, hair, and the wing coverts of her shield device. White is added for Athena's skin and swan device; rosette petals on clothing; baldrics of the two armed men.

The interior is glazed, with tondo reserved. A band of lotus buds and flowers encircles the bowl, under the groundline upon which the figures stand. Below the lotus band, 23 base rays. The handles are reserved inside, and decorated on the outside with ivy vines. Added red for the lotus buds, and for alternating ivy leaves and the knob-tops on the handles. Added white for the calyxes of the lotus flowers on the lower bowl.
artifact.shape_description: Cup without an offset lip, and with wishbone-shaped merrythought handles.

artifact.decoration_description:
The two scenes occupy the same architectural setting--a Mycenaean palace indicating by Aeolic columns (dividing the two scenes) supporting a continuous entablature.

Side A: A young woman, perhaps Chrysothemis (Agamemnon's youngest daughter), wearing a long chiton and himation, runs 3/4-view to the left, with an arm passing behind the Aeolic column, although she turns her head to the right, to view to the scene. She is slightly overlapped by Klytaimnestra, similarly dressed, who runs 3/4-view to the right, perhaps to aid her lover in killing Agamemnon. She stretches her left arm to her right (toward Agamemnon?), and holds an axe in her lowered right hand. Aigisthos, bearded and wearing a short chiton, lunges profile to the right at Aigisthos, shrouded in a filmy cloth. He holds Agamemnon's head with his outstretched left hand, and a sword in his lowered right hand. He seems to have already struck the king, who bleeds from his chest. The king, nude except his shroud, bearded and long-haired (just out of his bath, as observed by Prag), leans back, and supports himself feebly with his bent right leg. Behind him is Elektra, running 3/4-view to the left, with her right arm stretched toward Klytaimnestra, and her left hand raised behind her (in surprise or mercy?). Behind her, hiding almost behind the Aeolic column, is another young woman, perhaps Agamemnon's "prize," Kassandra (as she is shown in the dress of a slave: short-haired and without a himation), with her arms raised above her head, fleeing to the right, although she turns back to look at the others.

Side B: Klytaimnestra, wearing chiton and himation, advancing 3/4-view to the right, raises her axe above her right shoulder, and stretches her left hand toward Orestes' shoulder. Orestes, dressed as a soldier, with a helmet, strides 3/4-view to the right, in a similar posture to Aigisthos on the obverse: he holds his victim's head (that of Aigisthos) in his left hand, and pulls his weapon (a long sword) back in his lowered right hand. Aigisthos, bearded, is seated to the left on a klismos, or backed chair, wearing a himation draped across his thighs, while blood spurts from his chest. He stretches his right hand to his assailant (seeking mercy?), and holds a barbiton in his lowered left hand. Elektra, behind him, runs 3/4-view to the left, in a similar posture as in her appearance on side A, except that she holds her left hand in front of her chest.
artifact.inscriptions: Side A (between Aigisthos and Agamemnon): *E*E (cries of anguish). Side B (above Klytaimnestra's arm): *N*O*N*E*N*O*N (among other nonsense inscriptions).

artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: From the left, Pelopeia, bejeweled (with earrings, bracelets, necklace, and beaded fillet in yellow) and wearing a chiton, himation veiled over her head, and sandals, stands in 3/4-view to the left, turning away from the scene, and raises her hands in horror. Aigisthos, her son and brother, stands beside her, also turning to the left, leaning on a tall spear. He is nude, except for a chlamys falling down his back and a baldric on his left thigh. He holds a sword in his lowered left hand, however. Next is father Thyestes, running 3/4-view to the left, but turning his head back to the right. He is bearded and wears a pilos, chiton, and chlamys clasped with a brooch at his throat. He also holds a sword (with which he has just murdered Atreus) in his upraised right hand, and the scabbard in his lowered left hand. At the center is the cushioned throne of Atreus, mostly white (imitating ivory), shown frontally, on which the corpse of Atreus is sprawled upside down. Atreus is fully dressed in himation, chiton over tunic, and sandals, but he is clearly dead, with closed eyes, a bloody chest wound, and arms hanging loose below his head. His tall scepter stands to the left of the throne. To his right is another group of three characters. A winged fury named Poine (the personification of Vengeance) runs toward the king, with her right hand on his throne, but turns her eyes away from the sight. She wears high boots, a short belted chiton, and a short cloak over her left shoulder. She has snakes in her hair, and holds a red staff. She looks at a pair of women who are identified by inscription as slave women. They both wear long belted chitons, earrings, necklaces, and slippers, and embrace each other, while gesturing at the murdered king. The right one is short-haired, like a slave, but the left one wears a himation, a sakkos or hair net, and a bracelet. Spindles on the ground below them may indicate that they were interrupted in their spinning work.

Side B: On the left, in 3/4-view to the right, stand a maenad, wearing a chiton, and holding a mirror and a iunx wheel, and a nude satyr, who holds yellow and white grapes and a tympanum (drum). A maenad, perhaps Ariadne, is seated in 3/4-view to the left, but turns to the right to look at Dionysos, who likewise sits in 3/4-view to the right, but turns toward her. She wears a long belted chiton, himation, slippers and jewelry, and holds a thyrsos and a bunch of white grapes; he is nude, except for a himation draped down his back and a white taenia around his head, and holds an opened box and an empty kantharos. To his right stands another maenad, in 3/4-view to the left, wearing a chiton, slippers, and jewelry, and holding a torch and a situla.

The stem of the vessel is decorated with a ray design. A continuous frieze of women, youths, and erotes, all bearing gifts surrounds the entire vessel in the lower frieze, with a band of maeanders serving as a groundline. Bands of tendrils enclose the upper frieze on both sides. The neck is decorated with a painted decoration that imitates ribbing, surmounted by a band of rosettes and finally a tall lotus-palmette frieze. The rim is decorated with a vine tendril.
artifact.inscriptions: All characters on side A are named by incised labels: <foreign lang="Greek">*P*E*L*O*P*E*I*A, *A*G*I*S*Q*O*S, *Q*Y*E*S*T*H*S, *A*T*R*E*Y*S, [*P]*O*I*N*H,</foreign> and <foreign lang="Greek">*D*M*W*I*A*I.</foreign>
artifact.shape_description: Large Apulian Panathenaic. There is a large (original) hole in the bottom that renders this amphora useless as a container: it is thus likely that it was intended to stand on a tomb; vases of this shape are frequently depicted as standing on tombs. For a discussion of the (primary) funerary use of such amphorae see J.R. Green, <hi rend="ital">NumAntCl</hi> 20 (1991) 53.

artifact.name: Boston 01.8044
artifact.summary: "Chariot" krater depicting charioteers and belt-wrestlers.
artifact.other_bibliography: J. Doell, Sammlung Cesnola (1873) pl. XVII.8, 9; A. Fürtwangler and G. Loeschcke, Mykenische Vasen (Berlin, 1886), p. 27, figs. 14-15; Fairbanks 1928, p. X.143; E. Vermeule, Classical Journal 53 (1958), pp. 102-103, fig. 8; Chase & Vermeule 1963, fig. 13; A. D. Lacy, Greek Pottery in the Bronze Age (London, 1967), pp. 212-213, fig. 85B.
artifact.condit: Intact.
artifact.decoration_description:
"Chariot" krater depicting two charioteers in cloaks, driving a two-horse chariot, and a pair of naked belt-wrestlers. The scene is repeated on the krater's B side. The chariot is decorated with a scale-pattern; the wheel is ovoid, and descending into a triple-banded ground line which encircles the vase. The horses' bodies are extremely elongated, and reins stretch across the exaggerated distance from the chariot to the horses' bridles. Flowers spring from the horses' backs and from the chariot's front, on one side; on the other, a series of rippled triangles descends from the pole-stay. The wrestlers' hands are drawn with opposed thumbs visible. The faces of the charioteers and the wrestlers are strangely rendered, with a reserved area containing a dot for the eye, and with a bent line extending from nose to shoulder. This line apparently represents the front of the neck, but is confusing, as it encloses a reserved area which contrasts greatly with the solid-glazed faces. Vermeule and Karageorghis suggest the line could represent a face protector. Under each of the handles, a long bird with a curved beak and semicircles for feet looks back over its shoulder.

This vase marks the first appearance of a pair of wrestlers joined together by a belt. In belt-wrestling, an Oriental sport that sporadically appears in the Levantine Aegean, the opponents are strapped together around the middle and attempt to pull each other off balance. Vermeule and Karageorghis observe that the wrestlers' gestures on this krater are similar to those of boxers. The neck and foot are glazed, with an additional band just above the foot, and the handles are outlined as well.
artifact.shape_description: Tall, top-heavy amphoroid krater with flat handles.

artifact.decoration_description:
A (upper level): A female figure, perhaps Erato (labelled) standing 3/4-view to the left, with her right foot raised on a rock, bent at the waist, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton with a kolpos and shoulder straps, and a rayed ovolo taenia, black hoop earrings, and a black band necklace, rests a tympanon (decorated with a wreath on its rim, and maeanders on its edge) on her right knee, the top of which she holds with her right hand, while she plays it with her left hand; Mousaios (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, wearing a patterned, long-sleeved, oriental tunic, a chlamys draped down his back, calf-length leather boots, a laurel wreath, rests a kithara on his left knee, which he plays with both hands; above him and to the right, nude, red, winged Pothos (labelled), leaning 3/4-view to the right on the shoulder of Kalliope, with his left arm, weight on his right leg, left leg pulled back, wearing a red taenia, points his right hand down and to the right; Kalliope (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, with her legs crossed, and her head turned 3/4-view to the left, wearing a spangled himation draped over her legs, under her hips and back, over a medium-, button-sleeved, belted chiton, a rayed cross-hatched sphendone, black hoop earrings, and a black band necklace; Harmonia (labelled), emerging from behind a hill (only shown above her hips), wearing a belted, short-sleeved chiton, with shoulder straps, a black band necklace, two white bands on each wrist, and a short pony tail, holds her right hand below her chest, and her left hand above her left shoulder.

A (lower level): Melpomene (labelled), seated near profile to the right, with her legs crossed, wearing a bordered himation draped over her legs, over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton, a black band necklace, black hoop earrings, a rayed ovolo taenia, holds a harp on her lap, which she plays with both hands; Deiope (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, with her legs crossed, wearing a bordered himation draped around her legs, over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton, a black band necklace, black hoop earrings, a rayed, cross-hatched sphendone, holds her left hand on her knee, and raises her right hand slightly to the right, on the back of which is perched a small bird); she looks down to the nude baby, Eumolpos (labelled above his head), kneeling profile to the left, wearing a black band on his right wrist, and a black strap with trinket attached, draped over his right shoulder; he reaches his right hand up to Deiope, and lowers his left hand slightly; a short tree; nude, red Eros, with frontal wings, standing 3/4-view to the right, perched behind Aphrodite's right shoulder, with weight on his right leg, and his left leg relaxed, wearing a rayed taenia, points his right hand down to the left, and holds his left hand above his shoulder (in a speaking gesture?); Aphrodite (labelled above her right shoulder), seated 3/4-view to the left, with her legs crossed, wearing a spangled bordered himation over her legs, over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton with an overfold, sandals, a black band necklace, black hoop earrings, and a cross-hatched sphendone, with a rayed maeander ampyx, rests her left hand on her seat, and her right hand on her knee; Terpsichora (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her head 3/4-view to the right, weight on her right leg, left leg relaxed, wearing a belted peplos, a rayed ovolo taenia, a black band necklace, black hoop earrings, holds a plectron in her lowered right hand, and a lyre in her slightly raised left hand; Peitho (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left, with her right foot raised on a rock (?), wearing a himation draped over her legs and up her back, over a medium-sleeved, belted chiton, sandals, a black band necklace, two white bands on her right wrist, black hoop earring (fugitive), over a rayed patterned sphendone, looks up at Terpsichora.

artifact.decoration_description:
Upper level: Erosora, standing profile to the right, wearing a peplos, a sphendone, two bands on each wrist, a beaded necklace, and gold dot earrings, holds a chain in her upraised left and lowered right hands, and raises her left foot (on higher rock?); Pannychis, seated 3/4-view to the left, her head profile to the right, ankles crossed, wearing a belted, a button-sleeved chiton belted with a narrow black band, a himation over her legs, sandals, two bands on each wrist, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, and a sphendone, holds a wreath in her lowered left hand, and turns her left hand upwards toward her hair; Aphrodite, crouched near profile to right in chariot, wearing a short-sleeved, belted chiton, a himation draped over both arms, two bands on each wrist, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, and a sphendone, holds reins in both hands; the chariot is drawn by nude Pothos, 3/4-view to the right, wearing sandals and a wreath, holding a phiale at waist level in his left hand, and a laurel wreath in his lowered right hand; Himeros, standing 3/4-view to the right, with his head turned 3/4-view to the left, wearing a wreath, holds a thymiaterion in his left hand, and reaches his right hand behind Himeros; Hygieia, seated 3/4-view to the left, legs crossed, wearing sandals, a short-sleeved, belted chiton with shoulder straps, a sphendone, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, holds a beaded necklace between both upraised hands; Eudaimonia (labelled), seated near profile to the right, with her head turned 3/4-view to the left, legs crossed, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton, two bands on each wrist, a beaded necklace, and bead earrings, leans her right shoulder against Hygieia and holds her left hand in her lap.

Lower level: Chrysogeneia standing profile to the right, with her weight on her straight right leg (her left leg pulled back slightly), wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton with shoulder cords, a high pony tail, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, and two bands on each wrist, leans her left hand on the lap of Leura, and holds her right hand at waist level; Leura, seated 3/4-view to the left, her head 3/4-view to the right, and her ankles crossed, wearing a medium-sleeved, belted chiton, a himation over her legs and veiled over her head, a sphendone, two bands on each wrist, a beaded necklace, and bead earrings, holds a beaded necklace (or rod?) between both hands; a nude Eros, flying 3/4-view to the right, with his advanced left leg bent, wearing a taenia in his hair, reaches both arms to the right; Phaon, seated 3/4-view to the left, his head 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation over his left leg, and a long, broad taenia with a vertical flap, plays a lyre that he holds with both hands; Demonassa, seated 3/4-view to the left, legs crossed, wearing a belted, medium-sleeved chiton, a himation over her legs, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, two bands on each wrist, and a sphendone, holds a necklace to the left between her upraised right hand and lowered left hand; Leto, standing to 3/4-view to the right, with weight on her left leg, right leg relaxed, head tilted down, wears a belted peplos, a himation which she pulls over her right shoulder with her right hand, a beaded necklace, two bands on each wrist, bead earrings, and a stephane, cradles a scepter in her lowered left arm; Apollo, seated 3/4-view to the left, wearing a himation over his left leg, legs crossed, and an olive crown, rests his left hand on his seat, and holds an olive branch upright in his upraised right hand.

artifact.decoration_description: Chrysothemis, seated 3/4-view to the right, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, legs crossed, her head turned profile to the right, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton, a sphendone, two bands on each wrist, supports herself with her left hand placed on a rock, and holds her right hand behind her head; she speaks to a nude Eros, standing profile to the left, with his left foot raised on a rock, wearing a taenia in his hair, who places his left hand on his knee, and (perhaps) raises his right hand; below him, Eutychia, standing near profile to the right, with her left foot advanced, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, long hair tied with a broad taenia, and two bands on each wrist, reaches her left hand to the shoulder of Eudaimonia, and holds a mirror up to her; Eudaimonia, seated 3/4-view to the right, her head profile to the left, slightly tilted up, to look in the mirror, legs crossed, wearing a high-belted, medium-sleeved chiton, a sphendone, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, holds her left hand in front of her waist, and supports herself with her right hand on a rock; above her, Eurynoe, seated 3/4-view to the right, legs crossed, wearing a short-sleeved belted chiton, a sphendone, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, looks down at a bird that she supports on her upraised left hand, and touches with her right hand; a nude Himeros, hovering 3/4-view to the right, with his head tilted down, turns a iunx, which he holds in both hands, in front of Adonis, seated 3/4-view to the left, his legs crossed, wearing a himation draped over his left leg, and a long, broad taenia with a vertical flap; he tilts his head up, supports himself on the rock (?) with his lowered left hand, and holds his right hand in front of his face, while he leans in the arms of Aphrodite, standing 3/4-view to the left, her head tilted down, wearing a medium-sleeved, belted chiton, a broad taenia, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist; beneath them, another nude Himeros runs 3/4-view to the right, his bent left leg advanced, wearing a taenia, chasing a hare; Hygieia holds Paidia on her knees; Pannychis (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a belted sleeveless chiton, a high pony tail, and a beaded necklace, holds a tympanon in both hands, toward an Eros; above is Hygieia, seated 3/4-view to the right, her head 3/4-view to the left, wearing a medium-sleeved chiton, a stephane, and two bands on each wrist, placing her left hand on her seat, and holding her bent left arm in front of her body; Paidia, seated profile to the left in her lap, legs crossed, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, a stephane, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, reaches both her bent arms to the left; Pandaisia, seated profile to the right, head profile to the left, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, beaded necklace, high pony tail, and two bands on each wrist, rests her right hand on her seat, and holds her left hand behind her head.

artifact.collection_history: Bought in Paris in 1880.
artifact.decoration_description: A female figure (perhaps Eudaimonia?), seated profile to the right, wearing a himation around her lower body, over a medium-sleeved, belted chiton, a sphendone, hoop earrings, and a beaded necklace, holds a string of beads between her upraised right hand and her lowered left hand; a female figure, probably Paidia (labelled), standing near frontal (slightly to the right), with her weight on her straight left leg, her right leg relaxed, and her head profile to the left, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a high pony tail, and a beaded necklace, holds a short string of beads between her hands, which she raises in front of her chest; Aphrodite (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton and a himation pulled over her head and shoulders, a beaded necklace, disk earrings (?), and a stephane, holds a scepter in her right hand, and an unidentifiable object over her left shoulder; Adonis (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, on his himation, with his left foot raised on a rock, his head profile to the left, wearing an olive wreath, rests his right hand on his seat, and in his left arm cradles a lyre; a nude, winged Eros, standing profile to the left, with his weight on his straight left leg, wearing a grain (?) wreath, holds a plate of fruit in both hands.

artifact.decoration_description:
A: Nude Theseus (labelled), advancing 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his bent, forward left leg (partially obscured by a rock), wearing a white taenia, and a black/red scabbard strap over his right shoulder, holds a bronze podanipter, or large shallow dish (brown wash to indicate bronze), in his right hand, behind his head, and reaches forward his left hand to pull the head of Skiron; nude, bearded Skiron (labelled) seated on rock 3/4-view to the left, rests his left hand on a rock, while he reaches his right arm straight to Theseus, turning up his right hand to beseech the hero; a tortoise behind the rock; Theseus (labelled), advancing 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his bent, forward left leg, wearing a chlamys over his left arm, a white wreath, and a red/black scabbard band over his right shoulder, holds a sword in his extended right hand arm, and a rock in his left hand, which is obscured by his chlamys; a barren olive tree; a sow, advancing profile to the left, raises her front legs on the rocks; in front of the sow, Krommyo (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her left leg, pulled back (her age is revealed in her bent posture, as well as her wrinkles and white hair), wearing a button-sleeved, belted chiton, holds a staff in her left hand, and beseeches Theseus with her outstretched right hand; nude Theseus (labelled), standing near frontal, with his right leg bent profile to the left, his left leg straight to the right, and his head profile to the right, wearing a black/red scabbard strap over his left shoulder, holds a branch of the pine-tree with his right hand above his head, and reaches his left arm to the curly hair at the top of the head of Sinis; nude, bearded Sinis (labelled), kneeling frontal on the ground, with his head profile to left, and his right leg and arm (beseeching) straight to the left, raises his left hand to the trunk of the tree.

Tondo: Athena (labelled) in front of a palace with an Ionic facade; Theseus (labelled) and the Minotaur (labelled).
artifact.inscriptions: Signed <Foreign lang=Greek>*A*I*S*W*N *E*G*R*A*Y*E*N</Foreign>)

artifact.name: Athens, Agora P 9189
artifact.summary: Dancing maenads
artifact.collection_history: Athens, Agora, Section I #971, in a well (found 15-16 May 1936)
artifact.decoration_description: Maenads dancing (?): On fragment (a) Paidia (labelled), near profile to the right (front of head, left shoulder, breast, and left hand preserved), with her hair tied back, wearing a thin sleeved chiton, and a white wreath, holds a round object in her (missing) right hand, and raises a bossed round object (cymbals, phiale, or pyxis lid) in her right hand. On fragment (b) a maenad, thought to be Thymedia (labelled), 3/4-view to the right (back of head, right shoulder and right arm above wrist preserved), wearing a sleeveless chiton, a pony tail, and a white beaded necklace, is partially obscured by her thyrsos; on fragment (c) is preserved only a small portion of drapery from a thin chiton.

artifact.summary: A: The retinue of Dionysos<lb>B: Maenad, satyr, maenad

artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Lamberg Collection 189.
artifact.decoration_description: A: Olive tree rising above groundline; Hedyoinos (labelled), leaning on a rock 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his left hand and/or knee, wearing a white/red ivy wreath, holds a kantharos in his right hand; a maenad, Eirene (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, hoop earring, and a broad white taenia over an ivy wreath, cradles a double-torch in her left arm, and holds up a rhyton in her left hand; below, a nude bearded satyr, probably Dithyrambos or Gelos, seated 3/4-view to the right on a panther skin, with his left leg pulled back slightly, wearing a red/white ivy wreath, holds a lyre in his left hand, and plucks it with his right; Dione (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a patterned himation over a chiton, a sphendone, a white/red ivy wreath, and a hoop earring, holds a plate of fruit in both hands; Dionysos (labelled ), seated 3/4-view to the left on drapery (which also drapes over his lap and left arm), on the omphalos on a two-stepped base, with his head profile to the right, nude, wearing a long, broad taenia with a vertical flap, and an ivy wreath, holds a brown kantharos in his right hand, and a thyrsos upright in his left hand; below, a panther, profile to the left; above Dionysos' left shoulder, a small, nude, white Himeros (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a white taenia, offers a wreath or necklace to Dionysos; a maenad, Opora (labelled), standing profile to the left, also wearing a sleeveless tunic over a chiton, a broad white/red ivy wreath over a taenia, a dark red necklace, black hoop earrings, raises her left foot on rock, and holds a plate of fruit in both hands; a nude, bearded satyr, Komos (labelled), standing near frontal, with his weight on his right leg, and his head profile to the left, wearing a nebris tied in front of his neck, draped over his left arm, and a red/white ivy wreath, cradles a thyrsos in his lowered left arm, and holds his beard in his right hand; above, a maenad, Oinanthe (labelled), reclining on rock 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, and a taenia over her ivy wreath, rests her right elbow on rock, and her left hand on her knee; a bearded, nude satyr, standing 3/4-view to the left, with his right foot raised on a rock, wearing a red/white ivy wreath, extends both arms to the left (to Oinanthe).

artifact.decoration_description: A female figure standing near profile to the right, emerging above the handle (shown from the mid-calf up), with her weight on her straight, right leg, and her left foot on a rock, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a sphendone, white dot earrings, a white beaded necklace, and two white bands on each wrist, rests her right hand on her hip, and reaches her left hand behind a female figure seated 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a red/white wreath, a white beaded necklace, and two white bands on each wrist, places her right hand on the knee of the first female figure, and holds her left hand, palm out; below, a female figure seated 3/4-view to the left, with her head profile to the right, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, and a broad red taenia over a rayed, white wreath, rests her right hand on her right knee, and her left hand on a rock; an olive branch above; Kadmos, standing profile to the right, with his weight on his left leg, and his head tilted up, wearing a chlamys clasped over his right shoulder, a petasos, and a white taenia, crowned by Athena (?) with a wreath, holds both arms at waist level, his right palm turned up, and holding in his left hand two upright spears; at the bottom of the spears is a bronze hydria; Athena, standing 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his right leg, her left leg relaxed, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a checkerboard aegis, a red Corinthian helmet, white bead earrings, a white beaded necklace, and a white band on her left wrist, reaches her bent right arm (at waist level) to Kadmos, and lowers her left hand at her side, holding her spear at a slight diagonal over her left shoulder; she is crowned by a white Nike (with red wings) in the field to her right), flying profile to the right, with her knees bent, wearing a yellow and white striped chiton, a high pony tail, reaches both arms to the right (with her right hand above her left), and holds a beaded chain to Athena; Harmonia seated 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a stephane, a white beaded necklace, white bead earrings, and two white bands on each wrist, rests her left hand on her knee, and her right hand on her hip; a spotted snake crawls up from behind and is entwined around her left arm; a female figure, perhaps Themis, standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on both legs, and her head tilted up, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton with straps across her chest, and a high pony tail, leans on Harmonia, rests her right hand on her knee, and her left hand on her hip; a loutrophoros behind her; above, a female figure, seated 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a white bead necklace, white bead earrings, a double red taenia, a white/red wreath, two white bands on her right wrist, rests her right hand on a rock, and holds her drapery in her left hand, over her shoulder; Hermes, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a chlamys draped over his left shoulder, fastened over his right shoulder, a petasos on his neck, a white taenia over a red wreath, and calf-length, strap boots, with his weight on his right leg, and his left leg relaxed, reaches his right hand, lowered at his side, slightly to the left, and holds a kerykeion in his left hand.

artifact.decoration_description: Tripod atop Doric colonette; Harmonia (labelled), seated on a rock 3/4-view to the left, with her head profile to the right, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, over a medium-sleeved chiton, a high pony tail, and disk earrings, rests her left hand on the rock, and raises her right hand behind her head; below her a deer, standing profile to the right; bearded Kadmos (labelled), lunging 3/4-view to the right, with his advanced left leg bent, wearing a chlamys over his left arm, an exomis belted over a wreath, a petasos on the back of his neck, a scabbard strap over his right shoulder, and calf-length strap boots, holds a rock (?) in his left hand, covered by the chlamys, and a sword in his lowered right hand; above him, Nike (labelled), hovering 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a sakkos, holding a garland in between her lowered hands; Athena (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her straight right leg, wearing an aegis over a belted peplos, a Corinthian helmet, holding a spear in her upraised left hand, and a wreath in her lowered right hand; a snake-like dragon; above, Demeter (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a spiked (grain) crown, holds a scepter upright in her upraised left hand, and holds her bent right arm in front of her body; below, Eros lunging 3/4-view to the right, with weight on his advanced, bent, left leg, holding a garland between both lowered hands; Thebe (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left, with her legs crossed, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, veiled over her head, over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a taenia, resting on her bent left elbow, her right hand in her lap; emerging from behind her head, a ladder (?); a tripod on a Doric colonette.

artifact.decoration_description: A (upper level): A female charioteer emerges from behind a hill (her feet obscured), standing in the chariot box 3/4-view to the right (labelled), driving a quadriga, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton with patterned yoke, long curly dark hair in a pony tail, a red taenia (?), white dot earrings, a white necklace, two white bands on each wrist, bends her right arm at waist level, and holds reins and whip in her left hand, advanced to the right; Eris (labelled), standing frontal, with her head profile to the right, weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a belted, long sleeved, oriental tunic, belted over a chiton, a stephane with three white rays, a white bead necklace, a short, high pony tail, rests her right hand on her hip, and lowers her left hand at her side, bending her left arm slightly; Themis (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a double-belted, short-sleeved chiton with shoulder straps and a short overfold, white dot earrings, a rayed ovolo taenia over rolled hair, and a white bead necklace, rests her right hand on the left shoulder of Eris, and her left hand on her hip; another quadriga profile to the left (only ears and forehead of foremost horse, and the rear of the two latter horses remain), emerging from behind a hill, driven by a winged woman standing frontal in a chariot box (neck and head missing), wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, two white bands on each wrist, holds the reins in her right hand, bent to the left, at waist level, with her left arm lowered at her side; bearded Zeus standing near profile to the left, wearing a patterned, bordered himation, draped around his waist and over his left shoulder, a white/yellow taenia, olive wreath, his left arm enveloped in his himation, leans on his straightened left leg, his right leg advanced slightly, lowers his right hand at his side, holding a scepter with a floral finial.

artifact.decoration_description:
A (body, upper level): Eudaimonia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her left foot raised on a rock, wearing a belted peplos, and a sphendone, rests her left arm on her knee, and holds a branch (?) in her upraised right arm; above, a bearded satyr (only upper half of body shown emerging from behind a hill), 3/4-view to the right, wearing an ivy wreath, holds both bent arms in front of his body, the left arm raised higher; a bearded satyr, Simos (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, wearing an ivy wreath, looks down to an amphora in his lap, held in his left hand, from which he pours wine into a kantharos, held in his right hand; a nude, winged, laureate Eros (labelled), hovering above, 3/4-view to the right, with his left leg raised, resting his right hand on his hip, and curving his right arm in a speaking gesture; Eudia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, and a sphendone, holds her right arm at her side, and an upright thyrsos in her upraised left hand; Dionysos, reclining 3/4-view to the left on an ornate couch, wearing a himation around his legs, and a wreath, holds a thyrsos in his upraised right hand; he is attended by a nude, winged, laureate Himeros (labelled), at his feet, standing profile to the right, with his weight on his right leg, and his left foot advanced; and Opora (labelled), emerging from behind the hill (visible above her knees), standing near frontal, with her head turned profile to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton, a nebris over her left shoulder, a long pony tail, and an ivy wreath, holding a trefoil-lipped oinochoe in her lowered left hand, and a plate of fruit in her bent left arm; a vine; Thyone (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right, with her head turned profile to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton and a himation draped over her legs, and a crown, resting her left arm on her knee, and cradling a thyrsos in her right arm; a nude, winged, laureate Pothos (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with his right leg raised on a rock, resting his left arm on his hip, and holding in his right hand a grape bunch; a kantharos below him; a female figure, perhaps Oreias (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a himation draped over her left shoulder, over a chiton, and a kekryphylon (?), holds a thyrsos upright in her upraised left hand, and reaches her right arm to the left; a tripod on Doric column; a bearded satyr, Oinopion (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right on a rock, with his head profile to the left, wearing a nebris over his left shoulder, and an ivy wreath, rests his left hand on his knee, and his right hand on the rock.

A (body, lower level): A deer standing profile to the right, left front leg advanced; Hebe (labelled), standing near frontal, with her head profile to the left, wearing a long-sleeved, patterned, oriental tunic over a chiton, and a sphendone (?), reaches her right hand to the deer, and bears plate of food on her bent left arm; a nude satyr reclining 3/4-view to the left, leaning on an amphora, with his head turned profile to the right, hidden partially by his bent right arm, wearing an ivy wreath, rests his left hand on the ground; a palm tree behind him; a tripod on doric column; a young satyr, Sikinnos (labelled), standing profile to the right, with his weight on his right leg, and his left leg bent, wearing an ivy wreath, stretches both arms to the head of an ass, standing profile to the left; a lekanis between them; above, a nude, bearded satyr, Silenos (labelled), seated profile to the left, leaning back on a wine skin, legs crossed, wearing an ivy wreath, playing a double flute held in both hands; a tripod on doric column; a female figure seated 3/4-view to the left, enveloped in a himation, which is veiled over her head, a chiton, and a taenia, holds both arms (obscured by the himation) at her sides, and looks up.

artifact.name: Warsaw 142458
artifact.summary: Dancing Maenads (Islands) and Satyrs
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Goluchow Collection 77.
artifact.decoration_description:
A: A nude bearded satyr, labelled Aietos, standing profile to the right, leaning back on his bent right leg, holds the stem of a kantharos in both hands, and tilts his head up; Euboia (labelled), dancing 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a belted, sleeved chiton with a long kolpos, a kekryphylon, tilts her head down, and bends both arms, the right one down, and the left one up, and holds in her left hand and thyrsos which she rests diagonally across her left shoulder; a nude, bearded satyr, Kissos (labelled), dancing near frontal, with his head profile to the left, tilted down, bends both legs; a maenad, Kinyra (labelled), dancing 3/4-view to the left, with her left leg bent back, wearing a sleeved chiton with a long kolpos, an ivy wreath, and a long pony tail, holds her right hand at her side, palm down, and holds a thyrsos at diagonal in her left hand.

B: A nude bearded satyr, Lemnos (labelled), moving profile to the right, with both legs bent, holds a wineskin in both hands, in his lowered left hand and raised right hand, and faces a maenad, Delos (labelled), dancing profile to the left, with her weight on her forward right leg, wearing a sleeved, belted chiton with a long kolpos, and a red taenia, tilts her head back, and plucks with her right hand at a lyre which she holds in her left hand; a nude bearded balding satyr, dancing near frontal, with his head profile to the right, and his legs crossed, tilts his head, holds his right arm straight at his side, and raises his left arm; a maenad, Tethys (labelled), dancing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a high-belted, long-sleeved chiton with a long kolpos, and a kekryphylon, advances her left leg and spreads her arms.

Tondo: A nude bearded satyr, Demon (labelled), dancing profile to the right, with his weight on his left leg, bends both legs, holds his left arm down, and holds a kantharos in his right hand; a maenad, Choro (labelled), moving 3/4-view to the left, wearing a long-sleeved chiton with a long kolpos, a kekryphylon, and a red band necklace, holds her right hand at her side, and holds a lyre at waist level in her left hand.

artifact.decoration_description:
A (Wedding of Harmonia): Aphrodite (labelled), mother of the bride, seated on stool near profile to the right, legs crossed, feet on low footstool, kekryphylon, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation around her lower body, two black bands on each wrist, black dot earrings, holds a necklace in both hands; a wreath on the wall above her; Eros (labelled), standing in 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his right leg, long curly hair bound in a leafy wreath, holds a jewelry box in his left hand, the lid in his right hand; Peitho (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a belted peplos, black dot earrings, a high pony-tail and black dot on a chain around her neck, two black bands on her right wrist, raises both hands, and holds a mirror in her left hand; Harmonia (labelled), seated on stool near profile to the left, but with her head profile to the right, with her legs crossed, and her feet on a footstool, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation around her lower body, a kekryphylon, black-dot earrings, a necklace as on Peitho, two black-bands bracelets on each wrist, rests her right hand on her knee, and her left hand on her seat; Kore (labelled), standing profile to the left, legs crossed, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton with a long kolpos, a kekryphylon, black-dot earrings, a black chain necklace, two black bands on her left wrist, leans on Harmonia, with her right arm around Harmonia's shoulders, and holds Harmonia's left wrist in her left hand; Hebe (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton with a long kolpos, raises both hands behind her neck to bind her hair; a nude Himeros (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right on a himation draped over his chair, with his head and wings profile to the left, legs crossed and feet on a footstool, wearing a leafy wreath (hair bound in krobylos), holds a pointed amphoriskos right hand, raised up to Hebe, and rests his left arm on the back of his chair.

B (Peleus and Thetis): A Nereid, labelled Datis (?), running profile to the right, wearing a peplos, a stephane, a long pony tail, and two red bands on each wrist, reaches both arms to the right; Melite (labelled), running frontal, with her head profile to the right, wearing a short-sleeved chiton with a long kolpos, a sphendone, a short pony tail, and two red bands on each wrist, holds a himation (?) in her outstretched left hand, and her own chiton in her outstretched right hand; Eulimene (labelled), running frontal to the left, with her head and arms profile to the right, wearing a thin belted peplos, a short pony-tail, a sphendone, and two red bands on each wrist; nude Peleus (labelled), wearing a leafy wreath around his curly dark hair, lunges toward Thetis at the right, and is attacked on his right side by a hippocamp; Thetis (labelled), dressed as Melite, standing frontal, but with her legs profile to the right, and her head profile to the left, is pulled back by Peleus; Nereus (labelled) standing 3/4-view to the left, with his head profile to the left, wearing a himation draped diagonally over his left shoulder, extends his right hand to the left (beseeching?), and holds a scepter up in his left hand; a female figure (labelled) running profile to the left, wearing a short-sleeved chiton with a long kolpos, a sphendone, two red bands on each wrist, stretches both arms ahead of her body, to the left; a female figure (labelled) running profile to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation, a long pony-tail, a kekryphylon, dot earrings, and a dot on a chain necklace.

artifact.collection: New York, Metropolitan Museum of Art
artifact.collection_history: Said to have been found in Athens (purchased 1931).
artifact.decoration_description: Middle (white ground): A column denoting interior space; nude Achilles (labelled), seated profile to the right in a klismos, with his right knee crossed over his left knee, his hands clasped in his lap, and his head bowed, in front of a kline on which lies Patroklos (labelled), lying profile to the left, with his head tilted up and his eyes closed, wrapped in a shroud, wearing a white taenia; a thin cloth hangs in front of him; another column; Klymene (labelled), seated on a dolphin 3/4-view to the left, with her head turned profile to the right, and her legs crossed, wearing a himation around her legs, over a medium-sleeved, belted chiton with an overfold, a brown band necklace, a brown dot earring, two bands on each wrist, a high pony tail tied in a pink band, holds a sword (in a scabbard) upright in her upraised right hand, and reaches her left hand, beseeching (?), toward Psamathe (labelled) (most of her left arm missing) seated 3/4-view to the left on a dolphin, with her head turned 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation around her legs, over a medium-sleeved, belted chiton, with an overfold, a white taenia, two bands on each wrist, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, holds a helmet, profile to the right, in her upraised right hand, and holds her left hand in front of her mouth (in a speaking gesture?); Thetis (labelled) seated 3/4-view to the left, on a dolphin, with her legs crossed, wearing a himation around her lower body, over a short-sleeved, belted chiton, a rayed taenia, a single band necklace, a disk earring, a snake band on her right wrist, a diagonal spear and a frontal shield (decorated in relief, with a lion sema prancing profile to the left) on her left arm, her right hand above her knee, on a dolphin; a Nereid seated 3/4-view to the left on a dolphin (head and parts of body missing), wearing a himation around her lower body, over her left shoulder, and a short-sleeved chiton, holds a cuirass (?) and reins with both hands; a Nereid (some of the top of her head, and her body below her waist are preserved) seated 3/4-view to the left on a dolphin, wearing a himation around her lower body, over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton, and a pink snake bracelet on her right hand, holds her left hand on her knee, and a greave in her right hand; Galene (labelled) (missing the middle of her body), seated profile to the left on a dolphin, wearing a short-sleeved, belted chiton (with shoulder straps?), a dot earring, and her hair tied in a bun (?), holds a brown necklace in her upraised right hand; Eunomia (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left on a dolphin, her head turned profile to the right, wearing a himation around her lower body, over a belted, short-sleeved chiton, a single band necklace, a dot earring, and a sphendone, holds reins in her lowered right hand, and a profile shield (?) in her upraised left hand; Kymodoke (labelled), only the back of her hair, and her body below her waist, are preserved), seated 3/4-view to the left on a dolphin, wearing a himation around her lower body, over a chiton, holds her right hand to the left, at waist level, and rests her left hand on her lap, touching an unidentifiable curving object; a rocky cliff behind her.

artifact.decoration_description: Peitho (labelled) standing near frontal, with her weight on her left leg, and her head profile to the left, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, black fibulae on her shoulders, her hair tied in a bun, holds up a branch in her left hand, and holds her slightly bent right arm at her side; a nude, bearded Menelaos (labelled), running 3/4-view to the right, with his left leg advanced, wearing a helmet, and a patterned chlamys and shield on his bent left arm, as well as a scabbard on his left hip, attached to a band over his right shoulder, holds his straight right arm behind his body, where a sword has just fallen from his opened right hand; a small, nude Eros, flying profile to the right, holds a small white garland (fugitive) out to Menelaos; Aphrodite (labelled), standing frontal, with her weight on her right leg, and her head profile to the left, wearing a himation over a button-sleeved chiton with shoulder straps, and a kekryphylon, holds in her left arm her himation over her shoulder, and with her right arm wraps her himation in front of her body; Helen (labelled), running 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, and her weight on her forward, bent left leg, wearing a peplos fastened with black fibulae, her hair in a bun, but also cascading from the sides, raises slightly both arms bent, the fingers of her right hand spread, palm out, and the left hand reaching behind the shield of the cult statue of Athena Promachos, standing profile to the left on a four-step base, wearing a belted peplos, a Corinthian helmet, a shield on her left arm, holding a spear diagonally in her upraised right hand.

artifact.summary: Eleusinian Procession
