artifact.collection_history: Acquired through the Dr. Hazel D. Hansen Fund
artifact.decoration_description:
A: Under the left handle, bearded Pan (with goat ears and horns), running 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his bent left leg, his right foot slightly above the ground, and his head turned profile to the right, wearing a nebris fastened around his neck and slung over his upraised left arm, hangs his right arm at his side; Demeter (labelled) (legs, upper right arm, upper torso, left hand, neck, and back of head preserved), seated on a rock 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation draped around her lower body (and probably over her left shoulder), over a medium-, button-sleeved chiton, a sakkos, and tear-drop earrings, holds her bent right arm at her side, and holds upright two torches in her upraised left hand; she looks up to a young female figure, Parthenos (labelled) standing near frontal, with her head profile to the left and her feet profile to the right, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left shoulder, over a bordered, medium-sleeved chiton, and a rayed taenia, holds her bent right arm at her side, and rests her left arm seemingly on a short torch; Triptolemos (labelled), seated profile to the right in his winged, snaky chariot with snakes (torso, upper arms and shoulders, and lower half of his wings are missing), wearing a himation draped over his legs, over a chiton, and a grain wreath, bends both arms at waist level, holds three grain stalks in his slightly raised left hand, and a phiale in his left hand; Kore (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her right leg, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a rayed taenia tied elaborately at the back, and black hoop earrings, pours a libation from a frontal oinochoe, held in her upraised right hand, at an angle toward the viewer, and holds her left hand at her side, her arm slightly bent; a female figure, perhaps Hekate (labelled), as suggested by the Raubitscheks, standing profile to the left, wearing a himation wrapped around her torso, and over her left shoulder/arm, over a medium-sleeved chiton, and a rayed taenia, holds a scepter, with a floral finial, upright in her upraised right hand, her left hand obscured by the himation; under the handle, a satyr (missing his upper left arm, shoulders and above) running 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his advanced, bent, left leg, wearing a nebris fastened around his neck and draped over his left shoulder, cradles a thyrsos in his bent right arm, and raises his left arm to the right.

B: Pompe (labelled; missing her waist), standing profile to the right, with her left foot slightly advanced, wearing a himation fastened at her shoulders, over a peplos, and a black hoop earring, holds a missing object in her right hand, at waist level, and a barbiton in her left hand; a balding Papposilenos, with a white beard, standing frontal, his head turned profile to the left, rests his bent right arm on a crooked staff, and holds the end of a wine skin, decorated with some ivy, held in his left hand and slung over his left shoulder bearded Dionysos (labelled; missing his upper torso and both arms), standing profile to the right, with his left foot slightly advanced, wearing a himation over a chiton, and an ivy wreath, holds a thyrsos upright in his upraised left hand, and holds in his lowered right hand a kantharos, just in front of his body; a female figure, perhaps Eleusis (incomplete label; missing the back of her head, face, shoulders, and upper arms) standing frontal, with her weight on her right leg, and her head turned profile to the left, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left arm, over a medium-sleeved, patterned chiton, and a sakkos, holds in her lowered right hand an oinochoe, frontal but tipped forward slightly to the viewer, and a short (Eleusinian) torch in her slightly raised left arm, held to the right.

artifact.decoration_description: A: Dithyrambic victory: a bull, standing profile to the right, before a tripod on a one-stepped base, is being adorned with stemmata by a female figure, leaning profile to the left, with her right foot advanced, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, a long pony tail, and a plain stephane; a female figure standing profile to the right, wearing a peplos and a sakkos, as well as an olive wreath, places stemmata over the horns of another bull, standing profile to the left, in front of similar tripod.

artifact.decoration_description: Leto, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a star-patterned himation over her shoulders, veiled over her head, and a medium-sleeved chiton (?), a leafy wreath over a taenia, pours a libation from a phiale held in her right hand, and raises her left hand, palm out; a small deer prances profile to the right, and raises its head and left front leg; a fruitful palm tree; Apollo Kitharoidos standing profile to the right, wearing a star-patterned himation, olive wreath over his long hair, holds a kithara in his bent left arm, and reaches his bent right arm to the right, pouring a libation from a phiale held in his right hand, over a low brazier; Artemis standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her right leg, himation over her left shoulder and around her waist, wearing a short-sleeved chiton, a red taenia with white rays, her hair in a bun, quiver and bow on her back, holds an oinochoe in her lowered right hand, and an enflamed torch in her lowered left hand; fruitful olive tree; Delos (labelled) seated 3/4-view to the left on an omphalos (around which is tied a wreath and a chain), legs crossed, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton with cross-straps, a star-pattern himation around her lower body, pulled up her back and the back of her head, a rayed stephane over hair tied in a bun, a black snake bracelet on each wrist, holds a phiale to the left in her right hand, and raises her left hand, of which the palm faces out; Hermes, standing near profile to the left, with his right foot raised on low rock, wearing calf-length strap-boots, a chlamys bound in front of his neck, a winged pilos, rests his left hand on hip, and his right elbow on his right knee, and holds a kerykeion in his right hand; tripod.
artifact.shape_description: Type A (with tripod foot)

artifact.name: Berlin F 2290
artifact.summary: Interior: Dionysos and satyr. Side A and B: maenads dancing at the image of Dionysos.
artifact.other_bibliography: Greifenhagen A.K. pl. 65-67.
artifact.collection_history: The cup was once in the Canino collection. It was acquired by the museum in 1841.
artifact.condit: The cup is in very good condition. There are small patches where the surface has been damaged.
artifact.decoration_description:
Interior: Dionysos and satyr. Dionysos, holding a sprouting grape vine in his left hand and a thyrsos in his right, stands listening to a flute-playing satyr. The satyr, on the left, plays a double flute. He wears fringed boots and a wreath, and has a tail, pointed ears and a bald head. Dionysos wears a chiton and mantle, a wreath and soft shoes.

Sides A and B: maenads dancing at the image of Dionysos. Maenads dance to the right, hair flying, completely caught up in their rapture, toward the altar and image of Dionysos on side B. On side A, the maenad on the far left carries a thyrsos, her other hand reaching forward. In front of her is a maenad playing krotala. A third maenad spins around in front of her, carrying a small fawn in one hand and a thyrsos in the other. To the right dances another maenad, one arm curved over her head, the other cradling a krater decorated with a satyr, palmettes and ivy leaves. In front of is another dancing maenad with a thyrsos, and on the far right a sixth maenad, one hand over her head, the other reaching toward the large wreath-bedecked krater standing under the handle of the vase. The image of Dionysos stands in the center of side B. It is a low pillar draped with clothes and a mask of Dionysos. Behind it stands a tree decorated with round balls of uncertain meaning. The altar to the right is a low structure crowned by a palmette and decorated with a painting of a seated man with a beard wearing a mantle and leaning on a staff (Dionysos?). On the far left, continuing the procession from side A, is a dancing maenad, hair flying as she spins, one arm outstretched. To the right, standing just behind the statue of Dionysos, is a maenad playing a double-flute. She wears a sakkos. A maenad dances to the right of the statue, partly hidden by the altar. Two more dancing maenads occupy the space to the right of the altar, the one nearest the altar carrying a thyrsos, her other arm outstretched. The maenad on the far right dances with one hand over her head, her body curved toward the altar. All the maenad wear chitons with overfolds. The statue of Dionysos, which perhaps consists of simply a mask on a post, is clothed in chiton, mantle and wreath.
artifact.inscriptions: The signature of the potter is incised on one handle: &epig-rough;*I*E*R*O*N *E*P*O*I*E*S*E*N, Hieron made it (or me).
artifact.shape_description: For the shape see Bloesch 92, Hieron no. 19.

artifact.name: Würzburg L 491
artifact.summary: Sides A and B: Maenads and satyrs<lb>Tondo: Peitho and Pothos attend Ariadne and Dionysos

Simis, Simon, Simos no. 9 (A. Kossatz-Deissmann); <bibl>Shapiro 1993</bibl>, 122, 181, 183, 201 n. 463, 203, 204, 257 no. 118, fig. 135-36, 166; <bibl>Kossatz-Deissmann 1991</bibl>, 187; <bibl>Add2</bibl>, 356; U. artifact.collection: Martin von Wagner Museum, University of Würzburg
artifact.decoration_description:
A: A nude satyr (preserved below mid-torso), standing profile to the right, with his weight on his right leg, his left leg bent, reaches his right hand to the right; Paidia (labelled in the field to the left of her head) standing near profile to the left, with her weight on her right leg, and her left leg bent, wearing a nebris draped over her left shoulder, belted over a sleeveless chiton, two bands on each wrist, and long hair, cradles a thyrsos in her left arm, and hangs her right arm at her side; a satyr running 3/4-view to the left (shoulder/head and middle of legs are not preserved), both legs bent, advances his right leg; a female figure standing profile to the right, is barely preserved, except for the lower portion of her drapery; a satyr standing profile to the left (only preserved below the waist) crosses his legs.

B: A satyr advancing 3/4-view to the right, bent at his waist and both knees, with his right leg advanced, holds, in both hands, to the right a piece of drapery; a maenad, perhaps Paidia, or more likely Eudia, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted peplos, and a himation, holds a kantharos in her right hand, and cradles a thyrsos in her left arm; a satyr standing 3/4-view to the right, with weight on his left leg, and his right leg bent, rest his right hand on his waist, and holds a stick in his left hand; a maenad standing profile to the right, wearing a chiton with a long kolpos, holds a thyrsos diagonally in her left hand, and reaches her right hand forward; a satyr standing profile to the left, with his weight on his left leg, and his right leg bent back, wears a nebris draped down his back.

Tondo: Peitho (labelled), standing profile to the right, wearing a peplos, a himation, and a stephane, holding her right hand up (in a speaking gesture?), and resting her left hand on the shoulder of a small Pothos (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, legs crossed, rests his right arm on Peitho, and hangs his right hand at his side; Ariadne and Dionysos are entwined, Ariadne wearing a chiton (?), a sphendone (?), and 2 black bands on each wrist; bearded Dionysos, wearing an ivy wreath, long leather boots, a short tunic, and a himation draped over his right arm, holds a thyrsos in his left hand, and a kantharos in his right hand, which he reaches to the right; nude, young satyr, Komos, standing profile to the left, with legs crossed, holds a torch in his left arm, and a handle of Dionysos' kantharos in his upraised right hand.

artifact.name: Würzburg L 248
artifact.summary: Side A: Theseus and Minotaur<lb>Side B: Herakles and the Nemean lion
artifact.sources_used: Langlotz 1932, 248, pl. 80 and 84; Simon 1975, 104; LIMC, 5, s.v. Herakles, n. 1833, with plate
artifact.collection: Martin von Wagner Museum, University of Würzburg
artifact.collection_history: From the Feoli Collection
artifact.condit: Good
artifact.comparanda: Similar scenes with Herakles and the lion in the same position and with the sword into the jaws in another eight vases, among which are London B 160 (ABV, 134,15); Würzburg 245 (ABV, 133, 1) and Würzburg 247 (ABV, 134, 17). For the complete list see LIMC, 5, s.v. Herakles, n. 1833. For scenes with Iolaos and Athena see LIMC, 5, s.v. Iolaos n. 13
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: Theseus and the Minotaur. In the middle of the scene, Theseus is standing with the sword in his right hand, plunging it into the Minotaur's forehead. He is dressed with a tight chitoniskos decorated with stripes. The Minotaur, with a naked human body and the head of a bull, is kneeling in front of Theseus at right. He has been wounded and is dying. Behind Theseus at left there are a youth and a maiden with a wreath in her hand. The youth is naked and has long hair and the maiden is dressed with a decorated peplos. At the right, two youths are standing, and between them and the Minotaur is another maiden, also holding a wreath. She is dressed also in a decorated peplos, but on her head is a diadem. The diadem may identify her as Ariadne; the wreaths carried by the maidens may be gifts for Theseus. Both maidens and youths seem to belong to the tribute given by the city of Athens to Crete for the Minotaur.

The inscriptions on the background make no sense. Simon 1975 suggests that there may have been a picture by Exekias with the same theme and with all the names inscribed, from which the painter of this piece took the inspiration.

Side B: Herakles and the Nemean lion. Herakles, in the middle of the scene, holds the lion by the neck and plunges his sword into its jaws, both wrestling side by side. The lion scratches Herakles with a hind paw and fore paw, digging them into his shoulder and calf. The lion is usually behind Herakles and turning its head back, but in this case it is in front. Athena stands at left, looking inwards at the scene. She is dressed with a chiton and himation and carries a spear. At right, a helmeted Iolaos standing and looking to the scene, carries the scabbard for the sword that Herakles has used.

The first labor of Herakles was to subdue a lion living near Nemea. In some of the literary sources it is said that the lion was invulnerable to weapons or to iron weapons (Diod. Sic. 4.11.3-4). Most artists chose to illustrate Herakles strangling the lion or knocking him with the club, as a variety of literary sources relate the myth: Hes. Th. 326-322, the Diodorus passage cited above, Theocritus 25.266-271, and Apollod. 2.5.1. In this case, as in many other representations, the lion is being killed with a sword, contradicting most of the literary sources, which are mostly later in date.

artifact.name: Würzburg L 481
artifact.summary: Sides A and B: Five men and a flute player in a symposion<lb>Tondo: youth seated with lyre
artifact.other_bibliography: Langlotz 1932, n. 481, pls. 150-51, 164; Hagenow, G., Aus dem Weingarten in der Antike: der Wein in Dichtung, Brauchtum und Alltag, Mainz 1982, 45, fig. 16; Paquette 1984, 183, b15.

artifact.collection_history: From the Feoli Collection

artifact.comparanda: The scene of the symposion is very similar to another cup, Berlin F 2298 (ARV2, 364, 52).
artifact.decoration_description:
On sides A and B, over a maeander band, a continuous scene of five men and a flute player at a symposion. Side A: three men in a drinking party (symposion). Three men draped in himations are lying on decorated cushions and talk gesticulating with their arms. All three have beards and curly black hair and hold drinking vessels in their left hands. The first from left, looking to the right, holds a cup. The second, looking to the left, holds also a cup, and the one at right, faces to left and holds a skyphos. On the wall behind them is hanging a basket.

Side B: Two men and a flute player. Two more men belonging to the same scene as in A, are lying on cushions, draped in himations. Both men, first and second figures from left, turn their heads to look at a youth playing the double flute (aulos) behind them. The men are bearded and have curly black hair. The one at left holds a skyphos in his left hand and the one in the middle, a cup. The flute player, rightmost figure, wears a tunic or mantle around his lower body and leans on a decorated cushion.

Tondo: A seated youth with a lyre. A black haired youth is sitting on a stool, holding a lyre in his left hand, while his right hand goes back as he were ready to start playing. He is draped in a himation and wears shoes open in the front.

artifact.name: Würzburg L 507
artifact.summary: Side A: warrior leaving home (extispicy)<lb>Side B: Komos: two men and a woman in a procession<lb>Lid: chariot race
artifact.other_bibliography: Beazley 1933b, 111f. 23 nr. 1
artifact.collection: Martin von Wagner Museum, University of Würzburg
artifact.collection_history: From the Feoli Collection
artifact.decoration_description:
Side A: A scene of departure of an hoplite with extispicy (omen-taking by examining the entrails of animals). The hoplite is standing towards the left, taking the omen; in front of him is a nude boy who presents the entrails. This group is framed by secondary figures: a Scythian and a woman (the hoplite's wife?). The hoplite in the center of the picture has just taken with his right hand part of the entrails which the boy is holding. On either side the Scythian and the woman raise a hand in astonishment. The hoplite is the tallest figure. His helmet breaks the frame above, a palmette frieze. He is completely armed and carries a long spear. The boy standing before him at left wears a red wreath on his hair. Behind the boy stands the Scythian warrior. The Scythian wears a tricot with a large circular neck-opening and decorated with horizontal stripes. He has a high-crowned cap with neck flap and two cheek-flaps on one side and he wears shoes. A gorytos (a combination of quiver and a bow-case) is hanging from his belt and a battle axe is in his right hand. He has a pointed beard, which is both short and thin (this "van Dyke" beard is distinctly different from the full beards of the Greek on side B).

Between the hoplite and the woman at right is a dog looking upwards at the woman. The dog is seen from the back, a very unusual depiction for the time. The woman, in chiton and himation, has her hair gathered up and wears a diadem on her head. She is carrying a cup (phiale) in her left hand.

The picture is framed by palmette friezes.

Side B: Two men and a woman to the right in an scene of komos. Two men and a woman, all nude and carrying drinking vases and musical instruments, seem to come from a drinking party or symposium. The woman at right is leading the procession. She advances to the right; her body is drawn in a frontal position, and she is turns her head back to the left to face the men. She is dark-haired and wears a red ivy wreath and a collar around her neck. She is carrying a flute on either hand and is using one of them to ward off the man behind her, in a suggestive fashion. This man in the middle carries a lyre in his left hand and a large skyphos in his right. He is also dark-haired and bearded and wears a taenia (a red fillet) on his head. The leftmost man seems to move to the left, but he is turning the whole body to the right, coming behind the other man. He has black hair, but a blond beard and wears a fillet on his head. He is carrying a large pointed amphora in his left hand; in his right hand he holds a kylix by the handle, as if to throw the contents in a game of kottabos. The men look drunk in their gestures. The anatomy of the woman is not realistic; the lines over the pubis are masculine and the disposition of her breasts is impossible.

Lid: Chariot race. Three chariots are running on a track represented by winning-post decorated with bands. The feeling of speed is extraordinary. One of the horses has broken out from one of the chariots and is galloping alone behind it with floating bridles.
artifact.inscriptions: The inscriptions on both sides make no sense
artifact.relief: The lines inside the figures have relief

artifact.name: Würzburg L 526
artifact.summary: Side A: Dionysos between two dancing satyrs<lb>Side B: Three naked youths in a procession (Komos)
artifact.sources_used: Simon 1975, 130; LIMC, III, s.v. Dionysos n. 291 with pl.
artifact.collection: Martin von Wagner Museum, University of Würzburg
artifact.date_description: Simon dates the vase between 490 and 480 B.C., whereas Gaspari (LIMC, III) takes it back around 500 B.C.
artifact.collection_history: From the Feoli Collection
artifact.condit: Dionysos' right foot, part of the head of satyr on the right, leftmost youth's calf and foot and part of the head of the second man from left are missing, as well as some of the dot decoration on side B.
artifact.comparanda: Compare with the scene of Dionysos with dancing satyrs in Louvre C 10759, ARV2, 239, 20.
artifact.decoration_description:
On both sides the picture is framed by a dot decoration on the sides and a line of tongues on the shoulder

Side A: Dionysos between two dancing satyrs. Dionysos moves towards the right accompanied by two drunk ithyphallic satyrs immersed in the dance. The god, bearded and richly dressed in a long chiton and a himation, holds a drinking horn in his left hand and a black kantharos in his right and turns his head to look at the satyr behind him. This satyr on the left, holding a wineskin on his left hand, follows the god and seem to be trying to get wine from him. The half bald satyr on the right is completely concentrated in the dance and acts with exaggerated gestures of his arms. Both satyrs are naked, bearded and with long hear falling over their shoulders and have horse tails. Dionysos and the two satyrs wear red wreaths on the head. Dionysos carries a drinking horn and a black kantharos, two of his attributes. According to Carpenter (Carpenter 1986, 125-126), around 540 B.C. there is a change in Dionysos iconography which affects also to the attributes like the kantharos and the drinking horn: the last one starts to be replaced by the first. Already in 530 B.C. in the Antimenes Painter's works both recipients can be found like in this case. This vase is a little late to present both attributes.

Side B: A scene of a komos. Three young men in a procession carrying utensils through the street as if coming from a drinking party. Behind the youth leading the procession at right, come two other youths; the one in the middle carries a basket with food and the leftmost, a big pointed amphora. The young man at right is seen from the back and turns his head towards his companions. All three are naked. The first two wear wreaths on their heads and the third one, a band, all of them in red.

Rim: On the top of the rim, there is a black figured frieze of animals; a motif already ancient for this time. There are four pairs of a panther and a wild goat facing one another. On the handle-plate were palmettes. The one on the right side is missing because of the restoration.

artifact.summary: Side A: Bride sitting on a couch, with Eros, Aphrodite and woman. Side B: two Erotes wrestling, Aphrodite and women
artifact.sources_used: Richter 1958; Simon 1975b, 144; M. Robertson 1975, pl. 132b; LIMC, II, pl. 126, s.v. Aphrodite n. 1251; III, pl 629, s.v. Eros 388.
artifact.other_bibliography: Buschor, AM 71, 1956, 205; Beil. 115, 2; 116,2;Greifenhagen 1957, 42, fig. 31-33; Simon, AK 15 (1972) pl. 6, 1-3; CVA, 2, pls. 33.4, 34.1-5, 35.1-8; Roberts 1978, pl 76.1; Scheibler 1983, 45, fig. 44; Paquette 1984, 201, H13; Hesp. 53 (1984) pl. 64b.
artifact.collection: Martin von Wagner Museum, University of Würzburg
artifact.condit: Several fragments are missing in most of the figures. The glaze is worn almost completely.
artifact.comparanda: Similar scenes on vases in Breitbrunn and Athens: ARV2, 1133, 6bis and 20
artifact.decoration_description:
Nuptial scene. On side A, a bride in the center of the scene sitting in a kline, and an Eros coming from left flying to assist her. At left Aphrodite is standing looking at the bride. On the other side of the bride, at right, a woman is coming toward the couch bringing a loutrophoros, the vase used in the marriages for the bride's bath. The bride is dressed with a pleated belted peplos, and her hair is tied up in a wide white band dotted in black. Aphrodite is shown at the moment of putting a veil over her head.

On side B, in the middle of the scene two Erotes are fighting in the presence of three women or goddesses. The female figures hold a special variety of umpire's staff (rhabdos; not a spear). One of them, at right, is sitting in a klismos, and therefore may be identified as Aphrodite; she has also this kind of staff leaning on her shoulder. The women may also be the Moirai, according to Simon. Behind the seated woman, is standing another (perhaps identified as Peitho?). Behind her another woman is seated, playing the trigonon, a three-cornered greek harp. On the wall is hanging a wreath and on the floor, a basket sits.

The scene is a typical scene of a bride getting ready for her wedding. As she ties up her hair (or perhaps unties her hair to take a bath) she thinks of her upcoming marriage. While she is thinking of love, Eros comes to her bed to assist her. Aphrodite is there veiling (or unveiling) herself like a bride. A woman belonging to real life brings water in a loutrophoros to the bride for her bath. On the other side of the vase, Simon suggests that the two Erotes wrestling in the middle of the scene represent the struggling feelings of the bride, between love of marriage and love of maidenhood. The goddesses assisting the fighting could be the Moirai according to Simon. The seated woman could be Aphrodite and the woman behind her Peitho, goddesses related to love, seduction and destiny, all elements present in an event like a wedding. The three-cornered harp, the trigonon, occurs much less frequently on Attic vases than the lyre or the kythara, but it was apparently in favor in the late fifth and the fourth century B.C.

The Washing Painter, so called from his pictures of women washing on small hydriai and pelikai, also decorated several large nuptial vases and loutrophroi with wedding scenes
artifact.shape_description: The pyxis was a vessel for jewelery and was a common gift for a wedding

artifact.name: Würzburg L 466
artifact.summary: The Judgement of Paris. Side A: Paris, Hermes, Hera and Athena. Side B: Aphrodite. A woman between two youths.
artifact.sources_used: Raab 1972, 173, no. 22 type A IV; Simon 1975, 63; Clairmont 1951, K19 Wust 45
artifact.collection: Martin von Wagner Museum, University of Würzburg
artifact.collection_history: From Margaritis Collection
artifact.condit: Athena's head is missing. The added red is almost all gone.
artifact.decoration_description:
Judgement of Paris around the entire vessel. Side A: Hermes, with travel hat, winged shoes and kerykeion, leads Hera and Athena to Paris. Paris is bearded, dressed in short chiton, sitting on a stool and carries a large lyre in his left hand and the plektron in his right. Hera is a tall figure wrapped in a himation and resembling an archaic kore sculpture. Athena is also dressed in chiton and himation, and carries a spear; her head is missing.

Side B: Aphrodite, a woman and two youths. The female figure on the left is probably Aphrodite, belonging to the Judgement of Paris scene on the opposite side; she faces to the left rather than towards the center of this scene. She is dressed like a normal mortal woman, wrapped in a himation and looking, as does Hera, like an archaic sculpture. To the right, a veiled woman between two youths draped in mantles is holding a love wreath. Behind her a veiled woman offering a love wreath to a men at her left. Behind her another youth facing left.

This is another variation of the representation of the Judgement of Paris, in which Paris does not come to meet the divine procession, but is surprised while seated doing something, as here playing the lyre. The archaic sources for this event are Hom. Il. 24.25-30 and Cypr. (EGF 17).
artifact.shape_description: This type of kantharos with high double handles looking like ears comes to Boeotian pottery at the beginning of the V century B.C.

artifact.name: Berlin F 2705
artifact.summary: Eunomia and Eukleia with Eros and Adonis
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>Shapiro 1993</bibl>, 76-77, 236 no. 25, figs. 28-29; I. Wehgartner, CVA Berlin, Antikenmuseum 8 (1991) 66-67, pls. 46, 48.4, ill. 22.3 (with previous bibliography); G. Körte, "Eichelförmige Lekythos mit Goldschmuck aus Attika," <hi rend="ital">AZ</hi> 37 (1879) 93-96 pl. 10.
artifact.decoration_description:
Eunomia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a sleeveless chiton, a himation draped around her legs and over her left shoulder, a long pony tail, and a black band necklace, holds a tray of fruit at waist level in her left hand, and hangs her right hand at her side; Adonis, seated 3/4-view to the left on a klismos, with his head turned profile to the right, wearing a himation around his hips and legs, and a grain crown, places his feet on a footstool, holds his right hand in front of his body, where it meets the hand of Eros, and kisses Eros, standing 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his left leg, his right leg relaxed, both arms reaching around Adonis; Eukleia (labelled), standing nearly frontal, with her head profile to the left, and her weight on her right leg, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton, part of which is rewrapped around her hips, and a black band necklace, holds a lyre in her bent left hand, and raises to the left her right hand, on which a small bird is perched.

Adonis has alternately been identified as Phaon (Beazley). Wehgartner suggests that this vase is a warning of danger in excess, and that Eunomia and Eukleia are here balancing Eros' lack of restraint.

artifact.decoration_description: A female figure, probably Peitho (seemingly labelled above her right arm, but now unreadable), standing profile to the right, with her left foot raised on a rock, bent at the waist, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, with shoulder straps, a rayed sphendone, two (red?) bands on her right wrist, arranges sprigs of vegetation with her right hand, on a flat basket/plate held in her left hand, and rests her left elbow on her knee; Aphrodite (labelled) seated 3/4-view to the left, with her head profile to the right, her calves crossed, wearing a himation around her legs and up her back, which she holds over her right shoulder in her right hand, over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton, and a rayed sphendone, rests her left hand on her seat; beneath her, a footed box with shoes atop; a nude winged Pothos (labelled on either side of his wings), leaning near profile to the right, with his weight on his right leg, his left leg relaxed, and crossing his right calf, rests his left elbow near the lap of Chryippos (labelled above his head), and points his right hand to the left, to Aphrodite; Chrysippos (mortal youth/bridegroom?), seated on his chlamys (?) 3/4-view to the left, with his legs crossed, wearing boots, a scabbard strap over his right shoulder, and a petasos behind his neck, holds his right hand on his knee, and his left hand at his side; a palmette beneath him; a faded kanoun; Pompe (labelled above her head), seated 3/4-view to the right, with her head turned profile to the left, wearing a short-sleeved, belted chiton with shoulder straps, a black band necklace, and a rayed sphendone, holds her right arm in front of her chest, her upraised left hand behind her head, and looks down to the left, at the kanoun.

artifact.name: Louvre MNB 1320
artifact.summary: Personifications
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 7.248 s.v. Peitho no. 54 (N. Icard-Gianolio); <bibl>Add2</bibl>, 364; <bibl>Burn 1987</bibl>, 114 MM 109 pl. 14c-e; <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 2.150 s.v. Aphrodite no. 1563, pl. 152 (A. Delivorrias); <bibl>Lezzi-Hafter 1976</bibl>, 48, 117, O 22, pl. 166a-b; <bibl>EAA</bibl> 7 (1966) 1040 s.v. Tyche (J.G. Szilágyi); <bibl>Hamdorf 1964</bibl> 100 no. 325b; <bibl>Papadaki 1960</bibl> 123.
artifact.collection_history: This acorn lekythos perfectly fits the description of two lekythoi found together in Attika, once known in a private collection in Athens, reported as seen by Körte in the winter of 1877-1878. It is unclear whether the two were exact duplicates, whether both were labelled, and if so, which one eventually came into the collection at the Louvre. They have become conflated in bibliographies, although here I list separately the bibliography for the "once Athens,"" citations that either pre-date the Louvre acquisition (?), or otherwise ignore it.
artifact.decoration_description: A female figure, perhaps Hygieia, standing near profile to the right, wearing a peplos, a short pony tail, a black band necklace, and disk earrings, holds a box in her left hand, and holds her right hand at waist level; a female figure, perhaps Peitho, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a sleeveless, high-belted chiton, holds a sprig of vegetation in her left hand, and points her right hand to Tyche (?); a winged Eros, crouching 3/4-view to the right, crowns the female figure to his right, possibly Tyche, seated on a stool 3/4-view to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation around her legs, a short pony tail, a black band necklace, and black hoop earrings; she tilts her head back, holds her left arm at her side, and raises her right hand in front of her face; a female figure, perhaps Harmonia, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation draped over her left shoulder, a kekryphylon, a beaded necklace, and dotted-disk earrings, holds her left hand at waist level, and raises her right hand in front of her face.
artifact.inscriptions: According to Beazley, the labels identifying these characters are modern. As all, with the possible exception of Tyche, are paralleled in contemporary vase paintings, they are believable, although on the basis of iconographic parallels it is more likely that the seated female figure is Aphrodite, and that the female figure behind her (to the right) is Peitho.

artifact.decoration_description: Harmonia (labelled), seated near profile to the right in a klismos, wearing a short-sleeved, belted chiton, a himation over her legs, a sphendone (with a white wreath?), and a black band necklace, rests her left arm on the back of her chair, and proffers in her right hand a box with two white balls atop, and a fringed sash; a kalathos; Eukleia (labelled), standing profile to the left, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a sphendone, a peplos, and a black band necklace, holds white fronds in her lowered left hand and her upraised right hand; Eunomia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a belted peplos, with her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, holds in her right hand an inverted keras (?) with white strings, and extends, in her left hand, an alabastron; a kalathos below; Pannychis (labelled), standing profile to the right, with her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a sakkos, and a peplos, partially obscures a cushioned stool, and holds white fronds in her upraised right hand, and her lowered left hand; a swan (?); Aphrodite (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the right on a klismos, wearing a short-sleeved, belted chiton with shoulder straps, a himation over her legs, a black band necklace, a red taenia (with a white wreath?), holds drapery over her right shoulder with her right hand, and on her left hand a small, nude, red Eros, crouched profile to the left, wearing a red taenia, and holding a white necklace between his upraised right hand and his lowered left hand; a kalathos; Klymene (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her right leg and her left leg relaxed, wearing a belted peplos, a sphendone, and a black band necklace, holds in her left hand an object shaped like an inverted keras with white strings, and in her left hand a footed plemmochoe and a fringed sash.

artifact.name: Mainz 118
artifact.summary: Eunomia and Eukleia with Paidia and others
artifact.sources_used: E. Böhr, CVA Mainz University 2 (1993) 45-47 pl. 27 (with previous bibliography).
artifact.collection_history: Formerly in the Prussian Royal Collection
artifact.decoration_description:
Eukleia (labelled in the left field), bending profile to the right, with her right leg bent back, wearing a belted peplos, a short, high pony tail, hoop earrings, proffers a large box held in both hands; a low table; a sprig of vegetation; Eunomia (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left on a rock, wearing a belted peplos, a sphendone, and hoop earrings, rests her left hand on a rock, and holds an indistinct bird (identified by Böhr [1993] as a nightingale) on her right hand; another sprig; a goose; a female figure standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted peplos, and a sakkos, holds a plemmochoe and a fringed sash in her left hand, and reaches her right hand to the left; a kalathos; a female figure, Pa(i)dia (labelled), standing profile to the right, wearing a belted peplos, bends both arms to the right, holds a beaded necklace (?) in her lowered left hand, and a large box and a himation in her right hand; another female figure seated on the rocks 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, raises an alabastron in her right hand, and rests her left hand on the rock, above a large box; a sash (?) hanging; a female figure, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted peplos, a sakkos (eroded), holds drapery or a fan (?) in her lowered right hand, and a plemmochoe and himation in her upraised left hand.

Hampe (123) suggested that Eukleia was shown here welcoming Eunomia into her cult with a gift; this suggestion is encouraged by Böhr's interpretation of Eunomia's bird as a nightingale, a symbol of (the welcoming into) society, for according to Aelian, NA 5.38, the nightingale sings more enthusiastically when (it has an audience) in society.

artifact.decoration_description:
Goose or swan, standing profile to the right (only head preserved); Chryse (labelled), standing near frontal, slightly to the left, with her weight on her right leg, and her left knee bent, wearing a belted peplos, a sphendone, black necklace, dotted-hoop earrings, and a black band on each wrist, looks down at the bird, and holds her right hand just above the bird, and holds her left arm down and back; Eunomia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted, sleeved chiton with a kolpos, a white taenia, a short pony tail, black hoop earrings, a black necklace, and black bands on each wrist, holds a flower (?) in her left hand, at waist level, and a beaded necklace (?) in her upraised right hand; Eukleia (labelled), standing profile to the right, wearing a belted peplos, a sphendone with a wreath, a black necklace, black leaf-shaped earrings, and a black band on each wrist, raises her left foot on a rock, and holding a necklace between her upraised right hand and her lowered left hand, to a female figure, perhaps Nikopolis (labelled); a small deer (?) moving profile to the right; "Nikopolis" seated near profile to the right, head profile to the left, wearing a belted peplos, a black necklace, a sphendone with a wreath, and a black (?) band on her right wrist, rests her right hand on a rock, and her left hand on her lap; a laurel (?) branch.

The name of the fourth female figure has been alternatively read as Nike, Aike, Dike, or Nikopolis.

artifact.collection_history: Found at Eretria in 1893.
artifact.decoration_description:
Lid: Dionysos, seated maenad, five dancing maenads practicing sparagmos, standing maenad attending Dionysos.

Pyxis: Aphrodite (labelled), standing profile to the right, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton with a kolpos, a stephane, beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, holds a scepter in her right hand, and holds the white reins of her chariot with both hands; Pothos (labelled) and Hedylogos (labelled), both nude, white, winged, wearing chest straps holding the reins, rayed crowns, and sandals, pulling Aphrodite's chariot; a small tree; Hygieia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a belted, sleeved chiton, a stephane, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist; Eunomia (labelled), seated in a chair 3/4-view to the right, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation around her legs, a sphendone, bead earrings, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, holds a beaded necklace with both hands; Paidia (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted peplos, a beaded necklace, a sphendone, bead earrings, and two bands on each wrist, holds a box in her left hand, and a beaded necklace in her extended right hand; Eudaimonia (labelled), standing near profile to the right, with her weight on her right leg, wearing a belted peplos (?), a high pony tail, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, and two bands on her right wrist, ties a sandal on her left foot with both hands; a nude, winged Himeros (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his right leg, wearing a rayed crown and sandals, holds a beaded necklace in his right hand, and an apple (?) in his left hand; Harmonia (labelled), seated 3/4-view to the left, with her head 3/4-view to the right, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation around her legs, a spiked crown, bead earrings, a beaded necklace, and two bands on each wrist, rests her left arm on the back of her chair, stretches her right arm to the left, and holds branches in each hand; Kale (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a sleeveless chiton draped over her left shoulder, a sphendone, a beaded necklace, bead earrings, and two bands on each wrist, raises a beaded necklace between both hands.

This image of Aphrodite riding a chariot led by Erotes compares to an unlabelled scene on a squat lekythos in a private collection in Mühlenstein (ARV2, 1317.3).

artifact.collection: New York, Metropolitan Museum of Art
artifact.collection_history: Purchased in 1909.
artifact.decoration_description:
Ionic column; Peitho (labelled to the right of her head), standing 3/4-view to the right, her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a peplos belted over a long overfold, holds her right arm at her side, and holds a footed chest, with three balls atop, and a sash, in her left arm; Aphrodite (labelled), seated on a klismos 3/4-view to the left, with her legs crossed, wearing a himation around her legs, over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton with shoulder straps, a rayed sphendone, two bands on each wrist, and a dotted disk earring, rests her left arm on the back of her chair, and holds her right hand in front of her chest, in a speaking gesture; a kalathos basket; Hygieia (labelled above her head), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her right leg, her left leg relaxed, wearing a peplos, belted over a long overfold, holds a plemmochoe to the left, in her right hand, and a footed chest in her left hand; Eudaimonia (labelled), standing near frontal, slightly to the right, with her head profile to the right, her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a himation draped over her left shoulder, around her lower body, and back over her bent left arm, over a short-sleeved chiton with shoulder straps, and a high pony tail, holds an eight-bead necklace down to the left, in her right hand, and holds her left hand, palm up (in a speaking gesture?), to the right; Paidia (labelled above her head), running 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her forward, bent, right leg, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton with a kolpos and shoulder straps, and loose, windswept hair, balances a stick on her outstretched right hand, and holds her left hand up behind her head; Eukleia (labelled above her head), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a belted peplos and a sphendone, holds her right arm at her side, and holds a round (?) wicker basket and a sash in her left arm; Eunomia (labelled vertically, down the right side of her body), standing 3/4-view to the left, with weight on her right leg, her left leg relaxed, wearing a himation draped around her lower body and over her left arm (obscuring it), over a belted, medium-sleeved chiton, a broad taenia, and disk earrings, points the index finger of her right hand down to the left.

The long-standing misreading of "Eunomia" as "Aponia" has recently been corrected, and confirmed by Richard Stone, Conservator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, at the instigation of Gloria Ferrari (see bibliography below).

artifact.decoration_description:
A (Gigantomachy): Enkelados (labelled above his head), crouched profile to the right, both legs bent, wearing an Attic helmet, and a shield shown in 3/4-inside-view on his bent left arm; Mimas (labelled in red wash, below his rock), leaning 3/4-view to the right, with his head frontal, both legs bent, holding a large rock (shaped like a wine skin!) in both arms, wearing a nebris on his left arm; above him, two nude men, of whom only the legs are preserved; a giant (labelled above his head), lunging 3/4-back-view to the right, both legs bent, with weight on his left leg, wearing a nebris over his left arm, and holding an unidentifiable object in his right hand, extended to the right; another male figure above him, crouching near profile to the right, with his bent, left leg raised on a rock, holds a short spear in his lowered right hand, and raises his left hand on top of a rock; another male figure, standing 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his bent, right leg, wearing a nebris over his left arm, raises a large rock in both arms; a female figure, probably Attika or Ge, shown only above her hips, standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a belted peplos, and long hair, raises both bent arms, and looks up; Helios (shown from his hips up; the tops of the four horses also shown) riding a quadriga 3/4-view to the left; another quadriga (?).

B: The feet and drapery of some satyrs; a maenad, Paidia (labelled), lunging 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her forward, bent, left leg, wearing a belted, sleeveless chiton, a nebris draped over her left arm, and a rayed, red ivy wreath, raises a rock in her right hand, held behind her head, and a thyrsos, to the right, in her upraised left hand; a nude, bearded satyr (labelled to the right of his head), lunging 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his raised, bent, forward, left leg, wearing a crested Attic helmet, and a nebris over his extended left arm (left hand not preserved), holds his spear horizontally in his lowered right arm; the edge of a wheel (?) above; the extended left leg, and part of a bent right leg (and buttocks) of a nude male figure shown in 3/4-back-view to the right; a tree with ivy branches below.

artifact.name: Eichenzell AV 77
artifact.summary: A (upper level): Birth of Erichthonios<lb>A (lower level): Zeus, two women, Poseidon, Eros pointing toward Erichthonios.<lb>B: Eros, Apollo (?), a female figure, perhaps Krete; Herakles lunging at the Cretan bull, crowned by Nike, Athena and another Nike

artifact.decoration_description: A (upper level): Birth of Erichthonios: A female figure standing near profile to the right, wearing a belted chiton, a long pony tail, a stephane, dotted-disk earrings, and a beaded necklace, points her right hand to the right, and rests her left arm on the shoulder of another female figure, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her head 3/4-view to the left, wearing a chiton, a long-sleeved oriental tunic, a wreath, and hoop earrings, who rests her right hand on her hip, and reaches her left arm to an adjacent, seated female figure; a small, white, nude Eros, standing profile to the right, with his left foot raised, rests his right hand on knee, and his left hand on the shoulder of a female figure seated 3/4-view to the left, with her head profile to the right, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation draped around her legs and over her left shoulder, a sphendone, wreath, dotted-disk earrings with pendant hoops, a beaded necklace, and three or more white bands on each wrist; Kekrops, seated 3/4-view to the right before an altar, with his scaly snake tail coiled beneath him, pointing to the left, wearing a sleeveless oriental tunic (illustrating a Nereid on a hippocamp), a himation over both forearms and his back, a mustache, and a white taenia, holds a phiale in his right hand, a lamb and branches in his left hand, and rests a scepter over his left shoulder; olive tree behind; above, a nude, red Nike (?), flying 3/4-view to the right, with frontal wings, wearing a white taenia, holds an alabastron in her right hand, and branches in her left hand; Athena, standing near frontal, with her weight on her left leg, and her head profile to the left, wearing a sleeved chiton, a himation draped over her left shoulder and wrapped around her torso, partially obscuring her gorgoneion, a stephane, a beaded necklace, and two white bands on her right wrist, holds a phiale in her lowered right hand, and a spear upright in her upraised left hand; a female figure, perhaps Attika, seated 3/4-view to the left on white strut (?), wearing a sleeved chiton with chest straps, a himation over her thighs, a beaded necklace, an olive wreath, and two white bands on each wrist, rests her left arm on a shield with a gorgon, and raises a frontal Corinthian helmet in her right hand; Hermes, standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a chlamys bound at the front of his neck, a winged pilos, and black boots, raises his left foot on a rock, places his left hand on his knee, and holds a kerykeion up in his right hand; a tripod below; over the handle, Hephaistos, reclining 3/4-back-view to the left, wearing a himation draped around the lower body, a krobylos, and an olive wreath, holds a kerykeion in his/her left hand, and a phiale in his/her right hand; an olive tree behind; a small Eros, flying near profile to the left, wearing a wreathed, holds an olive wreath in his lowered left hand, and in his right hand an oinochoe, from which he is about to pour a libation into a phiale.

artifact.decoration_description: Teukros (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his right leg, legs crossed, wearing a blue and pink himation, a scabbard strap over his right shoulder, yellow boots, gold hair, rests his right hand on his hip, and reaches his left hand behind the nude baby Eurysakes (labelled) (with gold hair), kneeling 3/4-view to the right, with his right leg falling behind, and his left knee on the lap of a female figure (perhaps Tekmessa), to whom he reaches up both arms. She is seated 3/4-view to the left on a throne, with her head tilted down, wearing a long-sleeved, green chiton, a blue-white himation around her legs and the back of her chair, yellow slippers, long gold hair; Adonis (labelled), seated profile to the right on a klismos, wearing a blue himation around his legs and over the back of the klismos, rests his right elbow on the back of the klismos, and reaches his left arm to the right shoulder of Peitho; nude Eros, with gold hair and wings, leaning 3/4-view to the right over the left arm of Adonis, with both arms resting on Adonis' arm, looks up to Peitho (labelled), standing frontal, with her head turned 3/4-view to the left, wearing a pink himation over a pink medium-sleeved, chiton veiled over her head, braided gilded hair, and pendant earrings, resting her right hand on the lap of Adonis, and raising her left arm; Aphrodite (labelled), seated profile to the left on a throne, wearing a belted sleeveless chiton, a pink and green himation around her lower body, veiled over her gold hair, and held above her shoulder in her right hand, a red sakkos, a beaded necklace, disk earrings, and a twisted band on her left wrist, holds a gilded mirror in her left hand.

artifact.decoration_description: A maenad, labelled Paidia, running to the right, and part of a standing maenad, holding a thyrsos.

artifact.name: Mannheim Cg 123
artifact.summary: Side A: Tribal victory<lb>Side B: Three draped youths with strigils
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 1.304 s.v. Agon no. 5, pl. 223 (F. Canciani); A. Greifenhagen, CVA Mannheim, Reiss-Museum 1 (1958) 40-41, pl. 29.4, 30.1-2, 4-5 (with previous bibliography).
artifact.decoration_description:
A: Eros, running 3/4-view to the right, with his left leg advanced, wearing a wreath, arms bent, holds his hands forward at waist level; a white bull (which Eros leads to sacrifice?), before an Ionic column with white disk above; a female figure, running 3/4-view to the right, with her head profile to the left, wearing a belted peplos (?), an olive wreath, a beaded necklace, and two white bands on each wrist, raises her right arm to touch the horn of the bull, and holds a sword upright in her left hand.

Beazley suggested that the female figure was "victorious Phyle," celebrating a victory in the torch race; this figure is comparable to "Phyle" on the Munich vase by the Hector Painter (Munich J 386) (also cf. a possible Phyle on London E 284). It has further been suggested that the running Eros is meant to be Agon. Neither figure is labelled, and no sure comparanda exist, however, for either identification.

artifact.name: Empúries 1494
artifact.summary: Choral festival/victory?

artifact.collection_history: Found at Empúries, from an unidentified tomb (said to be on a road near the beach. Formerly in Barcelona, Museo Arqueológico 33, and earlier Palace de la Diputacio, Formerly in the Alfaras Collection [before 1908]).
artifact.decoration_description:
This vase is thought to have commemorated a choral victory, perhaps at the Thargelia festival, as suggested by the presence of Apollo. It would then have been commissioned by the choregos.

A: Centauromachy?

B (upper level): Nike flying profile to the right, wearing a sleeveless, belted chiton, decorated a short pony tail, and a white-peaked crown, bends her right arm at waist level, and reaches her left arm (missing beyond the shoulder) to the right; Dionysos (head, neck, upper torso, and feet missing) seated 3/4-view to the left, wearing a himation around his legs, holds a thyrsos (?) diagonally in his lowered right hand, and holds his left arm in front of his body; a winged female figure (Hygieia?), standing profile to the right, bends her right arm at her side, and reaches her left arm up to decorate a trophy; a winged Nike (labelled above her head) (only top of head, wings, lower legs preserved), standing profile to the left, with her weight on her advanced left leg, presumably also decorating the trophy; Apollo (labelled above his lyre) (left leg, lower torso, left elbow, and right hand missing, upper torso details indistinct), seated 3/4-view to the right, with his head profile to the left, wearing a himation around his legs, and an olive wreath, holds a lyre in his left arm, and rests his right hand on his seat (rock?); a female figure (only the back of neck and hair, the right shoulder, and the legs below the thighs are preserved), standing profile to the right, wearing a sleeveless chiton, and a long pony tail, holds a thyrsos (?); a satyr (?), dancing to the left (only lower legs are preserved); Komoidia (?), standing (or seated?) 3/4-view to the left (only head, shoulders, and mask held up in right hand are preserved, details lost), wearing a sleeved chiton (?), and a sphendone with an ivy wreath above, rests a thyrsos on his left shoulder; below, a small animal (griffin?), profile to the right; an acanthus column, aligned almost directly below the tripod; more (missing) figures, including Galene (labelled), a satyr seated 3/4-back-view to the right (the left of his head, his left arm, and his feet are missing), wearing an ivy wreath, raises an oinochoe in his right hand; below, a maenad; a satyr dancing (?, only feet preserved, one profile to the left, and one nearly frontal); a maenad seated 3/4-view to the right (only her head and the bottom of her drapery are preserved), with her head profile to the left, tilted up, wearing a sphendone (with a wreath?); a maenad standing profile (?) to the left (only the back of her head and her right forearm are preserved), wearing a pony tail, holds a mask with straight hair in her upraised right hand; Paidia (labelled above her head), standing 3/4-view to the left, wearing a sleeveless chiton, a long pony tail, and an ivy wreath, holds a thyrsos to the left in her right hand, and holds her left arm back, at her side.

artifact.name: Athens, NM 1435
artifact.summary: Personifications of festivals and months
artifact.sources_used: <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 7.435 s.v. Pompe no. 3 (E. Simon); <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 6.482 s.v. Menses no. 1, pl. 256 (D. Parrish); <bibl>Robertson 1992</bibl>, 280 fig. 282; <bibl>Add2</bibl>, 377; <bibl>Simon 1983</bibl>, 5-6, pl. 4; <bibl>LIMC</bibl>, 2.303-304 s.v. Apollon no. 1003, pl. 270 (B. Lambrinudakis et al.); <bibl>Para</bibl>, 492; E. Simon, "Attische Monatsbilder," <hi rend="ital">JdI</hi> 80 (1965) 105-13, 116-23, figs. 1-4, 11; S. artifact.dimensions: Pres. H. 0.271 m; max. diam. (body) 0.335 m
artifact.decoration_description:
A (upper level): Pompai and Theoriai with seven (?) youths (Menes?), including Posideon (December-January) and Elaphebolion (March-April), probably together (only lower bodies of three standing figures preserved).

A (lower level): A white female figure, perhaps Pompe (Eiresione), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, and her right leg relaxed, wearing a red himation draped diagonally over her chest and left shoulder/arm, and a high pony tail, holds her left arm at her side, and raises in her right hand a laurel wreath with which she crowns a youth, perhaps Pyanopsion (October-November), seated 3/4-view to the left, with his legs crossed, wearing a himation over his lower legs, and a wreath over his long hair, raising his right hand, palm out (in a speaking gesture?) to "Eiresione"; in his left hand, he holds a laurel (?) branch, above which is a (waning) moon crescent; a white female figure, Pompe (perhaps a procession to Eleusis), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, and her right leg relaxed, wearing a himation around lower body and draped over her left arm, and a high pony tail, lowers her right hand at her side, and holds in her left hand a wreath aloft, although the hand, and the wreath, are curved in; a youth, perhaps Boedromion (September-October), seated 3/4-view to the right, with his head profile to the left, wearing a himation around lower body, and a laurel (?) wreath around his long hair, holds with both hands on his lap a young, white goat, standing profile to the right; a low altar; above, a (waxing) moon crescent ; a white, female figure, perhaps Theoria (neck and head missing), seated 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation draped around her lower body, holds both bent arms aloft, to either side (missing hands and neck/head); a youth, perhaps Hekatombaion (July-August), standing 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on left leg, his right leg relaxed, leans on a staff under his left armpit, wearing a himation around his lower body, and short hair, turns his head profile to the left, rests his left hand at his side, and raises his right hand, palm out (perhaps in a speaking gesture); a female figure, perhaps Pompe (Hieros Gamos), standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, her right leg relaxed, wearing a himation around lower body, and over her left arm, hangs her left hand at her side, and raises her right arm (missing above the shoulder, as is her head); a youth, perhaps Gamelion (missing the top of his head), standing 3/4-view to the left, with his weight on his right leg, and his left leg relaxed, hangs his right arm at his side, with his forefinger pointing down, and cradles in his left arm a loutrophoros, the top of which is missing; a youth, perhaps Metageition (August-September) or Maimakterion (November-December) (missing his head), seated 3/4-view to the left, with his legs crossed, wearing a himation around lower body, holds his left hand in front of his chest, just above waist level, and holds with his right hand a box (or the bottom of a vase?) on his left shoulder; at least two missing figures.

B: Perhaps a male figure (only left forearm and knee preserved), seated 3/4-view to the right, holding his left hand, palm out, above his lap.

artifact.decoration_description: Nude, white, Eros (labelled), standing on a rocky piece of land (?), near profile to the right, bent over to tie his left sandal (drawn in tiny red lines) with both hands, with his weight on his slightly bent right leg, his bent left leg raised, with frontal, relief gold wings, red/black medium-length, curly hair, ringlets by each ear; tripod kanoun, with lion-claw feet, in gold-decorated relief; Pompe (labelled), standing 3/4-view to the left, with her head profile to the right, her weight on her right leg, and her left leg bent, wearing a purple (?) himation draped around her lower body, held between her knees, and veiled up over her back (she holds the top edge in her mouth), over a pink chiton (?), a relief grain wreath, a relief beaded necklace, a single bead earring, two relief bands on each wrist, and a white anklet on each foot (perhaps denoting the edge of each slipper?), holds an untied wreath between both hands, her right hand raised above her shoulder, and her left hand just above waist level; Dionysos (said to be labelled) seated 3/4-view to the right, in a chair mounted on low platform, with his head turned profile to the left, his right leg pulled back, his left leg extended to the right, wearing a himation draped around his lower body, and up over his back, slightly protruding over his shoulders, and a relief red ivy wreath, his hair tied back, but long ringlets cascading over his shoulder, rests his right arm on the back of his klismos, and holds in his upraised left hand an upright thyrsos with a gold finial.

artifact.decoration_description:
Upper level: A female figure, seated profile to the left, with her head turned profile to the right, wearing a himation wrapped around lower body, a sakkos, a gold beaded necklace, gold bead earrings, and two gold bands on her left wrist, holds with her right hand drapery above her right shoulder, and rests her left hand on the rock to her right; Triptolemos, seated near profile to the right in his winged chariot, legs crossed, wearing a red taenia, holds a phiale in his slightly raised left hand, leans a scepter on his left shoulder, and raises one stalk of grain in his right hand; a female figure seated 3/4-view to the right, with her legs crossed, and her head tilted up, wearing a peplos, a sphendone, a gold necklace, and sandals, holds an implement (usually interpreted as a temple key, although it is large enough to be a plow ) over her right shoulder, and places her right arm on the back of her chair; a youth, standing profile to the left, with his right foot raised on a box, wearing a chlamys and a narrow taenia, holds in his upraised right hand in front of his head, and points down to the left with his left hand.

Lower level: A female figure, standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a himation enveloping her arms, a kekryphylon (?), and a flower over her ear; Kore, standing near frontal, with her head profile to the right, wearing a chiton with shoulder straps, a himation draped over her thighs, a taenia, two necklaces, and two bands on her right wrist, holds an indeterminate object in her left hand, and in her upraised right hand torches resting over her shoulder; to the right of her, a long cylindrical object with a tip; a large female figure, probably Ge, rising out of the ground, 3/4-view to the right, wearing a peplos, a sakkos (?), a grain crown, and a necklace, rests a staff on her left shoulder, and with both hands lifts a keras on top of which is seated Ploutos, 3/4-view to the left, with his head turned profile to the right, wearing a himation over his lower body, extending both arms toward Demeter; a small square object is above "Ge," divided in half and decorated with two large sigmas (perhaps a Bakchos ring, as suggested by Beazley 1941, 4); Demeter, standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her right leg, her left leg relaxed, wearing a peplos, a himation veiled over her left shoulder and head, a grain crown, a gold beaded necklace, and two gold bands on each wrist, holds a scepter in her upraised right hand, and holds her left hand at waist level, reaching toward Ploutos; Iakchos, running 3/4-view to the right, wearing a short, belted oriental tunic, a taenia, and high leather boots, holds a short torch in each hand.

artifact.decoration_description: Eirene and Ploutos, presumably atop a column (or perhaps Tyche and Ploutos): Female figure (preserved except for her right hand, both shoulders, and left arm) standing 3/4-view to the left, with her weight on her right leg, and her head turned 3/4-view to the right, tilted slightly down, wearing an unbelted peplos, a wreath (painted white dots), some strands of hair falling around neck, holds a scepter in her upraised right hand, and cradles in her left arm a keras (black outlined with a white double-line), from which emerges Ploutos (head and top of shoulders revealed), also wearing a white wreath (dotted).

artifact.decoration_description:
A: An inscription, *A*R*X*W*N*K*A*L*L*I*M*H*D*H*S, along a tall black column on a single-stepped base, with a single white band below a white, Ionic capital, a white plinth, and a broader black plinth, on which stands a statue of Eirene, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, and her head turned profile to the right, raising her right hand, and cradling in her left arm a small white boy, Ploutos, wearing a black himation, and holding a white keras in his left hand; he reaches his right hand towards Eirene; an archaistic Athena Promachos standing profile to the right; an inscription, *T*O*N*A*Q*E*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L*O*N, along a column with statue group identical to that on the left.

B: A bearded male figure, standing 3/4-view to the right, wearing a white olive wreath, a himation wrapped around his lower body, draped over his left shoulder and bunched in his left arm, obscuring his left hand, which he rests on his hip, holds a white/gold grain stalk diagonally in his left hand, lowered by his side; two nude wrestlers, still standing, both with short-cropped hair, one with his arms wrapped around the chest of the other; another nude male figure (the ephedros) with short hair, with his weight on his left leg, standing profile to the left, his hands clenched.

artifact.decoration_description:
A: An inscription, *A*R*X*W*N*K*A*L*L*I*M*H*D*H*S, along a black Ionic (?) column on a one-stepped base, topped with a white plinth, with broader black plinth above; on the plinth a female figure, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, and her head in profile to the right, raises her right hand, and cradles in her left arm a white keras from which emerges a small, white boy, Ploutos, with black hair, wearing a black himation (?); he reaches his right hand up towards the head of the female figure; in the center, an archaistic Athena Promachos, standing profile to the right; an inscription, *T*O*N*A*Q[*E]*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L*O*N, along another black column supporting a statue, identical except that the boy is shown holding a smaller white keras, rather than emerging from it.

B: A bearded male figure, probably the referee, standing 3/4-view to the right, with his weight on his left leg, and his head turned profile to the right, wearing a white olive wreath, and a black diagonal himation draped over his left shoulder, arm, and hand (the latter resting on his left hip), holds a white grain stalk diagonally in his right hand, which hangs by his side; a white Nike with black wings, flying 3/4-view to the right, wearing a black chiton with a long kolpos, awarding a white garland to a nude pankratiast, with himantes (leather hand thongs), leaning 3/4-view to the right over another nude pankratiast, also with himantes, on the ground, 3/4-view to the left; a white female figure, perhaps Olympias, standing 3/4-view to the left, legs crossed, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a black himation draped over her left shoulder and obscuring her left hand, which she rests on her left hip, and a long pony-tail, leans on a short thick white column (?) with a flat base.

artifact.decoration_description:
A: An inscription, *T*O*N*A*Q[*E]*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L*O*N, along a tall black column on a single-stepped base, with a black Aeolic capital and a broader black plinth, on which stands a statue of Eirene, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her right leg, wearing a peplos, holds a black scepter in her upraised right hand, and cradles in her left arm Ploutos, a small, white boy, with yellow hair, wearing a black himation, holding a black keras in his left arm, while he reaches with his right arm to the chest of Eirene; an archaistic Athena Promachos, standing profile to the right; a column with a statue identical to that on the left side.

B: A white Nike (acting as referee) with black wings, and red/black hair bound at the nape of the neck, standing profile to the right, with her right arm advanced, wearing a white wreath, a white chiton, and a black himation draped over her left shoulder, holds out a black palm frond, in her right hand; two wrestlers on the ground, each with short-cropped hair; a white Nike with black wings, above, flying down from the upper left, wearing a black himation draped over her left shoulder, awarding a white taenia to the male figure on top; another nude male figure (the ephedros), with short-cropped hair, standing profile to the left, with his weight on his left leg and his hands clenched.

A: An inscription, [*T*O]*N*A*Q[*E]*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L*O*N, along a black column on a two-stepped base, with a white Ionic capital and a white plinth (only preserved on the left side), and a broader black plinth, on which stands Eirene, 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a rayed black stephane, and a peplos belted over a long overfold, holds a black scepter in her upraised right hand, and cradles in her left arm Ploutos, a small, white boy (of which only the ghost remains), with black hair and a keras; Athena Promachos, striding profile to the left; an inscription, [*K]*A*L*L*I*M*H*D*H*S*A*R*X[*W*N], along a black column, like that on the left, but with a statue above (only the bottom of which is preserved) on which the drapery (a black peplos) is dissimilar to that of Eirene.

B: A bearded male figure, probably the referee, standing 3/4-view to the right, with his head profile to the right, wearing a white olive wreath, a black himation draped over his left shoulder, holds his right hand at waist level; two wrestlers, still standing, both with short wavy hair; a winged white female figure (almost completely faded, neck and head missing) standing frontal, with her weight on her left leg, wearing a black himation, rests her left hand on her hip.

A: An inscription, [*T*O*N*A*Q]*E*N*E*Q*E*N*A*Q*L[*O]*N, along a black Aeolic (?) column on a one-stepped base, topped with a black plinth; on the plinth Eirene, standing 3/4-view to the right, with her weight on her left leg, and her head in profile to the right, raises her right hand, and cradles in her left arm a small, white boy, Ploutos, with black hair, wearing a black himation (?), who reaches his right hand up towards the head of Eirene, and holds the keras in his left hand; in the center, an archaistic Athena Promachos, standing profile to the right; an identical column (?), with an inscription, [A*R]*X*W*N*K*A*L*L*I*M*H*D*H*S*.

B: A bearded male figure, probably the referee, standing 3/4-view to the right, with his left leg advanced, holds his right hand at his side, and his left hand in front of his body; two nude wrestlers, both near frontal, with their heads turned profile, wrestling, but standing on the ground (except for left leg of left-most wrestler); female figure (label, according to Themelis, to the right of her head, *O*L*U[*M*P*I]*A*S, standing near frontal, with weight on her left leg, and her head profile to the left, wearing a black himation wrapped entirely around her body, over her bent left arm, holds the back of her left hand on her hip.

For Olympias cf. Athens, NM 20045 and Cambridge 1925.30.124.
